````markdown
# kaggle-code-agent Milestones

Status: M0–M9 done; M9.2 ✓ done (/save-log operator-tooling skill); M10 in planning (notebook-submission regression — Petals to the Metal)  
Created: 2026-05-16  
Scope: hybrid human + AI code competition platform

## Product thesis

`kaggle-code-agent` is a platform for human users to collaborate with AI code agents on code competitions and authorized challenge environments.

Initial focus: Kaggle competitions.  
Later extensions: authorized CTF/lab challenges, Devpost, hackathons, benchmark competitions, and other policy-scoped coding contests.

The platform should help a human user:

- discuss ideas and strategies;
- research competition rules, data, notebooks, papers, discussions, and baseline approaches;
- create, modify, test, and iterate code;
- track experiments, artifacts, results, submissions, and analysis;
- require human approval for external side effects such as Kaggle submissions or remote kernel pushes;
- summarize learnings and produce final writeups.

## Source of truth

**GitHub repo + Claude Code + CI + Supabase migrations.**

All product source code, migrations, tests, architecture decisions, and task specs live in this repository. AI tools do not share hidden memory reliably across sessions or products. Claude Code is the primary development environment for all layers: CLI, backend, UI shell, and worker.

Lovable may be used for visual prototyping or landing-page mockups only. It is not the source of truth for schema, migrations, agent runners, or any backend logic.

## Terminology: two meanings of "code agent"

This project uses two related but distinct agent concepts.

### 1. Platform-development coding agents

These are external AI tools used to build this repository.

Examples:

- Claude Code CLI / VS Code / Desktop / Web (primary);
- ChatGPT Pro / Cursor (supplementary);
- GitHub Actions / Claude Code Web / Routines for cloud automation.

Role:

- write and review this product's source code;
- update docs, tasks, tests, and architecture decisions;
- run local tests and CI repair loops;
- open branches/PRs under human supervision.

Important rule: these tools do not share hidden memory reliably. GitHub repository files are the durable source of truth.

### 2. Runtime competition code agents

These are agents launched by the finished platform to help a human user compete.

Initial runtime direction:

- Claude Agent SDK as the first core worker/harness;
- isolated workspace/container per job;
- Python/notebook-first for Kaggle;
- TypeScript/Python service boundary depending on platform vs worker needs;
- future model router for Claude, GPT-style models, local vLLM/Ollama models, and specialized tools.

Runtime agents must operate under competition-specific policy, sandboxing, budget limits, approval gates, and audit logging.

## Architecture north star

```text
Human user / future UI
        ↓
TypeScript-first platform/control plane
  - project/session/job/task queue
  - policy and approval gates
  - discussion/research/analysis records
  - experiment/run/submission/artifact records
  - model router configuration
        ↓
Worker layer
  - Python-first Kaggle workers
  - Claude Agent SDK runtime sessions
  - notebooks/scripts/tools/kca wrappers
  - Playwright/browser/research tools
  - sandboxed execution and evaluation
        ↓
External systems
  - GitHub repo / branches / PRs
  - Supabase DB/storage/edge functions later
  - Kaggle API/CLI, only with approval for remote side effects
  - authorized CTF/lab/hackathon platforms under explicit policy
```

## Cross-cutting rules

- GitHub repo files are the project memory and source of truth.
- Each agent task gets a branch/worktree/PR when it modifies code.
- Main branch remains stable and protected.
- Do not allow multiple AI sessions to edit the same branch/files at the same time.
- No secrets in repo, prompts, logs, artifacts, or screenshots.
- Kaggle submissions, kernel pushes, dataset uploads, and other remote side effects require explicit human approval.
- CTF/lab work must be local/sandboxed or explicitly authorized.
- Every task prompt should include acceptance criteria and a stop condition.
- Every worker loop should have budget, turn, time, and side-effect limits.
- Tests and local validation should run before external submission.

## Milestone final-review protocol

After every milestone final review, before marking done:

1. Update `PROJECT_STATE.md` — set current milestone, summarize open decisions, and record any new known blockers.
2. Update `README.md` current milestone section to name the new active milestone and goal.
3. Update `docs/milestones.md` — mark the finished milestone `✓ done`, add a one-line summary of what landed, and note any follow-ups carried forward.
4. Write `docs/handoffs/m{x}-handoff.md` — a per-milestone, ready-to-paste context prompt for the next AI tool / session that will start M{x+1}. Use `docs/handoff-prompt.md` as the canonical template; populate the "State at handoff", "Read these files first", and "Current task" sections from the M{x} final review and the M{x+1} entry in this file. The generic `docs/handoff-prompt.md` stays as the template; the per-milestone instances live under `docs/handoffs/`.

## M6: multi-agent review + OTEL telemetry + local-model layer ✓ done

Goal: harden the M3–M5 worker with an independent reviewer agent, end-to-end
OpenTelemetry tracing, and a local-model layer that routes log-triage /
summarisation jobs to user-owned GPU hosts before paying for cloud tokens.

Planned capabilities:

- Reviewer agent (sync mode) fires before high-stakes ops
  (`kaggle_submit`, `supabase_migrate`, `git_force_push`, `dataset_upload`,
  `delete_artifact`). Verdict `approve | reject | abstain` lands in a new
  `agent_reviews` table; `approve` satisfies the matching approval gate
  without human intervention, `reject` escalates (default) or fails the
  job, `abstain` falls through to the existing human-decisions flow.
- Local-model layer (`src/worker/local_model.py`) talks to vLLM / Ollama
  endpoints on the user's GPU hosts (`snorlax` RTX 4090, `may` RTX 3090)
  via OpenAI-compatible HTTP. Numbered-slot env config
  (`KCA_LOCAL_ENDPOINT_<n>_*`), priority ordering, a TTL-cached probe, and
  a `KCA_LOCAL_FALLBACK_MODEL` cloud fallback.
- New job types `log_triage` and `summarise` route to the local layer by
  default; `kca local probe / pick / triage` surfaces endpoint state.
- OTEL instrumentation per ADR-0007 with three exporters: stderr (dev),
  SQLite (`.agent/telemetry.sqlite`), and Supabase
  (`agent_telemetry_spans`). Spans cover job / turn / tool / reviewer /
  local-probe.
- TC-3 Spaceship Titanic exercises the reviewer-gate path end-to-end on a
  binary-classification submission flow.

Exit criteria: all met. See `docs/m6-final-review.md`.

## M7: KCA CLI architecture — command / skill / tool / job / permission policy ✓ done

_Shipped 2026-05-21: four-layer CLI scaffold (command/skill/tool/job), skill loader, tool registry (16 tools), three permission profiles, `kca skill list/show/run` + `kca tool list/audit/doctor`, four seed skills, audit JSONL, 15 smoke tests, and `docs/architecture/kca-cli-architecture.md`. 28/28 exit checks PASS — see `docs/m7-final-review.md`._

Goal: implement the full KCA command/skill/tool/job architecture so the platform
has a stable, inspectable CLI that can drive agent workflows, replace ad-hoc
`python tools/kca/kca.py` calls, and enforce structured permission decisions.

This is distinct from the product UI shell (M8): M7 is operator/developer-facing
and headless. The UI in M8 will call into the same CLI/API surface.

See `docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-21-r1.md` §1–3 for full design rationale.

### Four-layer model

| Layer | Description |
|---|---|
| **Command** | Deterministic CLI/API entry points for operators (`kca job run`, `kca decision approve`). |
| **Skill** | Agent-facing workflow recipes stored under `.kca/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter. Callable via `kca skill run <name>` or slash-style invocation. |
| **Tool** | Executable actions with input/output schema, timeout, permission label, sandbox metadata, and audit logging. |
| **Job** | Durable records that run a skill through the agent loop with budget, turn, cost, runtime limits, and decision gates. |

### M7 task sequence

| Task | Description | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| M7-T000 | Audit + repair `.github/workflows/` — fix failing CI checks, add no-db + lint jobs | — |
| M7-T001 | Skill loader: read `.kca/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter; argument substitution | — |
| M7-T002 | Command registry: register KCA CLI subcommands declaratively | T001 |
| M7-T003 | Tool registry: tool metadata, approval policy labels, sandbox metadata | T001 |
| M7-T004 | Permission policy layer: allow/ask/deny resolution with structured JSON policy records | T003 |
| M7-T005 | Slash-style invocation: `kca skill run <name> [args] [--dry-run]` shows permissions + rendered prompt | T001, T004 |
| M7-T006 | Audit logging: record every tool execution in `agent_job_events` with policy decision | T004 |
| M7-T007 | Seed `.kca/skills/` with `run-milestone`, `triage-log`, `prepare-submission`, `review-pr` | T001 |
| M7-T008 | `tests/test_m7_smoke.py`: skill parsing, arg substitution, permission resolution, command registry, decision gates | T001–T006 |
| M7-T009 | Documentation: `docs/architecture/kca-cli-architecture.md` explaining Commands vs Skills vs Tools vs Jobs | all |
| M7-T010 | M7 exit criteria validation + `docs/m7-final-review.md` | all |

### Permission policy design

Runtime agent permissions are data, not ad-hoc prompts:

```json
{
  "operation": "kaggle.submit",
  "default_decision": "ask",
  "reason": "External competition submission",
  "allowed_in_modes": ["human-approved", "competition-finalization"],
  "audit_required": true
}
```

Allow by default: edit workspace files, run tests/benchmark, create artifacts,
summarize logs, call LiteLLM/local models, create branch, commit, create PR.

Decision gate: submit to Kaggle, merge PR, publish dataset/kernel, apply
remote Supabase migration, spend above budget threshold, change model tier,
change competition direction/objective.

Deny: read secrets, write outside workspace, sudo/root, rm outside workspace,
drop database/schema, force push, network exfiltration.

### Recommended directory layout

```text
.kca/
  skills/
    run-milestone/SKILL.md
    triage-log/SKILL.md
    prepare-submission/SKILL.md
    review-pr/SKILL.md
  tools/tools.yaml
  permissions/
    default.yaml
    permissive-dev.yaml
    competition-runner.yaml

tools/kca/
  kca.py
  commands/
    job.py  skill.py  tool.py  decision.py
    workspace.py  kaggle.py  supabase.py
  agent/
    runner.py  skill_loader.py  tool_executor.py
    permission_policy.py  audit.py
```

Exit criteria:

- `kca skill list` shows available skills from `.kca/skills/`.
- `kca skill show <name>` prints parsed metadata and body.
- `kca skill run <name> ... --dry-run` prints planned tool permissions and rendered prompt without executing.
- Permission policy resolves allow/ask/deny for any (operation, mode) pair.
- Audit log records every tool execution with policy decision.
- `.github/workflows/` CI passes on main branch (no-db + lint at minimum).
- `tests/test_m7_smoke.py` passes without API keys or DB.
- Documentation explains Commands vs Skills vs Tools vs Jobs.

- Test pass rate.
````

> ## Canonical Pattern Report for M11 Planning
> 
> Based on thorough exploration of the repository, here are the canonical patterns for milestone planning:
> 
> ### 1. **M10 Loop Prompts Structure** 
> **File:** `/home/harry/test/tt_pangu/docs/m10-loop-prompts.md`
> 
> **Structure:**
> - **Header block:** preamble with date, competition, execution platform, prerequisites
> - **"M10 at a glance":** 1–2 paragraphs + table of what's in/out of scope
> - **Task summary table:** `| Task | Goal | Loop Prompt |` mapping
> - **Per-prompt section:** numbered `## Loop Prompt N — M10-TN` with a code-block containing:
>   - `/goal` line (user-facing direction)
>   - `Follow: docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md`
>   - `Task spec: docs/tasks/M10-TN-*.md`
>   - `Read also:` (background context links)
>   - `Mission:` (paragraph summary)
> - **Approval gates section:** table with Gate name | When it fires | Where recorded | Who approves
> - **Required tests / evidence:** bulleted checklist of green-state artifacts
> - **Rollback / stop criteria:** conditions that block milestone advance
> - **Running on Arch Linux:** setup commands for DB DSN, credentials, per-prompt invocation
> - **Human decisions needed:** pre-recorded decisions from the proposal issue
> 
> **Field pattern in each Loop Prompt:**
> ```
> /goal Execute M10-TN <task> until acceptance criteria pass or stop after N turns…
> Follow: docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md
> Task spec: docs/tasks/M10-TN-<title>.md
> Read also:
>   - previous closeouts
>   - source files and tools
>   - precedent tasks from M9
> Mission: (full description)
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> ### 2. **Task Spec Layout**
> **Files:** `/home/harry/test/tt_pangu/docs/tasks/M10-T00*.md` (9 files, one per task)
> 
> **Canonical sections (from M10-T000):**
> 1. `## Milestone` — e.g., "M10: live end-to-end regression test"
> 2. `## Goal` — 1–2 sentences on deliverable
> 3. `## Read first` — numbered list of files to read (1–12 items)
> 4. `## Scope` — numbered steps, sub-steps with code/examples
> 5. `## Non-goals` — bullet list of what NOT to do
> 6. `## Acceptance criteria` — bulleted assertions (0.30 < acc < 0.99; etc.)

````markdown
# M10 — Loop Prompts

_Live end-to-end Kaggle regression test on
[Petals to the Metal — Flower Classification on TPU](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/tpu-getting-started)._
_For sequential, partly autonomous execution on Arch Linux._
_Prerequisite: M9 exit confirmed (live LB recorded, dry-run e2e green; see `docs/m9-final-review.md`)._
_Shared rules: every Loop Prompt below MUST follow `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` (sequencing, no real Kaggle/Anthropic outside designated approval paths, DB DSN + sandbox bypass, **per-milestone worktree by default**, secret denylist)._

---

## M10 at a glance

M10 is the **second end-to-end live Kaggle regression** for this platform, and
the first to exercise the **notebook-submission / kernel-push** path.
M9 validated the CSV-submission path (`kca kaggle submit` →
`kaggle competitions submit`) on Spaceship Titanic. M10 validates the
notebook-submission path (`kca kaggle push` → `kaggle kernels push` →
kernel run → public LB) on Petals to the Metal — Flower Classification on TPU
(`tpu-getting-started`).

Petals to the Metal is "Getting Started" tier: multi-class image
classification over 104 flower species, public leaderboard, no cash prize,
safe for repeated dry-run iteration and a single real kernel push under
explicit human approval. TPU is optional — Kaggle accepts GPU-backed
notebooks for this competition too — so the baseline can run locally
and only the kernel runner needs Kaggle's hardware.

M10 is **not** a leaderboard-chasing milestone. The acceptance criterion is
that the kernel-push loop *runs end-to-end correctly under the approval
gates*, not that the LB score is high. The CV / holdout thresholds in
`docs/milestones.md` §M10 are sanity guards, not targets.

Direct entry into M10 is blocked until **all** are true:

- M9 is merged on main (`docs/m9-final-review.md` exists and reports PASS).
- Issue #11 (dotenv-leak / Kaggle leaderboard pollution) is merged on main —
  hard pre-req for **M10-T007** so the new dry-run e2e test cannot leak
  into the `tpu-getting-started` leaderboard the same way M9 leaked into
  Spaceship Titanic. M10-T000 through M10-T006 may proceed in parallel
  with #11 work; only T007 is gated on it.
- The local Supabase container is running and the M9 DB rows (M9-T002 /
  M9-T004 / M9-T005) are reachable (M10-T006 references the M9 baseline
  for cross-milestone regression sanity).

### What's in scope

| Capability | Owned by | M10 touches |
|---|---|---|
| Kaggle credentials handling | `env.example`, `.env`, `KAGGLE_USERNAME`/`KAGGLE_KEY` | T000 — verifies env without printing secrets; gates push on presence |
| Competition register + workspace | `tools/kca/competition.py` (`register`, `clone`, `list`, `info`) | T000 / T001 |
| Data discovery for non-CSV competitions | `tools/kca/kg.py` (existing `cmd_download` / `cmd_verify` if extended) + a new manifest shape | T001 — notebook competitions read TFRecord-style data from Kaggle-hosted GCS at kernel runtime; the local manifest records `kaggle competitions files` output, not file checksums |
| Notebook authoring + percent-format round-trip | `kg-nb` skill (`tools/kca/notebook.py` or equivalent) | T002 / T007 |
| Worker loop (research → baseline → local CV → notebook artifact) | `src/worker/` + `tools/kca/run.py` + skills | T002 |
| Reviewer gate before kernel push | `src/worker/reviewer.py` + `services/decision_api/` + UI Approval Inbox (under `target_op="kernel_push"`) | T003 |
| Real Kaggle kernel push (under approval) | `tools/kca/kg.py::cmd_push` + `kaggle kernels push` + kernel-run polling | T004 — single real call |
| Second experiment (alt backbone / augmentation) | same worker, second run | T005 |
| Regression assertions | `tests/test_m10_e2e.py` + `runs` table + `submissions` table | T006 / T007 |
| GitHub issue / label workflow | `.github/labels.yml`, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`, `.github/pull_request_template.md`, `policy:approval-required` | every task — work order issue per task; issue #12 is the canonical M10 proposal |
| Final review | `milestone-final-review` skill + `worktree-milestone-pr` skill | T008 |

### What's NOT in scope

- Running Kaggle submit / kernel push / dataset upload / model upload outside
  T004's single approved kernel-push call.
- Changing production Supabase.
- Implementing M9 follow-ups A, C, D, E (tracked as issues #14, #15, #16, #17).
  They run in parallel; if M10 surfaces blockers, file follow-up issues —
  don't expand scope. Issue #11 is the only hard pre-req (see entry gates).
- Adding new CLI subcommands beyond what `cmd_push` already provides. M10
  uses the existing `kca` surface (`competition`, `kaggle`, `run`,
  `research`, `review`, `decisions`, `skill`) without inventing new ones.
  Internal helpers (e.g. kernel-run polling) may be added under
  `tools/kca/kg.py` as private functions if `cmd_push` doesn't already
  cover them, but no new top-level subcommand surface.
- Auto-selecting between CSV-submit and kernel-push paths based on
  competition metadata. That is the scope of issues #7 / #8 (submission-
  format awareness / competition-rules ingestion) and is a co-traveller
  for M10, not a deliverable.
- TPU runtime tuning. The baseline notebook may declare a TPU strategy
  for Kaggle's kernel runner, but local training is GPU/CPU; M10 does
  not own TPU-specific performance work.

DB / sandbox details: see `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` §3 — the local
`supabase-db` container (`postgresql://postgres:s3cr3t@172.21.0.4:5432/postgres`)
needs `dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true`. The real Kaggle CLI call inside
M10-T004 also needs sandbox bypass (network out to `kaggle.com`).

Each M10 task is filed as a GitHub issue using the `feature-work.yml` form,
labelled per task type. Issue #12 is the canonical M10 proposal /
decision-confirmation record; individual task issues link back to it.

| Task | Issue labels at file time | Labels added by triage | Labels at merge |
|---|---|---|---|
| M10-T000 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:kaggle`, `area:config`, `area:security` | `ai:ready` (after AC + owner) | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M10-T001 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:kaggle` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M10-T002 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:worker`, `area:kaggle` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M10-T003 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:worker`, `area:supabase`, `area:ui` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M10-T004 | `type:feature`, `ai:blocked`, `policy:approval-required`, `decision:needed`, `area:kaggle`, `priority:P0` | `decision:confirmed` + `ai:ready` only after human comment "approved to push" | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M10-T005 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:worker`, `area:kaggle` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M10-T006 | `type:test-gap`, `ai:triage`, `area:testing` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M10-T007 | `type:test-gap`, `ai:triage`, `area:testing`, `area:ci` | `ai:ready` only after issue #11 is closed | `ai:implementing` → close |

T004 is the only task that starts `ai:blocked` and requires a
`decision:confirmed` comment with an explicit "approved to push" record
before triage may promote it to `ai:ready`. This is enforced by the
`github-issue-triage` agent rules in `.claude/skills/github-issue-triage/`.

T007 is the only task gated on closing a separate issue (#11). The
triage agent should refuse to promote T007 to `ai:ready` while
`gh issue view 11 --json state` returns `"OPEN"`.

The PR for each task uses `.github/pull_request_template.md`. The

## Approval gates (summary)

| Gate | When it fires | Where the approval is recorded | Who can approve |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kernel_push` | Worker stages a notebook + kernel-metadata.json and calls into `tools/kca/kg.py::cmd_push` | `human_decisions` row + comment on the closing GitHub issue | Project owner / reviewer named on the issue |
| `kaggle_submit` | Not used in M10 (would be a second-submission path; out of scope) | n/a | n/a |
| `dataset_upload` | Not used in M10 | n/a | n/a |
| `model_upload` | Not used in M10 | n/a | n/a |

The Kaggle approval flow inside M10 is:

```
worker stages notebook + kernel-metadata.json
  → reviewer-gate writes agent_reviews row + agent_job_events
    (target_op="kernel_push")
  → decision_api surfaces pending decision (POST /decisions queued; UI
    reads via supabase-js until issue #15 lands GET /decisions)
  → UI Approval Inbox renders pending decision
  → human approves via UI (POST /decisions/<id>/approve) OR
    `kca decisions approve --id <id>`
  → human comments "approved to push" on the closing issue
  → triage agent promotes issue to `decision:confirmed` + `ai:ready`
  → M10-T004 Loop Prompt runs ONE `kca kaggle push`
  → poll kaggle kernels status until non-running
  → LB score recorded; submissions row written with kernel-run linkage
  → PR opens with the approval comment linked
```

A second real Kaggle push inside M10 is **out of scope**. If a
follow-up experiment in M10-T005 turns out to need its own LB score,
file it as a new M11+ issue and gate it the same way.

## Rollback / stop criteria

Stop the milestone — do **not** advance to the next Loop Prompt — if any of
these is true:

- A real Kaggle kernel push returns an error from Kaggle (rate limit,
  bad notebook metadata, rules violation). The fix path is local:
  regenerate the notebook + kernel metadata and re-request approval;
  do NOT silently retry.
- The reviewer gate (M10-T003) fails to fire when it should, or fires
  when it shouldn't.
- Any `policy:approval-required` issue advances without the corresponding
  `decision:confirmed` label and comment.
- Any test in the validation suite regresses from green to red.
- The DSN, credentials, or `.env*` are accidentally printed in any log,
  audit row, or PR. Stop and rotate the credential immediately.
- Local CV / holdout scores diverge from the M10-T006 thresholds in a
  way that suggests a leakage bug (e.g. holdout near 1.0). Investigate
  before pushing.
- Issue #11 is reopened mid-milestone with evidence that the leak
  re-emerged. Halt T007 work until #11 is green again.

If M10 needs a new architectural decision (e.g. submission-format
auto-selection, a new artifact-storage shape for notebook payloads, a
TPU-specific resource model), **pause and ask** — those are M11+ /
issue #7 / issue #8 decisions, not M10 expansion. Open an ADR draft in
`docs/adr/` and stop the milestone there.
````

````markdown
# Milestone Loop Protocol

_Shared rules that apply to every milestone Loop Prompt (M0+) unless a
milestone explicitly overrides one._

Each `docs/m*-loop-prompts.md` should reference this file once at the top
rather than duplicating the rules per prompt.

---

## 1. Sequencing

- Loop Prompts within a milestone MUST execute in order.
- Each prompt's **acceptance checks MUST pass** before moving to the next.
- On failure: fix the specific issue and **retry that prompt only**; do
  not skip ahead and do not redo prompts that already passed.

## 2. External systems and side effects

- Do NOT call the **real Anthropic API or Kaggle API** outside of paths
  the milestone explicitly designates as live; default to `--dry-run`.
- Do NOT run real **Kaggle submit / kernel push / dataset upload /
  model upload** unless the milestone explicitly requests it AND a
  human-approval record exists.
- Do NOT change **production Supabase**.

## 3. Database validation

- Use `SUPABASE_DB_URL=postgresql://postgres:s3cr3t@172.21.0.4:5432/postgres`
  — the `supabase-db` container on the local Docker network.
- Container IPs change on `docker compose down/up`; refresh with:
  ```bash
  docker inspect supabase-db \
    --format '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}'
  ```
- DB calls and LAN-host calls require `dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true`.
  Cloud LLM calls stay **inside** the sandbox.

## 4. Reporting

- Report **PASS / FAIL / SKIP** inline for each prompt's verification
  step.
- At milestone end, write the milestone's defined **Closeout format**
  (see each milestone's last Loop Prompt for the exact fields).

## 5. Git / GitHub — worktree mode

This project executes each milestone inside a dedicated **git worktree**
branched off `main`.

- **Mid-milestone, mid-prompt:** do not `git commit` or `git push`
  unless the individual task spec explicitly says so. Stage with
  `git add` and surface diffs in the inline report.
- **At milestone end** — once every Loop Prompt has PASSed and the
  milestone's Closeout has been written — Claude Code SHOULD:
  1. `git add` only the files listed in the Closeout's "files changed"
     section (or its equivalent).
  2. `git commit` using either:
     - one squash commit per milestone, OR
     - one commit per Loop Prompt,
     depending on the milestone's preference. The default is **one
     commit per Loop Prompt**, with the milestone's final review as the
     last commit.
  3. `git push` the worktree's branch to the remote.
  4. `gh pr create` against `main` using the milestone's
     `docs/m{N}-final-review.md` as the PR body.

- The following **still require explicit human approval** at any time:
  - `git push --force` (any branch)
  - `gh pr merge` (any PR)
  - any push to `main` directly
  - any `gh label create/edit/delete`, `gh issue edit/comment`,
    `gh pr edit/comment` against issues or PRs **not** owned by this
    milestone

- If the milestone's task spec or scope says
  "do not commit / push / open PRs", that override **wins** — typically
  used for planning-only or evidence-only milestones.

## 6. Secrets and forbidden reads

These are always denied, regardless of milestone:

- `.env*`
- `**/kaggle.json`, `~/.kaggle/kaggle.json`
- `~/.ssh/id_rsa`, `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`, any private key contents
- `~/.aws/**`, `~/.config/gcloud/**`
- `secrets/**`

Shell commands that would surface the above (`cat`, `grep`, `head`,
`tail`, `less`, `more`, file uploads) over these paths are blocked at
the hook layer.

---

## How a milestone references this file

In each Loop Prompt block, instead of repeating the rules above, include
one line near the top:

```
Follow: docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md
```

A milestone's `docs/m{N}-loop-prompts.md` should still spell out:

- the milestone's own scope, non-goals, and task list;
- per-Loop-Prompt read lists, scope, acceptance criteria;
- any **override** of a default in this file (e.g. a planning-only
  milestone overriding the worktree commit/push behavior).

---

## 7. Discovery / Debate Gate

_Added by M9.4. Additive only — §1–§6 above are unchanged._

Some tasks are large enough that "implement first, debate later"
loses load-bearing requirements (the canonical failure: `tools/legacy/kkr.py`
migration missing multi-Kaggle-account / owner / env semantics; see
`docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-24-r3.md` §6). The Discovery / Debate Gate
runs three role-isolated subagents — `legacy-archaeologist`,
`requirements-skeptic`, `design-red-team` — **before** any
implementation work begins.

The gate is **mandatory** for any task whose spec is tagged `arch:`
(introduces / revises an architectural primitive) or
`legacy-migration:` (migrates / rewrites / replaces a legacy artefact).
Routine tasks (bug fixes, doc edits, dependency bumps, small
refactors) do not trigger the gate.

When the gate fires, the executing session MUST:

1. Invoke `legacy-archaeologist` first if the task touches any
   legacy artefact (skip allowed only for greenfield `arch:` tasks,
   with explicit note in the closeout).
2. Invoke `requirements-skeptic` next.
3. Invoke `design-red-team` last.
4. Attach all three reports to the task closeout under
   `docs/evidence/<milestone>/<task>/discovery/`.
5. Verify all three canonical acceptance lines (defined in
   `docs/architecture/discovery-debate-gate.md`) byte-for-byte
   against the reports. A missing acceptance line is a task FAIL.

Full template, tag-placement options, and the verbatim acceptance
lines live in `docs/architecture/discovery-debate-gate.md`. The
orchestration skill `.claude/skills/design-archaeology/SKILL.md`
(owned by M9.3) is the inline alternative when the task is small
enough not to warrant separate subagents; the agent path and the
skill path emit compatible output shapes by design.

M9.4 enforces the gate via task-spec acceptance criteria and this
section's wording, **not** via hook-level denials. Hook-based
enforcement is a deferred follow-up; file a separate issue if you
want it built.

````

```markdown
# M10-T000: Kaggle credentials + competition registration (`tpu-getting-started`)

## Milestone
M10: live end-to-end regression test — Petals to the Metal (notebook-submission / kernel-push path).

## Goal
Confirm the agent can read Kaggle credentials without exposing them, run
READ_ONLY Kaggle calls against the kernel-runner path, and register
`tpu-getting-started` (Petals to the Metal) in the local control plane.
No real push, no submission, no dataset / model upload.

This task assumes **M9 is merged on main** (`docs/m9-final-review.md`
reports PASS) and that the M9-T000 deviation (AC #1 satisfied via
`kaggle.api.config_values` rather than the literal python-dotenv check)
is honoured here too.

## Read first

1. `PROJECT_STATE.md`
2. `AGENTS.md`
3. `CLAUDE.md`
4. `docs/milestones.md` §M10
5. `docs/engineering-practice.md`
6. `docs/m9-final-review.md` (M9-T000 deviation)
7. `docs/handoffs/m9-handoff.md`
8. `env.example`
9. `tools/kca/competition.py`
10. `tools/kca/kg.py` — `cmd_list`, `cmd_watch`, `cmd_fetch`, `cmd_push` (header / args only — do NOT call), `add_parsers`
11. `.claude/settings.json` — verify Kaggle `submit/push/upload/datasets`
    are on `ask`
12. `.claude/hooks/guard_tool.py` — verify `kaggle.json` / `.env` reads
    are denied

## Scope

1. Verify Kaggle credentials are reachable WITHOUT printing them. Two
   accepted paths:
   - Preferred: `python -c "from dotenv import load_dotenv; import os; load_dotenv(); print(bool(os.environ.get('KAGGLE_USERNAME')), bool(os.environ.get('KAGGLE_KEY')))"` prints `True True`.
   - Equivalent (per M9-T000 deviation): `python -c "from kaggle import api; api.authenticate(); cv = api.config_values; print(bool(cv.get('username')), bool(cv.get('key')))"` prints `True True`.
   Either is acceptable; the deviation exists because in some sandboxed
   views `.env` is bind-mounted to `/dev/null`. Booleans only — never
   the values.
2. Run `kca kaggle list --json` (READ_ONLY) to confirm credentials work.
   Capture only the count or slug presence, never the raw response.
3. Run `kaggle competitions files -c tpu-getting-started` (READ_ONLY) to
   confirm the kernel-runnable competition is reachable. **Do not run
   `kaggle kernels push`, `kaggle kernels init`, `kaggle datasets create`,
   or any write op.** Capture only the file-count and / or names; do
   not echo raw bytes.
4. Register Petals to the Metal via
   `kca competition register --slug tpu-getting-started --name "Petals to the Metal - Flower Classification on TPU"`
   (LOCAL_WRITE, gated on the local DB). If `cmd_register` errors due
   to the `competitions.repo_url` schema drift (M9 follow-up A, issue
   #14), document the workaround used and link issue #14 in the
   closeout; do not block the milestone on closing #14.
5. Run `kca competition info --slug tpu-getting-started --json` and
   confirm the entry is in the `competitions` table.
6. File or update the closing GitHub issue with the M10-T000 acceptance
   criteria, evidence links, and `ai:ready` once the decisions in issue
   #12 are `decision:confirmed` (they already are; recorded here for
   the audit trail).

## Non-goals

- Do not run `kca kaggle submit`, `kca kaggle push`,
  `kaggle competitions submit`, `kaggle kernels push`,
  `kaggle datasets create`, `kaggle datasets version`, or `kca kaggle upload`.
- Do not print credential values to stdout, logs, audit rows, or PR
  bodies.
- Do not change `.claude/settings.json` or `.claude/hooks/guard_tool.py`.
- Do not add a new `kca` subcommand for credential probing — use the
  existing READ_ONLY ones.

## Acceptance criteria

- Credentials are reachable per one of the two accepted paths in scope
  step 1 — produces `True True`, nothing else.
- `kca kaggle list --json` exits 0.
- `kaggle competitions files -c tpu-getting-started` exits 0 and
  reports a non-zero file count.
```

````markdown
## Scope

1. Drive a worker job (`kca skill run kaggle-experiment-loop --execute`

   - **Backbone:** small pretrained ImageNet model (e.g. MobileNetV2 or
     EfficientNetB0). Choose deterministically (record the choice in
     the closeout).
   - **Image size:** 192x192 by default (smallest variant — fastest
     local iteration). If 192 is unavailable, fall back to the next
     smallest the manifest reports.
   - **Train / val split:** the spec's recommended local split (the
     competition publishes train / val TFRecords separately; use them
     as-is and report holdout accuracy on val).
   - **Optimizer / epochs:** Adam, default learning rate, ≤ 5 epochs
     for the local sanity run. Local training is for the CV / holdout
     evidence, not for SOTA. The Kaggle kernel runner in M10-T004 will
     re-train (or load the same weights) on Kaggle's hardware.
   - **Random seed:** pinned per spec convention (default `seed=42`).
2. Author the kernel-runnable notebook at

   on macro F1, so record both if feasible).
5. Verify the notebook executes locally end-to-end at least once
   (e.g. `jupyter nbconvert --to notebook --execute` on a stub run
   with reduced epochs), to catch import errors before the live push.

## Non-goals

- Do not run `kca kaggle push` / `submit` / `upload`.
- Do not invent new top-level `kca` subcommands.
- Do not train for hours — local is for sanity, not LB chasing.

- Do not download the full Petals to the Metal dataset locally; use
````

```markdown
---
name: ctf-sandbox
description: Use for authorized CTF challenge solving only: local challenge analysis, sandboxed exploitation, solver scripts, flags, and writeups within explicitly provided scope.
---

# CTF Sandbox Workflow

Use this workflow only for explicitly authorized CTF challenges, local labs, or target scopes provided by the human.

## Safety scope

Allowed:

- Analyze local challenge files.
- Run challenge containers or binaries provided for the CTF.
- Interact with explicitly provided CTF endpoints.
- Write solver scripts and educational writeups.

Not allowed:

- Scan public IP ranges or unrelated domains.
- Attack third-party systems.
- Steal or exfiltrate real credentials.
- Deploy malware, persistence, or destructive payloads.
- Use CTF techniques outside the authorized scope.

## Workflow

1. Restate the authorized scope and target.
2. Inventory files, services, ports, and constraints.
3. Identify category: crypto, pwn, web, reversing, forensics, misc, OSINT, etc.
4. Form hypotheses and run minimal safe checks.
5. Keep commands and outputs logged.
6. Build a solver or exploit only within the challenge scope.
7. Produce a concise writeup with root cause, steps, flag, and mitigation idea if relevant.

If scope is unclear, ask the human to define the CTF target before running security tooling.
```

```markdown
## M11: authorized CTF/lab workflow

_Renumbered from old M10 on 2026-05-24 to make room for the
notebook-submission regression milestone (new M10)._

Goal: support CTF-style challenges only inside explicit authorization boundaries.

Planned capabilities:

- Challenge scope and authorization metadata.
- Local container/lab-only execution.
- Solver script generation and testing.
- Writeup generation.
- Hard policy blocks for external scanning, real targets, credential theft, persistence, or unsafe actions.

Exit criteria:

- CTF workflow is useful for local/sandbox labs and safely refuses out-of-scope activity.

---

## M12: Devpost/hackathon workflow

_Renumbered from old M11 on 2026-05-24._

Goal: generalize competition policy modules beyond Kaggle and CTF.

Planned capabilities:

- Hackathon rules and deadline tracking.
- Team discussion and idea board.
- App prototype workflows.
- Demo/video/readme generation.
- Submission checklist and approval gates.

Exit criteria:

- The same platform can represent different competition policies without changing worker core logic.

---

## M13: evaluation, reliability, and regression suite

_Renumbered from old M12 on 2026-05-24._

Goal: measure whether the platform improves over time.

Planned test cases:

- Tool smoke tests.
- Classic Kaggle practice tasks.
- Notebook/kernel dry-run workflows.
- Reasoning-heavy Kaggle-style test cases.
- Authorized local CTF labs.
- Regression comparisons across Claude/GPT/local model routes.

Metrics:

- Task completion rate.
- Test pass rate.
- Cost per successful run.
- Human intervention count.
- Approval gate correctness.
- Artifact/log completeness.
- Regression failure rate.

Exit criteria:

- New platform changes can be evaluated against known workflows before use in real competitions.

---

## Open design questions

- Should the first platform UI service be TypeScript-only, or TypeScript API + Python worker from day one?
- Which Supabase queue/job mechanism should be used first?
- What is the minimal local sandbox acceptable for Kaggle worker experiments?
- What policy schema best represents Kaggle vs CTF vs hackathon side effects?
- What model-router interface is stable enough for MVP without overengineering?

```
</details>

````markdown
inadvertently posted 3 ERROR submissions to the Spaceship Titanic
leaderboard because `tools/kca/db.py` re-injects `.env` credentials
````

````markdown
# Discovery / Debate Gate

_Status: M9.4 ships the gate (this doc + protocol §7 + the three agents). The
`.claude/skills/design-archaeology/SKILL.md` orchestration the gate
references is owned by M9.3; M9.3-T001 must land that skill before §7
becomes fully enforceable end-to-end._

## What this is

The Discovery / Debate Gate is the M9.4-shipped guardrail that turns
"please be more proactive in plan / design / architect mode" into a
**checkable artefact**. Three role-isolated subagents run before any
implementation work begins on an architecture-shaped or
legacy-migration-shaped task. Each agent has a canonical acceptance
line that the parent session verifies; the three lines together form
the gate.

Origin: `docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-24-r3.md` §6 — the observation
that the original `tools/legacy/kkr.py` migration missed
multi-Kaggle-account / owner / env semantics because no agent role
was responsible for surfacing them.

## Agents

| Agent | File | Phase | Reads | Emits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `legacy-archaeologist` | `.claude/agents/legacy-archaeologist.md` | 1 of 3 | legacy artefacts (read-only) | 10-section archaeology report |
| `requirements-skeptic` | `.claude/agents/requirements-skeptic.md` | 2 of 3 | proposed task spec + archaeology report | numbered question list across 5 categories + `explicit_unknowns:` |
| `design-red-team` | `.claude/agents/design-red-team.md` | 3 of 3 | proposed design + archaeology + skeptic reports | ≥3 alternatives, dropped-capability evidence, 4 cost axes, open disagreements |

Hand-off order is **archaeology → skepticism → red-team**. Skipping a
phase is not allowed when the gate is mandatory (see §"When the gate
fires" below). The orchestration mechanism is
`.claude/skills/design-archaeology/SKILL.md` (owned by M9.3); until
that skill file is on disk, the gate runs by direct subagent
invocation against this doc.

## Acceptance lines (verbatim — union of all three agents)

A parent session verifies these three lines, byte-for-byte, against
the three agents' outputs. Failing any one of them means the gate
did not pass.

> Output MUST contain ≥5 questions spread across ≥3 categories, and
> an `explicit_unknowns:` section listing things the agent could not
> answer without human input.

> Output MUST cover all 10 sections; ≥5 distinct legacy behavior
> dimensions must be named explicitly, including any multi-account /
> owner / env mapping the legacy artefact encodes.

> Output MUST include ≥3 alternatives, ≥1 dropped capability with
> file:line evidence, all four long-term-cost axes, and ≥1
> actionable `open_disagreements` entry.

## When the gate fires

The gate is **mandatory** for any task whose spec carries one of the
two task tags in its `## Milestone` line, first heading, or front-matter:

- `arch:` — the task introduces or substantially revises an
  architectural primitive (worker, runner, sandbox, queue, telemetry
  pipeline, schema dimension, permission policy).
- `legacy-migration:` — the task migrates, rewrites, replaces, or
  takes over a legacy tool / config / notebook.

Routine tasks (bug fixes, doc edits, dependency bumps, small
refactors inside an existing primitive) do **not** trigger the gate.
The tag is added by the human authoring the task spec, not inferred
by an agent.

When the gate fires, the executing session MUST:

1. Invoke `legacy-archaeologist` first if the task touches any legacy
   artefact. (Skip for greenfield `arch:` tasks with no legacy code
   in scope.)
2. Invoke `requirements-skeptic` next, regardless.
3. Invoke `design-red-team` last, regardless.
4. Attach the three reports to the task closeout under
   `docs/evidence/<milestone>/<task>/discovery/`:
   - `legacy-archaeologist.md` (skip allowed only with explicit note)
   - `requirements-skeptic.md`
   - `design-red-team.md`
5. Verify all three acceptance lines (above) byte-for-byte against
   the reports. Failure to verify is a task-spec FAIL — not a vibe.

## Task tag convention

Tag placement options (any of these is acceptable; the parent session
should grep all three):

```markdown
## Milestone
M11.3: arch: new sandbox runner

# legacy-migration: M9.4-T002 legacy-archaeologist agent scaffold
```

or in YAML front-matter:

````

```markdown
# CTF Sandbox Workflow

Use this workflow only for explicitly authorized CTF challenges, local labs, or target scopes provided by the human.

## Safety scope

Allowed:

- Analyze local challenge files.
- Run challenge containers or binaries provided for the CTF.
- Interact with explicitly provided CTF endpoints.
- Write solver scripts and educational writeups.

Not allowed:

- Scan public IP ranges or unrelated domains.
- Attack third-party systems.
- Steal or exfiltrate real credentials.
- Deploy malware, persistence, or destructive payloads.
- Use CTF techniques outside the authorized scope.

## Workflow

1. Restate the authorized scope and target.
2. Inventory files, services, ports, and constraints.
3. Identify category: crypto, pwn, web, reversing, forensics, misc, OSINT, etc.
4. Form hypotheses and run minimal safe checks.
5. Keep commands and outputs logged.
6. Build a solver or exploit only within the challenge scope.
7. Produce a concise writeup with root cause, steps, flag, and mitigation idea if relevant.

If scope is unclear, ask the human to define the CTF target before running security tooling.

```

````markdown
# M10 — Loop Prompts

_Live end-to-end Kaggle regression test on
[Petals to the Metal — Flower Classification on TPU](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/tpu-getting-started)._
_For sequential, partly autonomous execution on Arch Linux._
_Prerequisite: M9 exit confirmed (live LB recorded, dry-run e2e green; see `docs/m9-final-review.md`)._
_Shared rules: every Loop Prompt below MUST follow `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` (sequencing, no real Kaggle/Anthropic outside designated approval paths, DB DSN + sandbox bypass, **per-milestone worktree by default**, secret denylist)._

---

## M10 at a glance

M10 is the **second end-to-end live Kaggle regression** for this platform, and
the first to exercise the **notebook-submission / kernel-push** path.
M9 validated the CSV-submission path (`kca kaggle submit` →
`kaggle competitions submit`) on Spaceship Titanic. M10 validates the
notebook-submission path (`kca kaggle push` → `kaggle kernels push` →
kernel run → public LB) on Petals to the Metal — Flower Classification on TPU
(`tpu-getting-started`).

Petals to the Metal is "Getting Started" tier: multi-class image
classification over 104 flower species, public leaderboard, no cash prize,
safe for repeated dry-run iteration and a single real kernel push under
explicit human approval. TPU is optional — Kaggle accepts GPU-backed
notebooks for this competition too — so the baseline can run locally
and only the kernel runner needs Kaggle's hardware.

M10 is **not** a leaderboard-chasing milestone. The acceptance criterion is
that the kernel-push loop *runs end-to-end correctly under the approval
gates*, not that the LB score is high. The CV / holdout thresholds in
`docs/milestones.md` §M10 are sanity guards, not targets.

Direct entry into M10 is blocked until **all** are true:

- M9 is merged on main (`docs/m9-final-review.md` exists and reports PASS).
- Issue #11 (dotenv-leak / Kaggle leaderboard pollution) is merged on main —
  hard pre-req for **M10-T007** so the new dry-run e2e test cannot leak
  into the `tpu-getting-started` leaderboard the same way M9 leaked into
  Spaceship Titanic. M10-T000 through M10-T006 may proceed in parallel
  with #11 work; only T007 is gated on it.
- The local Supabase container is running and the M9 DB rows (M9-T002 /
  M9-T004 / M9-T005) are reachable (M10-T006 references the M9 baseline
  for cross-milestone regression sanity).

### What's in scope

| Capability | Owned by | M10 touches |
|---|---|---|
| Kaggle credentials handling | `env.example`, `.env`, `KAGGLE_USERNAME`/`KAGGLE_KEY` | T000 — verifies env without printing secrets; gates push on presence |
| Competition register + workspace | `tools/kca/competition.py` (`register`, `clone`, `list`, `info`) | T000 / T001 |
| Data discovery for non-CSV competitions | `tools/kca/kg.py` (existing `cmd_download` / `cmd_verify` if extended) + a new manifest shape | T001 — notebook competitions read TFRecord-style data from Kaggle-hosted GCS at kernel runtime; the local manifest records `kaggle competitions files` output, not file checksums |
| Notebook authoring + percent-format round-trip | `kg-nb` skill (`tools/kca/notebook.py` or equivalent) | T002 / T007 |
| Worker loop (research → baseline → local CV → notebook artifact) | `src/worker/` + `tools/kca/run.py` + skills | T002 |
| Reviewer gate before kernel push | `src/worker/reviewer.py` + `services/decision_api/` + UI Approval Inbox (under `target_op="kernel_push"`) | T003 |
| Real Kaggle kernel push (under approval) | `tools/kca/kg.py::cmd_push` + `kaggle kernels push` + kernel-run polling | T004 — single real call |
| Second experiment (alt backbone / augmentation) | same worker, second run | T005 |
| Regression assertions | `tests/test_m10_e2e.py` + `runs` table + `submissions` table | T006 / T007 |
| GitHub issue / label workflow | `.github/labels.yml`, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`, `.github/pull_request_template.md`, `policy:approval-required` | every task — work order issue per task; issue #12 is the canonical M10 proposal |
| Final review | `milestone-final-review` skill + `worktree-milestone-pr` skill | T008 |

### What's NOT in scope

- Running Kaggle submit / kernel push / dataset upload / model upload outside
  T004's single approved kernel-push call.
- Changing production Supabase.
- Implementing M9 follow-ups A, C, D, E (tracked as issues #14, #15, #16, #17).
  They run in parallel; if M10 surfaces blockers, file follow-up issues —
  don't expand scope. Issue #11 is the only hard pre-req (see entry gates).

  `research`, `review`, `decisions`, `skill`) without inventing new ones.

- TPU runtime tuning. The baseline notebook may declare a TPU strategy

## GitHub issue / label workflow for M10

Each M10 task is filed as a GitHub issue using the `feature-work.yml` form,
labelled per task type. Issue #12 is the canonical M10 proposal /
decision-confirmation record; individual task issues link back to it.

| Task | Issue labels at file time | Labels added by triage | Labels at merge |
|---|---|---|---|
| M10-T000 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:kaggle`, `area:config`, `area:security` | `ai:ready` (after AC + owner) | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M10-T001 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:kaggle` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M10-T002 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:worker`, `area:kaggle` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M10-T003 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:worker`, `area:supabase`, `area:ui` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M10-T004 | `type:feature`, `ai:blocked`, `policy:approval-required`, `decision:needed`, `area:kaggle`, `priority:P0` | `decision:confirmed` + `ai:ready` only after human comment "approved to push" | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M10-T005 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:worker`, `area:kaggle` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M10-T006 | `type:test-gap`, `ai:triage`, `area:testing` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M10-T007 | `type:test-gap`, `ai:triage`, `area:testing`, `area:ci` | `ai:ready` only after issue #11 is closed | `ai:implementing` → close |

T004 is the only task that starts `ai:blocked` and requires a
`decision:confirmed` comment with an explicit "approved to push" record
before triage may promote it to `ai:ready`. This is enforced by the
`github-issue-triage` agent rules in `.claude/skills/github-issue-triage/`.

T007 is the only task gated on closing a separate issue (#11). The
triage agent should refuse to promote T007 to `ai:ready` while
`gh issue view 11 --json state` returns `"OPEN"`.

The PR for each task uses `.github/pull_request_template.md`. The
"Remote side effects" section is load-bearing: T004's PR is the ONLY
M10 PR that may check the "Live Kaggle call" box, and must link the
approval comment from the closing issue.

## Approval gates (summary)

| Gate | When it fires | Where the approval is recorded | Who can approve |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kernel_push` | Worker stages a notebook + kernel-metadata.json and calls into `tools/kca/kg.py::cmd_push` | `human_decisions` row + comment on the closing GitHub issue | Project owner / reviewer named on the issue |
| `kaggle_submit` | Not used in M10 (would be a second-submission path; out of scope) | n/a | n/a |
| `dataset_upload` | Not used in M10 | n/a | n/a |
| `model_upload` | Not used in M10 | n/a | n/a |

The Kaggle approval flow inside M10 is:

```
worker stages notebook + kernel-metadata.json
  → reviewer-gate writes agent_reviews row + agent_job_events
    (target_op="kernel_push")
  → decision_api surfaces pending decision (POST /decisions queued; UI
    reads via supabase-js until issue #15 lands GET /decisions)
  → UI Approval Inbox renders pending decision
  → human approves via UI (POST /decisions/<id>/approve) OR
    `kca decisions approve --id <id>`
  → human comments "approved to push" on the closing issue
  → triage agent promotes issue to `decision:confirmed` + `ai:ready`
  → M10-T004 Loop Prompt runs ONE `kca kaggle push`
  → poll kaggle kernels status until non-running
  → LB score recorded; submissions row written with kernel-run linkage
  → PR opens with the approval comment linked
```

A second real Kaggle push inside M10 is **out of scope**. If a
follow-up experiment in M10-T005 turns out to need its own LB score,
file it as a new M11+ issue and gate it the same way.

## Rollback / stop criteria

Stop the milestone — do **not** advance to the next Loop Prompt — if any of
these is true:

- A real Kaggle kernel push returns an error from Kaggle (rate limit,
  bad notebook metadata, rules violation). The fix path is local:
  regenerate the notebook + kernel metadata and re-request approval;
  do NOT silently retry.
- The reviewer gate (M10-T003) fails to fire when it should, or fires
  when it shouldn't.
- Any `policy:approval-required` issue advances without the corresponding
  `decision:confirmed` label and comment.
- Any test in the validation suite regresses from green to red.
- The DSN, credentials, or `.env*` are accidentally printed in any log,
  audit row, or PR. Stop and rotate the credential immediately.
- Local CV / holdout scores diverge from the M10-T006 thresholds in a
  way that suggests a leakage bug (e.g. holdout near 1.0). Investigate
  before pushing.
- Issue #11 is reopened mid-milestone with evidence that the leak
  re-emerged. Halt T007 work until #11 is green again.

If M10 needs a new architectural decision (e.g. submission-format
auto-selection, a new artifact-storage shape for notebook payloads, a
TPU-specific resource model), **pause and ask** — those are M11+ /
issue #7 / issue #8 decisions, not M10 expansion. Open an ADR draft in
`docs/adr/` and stop the milestone there.
````

````markdown
M10: live end-to-end regression test — Petals to the Metal (notebook-submission / kernel-push path).

## Goal
Confirm the agent can read Kaggle credentials without exposing them, run
READ_ONLY Kaggle calls against the kernel-runner path, and register
`tpu-getting-started` (Petals to the Metal) in the local control plane.
No real push, no submission, no dataset / model upload.

This task assumes **M9 is merged on main** (`docs/m9-final-review.md`
reports PASS) and that the M9-T000 deviation (AC #1 satisfied via

is honoured here too.
````

````markdown
# Milestone Loop Protocol

_Shared rules that apply to every milestone Loop Prompt (M0+) unless a
milestone explicitly overrides one._

Each `docs/m*-loop-prompts.md` should reference this file once at the top
rather than duplicating the rules per prompt.

---

## 1. Sequencing

- Loop Prompts within a milestone MUST execute in order.
- Each prompt's **acceptance checks MUST pass** before moving to the next.
- On failure: fix the specific issue and **retry that prompt only**; do
  not skip ahead and do not redo prompts that already passed.

## 2. External systems and side effects

- Do NOT call the **real Anthropic API or Kaggle API** outside of paths
  the milestone explicitly designates as live; default to `--dry-run`.
- Do NOT run real **Kaggle submit / kernel push / dataset upload /
  model upload** unless the milestone explicitly requests it AND a
  human-approval record exists.
- Do NOT change **production Supabase**.

## 3. Database validation

- Use `SUPABASE_DB_URL=postgresql://postgres:s3cr3t@172.21.0.4:5432/postgres`
  — the `supabase-db` container on the local Docker network.
- Container IPs change on `docker compose down/up`; refresh with:
  ```bash
  docker inspect supabase-db \
    --format '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}'
  ```
- DB calls and LAN-host calls require `dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true`.
  Cloud LLM calls stay **inside** the sandbox.

## 4. Reporting

- Report **PASS / FAIL / SKIP** inline for each prompt's verification
  step.
- At milestone end, write the milestone's defined **Closeout format**
  (see each milestone's last Loop Prompt for the exact fields).

## 5. Git / GitHub — worktree mode

This project executes each milestone inside a dedicated **git worktree**
branched off `main`.

- **Mid-milestone, mid-prompt:** do not `git commit` or `git push`
  unless the individual task spec explicitly says so. Stage with
  `git add` and surface diffs in the inline report.
- **At milestone end** — once every Loop Prompt has PASSed and the
  milestone's Closeout has been written — Claude Code SHOULD:
  1. `git add` only the files listed in the Closeout's "files changed"
     section (or its equivalent).
  2. `git commit` using either:
     - one squash commit per milestone, OR
     - one commit per Loop Prompt,
     depending on the milestone's preference. The default is **one
     commit per Loop Prompt**, with the milestone's final review as the
     last commit.
  3. `git push` the worktree's branch to the remote.
  4. `gh pr create` against `main` using the milestone's
     `docs/m{N}-final-review.md` as the PR body.

- The following **still require explicit human approval** at any time:
  - `git push --force` (any branch)
  - `gh pr merge` (any PR)
  - any push to `main` directly
  - any `gh label create/edit/delete`, `gh issue edit/comment`,
    `gh pr edit/comment` against issues or PRs **not** owned by this
    milestone

- If the milestone's task spec or scope says
  "do not commit / push / open PRs", that override **wins** — typically
  used for planning-only or evidence-only milestones.

## 6. Secrets and forbidden reads

These are always denied, regardless of milestone:

- `.env*`
- `**/kaggle.json`, `~/.kaggle/kaggle.json`
- `~/.ssh/id_rsa`, `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`, any private key contents
- `~/.aws/**`, `~/.config/gcloud/**`
- `secrets/**`

Shell commands that would surface the above (`cat`, `grep`, `head`,
`tail`, `less`, `more`, file uploads) over these paths are blocked at
the hook layer.

---

## How a milestone references this file

In each Loop Prompt block, instead of repeating the rules above, include
one line near the top:

```
Follow: docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md
```

A milestone's `docs/m{N}-loop-prompts.md` should still spell out:

- the milestone's own scope, non-goals, and task list;
- per-Loop-Prompt read lists, scope, acceptance criteria;
- any **override** of a default in this file (e.g. a planning-only
  milestone overriding the worktree commit/push behavior).

---

## 7. Discovery / Debate Gate

_Added by M9.4. Additive only — §1–§6 above are unchanged._

Some tasks are large enough that "implement first, debate later"
loses load-bearing requirements (the canonical failure: `tools/legacy/kkr.py`
migration missing multi-Kaggle-account / owner / env semantics; see
`docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-24-r3.md` §6). The Discovery / Debate Gate
runs three role-isolated subagents — `legacy-archaeologist`,
`requirements-skeptic`, `design-red-team` — **before** any
implementation work begins.

The gate is **mandatory** for any task whose spec is tagged `arch:`
(introduces / revises an architectural primitive) or
`legacy-migration:` (migrates / rewrites / replaces a legacy artefact).
Routine tasks (bug fixes, doc edits, dependency bumps, small
refactors) do not trigger the gate.

When the gate fires, the executing session MUST:

1. Invoke `legacy-archaeologist` first if the task touches any
   legacy artefact (skip allowed only for greenfield `arch:` tasks,
   with explicit note in the closeout).
2. Invoke `requirements-skeptic` next.
3. Invoke `design-red-team` last.
4. Attach all three reports to the task closeout under
   `docs/evidence/<milestone>/<task>/discovery/`.
5. Verify all three canonical acceptance lines (defined in
   `docs/architecture/discovery-debate-gate.md`) byte-for-byte
   against the reports. A missing acceptance line is a task FAIL.

Full template, tag-placement options, and the verbatim acceptance
lines live in `docs/architecture/discovery-debate-gate.md`. The
orchestration skill `.claude/skills/design-archaeology/SKILL.md`
(owned by M9.3) is the inline alternative when the task is small
enough not to warrant separate subagents; the agent path and the
skill path emit compatible output shapes by design.

M9.4 enforces the gate via task-spec acceptance criteria and this
section's wording, **not** via hook-level denials. Hook-based
enforcement is a deferred follow-up; file a separate issue if you
want it built.

````

**Q:** *How should M11 handle CTF event credentials and registration?*

- Human registers; KCA reads credentials (Recommended): You register on each event site manually; KCA reads credentials from a per-event config (e.g. `~/.ctf/<event-slug>.json` or `CTF_<EVENT>_TOKEN` in `.env`), mirroring the Kaggle pattern. - Hybrid — human registers; KCA logs in: Human handles sign-up; KCA performs login (cookie / session refresh) through Playwright when credentials expire. Adds a `ctf_login` flow but keeps account creation out of scope.

**Q:** *What is M11's regression target — the equivalent of Spaceship Titanic (M9) / Petals to the Metal (M10)?*

- Frozen past event + 1 live event challenge (Recommended): Bundle 1–2 past-event challenges locally (picoCTF-style, permissively licensed) for the deterministic test path (mirrors `tests/test_m10_e2e.py`). Pick ONE current bbbctf.com or upcoming CTFtime-listed event for the single live end-to-end solve under approval (mirrors M9-T004 / M10-T004). Reproducible CI + one real-world demonstration.

- Live event only (bbbctf.com or next CTFtime pick): Skip the bundled past-event piece; M11's regression is purely against a current event. Higher fidelity but CI tests can't replay the solve later, and milestone timing is coupled to event windows. Closer to how you actually compete.

- Frozen past event only — no live solve: M11 is scaffolding + frozen-snapshot solve only; no live event in this milestone. Defer the live solve to M11.1 (mirrors how M9.2 / M9.3 / M9.4 sat alongside M10). Lower coupling to event calendars; lower fidelity.

**A:** Frozen past event + 1 live event challenge (Recommended)



**Q:** *Which CTF challenge categories should M11 support at the agent-loop level?*

- Web (Recommended): HTTP-based challenges — SQLi, XSS, auth bypass, SSRF, JWT, etc. Tooling: `requests` / `httpx`, Playwright for JS-heavy targets. Reuses existing research_fetch + Playwright code paths.

- Crypto (Recommended): Number theory, weak-RNG, padding-oracle, classical ciphers, etc. Tooling: `pycryptodome`, `sympy`, `gmpy2`. Local-only by design (no remote network). Strongest fit for local containerized regression.

- Reverse engineering: Static / dynamic analysis of binaries. Tooling: `pwntools`, `angr`, optionally `ghidra` / `radare2`. Heavyweight; agent-loop fit is weaker (LLMs handle small binaries OK, big ones don't). Most likely candidate to defer.

- Forensics / OSINT / misc: File-format puzzles, packet captures, metadata digging, public-source searches. Tooling: `binwalk`, `volatility`, `exiftool`, public web search. Mixed difficulty; good fit for the existing research-brief + ctf-sandbox skills.

**A:** Web (Recommended), Crypto (Recommended), Reverse engineering, Forensics / OSINT / misc, Binary Exploitation (Pwn),

- challenge_run + flag_submit + network_egress (Recommended): Three new operations in `.kca/permissions/*.yaml` + `src/worker/reviewer.py`: `challenge_run` (ask before invoking a solver against an authorized target), `flag_submit` (ask before POSTing a flag to an event), `network_egress` (deny outside an authorized `ctf_scopes.target_urls` row; ask only when scope+URL match). Records full audit shape comparable to kaggle_submit / kernel_push.

- challenge_run + flag_submit only: Two gates; let the sandbox network allowlist handle egress without a distinct `network_egress` operation. Simpler; weaker out-of-scope audit story.

- flag_submit only — reuse `bash` for everything else: Only the flag submission is gated as a distinct operation. Solver invocation runs under `bash` (ask). Fastest path; matches M9-style minimalism but loses CTF-specific intent in audit rows.

**A:** challenge_run + flag_submit + network_egress (Recommended)

```markdown
# M11 — Authorized CTF / lab workflow — Implementation Plan

## Context

`docs/milestones.md` § M11 (lines 834–852) defines M11 as the *authorized CTF /
lab workflow* milestone. It was renumbered from old M10 on 2026-05-24 to make
room for the notebook-submission regression (current M10). M11 is the first
**non-Kaggle** competition platform the project supports — its job is to prove
the platform can represent a different competition policy (CTF jeopardy) without
changing worker core logic (the abstract success target for M12 / hackathon
generalization).

M9 / M10 established the canonical pattern for "live-regression" milestones:
nine numbered tasks ending in a `docs/m{N}-final-review.md`, a single real
external side-effect under explicit human approval, a dry-run e2e test that runs
in CI without credentials, and a milestone-wide worktree per
`docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` §5. M11 mirrors that pattern, with two
deltas:

1. M11 fronts the work with a **Discovery / Debate Gate** task (M9.4 §7) because
   the data model (`ctf_events` / `ctf_challenges`), the three new approval
   operations (`challenge_run`, `flag_submit`, `network_egress`), and the
   `ctf_scopes` enforcement boundary are all `arch:` deliverables.
2. M11's single real external side-effect is a **flag submission to a live
   CTFtime-listed event** under human approval (not a Kaggle submission /
   kernel push).

The schema already has `ctf_scopes` from migration `0001_init.sql` (lines
`authorized_scope text`, `target_urls jsonb`, `local_only boolean`,
`expires_at timestamptz`) — unused so far. M11 lights it up and adds the
event / challenge / attempt tables alongside.

### Decisions locked (from the planning Q&A)

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| Credential / registration model | Human registers on each event site; KCA reads credentials from a per-event config (`~/.ctf/<event>.json` or `CTF_<EVENT>_*` env). No browser sign-up automation in M11. |
| Regression target | Frozen past-event bundle under `data/ctf/<event>/<challenge>/` (1 web + 1 crypto challenge from a permissively licensed source, e.g. picoCTF) for deterministic CI, **plus** ONE live flag submission against a current CTFtime-listed event (e.g. `bbbctf.com`) under approval. |
| Challenge categories | Web + crypto + reverse engineering + forensics/OSINT + pwn are all in the **taxonomy**; only web + crypto are exercised by the M11 agent-loop solve. Pwn / rev / forensics support is documented as scope vs. follow-up. |
| New approval gates | Three: `challenge_run` (ask), `flag_submit` (ask), `network_egress` (deny outside an authorized `ctf_scopes.target_urls` row; ask when scope+URL match). |

---

## Recommended approach

M11 is implemented as **10 numbered Loop Prompts** (T000–T009), one milestone
worktree, one PR against `main`. Each Loop Prompt follows
`docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` (sequencing, secret denylist, DB DSN, per-
milestone worktree). The M9.4 Discovery / Debate Gate fires for T000 only —
its evidence is referenced by every downstream task.

### M11 task sequence

| Task | Tag | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **M11-T000** | `arch:` | Discovery / Debate Gate for M11 architecture (event/challenge/scope data model, three new approval ops, CTFtime workflow taxonomy). All three subagent reports under `docs/evidence/m11/discovery/`. Acceptance lines verified byte-for-byte. **Blocks T001 onward.** |
| **M11-T001** | `arch:` | Migration `0008_m11_ctf.sql` — `ctf_events`, `ctf_challenges`, `ctf_attempts` tables; verify `ctf_scopes` (from 0001) is reachable. New DB helpers in `src/db/ctf.py`. Smoke tests against the local container. |
| **M11-T002** | `arch:` | Permission policy + reviewer-gate wiring for `challenge_run` / `flag_submit` / `network_egress`. Update `.kca/permissions/{default,permissive-dev,competition-runner}.yaml`, `src/worker/reviewer.py::should_consult_reviewer`, `src/worker/worker.py` op-extraction, `.claude/settings.json` ask-list. |
| **M11-T003** | — | `kca ctf` CLI surface: `event {register,list,info}`, `challenge {add,fetch,list,info}`, `scope {set,list,verify}`, `solver run` (dry-run path), `flag submit` (gated). All commands operate against the local DB; remote calls require `KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1` + `dangerouslyDisableSandbox`. |
| **M11-T004** | — | Frozen past-event challenge bundle under `data/ctf/<event-slug>/{web-<n>,crypto-<n>}/`. One web (HTTP/auth-bypass style) + one crypto (small RSA / classical-cipher style). Each ships a `challenge.yaml`, attachments, optional `docker-compose.yml`, and a `solver_template.py`. Manifest + scope row inserted. Source: permissively licensed (picoCTF archive or similar). Raw binaries / pcaps gitignored beyond a 1 MB cap. |
| **M11-T005** | — | Agent worker loop drives the `ctf-sandbox` skill end-to-end against the bundled challenges. Sequence: research (challenge description + attachments) → category triage → write solver → run solver (in scope) → recover flag → record `ctf_attempts` row + `experiment_runs` row. Local-only; no remote network. |
| **M11-T006** | — | Reviewer gates fire for `challenge_run` (before solver execution) and `flag_submit` (before any submission). Approval lands in UI Approval Inbox via `decision_api`; human approves via `kca decisions approve`. Mirrors M9-T003 / M10-T003. |
| **M11-T007** | — | **ONE** real `kca ctf flag submit` to a live CTFtime-listed event under explicit human approval. Records `ctf_attempts` row with `accepted=true/false` and the event's response (no flag string echoed). Pre-conditions: `decision:confirmed` on the closing issue, valid `~/.ctf/<event>.json`, valid `ctf_scopes` row with `target_urls` covering the submit endpoint, scope not expired. |
| **M11-T008** | — | `tests/test_m11_e2e.py` — dry-run + refusal-path coverage. Asserts: (a) `flag_submit` refused without approval; (b) `challenge_run` refused for a target URL outside `ctf_scopes.target_urls`; (c) `network_egress` denied to `kaggle.com` from a CTF job; (d) bundled web+crypto solver round-trip works locally; (e) `~/.ctf/*.json` / `.env` read-attempts surface in audit but never leak contents. **No real network, no credentials.** |
| **M11-T009** | — | M11 exit criteria + `docs/m11-final-review.md` (mirrors M9 / M10 layout). Update `PROJECT_STATE.md`, `README.md`, `docs/milestones.md` § M11 to `✓ done`. Write `docs/handoffs/m11-handoff.md`. Run `worktree-milestone-pr` to commit-per-Loop-Prompt, push, open PR. |

T007 is the only Loop Prompt that makes a real external network call. T000–T006
and T008 are local-only (DB + bundled fixtures). T009 only writes docs and runs
git/gh.

### Discovery / Debate Gate scope (M11-T000)

Per `docs/architecture/discovery-debate-gate.md` and
`docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` §7, T000 invokes three role-isolated
subagents **before any code work**:

1. `legacy-archaeologist` — read existing `ctf_scopes` (migration 0001),
   `.claude/skills/ctf-sandbox/SKILL.md`, `src/worker/reviewer.py` (CTF mention),
   `docs/adr/0005-job-taxonomy.md` (ctf platform enum), `docs/adr/0006-
   configurable-approval-gates.md`. Produce the 10-section report; name
   ≥5 behavior dimensions inherited from prior CTF design intent.
2. `requirements-skeptic` — produce ≥5 questions across ≥3 categories
   (scope authorization, credential handoff, multi-event identity,
   flag-submission semantics, audit retention) plus an
   `explicit_unknowns:` section.
3. `design-red-team` — produce ≥3 alternatives for the data model and the
   three new approval ops; name ≥1 dropped capability with `file:line`
   evidence (e.g. dropping per-challenge `attempts_per_hour` rate limit);
   cover all 4 cost axes; record ≥1 `open_disagreement`.

All three reports land at `docs/evidence/m11/discovery/{legacy-archaeologist,
requirements-skeptic,design-red-team}.md`. The verbatim acceptance lines from
`docs/architecture/discovery-debate-gate.md` are checked byte-for-byte; a
missing line is a T000 FAIL and blocks the rest of M11.

## Verification plan

End-to-end verification at milestone close (T009 runs these as the
validation matrix for `docs/m11-final-review.md`):

1. **Discovery / Debate Gate.** All three subagent reports exist under
   `docs/evidence/m11/discovery/`; the three verbatim acceptance lines
   from `docs/architecture/discovery-debate-gate.md` are present byte-
   for-byte. Failure → T000 FAIL.

   `select count(*) from ctf_events, ctf_challenges, ctf_attempts;`
   returns the rows seeded by T004 + T005.
3. **Permission gates.**
   `python -c "from src.worker.reviewer import should_consult_reviewer;
   print(all(should_consult_reviewer(op) for op in ['challenge_run',
   'flag_submit', 'network_egress']))"` → `True`.
4. **CLI surface.** `kca ctf event list --json`, `kca ctf challenge list
   --event <slug>`, `kca ctf scope list --json`, `kca ctf flag submit
   --dry-run` all exit 0; help text mentions reviewer-gated operations.
5. **Local solve.** `kca run list --project ctf --json` shows the two
   bundled challenges with `solved=true` and recorded flag length
   (not value). `experiment_runs` has the matching rows.
6. **Reviewer gate.** `select count(*) from agent_reviews where
   target_op in ('challenge_run','flag_submit');` ≥ 2.
   `human_decisions` has the matching approval rows.
7. **Live submission.** `select * from ctf_attempts where accepted is
   not null and event_slug = '<live-event>';` returns exactly one row

8. **Refusal paths.** `python -m pytest tests/test_m11_e2e.py -v` → all
   pass. Audit-grep the test run: 0 lines reaching a real network
   endpoint outside scope; 0 lines echoing `.env` or `~/.ctf/*` content.
9. **Full test suite.** `python -m pytest tests/ services/decision_api/
   tests -v` → 0 failures. `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .`
   clean. `pnpm -C ui …` (or SKIP if pnpm not on PATH, same posture as
   M9 / M10 — CI is authoritative).
10. **Docs round-trip.** `docs/m11-final-review.md` exists, mirrors the
    M9 / M10 layout, references each task's closeout, and the validation
    matrix above is filled in (PASS / FAIL per row). `PROJECT_STATE.md`
    + `README.md` + `docs/milestones.md` § M11 all updated to `✓ done`.
    `docs/handoffs/m11-handoff.md` exists.

Stop-and-ask triggers (mirror M10 §Rollback):
- Any real network call outside T007 reaches a non-allowlisted host.
- Any `target_urls` row is bypassed by the worker.
- `~/.ctf/*.json` or `.env*` content appears in logs / audit rows / PR
  bodies.
- T007 returns an error from the event site; do **not** silently retry —
  open a follow-up issue.
- Discovery / Debate Gate at T000 finds an undecided question that
  invalidates the data model (e.g. multi-event identity collision) —
  pause, draft a new ADR, restart T000.

### Out-of-scope follow-ups (file as issues, not M11 work)

- Pwn / reverse-engineering / forensics solver loops (taxonomy supported
  in the data model; solver loop deferred to a future milestone).
- Browser-automation sign-up flow (rejected here; M11 reads
  human-supplied credentials only).
- CTFtime calendar auto-watch + scheduled job submission (the manual
  `kca ctf event register` flow is sufficient for M11).
- Hook-level enforcement of `network_egress` outside scope (currently
  enforced by the reviewer-gate + worker code path; hook-level deny is
  a deferred follow-up, same posture as the M9.4 discovery-gate hook).
```

````markdown
the kaggle-code-agent stack._
_For sequential, partly autonomous execution on Arch Linux._
_Prerequisite: M9 exit confirmed (live LB recorded on Spaceship Titanic; see
`docs/m9-final-review.md`). M10 may run in parallel; the only hard dependency
M11 inherits from M10 is the dotenv-leak fix (issue #11), which must be
merged on `main` before **M11-T008** writes its e2e refusal tests._
_Shared rules: every Loop Prompt below MUST follow `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md`
(sequencing, no real Kaggle/Anthropic outside designated approval paths, DB DSN +
sandbox bypass, **per-milestone worktree by default**, secret denylist, **§7
Discovery / Debate Gate for `arch:` tagged tasks**)._
````
