## M11 at a glance

M11 is the **first CTF / authorized-lab regression** for this platform, and
the first milestone to validate that the worker / reviewer / approval-inbox
stack works for a **non-Kaggle competition policy**. M9 + M10 covered Kaggle
CSV submission and Kaggle kernel push respectively. M11 covers CTF jeopardy:
challenge inventory, scoped solver execution, and flag submission to the
event endpoint.

The CTF user pattern (from the planning Q&A) is:

1. Check [CTFtime calendar](https://ctftime.org/calendar/) for upcoming events.
2. Register on the event site **as a human** (no browser-automated sign-up in
   M11); record event credentials under `~/.ctf/<event-slug>.json` or
   `CTF_<EVENT>_*` env vars.
3. For each challenge: read description, download attachments, decide whether
   the challenge is local-only (zip / docker bundle) or remote (must hit the
   event's challenge endpoint).
4. Solve locally where possible; submit the flag to the event's API.

M11 brings (1) into a `kca ctf event register` LOCAL_WRITE flow, defers (2)
to the human, exercises (3) end-to-end against a **frozen past-event bundle**
under `data/ctf/<event>/<challenge>/` for deterministic CI, and exercises (4)
once for real against a **single live CTFtime-listed event** under explicit
human approval.

M11 is **not** a leaderboard-chasing milestone. The acceptance criterion is
that the CTF workflow runs end-to-end correctly under the approval gates and
hard-refuses out-of-scope targets. Solver quality / category coverage is
captured as future work — see `docs/architecture/m11-ctf-workflow.md` §
"Out of scope".

Direct entry into M11 is blocked until **all** are true:

- M9 is merged on `main` (`docs/m9-final-review.md` exists and reports PASS).
- The Discovery / Debate Gate (M11-T000) has produced all three subagent
  reports with byte-for-byte acceptance lines under
  `docs/evidence/m11/discovery/`.
- Issue #11 (dotenv-leak / secret-file hygiene in pytest subprocess) is
  merged on `main`. This is a soft pre-req for **M11-T008** (the e2e
  refusal-path test): M11-T000 through M11-T007 may proceed in parallel
  with #11 work.
- The local Supabase container is running; migration `0001_init.sql`'s
  `ctf_scopes` table is reachable.

### What's in scope

| Capability | Owned by | M11 touches |
|---|---|---|
| Discovery / Debate Gate for CTF data model + new approval ops | `.claude/agents/{legacy-archaeologist,requirements-skeptic,design-red-team}.md`, `docs/architecture/discovery-debate-gate.md` | T000 — all three reports + byte-checkable acceptance |
| Event / challenge / attempt schema | `supabase/migrations/0008_m11_ctf.sql` + `src/db/ctf.py` | T001 |
| New approval operations (`challenge_run`, `flag_submit`, `network_egress`) | `.kca/permissions/{default,permissive-dev,competition-runner}.yaml`, `src/worker/reviewer.py`, `src/worker/worker.py`, `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/hooks/guard_tool.py` | T002 |
| `kca ctf` CLI surface | `tools/kca/ctf.py` + `tools/kca/kca.py::add_parsers` | T003 |
| Frozen past-event challenge bundle (1 web + 1 crypto) | `data/ctf/<event-slug>/{web-1,crypto-1}/` | T004 |
| Agent worker drives ctf-sandbox skill to solve locally | `src/worker/`, `.claude/skills/ctf-sandbox/SKILL.md`, `tools/kca/run.py` | T005 |
| Reviewer-gate before solver run + flag submit | `src/worker/reviewer.py`, `services/decision_api/app.py`, UI Approval Inbox | T006 |
| ONE real flag submission to a live CTFtime event | `tools/kca/ctf.py::cmd_flag_submit`, `ctf_attempts` table | T007 — single real call |
| E2E refusal-path tests | `tests/test_m11_e2e.py`, `tests/test_m11_smoke.py` | T008 |
| ADRs + architecture doc | `docs/adr/0016-ctf-data-model.md`, `docs/adr/0017-ctf-approval-gates.md`, `docs/architecture/m11-ctf-workflow.md` | T001 / T002 / T009 |
| Final review + handoff | `milestone-final-review` skill, `worktree-milestone-pr` skill | T009 |
| GitHub issue / label workflow | `.github/labels.yml`, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature-work.yml`, PR template | every task |

### What's NOT in scope

- Running flag submissions outside T007's single approved call.
- Browser-automated event sign-up. M11 reads human-supplied credentials only.
- Pwn / reverse-engineering / forensics agent-loop solves. The taxonomy
  supports them (`ctf_challenges.category`) but the M11 solve loop exercises
  only `web` + `crypto`. Filed as follow-up issues at milestone close.
- CTFtime calendar polling / auto-event-watch / scheduled-job auto-submit.
- Changing production Supabase.
- Implementing M10 follow-ups (parallel milestone; cross-cutting items file
  as their own issues).
- Implementing M9 follow-ups A, C, D, E (still tracked as issues #14, #15, #16,
  #17). Issue #11 is the only soft pre-req (see entry gates).

DB / sandbox details: see `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` §3 — the local
`supabase-db` container (`postgresql://postgres:s3cr3t@172.21.0.4:5432/postgres`)
needs `dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true`. The real CTF event API call inside
M11-T007 also needs sandbox bypass and an approved `ctf_scopes.target_urls`
entry covering the submit endpoint.

| M11-T007 | `type:feature`, `ai:blocked`, `policy:approval-required`, `decision:needed`, `area:ctf`, `priority:P0` | `decision:confirmed` + `ai:ready` only after human comment "approved to submit" | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M11-T008 | `type:test-gap`, `ai:triage`, `area:testing`, `area:ci` | `ai:ready` only after issue #11 is closed | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M11-T009 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:release`, `area:docs` | `ai:ready` after T000–T008 closed | `ai:implementing` → close |

T007 is the only task that starts `ai:blocked` and requires a
`decision:confirmed` comment with an explicit "approved to submit" record
before triage may promote it to `ai:ready`. This is enforced by the
`github-issue-triage` agent rules in `.claude/skills/github-issue-triage/`.

T008 is the only task gated on closing a separate issue (#11). The
triage agent should refuse to promote T008 to `ai:ready` while
`gh issue view 11 --json state` returns `"OPEN"`.

The PR for each task uses `.github/pull_request_template.md`. The
"Remote side effects" section is load-bearing: T007's PR is the ONLY
M11 PR that may check the "Live external API call" box, and must link the
approval comment from the closing issue.

---

## Approval gates (summary)

| Gate | When it fires | Where the approval is recorded | Who can approve |
|---|---|---|---|
| `challenge_run` | Worker is about to invoke a solver against a target whose URL is in `ctf_scopes.target_urls` OR is a local in-scope service | `agent_reviews` row + `human_decisions` row + (T007 only) comment on the closing GitHub issue | Project owner / reviewer named on the issue |
| `flag_submit` | `tools/kca/ctf.py::cmd_flag_submit` is invoked with `--dry-run=False` | `agent_reviews` row + `human_decisions` row + (T007 only) approval comment | Project owner |
| `network_egress` | Worker attempts to call any host NOT in `ctf_scopes.target_urls` AND the host is not on the global allowlist | DENY at the reviewer-gate; recorded as `agent_reviews.verdict=reject` + audit row in `agent_tool_audit` | Not applicable — deny is final; the human must edit the scope row to widen it |
| `kaggle_submit` | Not used in M11 | n/a | n/a |
| `kernel_push` | Not used in M11 | n/a | n/a |

The CTF approval flow inside M11 is:

```
worker stages solver / flag artifact + target URL
  → reviewer-gate writes agent_reviews row + agent_job_events
    (target_op="challenge_run" or "flag_submit")
  → decision_api surfaces pending decision (POST /decisions queued;
    UI reads via supabase-js until issue #15 lands GET /decisions)
  → UI Approval Inbox renders pending decision
  → human approves via UI (POST /decisions/<id>/approve) OR
    `kca decisions approve --id <id>`
  → (T007 only) human comments "approved to submit" on the closing
    issue
  → triage agent promotes issue to `decision:confirmed` + `ai:ready`
  → M11-T007 Loop Prompt runs ONE `kca ctf flag submit`
  → ctf_attempts row written with accepted=true|false + http_status
  → PR opens with the approval comment linked
```

A second real flag submission inside M11 is **out of scope**. If a
follow-up challenge in M11-T005 or M11-T007 surfaces another flag
that the human wants submitted, file it as a new M11-followup issue
and gate it the same way.

## Rollback / stop criteria

Stop the milestone — do **not** advance to the next Loop Prompt — if any of
these is true:

- A real CTF event call returns an error from the event API outside T007's
  single approved call (rate limit, scope violation, bad credentials). The
  fix path is local: regenerate solver / re-verify scope and re-request
  approval; do NOT silently retry.
- The reviewer gate (M11-T006) fails to fire for `challenge_run` or
  `flag_submit` when it should, or fires when it shouldn't.
- Any `policy:approval-required` issue advances without the corresponding
  `decision:confirmed` label and comment.
- Any test in the validation suite regresses from green to red.
- The DSN, Kaggle credentials, `~/.ctf/*`, or `.env*` are accidentally
  printed in any log, audit row, or PR. Stop and rotate the credential
  immediately.
- The Discovery / Debate Gate at T000 surfaces an undecided question that
  invalidates the data model (e.g. multi-event identity collision; team-
  account vs. individual-account ambiguity). Pause, draft a new ADR, and
  restart T000.
- A `network_egress` deny fails to trigger for an attempted call to a host
  outside the scope row (silent egress = critical security regression).
- Issue #11 is reopened mid-milestone with evidence that the leak
  re-emerged. Halt T008 work until #11 is green again.

If M11 needs a new architectural decision (e.g. multi-event credential
rotation; pwn/rev solver harness; CTFtime calendar auto-watch), **pause
and ask** — those are M11-followup / M13 decisions, not M11 expansion.
Open an ADR draft in `docs/adr/` and stop the milestone there.

# M11-T000: Discovery / Debate Gate for the M11 CTF architecture

## Milestone
M11: authorized CTF / lab workflow. **`arch:` tagged** — Discovery / Debate
Gate per `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` §7 is mandatory before any T001+
implementation work begins.

## Goal
Run the three role-isolated subagents (`legacy-archaeologist`,
`requirements-skeptic`, `design-red-team`) against the proposed M11
architecture — the `ctf_events` / `ctf_challenges` / `ctf_attempts` data
model, the three new approval operations (`challenge_run`, `flag_submit`,
`network_egress`), and the CTFtime → event-credentials → challenge →
solver → flag-submit workflow taxonomy.

T000 is **gate-only**: no code, no schema, no permission edits.
A missing byte-checkable acceptance line is a T000 FAIL and blocks all
downstream M11 work.

## Read first

1. `PROJECT_STATE.md`
2. `AGENTS.md`
3. `CLAUDE.md`
4. `docs/milestones.md` §M11
5. `docs/architecture/discovery-debate-gate.md` — verbatim acceptance lines
6. `docs/architecture/design-archaeology.md`
7. `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` §7
8. `docs/handoffs/m9-handoff.md`
9. `docs/adr/0005-job-taxonomy.md` — `project_kind` enum + `ctf` slug
10. `docs/adr/0006-configurable-approval-gates.md` — operation data shape
11. `supabase/migrations/0001_init.sql` — existing `ctf_scopes` table
12. `.claude/skills/ctf-sandbox/SKILL.md` — current workflow body
13. `src/worker/reviewer.py` — existing reviewer-gate pattern
14. `docs/evidence/m9_4-kkr-replay/` — worked precedent (kkr.py)
15. `.claude/agents/{legacy-archaeologist,requirements-skeptic,design-red-team}.md`

## Scope

1. **Invoke `legacy-archaeologist` first.** Pass it the CTF-related
   artefacts already in the repo: `ctf_scopes` table (migration 0001),
   `.claude/skills/ctf-sandbox/SKILL.md`, `src/worker/reviewer.py` CTF
   mentions, `docs/adr/0005-job-taxonomy.md` `ctf` platform enum,
   any prior CTF references in meeting notes. Produce the 10-section
   report and write it to
   `docs/evidence/m11/discovery/legacy-archaeologist.md`.

2. **Invoke `requirements-skeptic` next.** Pass it the planning Q&A
   decisions (credential model, frozen-bundle + 1 live submission,
   five-category taxonomy with web+crypto exercised, three new ops).
   Produce ≥5 questions across ≥3 categories (scope authorization,
   credential handoff, multi-event identity, flag-submission semantics,
   audit retention) plus an `explicit_unknowns:` section. Write to
   `docs/evidence/m11/discovery/requirements-skeptic.md`.

3. **Invoke `design-red-team` last.** Pass it the proposed data model
   shape (`ctf_events` / `ctf_challenges` / `ctf_attempts`), the three
   new ops, and the two prior reports. Produce ≥3 alternatives for the
   data model and for the approval-op design; name ≥1 dropped capability
   with `file:line` evidence (e.g. dropping per-challenge
   `attempts_per_hour` rate-limit); cover all 4 cost axes; record ≥1
   `open_disagreement`. Write to
   `docs/evidence/m11/discovery/design-red-team.md`.

4. **Verify acceptance lines byte-for-byte.** Compare each report's
   canonical acceptance line against the verbatim text in
   `docs/architecture/discovery-debate-gate.md`. Any mismatch is a
   T000 FAIL.

5. **File or update the closing GitHub issue.** Link the three evidence
   files. Add the `arch:` label. Promote to `decision:confirmed` only
   after the human has read all three reports and signed off.

## Non-goals

- Do not modify `supabase/migrations/`, `.kca/permissions/`,
  `src/worker/`, or `tools/kca/` in this Loop Prompt.
- Do not author migration `0008_m11_ctf.sql` — that's T001.
- Do not write ADRs 0016 / 0017 yet — they land with the implementation
  tasks (T001 / T002) that reference the relevant red-team findings.
- Do not skip an agent because "the answer seems obvious". Each agent
  has a load-bearing acceptance line; skipping = FAIL.

## Acceptance criteria

- All three reports exist under
  `docs/evidence/m11/discovery/{legacy-archaeologist,
  requirements-skeptic,design-red-team}.md`.
- `legacy-archaeologist.md` contains all 10 sections and names ≥5
  behavior dimensions inherited from the existing CTF artefacts.
- `requirements-skeptic.md` contains ≥5 questions across ≥3
  categories and an `explicit_unknowns:` section.
- `design-red-team.md` contains ≥3 alternatives, ≥1 dropped
  capability with `file:line` evidence, all 4 cost axes, and ≥1
  `open_disagreement`.
- Each report's canonical acceptance line matches
  `docs/architecture/discovery-debate-gate.md` byte-for-byte.
- The closing issue is `decision:confirmed` (or this Loop Prompt
  halts and asks the human to confirm).
- No files changed outside `docs/evidence/m11/discovery/` and the
  closing GitHub issue.

## Permissions

- Local file reads (excluding the secret denylist) and Agent tool
  invocations for the three subagents are allowed.
- `git commit` and `git push` require explicit human approval (default
  per protocol §5 — overridden only by the milestone closeout in T009).
- Do not modify any file outside `docs/evidence/m11/discovery/`.

## Closeout format

```
M11-T000 closeout
  legacy-archaeologist: PASS | FAIL — sections present: 10/10; behavior dims: <n>
  requirements-skeptic: PASS | FAIL — questions: <n> across <m> categories; explicit_unknowns: yes/no
  design-red-team: PASS | FAIL — alternatives: <n>; dropped capabilities: <n>; cost axes: 4/4; open_disagreements: <n>
  Acceptance lines (byte-checkable): 3/3 match | <n>/3 match — list mismatches
  Closing issue: <url> — decision:confirmed | decision:needed
  Acceptance: PASS | FAIL — link to issue
  Risks / blockers: ...
  Next: M11-T001 ready to start
```

## Related issues

- M11 proposal issue (TBD) — collects the planning Q&A decisions
  (credential model, frozen+live regression target, category exercise
  scope, three new approval ops). This task closes the Discovery /
  Debate Gate bullet on that issue.

## Stop condition

Stop after 80 turns. If any subagent report fails its canonical
acceptance line, halt and ask the human — do **not** fudge the report
to make it pass. If `legacy-archaeologist` surfaces a load-bearing
requirement that invalidates the planned data model (e.g.
multi-event identity collision), halt and propose a new ADR draft
under `docs/adr/` before re-running T000.

# M11-T001: CTF schema (migration 0008) + DB helpers

## Milestone
M11: authorized CTF / lab workflow. **`arch:` tagged** — Discovery / Debate
Gate evidence (T000) is the source of truth for the schema shape.

Author `supabase/migrations/0008_m11_ctf.sql` adding `ctf_events`,
`ctf_challenges`, and `ctf_attempts` tables; confirm the existing
`ctf_scopes` table (migration 0001) is reachable; add DB helpers in

   precedent

## Scope

1. **Author `supabase/migrations/0008_m11_ctf.sql`** with three tables:

   ```sql
   create table ctf_events (
     id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
     project_id uuid not null references projects(id) on delete cascade,
     slug text not null unique,
     name text not null,
     ctftime_event_id integer,
     event_url text,
     start_at timestamptz,
     end_at timestamptz,
     scoring text default 'jeopardy',
     credentials_ref text,  -- path hint, e.g. '~/.ctf/<slug>.json'; never the value
     notes text,
     created_at timestamptz not null default now()
   );

   create table ctf_challenges (
     id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
     event_id uuid not null references ctf_events(id) on delete cascade,
     scope_id uuid references ctf_scopes(id) on delete set null,
     slug text not null,
     name text not null,
     category text not null check (category in ('web','crypto','rev','pwn','forensics','osint','misc')),
     points integer,
     description text,
     expected_flag_format text,
     attachments_path text,
     remote_endpoint text,
     created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
     unique (event_id, slug)
   );

   create table ctf_attempts (
     id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
     challenge_id uuid not null references ctf_challenges(id) on delete cascade,
     run_id uuid references experiment_runs(id) on delete set null,
     accepted boolean,
     http_status integer,
     flag_length integer,  -- NEVER the flag value
     submitted_at timestamptz not null default now(),
     response_excerpt text  -- 256-char cap, redact any string that looks like a flag
   );
   ```
   RLS enabled on all three; no policies yet (same posture as `ctf_scopes`
   in migration 0001).

2. **Apply against the local container only.**
   `dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true`; `psql $SUPABASE_DB_URL -f
   supabase/migrations/0008_m11_ctf.sql`. NEVER apply to a remote /
   production DSN.

# M11-T002: New approval operations + reviewer-gate wiring

## Milestone
M11: authorized CTF / lab workflow. **`arch:` tagged** — introduces three
new approval-policy operations (`challenge_run`, `flag_submit`,
`network_egress`) and wires them through the reviewer-gate path. Discovery
/ Debate Gate evidence (T000, specifically `design-red-team.md`) is the
source of truth for the operation shape and defaults.

## Goal
Add the three new operations to `.kca/permissions/*.yaml`, extend
`src/worker/reviewer.py::should_consult_reviewer`, extend
`src/worker/worker.py::_tool_call` to emit the new `target_op` strings,
add the relevant entries to `.claude/settings.json` and
`.claude/hooks/guard_tool.py`, and document the contract in
`docs/adr/0017-ctf-approval-gates.md`.

    precedent)

## Scope

1. **Permission policy entries.** Add to each profile:

   ```yaml
   - operation: challenge_run
     default_decision: ask
     reason: Executing a solver against an authorized CTF target — gate by default.
     audit_required: true
   - operation: flag_submit
     default_decision: ask
     reason: Submitting a flag to a CTF event API — external side effect.
     audit_required: true
   - operation: network_egress
     default_decision: deny
     reason: Egress outside ctf_scopes.target_urls is denied; widen scope row to allow.
     audit_required: true
     conditional_allow:
       when_in_scope: ask   # if request URL ∈ ctf_scopes.target_urls
   ```
   In `permissive-dev.yaml`, `challenge_run` and `flag_submit` stay on
   `ask` (no auto-allow for the live submission path). In
   `competition-runner.yaml`, `challenge_run` may move to
   `conditional_allow: allow when_in_scope` but `flag_submit` stays on
   `ask` regardless — flag submission is the highest-blast-radius op.

2. **`src/worker/reviewer.py`.** Extend `should_consult_reviewer` to
   return `True` for the three new ops; extend `run_review` to render
   the right context for each (target URL for `challenge_run` /
   `network_egress`; event slug + challenge slug for `flag_submit`;
   NEVER the flag value).

3. **`src/worker/worker.py`.** Extend `_tool_call` to emit `target_op`
   for the new operations. `challenge_run` fires when a solver tool is
   about to invoke against a target whose URL is in a `ctf_scopes`
   row or is a local in-scope service; `flag_submit` fires when
   `tools/kca/ctf.py::cmd_flag_submit` is invoked with `--dry-run=False`;
   `network_egress` fires when any worker-issued HTTP call's host is
   NOT in the union of `ctf_scopes.target_urls` rows for the current
   project AND NOT on the global allowlist.

4. **`.claude/settings.json`.** Add to the ask-list:
   - `Bash(kca ctf flag submit*)` — ask
   - `Bash(kca ctf solver run*)` — ask (only when `--dry-run=False`)
   - Do NOT add `kca ctf event/challenge/scope` — those are LOCAL_WRITE
     and run under `allow`.

5. **`.claude/hooks/guard_tool.py`.** Extend the secret denylist to
   cover `~/.ctf/*.json`, `**/ctf-credentials.json`, and any path
   matching `CTF_*_TOKEN` env-var dumps. The hook denies direct file
   reads of these paths except when invoked from within
   `tools/kca/ctf.py::_load_event_credentials` (single allow-listed
   call-site).

6. **`docs/adr/0017-ctf-approval-gates.md`.** Document:

     checks `ctf_scopes.target_urls` membership).

# M11-T003: `kca ctf` CLI surface

## Milestone
M11: authorized CTF / lab workflow.

## Goal
Add `tools/kca/ctf.py` with the `event` / `challenge` / `scope` / `solver` /
`flag` subcommands; register the `ctf` subparser in
`tools/kca/kca.py::add_parsers`; document the surface in
`tools/kca/COMMANDS.md`. All LOCAL_WRITE commands write only to the local
DB. Remote calls (challenge fetch, flag submit) require
`KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1` + `dangerouslyDisableSandbox` AND a matching
`ctf_scopes.target_urls` row.

## Read first

1. M11-T001 closeout (DB helpers in `src/db/ctf.py`)
2. M11-T002 closeout (new approval ops + worker wiring)
3. `tools/kca/competition.py` — `cmd_register` precedent (LOCAL_WRITE,
   idempotent)
4. `tools/kca/kg.py` — `cmd_submit` + `cmd_push` (credential-gate +
   reviewer-gate + audit-row sequence)
5. `tools/kca/research_fetch.py` — HTTP + Playwright; **reuse**, do
   not fork
6. `tools/kca/kca.py::add_parsers` — subparser registration pattern
7. `tools/kca/COMMANDS.md` — CLI documentation pattern
8. `.claude/settings.json` — ask-list (Bash(kca ctf …) entries from T002)

## Scope

1. **`tools/kca/ctf.py` subcommands.**

   ```text
   kca ctf event register --slug <slug> --name <name> [--ctftime-id <n>]
                          [--url <event-url>] [--start-at <iso>]
                          [--end-at <iso>] [--credentials-ref <path-hint>]
   kca ctf event list [--project <slug>] [--json]
   kca ctf event info --slug <slug> [--json]

   kca ctf challenge add --event <slug> --slug <slug> --name <name>
                         --category {web,crypto,rev,pwn,forensics,osint,misc}
                         [--points <n>] [--description <text>]
                         [--expected-flag-format <regex>]
                         [--attachments-path <path>]
                         [--remote-endpoint <url>] [--scope <scope-slug>]
   kca ctf challenge fetch --event <slug> --slug <slug>
                           [--via {http,playwright}]
                           # remote fetch requires KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1
                           # AND ctf_scopes.target_urls match
   kca ctf challenge list --event <slug> [--json]
   kca ctf challenge info --event <slug> --slug <slug> [--json]

   kca ctf scope set --slug <slug> --authorized <text>
                     --target-urls <url[,url...]>
                     [--local-only] [--expires-at <iso>]
   kca ctf scope list [--json]
   kca ctf scope verify --slug <slug> --url <url>
                        # returns exit 0 if url ∈ target_urls AND not expired

   kca ctf solver run --event <slug> --challenge <slug>
                      [--dry-run] [--reviewer-gate]
                      # if --dry-run, no challenge_run gate fires
                      # if --reviewer-gate AND not --dry-run, gate fires

   kca ctf flag submit --event <slug> --challenge <slug>
                       --flag-file <path>
                       [--dry-run]
                       # if --dry-run, prints request shape, no network
                       # if not --dry-run, requires:
                       #   1) KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1
                       #   2) dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true
                       #   3) ctf_scopes row covering submit endpoint
                       #   4) reviewer-gate approved (T006)
                       # flag is read from --flag-file, never echoed
   ```

2. **Credential loading.** `_load_event_credentials(event_slug)` reads
   `~/.ctf/<slug>.json` (with `username`, `token`, optional `team_id`)
   OR `CTF_<EVENT>_USERNAME` + `CTF_<EVENT>_TOKEN` env vars. This is the
   single allow-listed call-site for the guard_tool deny exception
   added in T002. Echo only boolean presence — never the value.

3. **`tools/kca/kca.py::add_parsers`.** Register the `ctf` subparser.
   Mirror the shape of `kaggle.add_parsers` / `competition.add_parsers`.

4. **`tools/kca/COMMANDS.md`.** Document each subcommand with: purpose,
   side-effect level (`READ_ONLY` / `LOCAL_WRITE` / `REMOTE_WRITE` /
   `SUBMISSION`), required env, reviewer-gate it triggers (if any),
   and a one-line example. The `flag submit` entry MUST note that the
   flag value is read from `--flag-file` and never echoed.

5. **Smoke tests.** Add `tests/test_kca_ctf_cli.py` covering:
   - `kca ctf event register` is idempotent (re-running with the same
     slug updates rather than duplicates).
   - `kca ctf scope verify` returns exit 0 for in-scope URL and exit
     non-zero for out-of-scope URL.
   - `kca ctf flag submit --dry-run` prints the request shape WITHOUT
     reading the flag file content (read header only; mock the file).
   - `kca ctf flag submit` (no `--dry-run`) refuses without
     `KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1` and without a matching scope.
   - No credential value or flag value appears in any test's stdout /
     stderr (audit-grep assertion).

## Non-goals

- Do not insert any challenge / event rows here. T004 owns fixtures.
- Do not exercise the reviewer-gate end-to-end. T006 owns that.
- Do not make any real network call. T007 owns the single live submit.
- Do not add a `kca ctf event watch` calendar-poll subcommand — that's
  out-of-scope follow-up.

## Acceptance criteria

- `kca ctf --help` lists the five sub-namespaces (`event`, `challenge`,
  `scope`, `solver`, `flag`).
- Each subcommand prints a useful `--help` description matching the
  side-effect level documented in COMMANDS.md.
- `tests/test_kca_ctf_cli.py` passes; no flag / credential values
  appear in stdout / stderr.
- `tools/kca/COMMANDS.md` documents each subcommand with side-effect
  level + reviewer-gate trigger.
- `kca ctf flag submit --dry-run` works without `KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1`;
  same command without `--dry-run` refuses without it.
- `ruff check tools/kca/` clean.

## Permissions

- Local file edits to `tools/kca/`, `tests/`.
- LOCAL_WRITE DB calls via `src/db/ctf.py` (via the local container).
- No real external network calls in this Loop Prompt.

## Closeout format

```
M11-T003 closeout
  tools/kca/ctf.py: <n> subcommands across {event, challenge, scope, solver, flag}
  Registered in tools/kca/kca.py::add_parsers: YES
  tools/kca/COMMANDS.md: kca ctf surface documented
  tests/test_kca_ctf_cli.py: <n> passed
  Audit-grep for flag/credential leakage in test stdout: 0 lines
  ruff check tools/kca/: clean
  Acceptance: PASS | FAIL — link to issue
  Risks / blockers: ...
  Next: M11-T004 ready to start
```

## Related issues

- M11 proposal issue (TBD). M11-T003 closes the "CLI surface" bullet.

## Stop condition

Stop after 60 turns. If `kca ctf flag submit` cannot be authored
without ever holding the flag string in a logged variable, halt and
propose an ADR amendment (the file should be opened, read into memory,
POSTed, and the local reference dropped — but never `print()`/`logger
.info()` the value).

# M11-T004: Frozen past-event challenge bundle (1 web + 1 crypto)

## Milestone
M11: authorized CTF / lab workflow.

## Goal
Bundle a small set of permissively licensed past-event CTF challenges under
`data/ctf/<event-slug>/<challenge-slug>/` so the M11 agent loop (T005), the
reviewer-gate exercise (T006), and the dry-run test suite (T008) all have
deterministic local fixtures. M11 ships **one web** + **one crypto**
challenge; pwn / rev / forensics / OSINT are taxonomy-supported but not
fixtured here.

## Read first

1. M11-T001 closeout (`ctf_events` / `ctf_challenges` / `ctf_scopes` shape)
2. M11-T003 closeout (`kca ctf event register` + `challenge add` flow)
3. `.gitignore` — current `data/` rules
4. `.claude/skills/ctf-sandbox/SKILL.md` — workflow expectations
5. The picoCTF archive (`https://picoctf.org/`) or another permissively
   licensed past-event source — research-brief licensing first.
6. `data/spaceship-titanic/manifest.json` (M9 manifest precedent)
7. `data/tpu-getting-started/manifest.json` (M10 manifest precedent,
   when T001 of M10 lands)

## Scope

1. **Licensing research-brief.** Use the `research-brief` skill against
   the candidate past-event source. Confirm:
   - License permits redistribution / inclusion in a CC-BY / Apache-2-
     compatible repo.
   - Source author attribution requirements (record in
     `data/ctf/README.md`).
   - The chosen challenges contain NO real-world flag values that
     might still be in active scoring elsewhere (use a past, closed
     event).

2. **Bundle layout.** For each of the two chosen challenges, create:

   ```text
   data/ctf/<event-slug>/<challenge-slug>/
     challenge.yaml          # metadata; canonical source of truth
     description.md          # human-readable challenge text
     attachments/            # files <1MB; bigger entries gitignored
     docker-compose.yml      # web challenge only
     solver_template.py      # T005 fills in
     expected.sha256         # checksum of the known-good flag (NOT the flag)
   ```

   `challenge.yaml` schema (validated by the `kca ctf challenge add`
   command):

   ```yaml
   slug: <slug>
   event: <event-slug>
   name: <name>
   category: web | crypto
   points: <int>
   description: <inline or @description.md>
   expected_flag_format: '^picoCTF\{[^}]+\}$'   # or event-specific regex
   attachments_path: ./attachments
   remote_endpoint: null                         # local-only
   scope_ref: ctf-local-<event-slug>             # the scope row slug
   license: <SPDX-id> (<attribution>)
   ```

3. **Web challenge.** Pick a challenge whose intended solution path is
   HTTP-only (auth bypass, IDOR, SSRF, command injection, etc.). The
   bundle ships a `docker-compose.yml` that brings up the vulnerable
   service on a private Docker network (no host port exposure beyond
   localhost). The solver_template.py uses `httpx` against
   `http://localhost:<port>` only.

4. **Crypto challenge.** Pick a small RSA / classical-cipher / weak-RNG
   challenge that runs entirely in-process (no docker). The solver_
   template.py imports `pycryptodome` / `sympy` as needed.

5. **Scope rows.** Insert one `ctf_scopes` row per challenge via
   `kca ctf scope set`:
   - web: `local-only=true`, `target_urls=["http://localhost:8080"]` (or
     whatever port the docker-compose exposes), `expires_at=null`.
   - crypto: `local-only=true`, `target_urls=[]` (no network).
   Both scope slugs are referenced from the matching `challenge.yaml`
   `scope_ref`.

6. **Event row.** Insert one `ctf_events` row for the past event via
   `kca ctf event register`. Record source attribution in the `notes`
   column.

7. **`data/ctf/README.md`.** Document the licensing chain, the two
   bundled challenges, and the `expected.sha256` convention (the hash
   covers the flag string, so anyone running the harness can verify
   a recovered flag without the bundle revealing the value).

8. **Gitignore additions.** Update `.gitignore` to gitignore
   `data/ctf/*/*/attachments/*.{bin,pcap,iso,img}` and any file >1MB
   under `data/ctf/`. Small text fixtures (HTML responses, ciphertext
   blobs) are committed.

## Non-goals

- Do not have the agent solve the challenges here. T005 owns the solve
  loop.
- Do not bundle more than 2 challenges. Web + crypto only.
- Do not bundle pwn / rev / forensics fixtures (out-of-scope follow-up).
- Do not register the chosen event as the live submission target —
  T007 picks a separate, **currently open** CTFtime event.
- Do not commit flag values, `expected.sha256` notwithstanding.

## Acceptance criteria

- `data/ctf/<event-slug>/<web-slug>/` and
  `data/ctf/<event-slug>/<crypto-slug>/` exist with all six files
  named in scope step 2.
- `kca ctf event list --json` shows the registered past event.
- `kca ctf challenge list --event <event-slug> --json` shows both
  challenges.
- `kca ctf scope list --json` shows both scope rows.
- `data/ctf/README.md` documents the licensing chain.
- `.gitignore` covers oversize / binary attachments.
- `git status` shows no untracked files >1MB under `data/ctf/`.
- No flag value is committed anywhere (manual grep:
  `grep -rE "(picoCTF|flag|FLAG)\{" data/ctf/` returns 0 lines, or only
  format-regex hits in `challenge.yaml`).

## Permissions

- Local file writes under `data/ctf/`, `.gitignore`,
  `data/ctf/README.md`.
- LOCAL_WRITE DB inserts via `kca ctf event register` / `challenge add`
  / `scope set`.
- `research-brief` skill invocation for licensing check.
- No real external network calls (the past-event source download can
  happen via `tools/kca/research_fetch.py` HTTP path — covered by
  the `web_fetch` allow gate).

## Closeout format

```
M11-T004 closeout
  Source: <event name> — <SPDX license> (<attribution>)
  Bundled: data/ctf/<event-slug>/{<web-slug>,<crypto-slug>}/
  Web: docker-compose up brings vulnerable service on localhost:<port>

  data/ctf/README.md: licensing + bundle list documented
  Gitignore additions: <list of new patterns>
  Flag-value grep: 0 hits (or N format-regex-only hits in challenge.yaml)
  Acceptance: PASS | FAIL — link to issue
  Risks / blockers: ...
  Next: M11-T005 ready to start
```

## Related issues

- M11 proposal issue (TBD). M11-T004 closes the "frozen bundle" bullet.

## Stop condition

Stop after 80 turns. If the chosen past-event source has license terms
that disallow inclusion in this repo, halt and propose an alternative
source (pwnable.kr / CSAW Quals / bespoke-author challenges). Do not
bundle anything with unclear licensing. If a candidate flag value
appears to still be in active scoring on the source site, switch to a
different challenge.

# M11-T005: Agent worker loop solves bundled challenges locally

## Milestone
M11: authorized CTF / lab workflow.

## Goal
Drive `AgentWorker` through one solve cycle per bundled challenge from
T004 — web and crypto — recovering both flags locally without real
network. Record `ctf_attempts` rows (`accepted=true`) and matching
`experiment_runs` rows with `flag_length` only (not value). No reviewer
gate fires in this Loop Prompt: gates are exercised in T006 with the
gates ON.

## Read first

1. M11-T004 closeout (bundled challenges + scope rows)
2. `.claude/skills/ctf-sandbox/SKILL.md` — workflow body; may be
   extended here to cite the new `kca ctf` commands
3. `src/worker/worker.py` — `AgentWorker` loop, `_tool_call`,
   `_should_consult_reviewer` (T002 wiring)
4. `tools/kca/run.py` — run-init + record-metric
5. `tools/kca/ctf.py::cmd_solver_run` (T003)
6. `src/db/ctf.py::record_attempt`
7. `docs/tasks/M9-T002-baseline-loop.md` — closest precedent (Kaggle
   baseline-loop pattern)

## Scope

1. **Per-challenge solve cycle.** For each bundled challenge:
   - Read `challenge.yaml` + `description.md` + attachments.
   - Category triage (web vs. crypto — straightforward from `category`
     field, but the agent should restate the strategy in its log).
   - For web: `docker compose -f data/ctf/<event>/<web-slug>/docker-
     compose.yml up -d` brings up the local service on the private
     network; agent solver uses `httpx` against `localhost:<port>`.
   - For crypto: in-process solve — no docker, no network.
   - Recover the flag.
   - Verify against `expected.sha256` (sha256 of the flag string).
   - Record via `kca ctf solver run --event <slug> --challenge <slug>
     --dry-run` (since the reviewer-gate exercise is T006, this T005
     pass runs with `--dry-run` semantics for the gate path, but
     **does not** skip the actual solve).

2. **Run / attempt records.** For each successful solve:
   - `kca run init --competition ctf-<event-slug> --run-id <challenge-slug>`
   - `kca run record-metric --run-id <run-id> --name flag_length --value <len>`
   - `record_attempt(challenge_id=..., accepted=True, http_status=None,
     flag_length=<len>, response_excerpt='<solver excerpt with flag
     redacted>', run_id=<run-id>)`
   - NEVER pass the flag string to any recorder.

3. **Skill extension.** Optionally extend
   `.claude/skills/ctf-sandbox/SKILL.md` workflow body to cite the
   `kca ctf solver run` / `kca ctf flag submit` commands. Keep the
   safety-scope section unchanged.

4. **Docker cleanup.** After each web challenge solve:
   `docker compose -f <path> down -v`. The closeout must show no
   dangling containers from this Loop Prompt.

## Non-goals

- Do not fire any reviewer gate in this Loop Prompt. T006 exercises
  gates ON.
- Do not submit any flag to a real event. T007 owns that.
- Do not solve more than the two bundled challenges from T004.
- Do not log the flag value anywhere — `experiment_runs.metrics`,
  `ctf_attempts.response_excerpt`, agent log, audit row, closeout.
- Do not modify `src/worker/worker.py` or `tools/kca/ctf.py` in this
  Loop Prompt (their scaffolding is owned by T002 / T003). If the
  solve surfaces a worker bug, file it as a follow-up issue and stop.

## Acceptance criteria

- Both bundled challenges solved: flag recovered and verified against
  `expected.sha256`.
- `ctf_attempts` has exactly 2 new rows with `accepted=true` for the
  current solve cycle.
- `experiment_runs` has 2 matching rows; each row's `metrics` JSON
  contains `flag_length` but NO `flag`, `flag_value`, or any string
  that matches the flag-format regex.
- Agent log / stdout / stderr audit-grep: 0 occurrences of the actual
  flag string (sha256-check after redaction).
- `docker ps --filter "name=m11-" --format "{{.ID}}"` returns empty
  after solve cleanup.
- The two `experiment_runs` rows are visible via `kca run list --json`.

## Permissions

- Local file reads under `data/ctf/`.
- LOCAL_WRITE DB inserts via `src/db/ctf.py` helpers.
- `docker compose up -d` / `down -v` on local-only networks.
- Local HTTP calls to `localhost:<port>` (in scope per the web
  challenge's `ctf_scopes.target_urls`).
- `dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true` for DB calls (per protocol §3).

## Closeout format

```
M11-T005 closeout
  Web challenge: <slug> — solved, flag_length=<n>, sha256 verified
  Crypto challenge: <slug> — solved, flag_length=<n>, sha256 verified
  ctf_attempts new rows: 2 (accepted=true)
  experiment_runs new rows: 2 — flag_length recorded; flag NOT logged
  Docker cleanup: no dangling containers
  Audit-grep for flag string in logs: 0 hits
  Acceptance: PASS | FAIL — link to issue
  Risks / blockers: ...

```

Stop after 100 turns. If either challenge cannot be solved within 40

# M11-T006: Reviewer gate fires for `challenge_run` and `flag_submit`

## Milestone
M11: authorized CTF / lab workflow.

## Goal
Exercise the reviewer-gate path for **both** new ops end-to-end —
`challenge_run` (before invoking a solver against an authorized target)
and `flag_submit` (before submitting a flag). Each gate writes an
`agent_reviews` row + `human_decisions` row; the `decision_api` exposes
both pending decisions to the UI Approval Inbox; the human approves both
via `kca decisions approve --id <id>` (NOT via real external calls).

The real flag submission to a live event is **out of scope** for T006 —
that's T007. T006 closes with the round-trip recorded for both ops, but
the actual external POST is not made.

## Read first

1. M11-T002 closeout (the new ops + worker wiring)
2. M11-T005 closeout (solver loop, gates OFF)
3. `src/worker/reviewer.py`
4. `services/decision_api/app.py`
5. `tools/kca/decisions.py`
6. `supabase/migrations/0006_m6_reviews_spans.sql` (agent_reviews shape)
7. `ui/src/pages/ApprovalInbox.tsx`, `ui/src/pages/DecisionGate.tsx`
8. `docs/tasks/M9-T003-reviewer-approval-gate.md` — `kaggle_submit`
   precedent
9. `docs/tasks/M10-T003-kernel-push-reviewer-gate.md` — `kernel_push`
   precedent
10. Issue #15 — no `GET /decisions` endpoint (work around as M9/M10 did)
11. Issue #16 — `reviewer_decision` event_type wording drift

## Scope

1. **Drive `challenge_run` to the gate.** Re-run the bundled-web-
   challenge solve from T005, this time WITHOUT `--dry-run`. The
   worker reaches the point where it would invoke the solver against
   `localhost:<port>` (in scope per the web challenge's `ctf_scopes`
   row). The reviewer-gate fires; `agent_reviews` row written with
   `target_op="challenge_run"`; `human_decisions` row created via
   `decision_api`. The agent halts waiting for approval.

2. **Approve `challenge_run`.** `kca decisions approve --id <id>` (or
   via the UI Approval Inbox). The worker resumes, invokes the solver,
   recovers the flag, records the attempt. Verify the second
   `ctf_attempts` row for this challenge has the gate's review-id
   linkage (via `agent_job_events`).

3. **Drive `flag_submit` to the gate (LOCAL_WRITE only).** Invoke
   `kca ctf flag submit --event <past-event-slug> --challenge <web-
   slug> --flag-file <path-to-recovered-flag>`. Because the chosen
   event is the **past** event from T004 (no live endpoint), the
   command must:
   - Fire the `flag_submit` reviewer-gate.
   - When approved, refuse to actually POST (no live endpoint;
     `remote_endpoint=null` in `challenge.yaml`).
   - Record a `ctf_attempts` row with `http_status=null` and a
     `response_excerpt` noting "dry-run path; no remote endpoint".
   - Confirm the gate fired even though no real network call follows.

4. **Approve `flag_submit`.** Same approval path. Confirm the
   `human_decisions` row + the `agent_job_events` linkage.

5. **Smoke the refusal direction.** With the gates ON, attempt a
   challenge_run against `http://kaggle.com` (a host NOT in any
   `ctf_scopes.target_urls` row). Expected:
   - `network_egress` denies the call at the reviewer-gate layer.
   - `agent_reviews.verdict=reject` recorded.
   - The worker halts and does NOT attempt the call.

## Non-goals

- Do not make any real external network call to a CTF event API. T007
  owns that single call.
- Do not approve any decision without the human's explicit
  `kca decisions approve` invocation.
- Do not modify `services/decision_api/app.py` to add `GET /decisions`
  — that's issue #15's scope.
- Do not change the `target_op` wording emitted by the worker — that's
  issue #16's scope.

## Acceptance criteria

- `agent_reviews` has at least 2 new rows with
  `target_op in ('challenge_run','flag_submit')`.
- `human_decisions` has at least 2 new rows matching the reviews
  (target_op aligned).
- `agent_job_events` has the linking events for both round-trips.
- The challenge_run gate's verdict is `approve`; the worker resumed
  and recovered the flag.
- The flag_submit gate's verdict is `approve`; the LOCAL_WRITE-only
  `ctf_attempts` row was recorded with `http_status=null`.
- The refusal smoke (challenge_run against `kaggle.com`) recorded
  `agent_reviews.verdict=reject` and the worker did NOT POST.
- No flag value or credential value appears in `agent_reviews.context`
  or `human_decisions.notes`.
- UI Approval Inbox renders both pending decisions during the test
  window (manually verified; screenshot optional, link in closeout).

## Permissions

- LOCAL_WRITE DB inserts.
- `dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true` for DB / `localhost` calls.
- `kca decisions approve --id <id>` invocations.
- No real external network calls.

## Closeout format

```
M11-T006 closeout
  challenge_run round-trip: agent_reviews.id=<uuid>; human_decisions.id=<uuid>; verdict=approve
  flag_submit round-trip: agent_reviews.id=<uuid>; human_decisions.id=<uuid>; verdict=approve; ctf_attempts.id=<uuid> (http_status=null)
  Refusal smoke (challenge_run → kaggle.com): agent_reviews.verdict=reject; no POST
  agent_job_events linkage: <n> events tying job <id> to the two reviews
  UI Approval Inbox: pending decisions visible (manual check; <link or 'verified locally'>)
  Audit-grep for flag/credential leakage in review context: 0 hits
  Acceptance: PASS | FAIL — link to issue
  Risks / blockers: ...
  Next: M11-T007 ready to start
```

## Related issues

- M11 proposal issue (TBD). M11-T006 closes the "reviewer gate round-
  trip" bullet.
- Cross-link issue #15 / #16 (worked around, not closed).

## Stop condition

Stop after 80 turns. If the gate fails to fire when it should, halt
and re-check `src/worker/reviewer.py::should_consult_reviewer` from
T002. If the refusal smoke does NOT deny `kaggle.com`, halt and
re-check the `network_egress` policy resolution — that is a
security-critical bug and blocks the milestone.

````

# M11-T007: ONE real flag submission to a live CTFtime-listed event

## Milestone
M11: authorized CTF / lab workflow.

## Goal
Run exactly ONE real `kca ctf flag submit` against a live CTFtime-listed
event (e.g. `bbbctf.com` or the next-pick from the planning Q&A) under
explicit human approval. Record the resulting `ctf_attempts` row with
`accepted=true|false` and the event's HTTP status. This is the ONLY
Loop Prompt in M11 that makes a real external API call.

## Read first

1. M11-T003 closeout (`kca ctf flag submit` credential-gate)
2. M11-T006 closeout (`flag_submit` reviewer-gate round-trip)
3. `tools/kca/ctf.py::cmd_flag_submit`
4. `.claude/settings.json` — `Bash(kca ctf flag submit*)` on ask
5. `supabase/migrations/0008_m11_ctf.sql` — `ctf_attempts` shape
6. `docs/tasks/M9-T004-real-submission.md` — single-submission precedent
   (Kaggle CSV submit)
7. `docs/tasks/M10-T004-real-kernel-push.md` — single-push precedent
   (Kaggle kernel push)

## Pre-conditions (verify ALL before running)

- M11-T006 closeout shows a `decision:confirmed` human decision on the
  closing issue.
- `~/.ctf/<event-slug>.json` (or `CTF_<EVENT>_USERNAME` +
  `CTF_<EVENT>_TOKEN`) is populated for the chosen event (human
  action; no automation).
- A `ctf_scopes` row exists for the chosen event with `target_urls`
  covering the submit endpoint; `expires_at` is null or in the future.
- The closing issue carries `policy:approval-required` AND a human
  comment explicitly approving the submission (this milestone's only
  such record). The wording MUST match the M9-T004 / M10-T004
  precedent.
- The flag to submit was recovered LOCALLY (or via an in-scope
  `challenge_run` against the live event's challenge endpoint, also
  under approval — that approval must have its own row in
  `agent_reviews`).
- `KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1` AND `dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true` are set
  for the agent shell.

## Scope

1. **Register the live event** (if not already): `kca ctf event
   register --slug <slug> --name <name> --ctftime-id <n> --url
   <event-url> --credentials-ref ~/.ctf/<slug>.json`.

2. **Set the scope row** for the submit endpoint:
   `kca ctf scope set --slug live-<event-slug>
   --authorized "Live CTFtime event <slug>; one-shot flag submission"
   --target-urls "<submit-endpoint>"
   --expires-at <iso, e.g. event end_at>`.

3. **Verify scope** before submitting: `kca ctf scope verify --slug
   live-<event-slug> --url <submit-endpoint>` — must exit 0.

4. **Submit the flag.** Run exactly ONE command:
   ```bash
   kca ctf flag submit \
     --event <slug> \
     --challenge <challenge-slug> \
     --flag-file <path-to-flag-file>
   ```
   The command:
   - Fires the `flag_submit` reviewer-gate (already approved per
     T006-style round-trip, recorded on the closing issue).
   - Reads the flag from `--flag-file`. NEVER echoes the value.
   - POSTs to the event's submit endpoint.
   - Records a `ctf_attempts` row with `accepted=<bool>`,
     `http_status=<int>`, `flag_length=<int>`, `response_excerpt=<256-
     char redacted excerpt>`.

5. **Post-submit hygiene.**
   - `shred -u <path-to-flag-file>` (or `rm` with `wipe -i` if
     available) — the flag file should not survive on disk past the
     submission.
   - `git status` — confirm no `~/.ctf/*` or flag file accidentally
     staged.

6. **Record the result on the closing issue** as a comment that
   includes:
   - `ctf_attempts.id=<uuid>`
   - `accepted=<bool>`
   - `http_status=<int>`
   - The approval comment link.
   - NEVER the flag value or any credential.

## Non-goals

- Do NOT submit a second flag inside this Loop Prompt. If the human
  later wants more, that's a follow-up issue.
- Do NOT retry on error. If the event returns rate-limit / invalid-
  flag / scope-drift, HALT and file a follow-up issue.
- Do NOT echo the flag value in stdout / stderr / log / DB row / PR
  body / GitHub comment.
- Do NOT modify `tools/kca/ctf.py` here — the credential-gate +
  reviewer-gate path is already wired in T003 / T006.
- Do NOT bypass the reviewer-gate "even if the human already
  approved on the issue". The gate must still fire and write the
  `agent_reviews` row for this specific run.

## Acceptance criteria

- Exactly ONE new row in `ctf_attempts` with `submitted_at` in the
  current Loop Prompt's window and `http_status` populated.
- `accepted` is `true` OR `false` (not null). If false, the closeout
  documents the event's rejection reason (excerpted, redacted).
- One new `agent_reviews` row with `target_op='flag_submit'` and
  verdict matching the approval.
- One new `human_decisions` row linked to the review.
- Closing GitHub issue has a comment linking the approval comment +
  the `ctf_attempts.id`.
- Flag file is wiped post-submit (verify with `ls <path>` returning
  non-existent).
- Audit-grep across the entire Loop Prompt's session: 0 lines echo
  the flag value.
- `git status` clean (no `~/.ctf/*` or flag file staged).

## Permissions

- LOCAL_WRITE DB inserts via `src/db/ctf.py`.
- One real external network call to the event's submit endpoint
  (the only such call in M11).
- `dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true` + `KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1`.
- `shred` / `rm` on the flag file.
- No `git push` / `gh pr` activity from this Loop Prompt — milestone
  closeout (T009) handles it.

## Closeout format

```
M11-T007 closeout
  Live event: <slug> (<ctftime-id>); endpoint: <submit-endpoint>
  Scope row: live-<slug> — target_urls covers submit endpoint; expires_at=<iso>
  flag_submit reviewer-gate: agent_reviews.id=<uuid>; verdict=approve
  ctf_attempts: id=<uuid>; accepted=<bool>; http_status=<int>; flag_length=<n>
  Flag file wiped: YES (path no longer exists)
  Closing-issue comment: <url>
  Audit-grep for flag value: 0 hits across session
  Acceptance: PASS | FAIL — link to issue
  Risks / blockers: ...
  Next: M11-T008 ready to start
```

## Related issues

- M11 proposal issue (TBD). M11-T007 closes the "single live
  submission" bullet AND must be the issue carrying
  `policy:approval-required` + `decision:confirmed`.

## Stop condition

Stop after 60 turns. If the event returns ANY error other than
`accepted=true|false`, HALT and file a follow-up issue. Do NOT retry.
If the credential file cannot be loaded, HALT and ask the human to
populate it — do NOT attempt to write it from inferred values.
If the scope-verify command does not return exit 0, HALT — do NOT
widen the scope row to make it pass; route through the human.

````

# M11-T008: E2E + smoke tests (dry-run + refusal paths, no credentials, no net)

## Milestone
M11: authorized CTF / lab workflow.

## Goal
Add `tests/test_m11_e2e.py` + `tests/test_m11_smoke.py` to lock the M11
workflow in CI: dry-run path runs without credentials, refusal paths
hard-deny out-of-scope targets, and no test echoes `.env` / `~/.ctf/*`
contents.

## Read first

1. `tests/test_m9_e2e.py` — closest pattern (Kaggle dry-run e2e)
2. `tests/test_m9_smoke.py` — DB-gated assertion pattern
3. `tests/test_m10_e2e.py` (if M10 has shipped) — kernel-push refusal
   shape; mirror it for `flag_submit` / `challenge_run`
4. `src/worker/worker.py` — `dry_run` path
5. `tools/kca/ctf.py::cmd_flag_submit` — credential-gate refusal
6. M11-T002 / T003 / T004 / T005 closeouts
7. Issue #11 — the dotenv-leak this test must NOT repeat

## Soft pre-req

Issue #11 (dotenv-leak / secret-file hygiene in pytest subprocess)
**should** be merged on `main` before this Loop Prompt runs. Verify with
`gh issue view 11 --json state` returns `"CLOSED"`. If #11 is not yet
closed, do NOT write any test that subprocess-shells in a way that would
inherit `.env` or `~/.ctf/*` to the child. The simpler form (no
subprocess; in-process import of CLI functions) is acceptable as a
workaround, but the closeout MUST note the deviation.

## Scope

1. **`tests/test_m11_e2e.py`** — five tests, no DB, no credentials, no
   network:

   **(a) `test_flag_submit_refused_without_approval`** — invoke
   `tools.kca.ctf.cmd_flag_submit` with `--dry-run=False` but no prior
   approval row; expect `RefusalError` (or whatever T003 / T006 wires)
   AND no POST attempt. Assert the audit row would have recorded
   `flag_submit` reject.

   **(b) `test_challenge_run_refused_for_out_of_scope_url`** — build a
   fake job context with a `ctf_scopes.target_urls` row covering
   `http://localhost:8080` only; attempt `challenge_run` against
   `http://example.com`. Expect refusal via the `network_egress`
   policy.

   **(c) `test_network_egress_denied_to_kaggle_from_ctf_job`** — same
   shape as (b) but with `https://www.kaggle.com` as the out-of-scope
   target. Cross-platform isolation: a CTF job MUST NOT touch Kaggle.

   **(d) `test_bundled_solver_roundtrip_local`** — using the T004
   fixtures, run the web solver against a recorded HTTP response
   (mocked via `respx` / `httpx_mock` to avoid bringing docker up in
   CI) and the crypto solver in-process. Expect both flags recovered
   and verified against `expected.sha256`. Assert the flag string
   appears nowhere in stdout / stderr.

   **(e) `test_no_secret_leak_in_test_stdout`** — run the full file's
   tests with `pytest --capture=tee-sys`; grep the captured output
   for any line that looks like `KCA_TOKEN=`, `CTF_*_TOKEN`, a
   ~/.ctf/*.json line, or a flag pattern. Assert 0 matches. This
   test is the M11 analogue of the M10 dotenv-leak regression and
   directly closes issue #11 from the CTF side.

2. **`tests/test_m11_smoke.py`** — DB-gated assertions (mirror M9 / M10
   smoke shape):
   - Migration `0008_m11_ctf.sql` applied (tables present).
   - `ctf_events` contains the past-event row from T004.
   - `ctf_challenges` contains 2 rows (web + crypto) for that event.
   - `ctf_scopes` contains the matching scope rows.
   - `agent_reviews` has at least 2 rows with
     `target_op in ('challenge_run','flag_submit')` from T006.
   - `ctf_attempts` has at least 2 rows with `accepted=true` from
     T005 + the T006 LOCAL_WRITE row + (if T007 ran) the live row.
   SKIPs cleanly without `SUPABASE_DB_URL`.

3. **CI integration.** Confirm the new tests are picked up by the
   existing `.github/workflows/test.yml` no-db + live-db jobs. No new
   workflow file. If `pytest -q tests/test_m11_e2e.py` exits clean on
   a fresh checkout (no `.env`, no `~/.ctf/`), the e2e test
   suite is portable.

4. **Audit-grep harness.** Add a small helper `tests/_audit_grep.py`
   (or extend an existing one if M9 / M10 already has it) that scans
   a captured pytest log for secret patterns + flag-format regexes.
   Use it in (e) above.

## Non-goals

- Do not write tests that subprocess-shell into the agent and inherit
  `.env` / `~/.ctf/*`. Use in-process imports.
- Do not write tests that make any real external network call.
- Do not bring `docker-compose` up in CI — mock HTTP responses for
  the web challenge in (d).
- Do not add `pytest --runslow` markers; the M11 e2e + smoke suites
  should run under the existing CI matrix.

## Acceptance criteria

- `python -m pytest tests/test_m11_e2e.py -v` → all 5 tests pass; 0
  network calls (verify with `pytest --capture=tee-sys | grep -c '
  GET http\|POST http'`).
- `python -m pytest tests/test_m11_smoke.py -v` → all pass with
  `SUPABASE_DB_URL`; SKIPs cleanly without.
- `python -m pytest tests/ services/decision_api/tests -v` → 0
  failures.
- `ruff check tests/` clean.
- Audit-grep helper detects synthetic secret-pattern + flag-pattern
  injections in a one-liner self-test.
- The M11 e2e test suite runs on a fresh checkout with no `.env`,
  no `~/.ctf/`, and 0 credentials — assert with a clean-env
  pytest invocation in the closeout.

## Permissions

- Local file writes under `tests/`.
- `pytest` invocations under sandbox (no DB / no net required).
- LOCAL_WRITE DB calls allowed for the smoke suite under
  `dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true`.
- No real external network calls.

## Closeout format

```
M11-T008 closeout
  tests/test_m11_e2e.py: 5/5 passed

````markdown
# Milestone Loop Protocol

_Shared rules that apply to every milestone Loop Prompt (M0+) unless a
milestone explicitly overrides one._

Each `docs/m*-loop-prompts.md` should reference this file once at the top
rather than duplicating the rules per prompt.

---

## 1. Sequencing

- Loop Prompts within a milestone MUST execute in order.
- Each prompt's **acceptance checks MUST pass** before moving to the next.
- On failure: fix the specific issue and **retry that prompt only**; do
  not skip ahead and do not redo prompts that already passed.

## 2. External systems and side effects

- Do NOT call the **real Anthropic API or Kaggle API** outside of paths
  the milestone explicitly designates as live; default to `--dry-run`.
- Do NOT run real **Kaggle submit / kernel push / dataset upload /
  model upload** unless the milestone explicitly requests it AND a
  human-approval record exists.
- Do NOT change **production Supabase**.

## 3. Database validation

- Use `SUPABASE_DB_URL=postgresql://postgres:s3cr3t@172.21.0.4:5432/postgres`
  — the `supabase-db` container on the local Docker network.
- Container IPs change on `docker compose down/up`; refresh with:
  ```bash
  docker inspect supabase-db \
    --format '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}'
  ```
- DB calls and LAN-host calls require `dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true`.
  Cloud LLM calls stay **inside** the sandbox.

## 4. Reporting

- Report **PASS / FAIL / SKIP** inline for each prompt's verification
  step.
- At milestone end, write the milestone's defined **Closeout format**
  (see each milestone's last Loop Prompt for the exact fields).

## 5. Git / GitHub — worktree mode

This project executes each milestone inside a dedicated **git worktree**
branched off `main`.

- **Mid-milestone, mid-prompt:** do not `git commit` or `git push`
  unless the individual task spec explicitly says so. Stage with
  `git add` and surface diffs in the inline report.
- **At milestone end** — once every Loop Prompt has PASSed and the
  milestone's Closeout has been written — Claude Code SHOULD:
  1. `git add` only the files listed in the Closeout's "files changed"
     section (or its equivalent).
  2. `git commit` using either:
     - one squash commit per milestone, OR
     - one commit per Loop Prompt,
     depending on the milestone's preference. The default is **one
     commit per Loop Prompt**, with the milestone's final review as the
     last commit.
  3. `git push` the worktree's branch to the remote.
  4. `gh pr create` against `main` using the milestone's
     `docs/m{N}-final-review.md` as the PR body.

- The following **still require explicit human approval** at any time:
  - `git push --force` (any branch)
  - `gh pr merge` (any PR)
  - any push to `main` directly
  - any `gh label create/edit/delete`, `gh issue edit/comment`,
    `gh pr edit/comment` against issues or PRs **not** owned by this
    milestone

- If the milestone's task spec or scope says
  "do not commit / push / open PRs", that override **wins** — typically
  used for planning-only or evidence-only milestones.

## 6. Secrets and forbidden reads

These are always denied, regardless of milestone:

- `.env*`
- `**/kaggle.json`, `~/.kaggle/kaggle.json`
- `~/.ssh/id_rsa`, `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`, any private key contents
- `~/.aws/**`, `~/.config/gcloud/**`
- `secrets/**`

Shell commands that would surface the above (`cat`, `grep`, `head`,
`tail`, `less`, `more`, file uploads) over these paths are blocked at
the hook layer.

---

## How a milestone references this file

In each Loop Prompt block, instead of repeating the rules above, include
one line near the top:

```
Follow: docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md
```

A milestone's `docs/m{N}-loop-prompts.md` should still spell out:

- the milestone's own scope, non-goals, and task list;
- per-Loop-Prompt read lists, scope, acceptance criteria;
- any **override** of a default in this file (e.g. a planning-only
  milestone overriding the worktree commit/push behavior).

---

## 7. Discovery / Debate Gate

_Added by M9.4. Additive only — §1–§6 above are unchanged._

Some tasks are large enough that "implement first, debate later"
loses load-bearing requirements (the canonical failure: `tools/legacy/kkr.py`
migration missing multi-Kaggle-account / owner / env semantics; see
`docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-24-r3.md` §6). The Discovery / Debate Gate
runs three role-isolated subagents — `legacy-archaeologist`,
`requirements-skeptic`, `design-red-team` — **before** any
implementation work begins.

The gate is **mandatory** for any task whose spec is tagged `arch:`
(introduces / revises an architectural primitive) or
`legacy-migration:` (migrates / rewrites / replaces a legacy artefact).
Routine tasks (bug fixes, doc edits, dependency bumps, small
refactors) do not trigger the gate.

When the gate fires, the executing session MUST:

1. Invoke `legacy-archaeologist` first if the task touches any
   legacy artefact (skip allowed only for greenfield `arch:` tasks,
   with explicit note in the closeout).
2. Invoke `requirements-skeptic` next.
3. Invoke `design-red-team` last.
4. Attach all three reports to the task closeout under
   `docs/evidence/<milestone>/<task>/discovery/`.
5. Verify all three canonical acceptance lines (defined in
   `docs/architecture/discovery-debate-gate.md`) byte-for-byte
   against the reports. A missing acceptance line is a task FAIL.

Full template, tag-placement options, and the verbatim acceptance
lines live in `docs/architecture/discovery-debate-gate.md`. The
orchestration skill `.claude/skills/design-archaeology/SKILL.md`
(owned by M9.3) is the inline alternative when the task is small
enough not to warrant separate subagents; the agent path and the
skill path emit compatible output shapes by design.

M9.4 enforces the gate via task-spec acceptance criteria and this
section's wording, **not** via hook-level denials. Hook-based
enforcement is a deferred follow-up; file a separate issue if you
want it built.

# M11 — Loop Prompts

_Authorized CTF / lab workflow milestone — first non-Kaggle competition platform on
the kaggle-code-agent stack._
_For sequential, partly autonomous execution on Arch Linux._
_Prerequisite: M9 exit confirmed (live LB recorded on Spaceship Titanic; see
`docs/m9-final-review.md`). M10 may run in parallel; the only hard dependency
M11 inherits from M10 is the dotenv-leak fix (issue #11), which must be
merged on `main` before **M11-T008** writes its e2e refusal tests._
_Shared rules: every Loop Prompt below MUST follow `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md`
(sequencing, no real Kaggle/Anthropic outside designated approval paths, DB DSN +
sandbox bypass, **per-milestone worktree by default**, secret denylist, **§7
Discovery / Debate Gate for `arch:` tagged tasks**)._

## M11 at a glance

M11 is the **first CTF / authorized-lab regression** for this platform, and
the first milestone to validate that the worker / reviewer / approval-inbox
stack works for a **non-Kaggle competition policy**. M9 + M10 covered Kaggle
CSV submission and Kaggle kernel push respectively. M11 covers CTF jeopardy:
challenge inventory, scoped solver execution, and flag submission to the
event endpoint.

The CTF user pattern (from the planning Q&A) is:

1. Check [CTFtime calendar](https://ctftime.org/calendar/) for upcoming events.
2. Register on the event site **as a human** (no browser-automated sign-up in
   M11); record event credentials under `~/.ctf/<event-slug>.json` or
   `CTF_<EVENT>_*` env vars.
3. For each challenge: read description, download attachments, decide whether
   the challenge is local-only (zip / docker bundle) or remote (must hit the
   event's challenge endpoint).
4. Solve locally where possible; submit the flag to the event's API.

M11 brings (1) into a `kca ctf event register` LOCAL_WRITE flow, defers (2)
to the human, exercises (3) end-to-end against a **frozen past-event bundle**
under `data/ctf/<event>/<challenge>/` for deterministic CI, and exercises (4)
once for real against a **single live CTFtime-listed event** under explicit
human approval.

M11 is **not** a leaderboard-chasing milestone. The acceptance criterion is
that the CTF workflow runs end-to-end correctly under the approval gates and
hard-refuses out-of-scope targets. Solver quality / category coverage is
captured as future work — see `docs/architecture/m11-ctf-workflow.md` §
"Out of scope".

Direct entry into M11 is blocked until **all** are true:

- M9 is merged on `main` (`docs/m9-final-review.md` exists and reports PASS).
- The Discovery / Debate Gate (M11-T000) has produced all three subagent
  reports with byte-for-byte acceptance lines under
  `docs/evidence/m11/discovery/`.
- Issue #11 (dotenv-leak / secret-file hygiene in pytest subprocess) is
  merged on `main`. This is a soft pre-req for **M11-T008** (the e2e
  refusal-path test): M11-T000 through M11-T007 may proceed in parallel
  with #11 work.
- The local Supabase container is running; migration `0001_init.sql`'s
  `ctf_scopes` table is reachable.

### What's in scope

| Capability | Owned by | M11 touches |
|---|---|---|
| Discovery / Debate Gate for CTF data model + new approval ops | `.claude/agents/{legacy-archaeologist,requirements-skeptic,design-red-team}.md`, `docs/architecture/discovery-debate-gate.md` | T000 — all three reports + byte-checkable acceptance |
| Event / challenge / attempt schema | `supabase/migrations/0008_m11_ctf.sql` + `src/db/ctf.py` | T001 |
| New approval operations (`challenge_run`, `flag_submit`, `network_egress`) | `.kca/permissions/{default,permissive-dev,competition-runner}.yaml`, `src/worker/reviewer.py`, `src/worker/worker.py`, `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/hooks/guard_tool.py` | T002 |
| `kca ctf` CLI surface | `tools/kca/ctf.py` + `tools/kca/kca.py::add_parsers` | T003 |
| Frozen past-event challenge bundle (1 web + 1 crypto) | `data/ctf/<event-slug>/{web-1,crypto-1}/` | T004 |
| Agent worker drives ctf-sandbox skill to solve locally | `src/worker/`, `.claude/skills/ctf-sandbox/SKILL.md`, `tools/kca/run.py` | T005 |
| Reviewer-gate before solver run + flag submit | `src/worker/reviewer.py`, `services/decision_api/app.py`, UI Approval Inbox | T006 |
| ONE real flag submission to a live CTFtime event | `tools/kca/ctf.py::cmd_flag_submit`, `ctf_attempts` table | T007 — single real call |
| E2E refusal-path tests | `tests/test_m11_e2e.py`, `tests/test_m11_smoke.py` | T008 |
| ADRs + architecture doc | `docs/adr/0016-ctf-data-model.md`, `docs/adr/0017-ctf-approval-gates.md`, `docs/architecture/m11-ctf-workflow.md` | T001 / T002 / T009 |
| Final review + handoff | `milestone-final-review` skill, `worktree-milestone-pr` skill | T009 |
| GitHub issue / label workflow | `.github/labels.yml`, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature-work.yml`, PR template | every task |

### What's NOT in scope

- Running flag submissions outside T007's single approved call.
- Browser-automated event sign-up. M11 reads human-supplied credentials only.
- Pwn / reverse-engineering / forensics agent-loop solves. The taxonomy
  supports them (`ctf_challenges.category`) but the M11 solve loop exercises
  only `web` + `crypto`. Filed as follow-up issues at milestone close.
- CTFtime calendar polling / auto-event-watch / scheduled-job auto-submit.
- Changing production Supabase.
- Implementing M10 follow-ups (parallel milestone; cross-cutting items file
  as their own issues).
- Implementing M9 follow-ups A, C, D, E (still tracked as issues #14, #15, #16,
  #17). Issue #11 is the only soft pre-req (see entry gates).

DB / sandbox details: see `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` §3 — the local
`supabase-db` container (`postgresql://postgres:s3cr3t@172.21.0.4:5432/postgres`)
needs `dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true`. The real CTF event API call inside
M11-T007 also needs sandbox bypass and an approved `ctf_scopes.target_urls`
entry covering the submit endpoint.

    against the live event's challenge endpoint, also under approval).

Run exactly ONE real `kca ctf flag submit --event <slug>
--challenge <slug> --flag <flag>` against the approved live event.
Record the ctf_attempts row with accepted=true|false and the event
response's HTTP status. Do NOT echo the flag string anywhere. Do
NOT iterate beyond this one submission inside this Loop Prompt. If
the event returns an error (rate limit, invalid flag, scope drift),
HALT and open a follow-up issue — do not silently retry.

labelled per task type. The canonical **M11 proposal issue** (TBD —
filed before T000 starts) collects the planning Q&A decisions; individual
task issues link back to it.

| M11-T002 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `arch:`, `area:worker`, `area:security`, `area:policy` | `ai:ready` (after T001 closed) | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M11-T003 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:cli`, `area:ctf` | `ai:ready` (after T001 + T002 closed) | `ai:implementing` → close |

---

## Approval gates (summary)

| Gate | When it fires | Where the approval is recorded | Who can approve |
|---|---|---|---|
| `challenge_run` | Worker is about to invoke a solver against a target whose URL is in `ctf_scopes.target_urls` OR is a local in-scope service | `agent_reviews` row + `human_decisions` row + (T007 only) comment on the closing GitHub issue | Project owner / reviewer named on the issue |
| `flag_submit` | `tools/kca/ctf.py::cmd_flag_submit` is invoked with `--dry-run=False` | `agent_reviews` row + `human_decisions` row + (T007 only) approval comment | Project owner |
| `network_egress` | Worker attempts to call any host NOT in `ctf_scopes.target_urls` AND the host is not on the global allowlist | DENY at the reviewer-gate; recorded as `agent_reviews.verdict=reject` + audit row in `agent_tool_audit` | Not applicable — deny is final; the human must edit the scope row to widen it |
| `kaggle_submit` | Not used in M11 | n/a | n/a |
| `kernel_push` | Not used in M11 | n/a | n/a |

The CTF approval flow inside M11 is:

```
worker stages solver / flag artifact + target URL
  → reviewer-gate writes agent_reviews row + agent_job_events
    (target_op="challenge_run" or "flag_submit")
  → decision_api surfaces pending decision (POST /decisions queued;
    UI reads via supabase-js until issue #15 lands GET /decisions)
  → UI Approval Inbox renders pending decision
  → human approves via UI (POST /decisions/<id>/approve) OR
    `kca decisions approve --id <id>`
  → (T007 only) human comments "approved to submit" on the closing
    issue
  → triage agent promotes issue to `decision:confirmed` + `ai:ready`
  → M11-T007 Loop Prompt runs ONE `kca ctf flag submit`
  → ctf_attempts row written with accepted=true|false + http_status
  → PR opens with the approval comment linked
```

A second real flag submission inside M11 is **out of scope**. If a
follow-up challenge in M11-T005 or M11-T007 surfaces another flag
that the human wants submitted, file it as a new M11-followup issue
and gate it the same way.

## Rollback / stop criteria

Stop the milestone — do **not** advance to the next Loop Prompt — if any of
these is true:

- A real CTF event call returns an error from the event API outside T007's
  single approved call (rate limit, scope violation, bad credentials). The
  fix path is local: regenerate solver / re-verify scope and re-request
  approval; do NOT silently retry.
- The reviewer gate (M11-T006) fails to fire for `challenge_run` or
  `flag_submit` when it should, or fires when it shouldn't.
- Any `policy:approval-required` issue advances without the corresponding
  `decision:confirmed` label and comment.
- Any test in the validation suite regresses from green to red.
- The DSN, Kaggle credentials, `~/.ctf/*`, or `.env*` are accidentally
  printed in any log, audit row, or PR. Stop and rotate the credential
  immediately.
- The Discovery / Debate Gate at T000 surfaces an undecided question that
  invalidates the data model (e.g. multi-event identity collision; team-
  account vs. individual-account ambiguity). Pause, draft a new ADR, and
  restart T000.
- A `network_egress` deny fails to trigger for an attempted call to a host
  outside the scope row (silent egress = critical security regression).
- Issue #11 is reopened mid-milestone with evidence that the leak
  re-emerged. Halt T008 work until #11 is green again.

If M11 needs a new architectural decision (e.g. multi-event credential
rotation; pwn/rev solver harness; CTFtime calendar auto-watch), **pause
and ask** — those are M11-followup / M13 decisions, not M11 expansion.
Open an ADR draft in `docs/adr/` and stop the milestone there.

# M11-T000: Discovery / Debate Gate for the M11 CTF architecture

## Milestone
M11: authorized CTF / lab workflow. **`arch:` tagged** — Discovery / Debate
Gate per `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` §7 is mandatory before any T001+
implementation work begins.

## Goal
Run the three role-isolated subagents (`legacy-archaeologist`,
`requirements-skeptic`, `design-red-team`) against the proposed M11
architecture — the `ctf_events` / `ctf_challenges` / `ctf_attempts` data
model, the three new approval operations (`challenge_run`, `flag_submit`,
`network_egress`), and the CTFtime → event-credentials → challenge →
solver → flag-submit workflow taxonomy.

T000 is **gate-only**: no code, no schema, no permission edits.
A missing byte-checkable acceptance line is a T000 FAIL and blocks all
downstream M11 work.

## Read first

1. `PROJECT_STATE.md`
2. `AGENTS.md`
3. `CLAUDE.md`
4. `docs/milestones.md` §M11
5. `docs/architecture/discovery-debate-gate.md` — verbatim acceptance lines
6. `docs/architecture/design-archaeology.md`
7. `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` §7
8. `docs/handoffs/m9-handoff.md`
9. `docs/adr/0005-job-taxonomy.md` — `project_kind` enum + `ctf` slug
10. `docs/adr/0006-configurable-approval-gates.md` — operation data shape
11. `supabase/migrations/0001_init.sql` — existing `ctf_scopes` table
12. `.claude/skills/ctf-sandbox/SKILL.md` — current workflow body
13. `src/worker/reviewer.py` — existing reviewer-gate pattern
14. `docs/evidence/m9_4-kkr-replay/` — worked precedent (kkr.py)
15. `.claude/agents/{legacy-archaeologist,requirements-skeptic,design-red-team}.md`

## Scope

1. **Invoke `legacy-archaeologist` first.** Pass it the CTF-related
   artefacts already in the repo: `ctf_scopes` table (migration 0001),
   `.claude/skills/ctf-sandbox/SKILL.md`, `src/worker/reviewer.py` CTF
   mentions, `docs/adr/0005-job-taxonomy.md` `ctf` platform enum,
   any prior CTF references in meeting notes. Produce the 10-section
   report and write it to
   `docs/evidence/m11/discovery/legacy-archaeologist.md`.

2. **Invoke `requirements-skeptic` next.** Pass it the planning Q&A
   decisions (credential model, frozen-bundle + 1 live submission,
   five-category taxonomy with web+crypto exercised, three new ops).
   Produce ≥5 questions across ≥3 categories (scope authorization,
   credential handoff, multi-event identity, flag-submission semantics,
   audit retention) plus an `explicit_unknowns:` section. Write to
   `docs/evidence/m11/discovery/requirements-skeptic.md`.

3. **Invoke `design-red-team` last.** Pass it the proposed data model
   shape (`ctf_events` / `ctf_challenges` / `ctf_attempts`), the three
   new ops, and the two prior reports. Produce ≥3 alternatives for the
   data model and for the approval-op design; name ≥1 dropped capability
   with `file:line` evidence (e.g. dropping per-challenge
   `attempts_per_hour` rate-limit); cover all 4 cost axes; record ≥1
   `open_disagreement`. Write to
   `docs/evidence/m11/discovery/design-red-team.md`.

4. **Verify acceptance lines byte-for-byte.** Compare each report's
   canonical acceptance line against the verbatim text in
   `docs/architecture/discovery-debate-gate.md`. Any mismatch is a
   T000 FAIL.

5. **File or update the closing GitHub issue.** Link the three evidence
   files. Add the `arch:` label. Promote to `decision:confirmed` only
   after the human has read all three reports and signed off.

## Non-goals

- Do not modify `supabase/migrations/`, `.kca/permissions/`,

## Acceptance criteria

  `docs/evidence/m11/discovery/{legacy-archaeologist,
