````markdown
# Discovery / Debate Gate

_Status: M9.4 ships the gate (this doc + protocol §7 + the three agents). The
`.claude/skills/design-archaeology/SKILL.md` orchestration the gate
references is owned by M9.3; M9.3-T001 must land that skill before §7
becomes fully enforceable end-to-end._

## What this is

The Discovery / Debate Gate is the M9.4-shipped guardrail that turns
"please be more proactive in plan / design / architect mode" into a
**checkable artefact**. Three role-isolated subagents run before any
implementation work begins on an architecture-shaped or
legacy-migration-shaped task. Each agent has a canonical acceptance
line that the parent session verifies; the three lines together form
the gate.

Origin: `docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-24-r3.md` §6 — the observation
that the original `tools/legacy/kkr.py` migration missed
multi-Kaggle-account / owner / env semantics because no agent role
was responsible for surfacing them.

## Agents

| Agent | File | Phase | Reads | Emits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `legacy-archaeologist` | `.claude/agents/legacy-archaeologist.md` | 1 of 3 | legacy artefacts (read-only) | 10-section archaeology report |
| `requirements-skeptic` | `.claude/agents/requirements-skeptic.md` | 2 of 3 | proposed task spec + archaeology report | numbered question list across 5 categories + `explicit_unknowns:` |
| `design-red-team` | `.claude/agents/design-red-team.md` | 3 of 3 | proposed design + archaeology + skeptic reports | ≥3 alternatives, dropped-capability evidence, 4 cost axes, open disagreements |

Hand-off order is **archaeology → skepticism → red-team**. Skipping a
phase is not allowed when the gate is mandatory (see §"When the gate
fires" below). The orchestration mechanism is
`.claude/skills/design-archaeology/SKILL.md` (owned by M9.3); until
that skill file is on disk, the gate runs by direct subagent
invocation against this doc.

## Acceptance lines (verbatim — union of all three agents)

A parent session verifies these three lines, byte-for-byte, against
the three agents' outputs. Failing any one of them means the gate
did not pass.

> Output MUST contain ≥5 questions spread across ≥3 categories, and
> an `explicit_unknowns:` section listing things the agent could not
> answer without human input.

> Output MUST cover all 10 sections; ≥5 distinct legacy behavior
> dimensions must be named explicitly, including any multi-account /
> owner / env mapping the legacy artefact encodes.

> Output MUST include ≥3 alternatives, ≥1 dropped capability with
> file:line evidence, all four long-term-cost axes, and ≥1
> actionable `open_disagreements` entry.

## When the gate fires

The gate is **mandatory** for any task whose spec carries one of the
two task tags in its `## Milestone` line, first heading, or front-matter:

- `arch:` — the task introduces or substantially revises an
  architectural primitive (worker, runner, sandbox, queue, telemetry
  pipeline, schema dimension, permission policy).
- `legacy-migration:` — the task migrates, rewrites, replaces, or
  takes over a legacy tool / config / notebook.

Routine tasks (bug fixes, doc edits, dependency bumps, small
refactors inside an existing primitive) do **not** trigger the gate.
The tag is added by the human authoring the task spec, not inferred
by an agent.

When the gate fires, the executing session MUST:

1. Invoke `legacy-archaeologist` first if the task touches any legacy
   artefact. (Skip for greenfield `arch:` tasks with no legacy code
   in scope.)
2. Invoke `requirements-skeptic` next, regardless.
3. Invoke `design-red-team` last, regardless.
4. Attach the three reports to the task closeout under
   `docs/evidence/<milestone>/<task>/discovery/`:
   - `legacy-archaeologist.md` (skip allowed only with explicit note)
   - `requirements-skeptic.md`
   - `design-red-team.md`
5. Verify all three acceptance lines (above) byte-for-byte against
   the reports. Failure to verify is a task-spec FAIL — not a vibe.

## Task tag convention

Tag placement options (any of these is acceptable; the parent session
should grep all three):

```markdown
## Milestone
M11.3: arch: new sandbox runner

# legacy-migration: M9.4-T002 legacy-archaeologist agent scaffold
```

or in YAML front-matter:

```yaml
tags: [arch, sandbox]
```

The tag is **opt-in by the task author** and reviewed by the human
who approves the task spec. M9.4 does not auto-attach tags.

## Closeout evidence path

```
docs/evidence/<milestone>/<task>/discovery/
  legacy-archaeologist.md
  requirements-skeptic.md
  design-red-team.md
```

`<milestone>` follows the existing convention (`m9_4`, `m10`, `m11_3`).
`<task>` follows the existing task-id convention
(`M9_4-T005-kkr-replay-and-smoke`, etc).

## Relationship to M9.3's `design-archaeology` skill

The skill in M9.3 encodes a 10-section archaeology *template* that any
session can run inline. The `legacy-archaeologist` agent in M9.4
emits the same 10-section report shape but in a role-isolated subagent
context: read-only tools, `permissionMode: plan`, no shell. Use the
skill for lightweight inline analysis; use the agent (via this gate)
when the task is large enough to warrant a separate subagent and a
gate-level acceptance check.

The two are deliberately compatible: the agent's output schema is a
strict subset of the skill's template, so a parent session can swap
between them without rewriting downstream consumers.

## Non-enforcement (M9.4 scope boundary)

M9.4 enforces the gate via **acceptance criteria** in task specs and
the milestone-loop-protocol §7 wording — not via tool-level denials
or hook-based blocks. Hook-based enforcement (e.g. a PreToolUse hook
that refuses `Edit` on `src/**` when an `arch:` task has no
`discovery/` evidence) is a deferred follow-up. File it as a separate
issue if you want it built.

## Cross-references

- Milestone protocol additive section: `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` §7.
- M9.4 planning: `docs/m9_4-loop-prompts.md`.
- M9.3 skill (sibling milestone): `docs/m9_3-loop-prompts.md`,
  `.claude/skills/design-archaeology/SKILL.md` (M9.3-T001).
- Origin observation: `docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-24-r3.md` §6.
````

````markdown
tools: Read, Glob, Grep

You are a legacy archaeologist. Before any code that migrates,
replaces, or wraps a legacy artefact is written, you read that
artefact and produce a structured report of what it *does* and what
it *assumes*. The canonical failure mode you exist to prevent: the
`tools/legacy/kkr.py` / `kkr.yaml` migration missed multi-Kaggle-
account / owner / env semantics because no agent role was responsible
for surfacing them
(see `docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-24-r3.md` §6).

This agent is paired with — but distinct from — `requirements-skeptic`
(asks questions about the proposed task) and `design-red-team`
(refutes the proposed design). The hand-off order, when invoked via
`.claude/skills/design-archaeology/SKILL.md` (M9.3), is
archaeology → skepticism → red-team. Acceptance criteria for all
three agents live in `docs/architecture/discovery-debate-gate.md`.

The `design-archaeology` *skill* (M9.3) and this *agent* are not the
same thing. The skill encodes a 10-section template that any session
can follow; this agent is the role-isolated subagent that produces
the report on demand, and whose tools / permission mode are
constrained so it cannot accidentally run the legacy code.

## What you must do

Read the named legacy artefacts (scripts, YAML / TOML / JSON configs,
READMEs, notebooks, accompanying dotenv example files). Produce a
report covering all ten mandatory sections below, in order. Each
section MUST cite `file:line` evidence — never a free-floating claim.

Mandatory output sections:

1. Workflows the legacy tool supports — the end-to-end flows a user
   could run (push / submit / watch / status / list / fetch /
   dry-run / verify / …). One bullet per workflow.
2. Hidden assumptions — environment variables, file-system layout,
   sentinel files, implicit ordering of operations, undocumented
   defaults, network reachability requirements.
3. User personas / owner accounts / env mappings — every distinct
   identity the artefact can act as (Kaggle owner, GitHub identity,
   service account, env-file slot). For each, name the config knob
   that selects it and where in the file it lives. This section is
   load-bearing for the kkr.py-style multi-account case.
4. Side effects — every remote / external write or read the artefact
   triggers (Kaggle pushes, dataset uploads, kernel pushes,
   filesystem writes outside the workspace, network egress).
5. State files / registries / dotenv overrides — every persistent
   thing the artefact reads or writes (manifest files, run
   registries, lock files, .env / .env.local / .env.<owner>).
6. Config dimensions — every CLI flag, env var, and YAML knob that
   changes behaviour. Include defaults.
7. Features to preserve — capabilities that the replacement MUST
   keep. Cite why (test coverage, audit obligation, user habit,
   compliance).
8. Features to deprecate — capabilities the replacement should drop,
   with reason (dead code, replaced by platform primitive, security
   risk, unmaintained dependency).
9. Questions that MUST be asked before implementation — handed off
   to `requirements-skeptic`. One bullet per question, with the
   evidence that triggered it.
10. Tests / fixtures that would prove behavior parity — what a
    `tests/test_<legacy>_parity.py` would have to cover so a
    migration cannot regress silently.

Acceptance line (the parent session checks this verbatim):

> Output MUST cover all 10 sections; ≥5 distinct legacy behavior
> dimensions must be named explicitly, including any multi-account /
> owner / env mapping the legacy artefact encodes.

## What you must NOT do

- Do not execute the legacy code. No `python kkr.py …`, no
  `kaggle …`, no shell invocation, no notebook execution. Your
  `permissionMode: plan` and read-only tool list already enforce
  this; treat it as load-bearing.
- Do not modify any legacy file. The artefact is evidence, not a
  workspace.
- Do not fetch external dependencies, install packages, or hit the
  network. Read what is on disk.
- Do not infer decisions from ambiguity. If two interpretations are
  equally plausible, name both in §9 (questions for skeptic) — do
  not pick one and present it as fact.

## Output shape (canonical example)

```
legacy-archaeologist report for <artefact path or set>

1. workflows:
   - <flow> — entry point: <file:line>; exit: <file:line>
2. hidden_assumptions:
   - <assumption> — evidence: <file:line>
3. personas_and_accounts:
   - <persona> — selector: <file:line>; storage: <file:line>
4. side_effects:
   - ...
5. state_files_and_registries:
   - ...
6. config_dimensions:
   - <flag/env/yaml-key> = <default> — effect: <file:line>
7. features_to_preserve:
   - <feature> — why: <reason>; evidence: <file:line>
8. features_to_deprecate:
   - <feature> — reason: <reason>; evidence: <file:line>
9. questions_for_skeptic:
   - <question> — triggered by: <file:line>
10. parity_tests:
    - <test name> — covers: <behaviour>; fixture: <path>
```

Return only this report. No prose preamble, no closing summary.
````

````markdown
You are a design red team. Given a proposed design (task spec, ADR
draft, planning doc) plus the upstream outputs from
`legacy-archaeologist` and `requirements-skeptic`, you refute the
proposal. You produce at least three alternative designs, name the
capabilities the proposal would drop, and argue the long-term costs.
You never approve a design. The human owns the decision; you make the
disagreement explicit.

This agent runs *last* in the Discovery / Debate Gate hand-off
(archaeology → skepticism → red-team), as documented in
`.claude/skills/design-archaeology/SKILL.md` (M9.3). The union of all
three agents' acceptance lines lives in

## What you must do

Read the proposed design plus the upstream archaeology and skeptic
reports. Produce a report with the four mandatory sections below.
Cite `file:line` evidence whenever you claim a capability would be
lost or a constraint would be violated — never a free-floating
assertion.

Mandatory output sections:

1. `alternatives:` — ≥3 alternative designs. Each entry MUST have a
   name, a one-paragraph sketch, and the key tradeoff vs the
   proposed design. Strawman alternatives (clearly weaker on every
   axis) do not count.
2. `dropped_capabilities:` — features / behaviours the proposed
   design would lose vs the legacy artefact OR vs any of the
   alternatives. Each entry MUST cite `file:line` evidence — the
   legacy file and line where the capability lives, or the
   alternative-design section where it would survive.
3. `long_term_costs:` — one sentence minimum per axis:
   - `cognitive_load` — how much a new contributor must hold in
     their head to use / change the design.
   - `ops_burden` — what breaks at 3am; what needs paging; what
     manual recovery looks like.
   - `extensibility` — how the design fares against the next two
     likely scope expansions (name them).
   - `blast_radius` — what fails if this design fails (data loss,
     leaderboard pollution, credential leak, audit gap).
4. `open_disagreements:` — explicit list of points where the
   red-team disagrees with the proposed design. Each item MUST end
   with an actionable next step: more research, write a spike, ask
   human, defer to a follow-up issue (with proposed labels).

Acceptance line (the parent session checks this verbatim):

> Output MUST include ≥3 alternatives, ≥1 dropped capability with
> file:line evidence, all four long-term-cost axes, and ≥1
> actionable `open_disagreements` entry.

## What you must NOT do

- Do not sign off on the design. The agent refutes; it does not
  ratify. Even if the design looks correct, your job is to surface
  the disagreement — emit an `open_disagreements: []` only if you
  have *exhausted* the search for one.
- Do not modify code, file GitHub issues / PRs / comments, or run
  shell commands. Your `permissionMode: plan` already refuses
  non-plan tool calls; treat that as load-bearing.

- Do not invent file:line citations. If you cannot find evidence in
  the artefacts the upstream agents read, mark the claim as
  `evidence: unavailable` in §2 and route it to §4 as
  `open_disagreements`.
````

```markdown
# CTF Sandbox Workflow

Use this workflow only for explicitly authorized CTF challenges, local labs, or target scopes provided by the human.

## Safety scope

Allowed:

- Analyze local challenge files.
- Run challenge containers or binaries provided for the CTF.
- Interact with explicitly provided CTF endpoints.
- Write solver scripts and educational writeups.

Not allowed:

- Scan public IP ranges or unrelated domains.
- Attack third-party systems.
- Steal or exfiltrate real credentials.
- Deploy malware, persistence, or destructive payloads.
- Use CTF techniques outside the authorized scope.

## Workflow

1. Restate the authorized scope and target.
2. Inventory files, services, ports, and constraints.
3. Identify category: crypto, pwn, web, reversing, forensics, misc, OSINT, etc.
4. Form hypotheses and run minimal safe checks.
5. Keep commands and outputs logged.
6. Build a solver or exploit only within the challenge scope.
7. Produce a concise writeup with root cause, steps, flag, and mitigation idea if relevant.

If scope is unclear, ask the human to define the CTF target before running security tooling.
```

````markdown
# ADR-0005: Job taxonomy and platform terminology

Status: accepted  
Date: 2026-05-19  
Decided in: `docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-19-r1.md`

---

## Context

The platform uses several related terms — project, competition, session, job, experiment,
run, submission — that are easily confused. This ADR defines each term precisely so that
all AI tools, platform code, and human users share the same vocabulary.

---

## Definitions

### Project
A top-level working context owned by a user.  
Corresponds to: `projects` table.  
Example: `"flower-tpu-2026"`, `"ctf-practice-may26"`.

One project can contain many competitions and sessions. It is the billing and
access-control boundary.

### Competition
A specific contest the user has entered on an external platform.  
Corresponds to: `competitions` table.  
Fields: slug, platform (kaggle / ctf / hackathon), metric, objective, daily submission limit.  
Example: `flower-classification-with-tpus` on `kaggle`.

A competition belongs to one project. It carries the rules, metric name, and current
best result.

### Session
A working period grouping related jobs under a shared goal.  
Corresponds to: `agent_sessions` table.  
Example: "May 19 afternoon — try EfficientNetB3 and Mixup augmentation".

A session has a branch/worktree reference and an overall goal. Jobs within a session
share context (but NOT file state — each job gets its own workspace).

### Job ← primary schedulable unit
**One discrete task assigned to one AI agent worker.**  
Corresponds to: `agent_jobs` table.  
The job is the smallest unit of work the platform queues, executes, and records independently.

A job has:
- `job_type`: the kind of work (see job types below)
- `prompt`: the English-language instruction to the agent
- `model`: LiteLLM model string
- `policy`: sampling params + budget limits + approval settings
- `workspace_path`: isolated git worktree for this job
- `status`: queued → running → succeeded / failed / paused
- `agent_job_events`: turn-by-turn audit log

**A job is NOT:**
- The whole competition (that is a `competition`)
- A multi-day session (that is a `session`)
- The code execution itself (that is an `experiment_run`)
- A human decision (that is a `human_decision`)

### Experiment
A hypothesis and configuration being tested.  
Corresponds to: `experiments` table.  
Example: "EfficientNetB3 with Mixup, lr=1e-4, 20 epochs".

An experiment is typically created by an `implement` or `experiment` job.
It records the hypothesis, code ref, config, and dataset version.

### Run (experiment run)
One execution of experiment code.  
Corresponds to: `experiment_runs` table + `runs/<competition>/<run_id>/` on disk.  
Created by `kca run init`, updated by `kca run record-metric`.

A run records: command, status, metrics (cv_score, val_loss, etc.), artifact paths,
wall-clock time, analysis notes.

### Submission
A file submitted to the external competition leaderboard.  
Corresponds to: `submissions` table.  
Created by a `prepare_submission` job; submitted by a `submit` job (or human).

### human_decision
A human approval or rejection of a proposed action.  
Corresponds to: `human_decisions` table.  
Created when a job hits a configured approval gate.  
Resolved by `kca decisions approve/deny` or the platform UI.

---

## Job types

| job_type | Description | Typical tools used | Approval needed (default) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `research` | Read competition pages, discussions, papers; produce a brief | read_file, grep, (browser via future MCP) | No |
| `implement` | Write or modify Python/notebook code | read_file, write_file, edit_file, run_bash(kca nb) | No |
| `experiment` | Run code, record metrics | run_bash(kca run, pytest), read_file | No |
| `debug` | Diagnose and fix a specific error | read_file, edit_file, run_bash(pytest) | No |
| `eval` | Compare runs, produce analysis | read_file, run_bash(kca run list) | No |
| `prepare_submission` | Generate and validate submission.csv | read_file, write_file, run_bash(kca) | No |
| `submit` | Submit to Kaggle leaderboard | run_bash(kca kaggle submit) | Configurable (default: No — see ADR-0006) |
| `kernel_push` | Push notebook to Kaggle kernel | run_bash(kca kaggle push) | Configurable (default: No — see ADR-0006) |
| `monitor` | Watch a Kaggle kernel run, fetch results | run_bash(kca kaggle watch, fetch) | No |
| `analysis` | Summarise results, recommend next steps | read_file, write_file | No |
| `git_commit` | Stage and commit workspace changes | run_bash(git add, git commit) | No |
| `git_push` | Push branch to remote | run_bash(git push) | Configurable (default: No — see ADR-0006) |

---

## Object hierarchy

```
Project
  └─ Competition (one or more)
       └─ Session (one or more per competition)
            └─ Job (one or more per session)       ← agent_jobs
                 ├─ agent_job_events               ← turn/tool audit log
                 ├─ human_decisions (0 or more)    ← approval gates
                 └─ Experiment (0 or more)         ← experiments table
                      └─ Run (one or more)         ← experiment_runs + runs/ dir
                           └─ Submission (0 or 1)  ← submissions table
```

---

## Consequences

- All code, prompts, and docs should use these exact terms.
- If a concept doesn't map to one of these terms, it's either a UI concern (future M7)
  or needs a new ADR.
- `agent_sessions` and `agent_jobs` table names already match these definitions.
- The term "task" is ambiguous (used differently in todos, Supabase, LangGraph); prefer
  "job" for the schedulable unit and "step" for sub-steps within a job turn.

````

```python
When the primary worker is about to call a high-stakes operation
(`kaggle_submit`, `supabase_migrate`, `git_force_push`, `dataset_upload`,
`delete_artifact`), the reviewer reads the job's event trail and final
plan, calls a reviewer model via LiteLLM, and returns a verdict
(`approve` | `reject` | `abstain`). Sync-only for M6.

import json
import os
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any


DEFAULT_REVIEWER_MODEL = "claude-opus-4-7"
DEFAULT_TRIGGER_OPS = (
    "kaggle_submit",
    "supabase_migrate",
    "git_force_push",
    "dataset_upload",
    "delete_artifact",
)


@dataclass
class ReviewRequest:
    job_id: str
    target_op: str
    tool_name: str
    tool_input: dict
    final_message: str | None = None
    event_trail: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)


@dataclass
class ReviewVerdict:
    verdict: str
    rationale: str
    evidence: dict
    cost_usd: float
    reviewer_model: str

    "Return STRICT JSON only (no prose, no markdown), exactly: "
    '{"verdict": "approve|reject|abstain", '
    '"rationale": "<one paragraph>", '
    '"evidence": {"key_signals": [...]}}\n\n'
    "Use approve when the plan and tool input clearly match the stated "
    "task and contain no destructive surprise. Use reject when the call "
    "would touch the wrong data, push the wrong file, leak secrets, or "
    "violate competition/CTF rules. Use abstain when context is too thin "
    "to decide; a human will be paged."
)


def _trim_event_trail(events: list[dict], max_events: int = 20) -> list[dict]:
    """Keep at most the most-recent max_events events, drop bulky fields."""
    if len(events) > max_events:
        events = events[-max_events:]
    pruned: list[dict] = []
    for ev in events:
        pruned.append(
            {
                "event_type": ev.get("event_type"),
                "turn_number": ev.get("turn_number"),
                "event_data": ev.get("event_data"),
            }
        )
    return pruned


_EVENT_TRAIL_TRIAGE_THRESHOLD = 8 * 1024  # 8 KB


def _render_prompt(req: ReviewRequest) -> str:
    trail = _trim_event_trail(req.event_trail)
    trail_json = json.dumps(trail, default=str, ensure_ascii=False)
    summary_block: str | None = None
    if len(trail_json) > _EVENT_TRAIL_TRIAGE_THRESHOLD:
        try:
            from src.worker import triage as _triage

            sresult = _triage.summarise_text(trail_json)
            if sresult.get("ok") and sresult.get("summary"):
                summary_block = (
                    f"(event_trail triaged to {sresult.get('endpoint')}:"
                    f"{sresult.get('model')})\n{sresult['summary']}"
                )
        except Exception:
            summary_block = None
    body = {
        "job_id": req.job_id,
        "target_op": req.target_op,
        "tool_name": req.tool_name,
        "tool_input": req.tool_input,
        "final_message": req.final_message,
    }
    if summary_block is not None:
        body["event_trail_summary"] = summary_block
    else:
        body["event_trail"] = trail
    rendered = json.dumps(body, default=str, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
    return f"REVIEW REQUEST:\n{rendered}\n\nReturn STRICT JSON only."


def _trigger_ops_from_env() -> set[str]:
    raw = os.environ.get("KCA_REVIEWER_TRIGGER_OPS", "")
    if not raw.strip():
        return set(DEFAULT_TRIGGER_OPS)
    return {p.strip() for p in raw.split(",") if p.strip()}


def should_consult_reviewer(operation: str) -> bool:
    """Return True if the given operation is in the configured trigger set."""
    return operation in _trigger_ops_from_env()


def escalate_reject() -> bool:
    return os.environ.get("KCA_REVIEWER_ESCALATE_REJECT", "1").strip() == "1"


class Reviewer:
    """Sync reviewer. Calls LiteLLM unless dry_run=True."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        model: str | None = None,
        max_tokens: int = 2048,
        timeout_s: int = 120,
        dry_run: bool = False,
        dry_verdict: str = "approve",
        dry_rationale: str = "dry-run reviewer auto-approve",
    ) -> None:
        self.model = (
            model or os.environ.get("KCA_REVIEWER_MODEL") or DEFAULT_REVIEWER_MODEL
        )
        try:
            self.max_tokens = int(os.environ.get("KCA_REVIEWER_MAX_TOKENS", max_tokens))
        except ValueError:
            self.max_tokens = max_tokens
        try:
            self.timeout_s = int(os.environ.get("KCA_REVIEWER_TIMEOUT_S", timeout_s))
```

````markdown
# ADR-0006: Configurable approval gates — default allow

Status: accepted  
Date: 2026-05-19  
Decided in: `docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-19-r1.md`  
Supersedes: prior implicit policy of "always require approval for remote writes"

---

## Context

Earlier platform design required human approval for all Kaggle submissions, kernel
pushes, and git pushes. This was chosen conservatively during M0–M2 setup.

The user's actual Kaggle workflow (see `docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-17-r1.md`) is
iterative and fast. Requiring manual approval on every submission adds friction
without meaningfully increasing safety for an experienced user who:
- Has already reviewed the code in the job's experiment run
- Understands the submission mechanics
- Wants the agent to handle routine mechanics autonomously

The main human decision points are **strategic** (switch model, switch approach,
ensemble), not operational (submit file X, push kernel Y).

## Decision

All approval gates are **configurable per project** and **default to allow (no approval required)**.

### Default policy

```json
{
  "approval_gates": {
    "kaggle_submit":    false,
    "kernel_push":      false,
    "dataset_upload":   true,
    "git_push":         false,
    "git_force_push":   true,
    "supabase_migrate": true,
    "delete_artifact":  true
  }
}
```

`true` = requires human approval before executing.  
`false` = agent executes autonomously (logged, auditable, but no pause).

`dataset_upload`, `git_force_push`, `supabase_migrate`, and `delete_artifact` default
to `true` because they are infrequent, higher-blast-radius operations.

### Per-competition override

A competition record can override the project defaults:
```json
{
  "competition_policy": {
    "kaggle_submit":  true,
    "max_daily_submissions": 5
  }
}
```

Useful if a competition has strict submission limits or the user wants to be more
careful during the final days before deadline.

### Per-job override

A job can further restrict (but not loosen) the project/competition policy:
```json
{
  "job_approval_override": {
    "kaggle_submit": true
  }
}
```

Jobs cannot lower gates below what the competition policy sets.

## Implementation

### In `tools/kca/kg.py` (previously `kaggle.py`)

Replace the hard-wired `KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1` env-var gate with a policy lookup:

```python
def _check_approval_gate(operation: str, policy: dict) -> None:
    """Raise ApprovalRequired if the operation needs human approval per policy."""
    approval_gates = policy.get('approval_gates', {})
    requires = approval_gates.get(operation, OPERATION_DEFAULTS[operation])
    if requires:
        raise ApprovalRequired(operation, policy)
```

`OPERATION_DEFAULTS` mirrors the table above. The `KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE` env var is kept
as an emergency override for CI/scripted contexts but is no longer the primary gate.

### In `src/worker/tools.py` (`ToolExecutor`)

`ToolExecutor` receives the job's resolved approval policy and calls `_check_approval_gate`
before executing any REMOTE_WRITE or SUBMISSION tool.

### In `scripts/run_job.py`

Policy resolution order (highest priority first):
1. Per-job `job_approval_override`
2. Competition `competition_policy`
3. Project `approval_gates`
4. Platform defaults (table above)

### In `kca decisions`

When an approval gate fires, the worker:
1. Inserts a `human_decisions` row with `status='pending'`.
2. Logs the decision_id to stderr.
3. Returns `WorkerResult(status='paused')`.

The human resolves with `kca decisions approve --id <id>` or via the future UI.
The job can then be restarted (M4+ resume logic).

## Consequences

- **Positive:** Faster iteration. Agent can run a full research → implement → submit
  cycle without human touch on routine operations.
- **Positive:** Experienced users are not blocked by unnecessary gates.
- **Positive:** All operations are still logged in `agent_job_events` — autonomy does
  not mean invisibility.
- **Negative:** Higher risk of an unintended submission on a fresh competition if the
  user forgets to set `kaggle_submit: true` for that competition.
- **Mitigation:** New competition records should remind the user to review the approval
  policy before the first `submit` job runs. Platform UI (M7) will surface this clearly.
- **Mitigation:** `kca decisions list` still works as an audit trail for all completed
  actions, even auto-approved ones.

## Human intervention points (unchanged)

The following always require human judgment regardless of approval gate settings:
- **Major direction changes:** switch model, switch approach, ensemble strategy.
- **Budget exhaustion:** when `max_cost_usd` is hit, human decides whether to increase.
- **Data policy decisions:** using external data, expanding training set beyond competition data.
- **Final submission selection:** choosing which 1–2 runs to use as final submissions.

These are not gate-able by the platform — they are judgment calls that belong to
the human and are surfaced via the analysis and eval job outputs.

````
</details>

```markdown
# legacy-archaeologist report for tools/legacy/kkr.py + tools/legacy/kkr.yaml

Source: tools/legacy/kkr.py @ 6231fd1f54b6, tools/legacy/kkr.yaml @ 0543e71a5aa1

_Produced under the M9.4 Discovery / Debate Gate as the demonstration
replay (M9.4-T005). The agent body lives in
`.claude/agents/legacy-archaeologist.md`; this artefact is a manual
execution of that agent's protocol because the
`.claude/skills/design-archaeology/SKILL.md` orchestration is owned by
M9.3-T001 and was not yet on disk at replay time._

## 1. Workflows supported

- `push <name>` — build a Kaggle notebook from `<code_file>` in
  `kkr.yaml`, push it as a Kaggle kernel under `<owner>/<slug>`.
  Entry: `kkr.py:2194`; main: `kkr.py:2293`; new-run impl:
  `_create_new_run` at `kkr.py:1511`.
- `submit [name]` — submit (a) a freshly built version or (b) an
  existing version selected by `NAME`, `--run`, or `--kernel/--version`.
  Entry: `kkr.py:2216`; existing-version path: `_submit_existing` at
  `kkr.py:1733`.
- `watch [name]` — poll remote kernel status until terminal.
  Entry: `kkr.py:2244`; impl: `_watch_impl` at `kkr.py:1943`.
- `fetch [name]` — download `source/output` artifacts for a selected
  run. Entry: `kkr.py:2267`; impl: `_fetch_impl` at `kkr.py:2006`.
- `status [name]` — one-shot remote-status query. Entry:
  `kkr.py:2272`; impl: `_status_impl` at `kkr.py:2074`.
- `list` — list tracked runs from the local registry. Entry:
  `kkr.py:2277`; row builder uses `_list_registry_entries` at
  `kkr.py:848`.

Cross-cutting flags on every subcommand: `--dry-run`, `--json`,
`--yaml`, `--run-root`, `--env`, `--quiet`, `-v/--verbose`
(`kkr.py:2158–2173`).

## 2. Hidden assumptions

- `kkr.yaml` has a `_base` block whose keys are merged with the
  per-config block via `_deep_merge` (`kkr.py:421–445`, validated at
  `kkr.py:491`). Per-config blocks override scalars and union-extend
  list-typed keys (`LIST_CFG_KEYS` at `kkr.py:60–66`).
- The `id` field MUST be `owner/slug`; `_slug_parts` at `kkr.py:466`
  raises if missing. Owner is derived from `id`, not specified
  independently — evidence: `kkr.py:520`.
- `_msg` template is `kkr@{ts}` by default (`kkr.py:514`,
  `_format_submit_message` at `kkr.py:551`), `{ts}` is filled at submit
  time, 500-character cap enforced at `kkr.py:558` — Kaggle rejects
  longer messages.
- `kkr.yaml` carries inline comments flagging two patches required
  against `kaggle==1.8.3`: one for `owner/model-slug` `model_sources`
  format (`kkr.yaml:31`), another to enable the H100 `docker_image`
  override (`kkr.yaml:38`). These patches are tribal knowledge — if the
  replacement does not preserve or supersede them, real pushes silently
  fail.
- Local registry root defaults to `.kkr/registry/` under
  `--run-root`; `--run-root` defaults to `DEFAULT_RUN_ROOT`
  (`kkr.py:2162`). Multiple concurrent runs on the same host all share
  one registry tree.

## 3. User personas / accounts / owners — load-bearing

This is the section the original migration missed (see
`docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-24-r3.md` §6). The legacy tool *encodes*
multi-Kaggle-account submission as a first-class concept and the
replacement must not erase it.

- **`harrysun2006`** owner — see `kkr.yaml:7` `_base.id`, `kkr.yaml:58`
  (`a09h`), `kkr.yaml:77` (`b09h`), `kkr.yaml:90` (`c09h`),
  `kkr.yaml:108` (`d09h`). The `h` suffix in config names means "owned
  by harrysun2006".
- **`firefly2006`** owner — see `kkr.yaml:66` (`a09m`), `kkr.yaml:83`
  (`b09m`), `kkr.yaml:98` (`c09m`), `kkr.yaml:116` (`d09m`). The `m`
  suffix in config names means "owned by firefly2006".
- **`andreasbis`** owner — appears only in `kernel_sources` for `a09*`
  configs (`kkr.yaml:61, 69`) — i.e. a third-party kernel reused by
  both `h` and `m` flows. Not an active submission account, but an
  upstream code source the replacement must keep allowed.
- **Owner-to-env-file mapping** lives in `_load_env_for_owner` at
  `kkr.py:528–548`. Three resolution paths in order:
  1. `--env <path>` override — raises `FileNotFoundError` if the
     given path does not exist (`kkr.py:535–537, 547`).
  2. Programmatic `env_map[owner]` lookup (`kkr.py:538–539`).
  3. Fallback to `Path(".") / f".env.{owner}"` (`kkr.py:541`).
  Calling `load_dotenv(path, override=True)` (`kkr.py:543`) overrides
  any in-process Kaggle credentials, so back-to-back pushes under
  different owners work without an external account switcher.
- Selector aliases by suffix (`h` / `m`) are convention, not enforced
  by code. The replacement must either (a) preserve the convention and
  document it, or (b) introduce an explicit `owner:` field per config
  and migrate the YAML in place.

## 4. Side effects

- Kaggle kernel push: `_get_kaggle_api()` at `kkr.py:587` returns an
  authenticated `KaggleApi`; subsequent `kernels_push` / `kernels_status`
  / `kernels_output` invocations write to Kaggle servers under the
  owner currently loaded into the in-process credentials.
- Kaggle competition submit: chained off a successful push (see
  `_submit_existing` at `kkr.py:1733`); writes a competition submission
  under the current owner.
- Filesystem writes inside `--run-root` (default `.kkr/`):
  - `manifest.json` per run (`kkr.py:824–828`).
  - `registry/<run_id>.json` per run (`kkr.py:816, 838`).
  - Cached kernel outputs in `extracted_dirs` (`kkr.py:178`).
- `load_dotenv(..., override=True)` (`kkr.py:543`) mutates
  `os.environ` for the lifetime of the process. Long-running
  orchestrators must isolate.

## 5. State files / registries / dotenv overrides

- `.kkr/<run_dir>/manifest.json` — per-run `RunManifest`
  (`kkr.py:201–222`).
- `.kkr/registry/<run_id>.json` — `RegistryEntry`
  (`kkr.py:230–250`); driven by `_save_registry` (`kkr.py:838`) and
  `_list_registry_entries` (`kkr.py:848`).
- `.env`, `.env.{owner}`, or `<env_override>` — read by
  `_load_env_for_owner` (`kkr.py:528–548`). Treat `.env.{owner}` as a
  load-bearing schema, not an ad-hoc convention.
- File names: `DEFAULT_PUSH_FILENAME`, `DEFAULT_WATCH_FILENAME`,
  `DEFAULT_FETCH_FILENAME`, `DEFAULT_SUBMIT_FILENAME`
  (`kkr.py:43–46`) — used as legacy artifact filenames inside a run
  directory.

## 6. Config dimensions

Flag / env / YAML knobs that change behaviour. Defaults in parens.

- CLI (common, `kkr.py:2158–2173`):
  - `--yaml` (`kkr.yaml`), `--run-root` (DEFAULT_RUN_ROOT),
    `--env` (none → `.env.{owner}`), `--json` (false), `--dry-run`
    (false), `--quiet` (false), `-v/--verbose` (count).
- CLI (selector, `kkr.py:2174–2187`): `name` (positional),
  `--run`, `--kernel`, `--version`.
- CLI (push, `kkr.py:2197–2215`): `--stub`, `--wait`,
  `--interval` (DEFAULT_INTERVAL), `--timeout` (DEFAULT_TIMEOUT).
- CLI (submit, `kkr.py:2221–2243`): `--stub`, `--msg`, `--wait`
  (BooleanOptional, default False), `--interval`, `--timeout`.
- CLI (watch, `kkr.py:2249–2266`): `--wait` (BooleanOptional,
  default True), `--interval`, `--timeout`.
- CLI (list, `kkr.py:2282–2289`): `--limit` (50), `--refresh`.
- YAML knobs (`kkr.yaml:1–47`): `id`, `title`, `code_file`,
  `language`, `kernel_type`, `is_private`, `enable_gpu`,
  `enable_tpu`, `enable_internet`, `competition`, `submit_file`,
  `submit_type`, `competition_sources`, `dataset_sources`,
  `kernel_sources`, `model_sources`, `docker_image`,
  `machine_shape`, `_msg`, `_stub`, `_exts`, `_refs`,
  `_drop_tags`.

## 7. Features to preserve

- Multi-Kaggle-account / owner / env mapping (see §3). Why: the
  legacy YAML encodes 4 active configs per session (a/b/c/d in `h` and
  `m` variants), each routed to a different owner; the replacement
  cannot collapse this without breaking the established submission
  workflow. Evidence: `kkr.yaml:57–121`.
- `--dry-run` on every subcommand. Why: dry-run is the canonical
  smoke-test path; `_create_new_run` short-circuits at `kkr.py:1529`
  when `args.dry_run` is set.
- Stable JSON emission via `--json`. Why: downstream automation
  (`_emit_ok` at `kkr.py:332`) consumes shape; rename or reshape
  breaks any consumer.
- Local registry (`.kkr/registry/`). Why: replays, audit, and
  cross-day status queries depend on it; the platform should mirror
  this into the DB but keep a local copy for offline operation.
- Watch / status / fetch lifecycle. Why: Kaggle kernel runs are
  asynchronous and a successful submit can take minutes — polling
  must survive process restarts.
- `_deep_merge` semantics for `_base` + per-config (`kkr.py:421`).
  Why: list-union behaviour on `kernel_sources` / `model_sources`
  is relied on by every per-config block in `kkr.yaml`.

## 8. Features to deprecate

- The two `kaggle==1.8.3` patches flagged in `kkr.yaml:31, 38`. Why:
  the platform can pin a known-good `kaggle` version (or use the
  Kaggle Python API directly) and remove monkey-patching. Verify
  newer `kaggle` accepts `owner/model-slug` and `docker_image`
  fields natively before dropping.
- The `_exts` mechanism for run-extensions
  (`kkr.yaml:47` listing `kkr_simple`, `kkr_report`, `kkr_pycoll`;
  invoked at `kkr.py:122`). Why: bespoke per-run report shims have
  been superseded by the platform's `agent_reviews` + OTEL telemetry
  in M6; if any extension still has unique value, lift it into the
  platform as a tool, not a YAML knob.

## 9. Questions for `requirements-skeptic`

- Does the replacement expose an explicit `owner:` field, or does it
  inherit the `id: owner/slug` convention? Evidence: `kkr.yaml:7`,
  `kkr.py:466`.
- How does the replacement resolve credentials when multiple owners
  are active in one orchestration run? Evidence: `kkr.py:528–548`.
- Is `.env.{owner}` part of the public contract, or an implementation
  detail? Evidence: `kkr.py:541`.
- What happens to the `andreasbis/aimo-3-utils` kernel-source
  dependency if the replacement no longer supports cross-owner
  `kernel_sources`? Evidence: `kkr.yaml:61, 69`.
- Does the replacement preserve `--dry-run` semantics on every
  subcommand, or only on push/submit? Evidence: `kkr.py:1529, 1749`.

## 10. Parity tests

- `test_kkr_parity_push_dry_run` — invoke `push a09h --dry-run`,
  assert the plan JSON contains `owner=harrysun2006`,
  `slug=gpt-oss-120b-a09h`, and resolves `.env.harrysun2006` (or
  documented replacement). Fixture: a minimal `kkr.yaml`.
- `test_kkr_parity_owner_switch` — push `a09h` then `a09m`, assert
  the in-process credentials switched and that the second run did
  not inherit the first run's owner. Fixture: two-owner `kkr.yaml`.
- `test_kkr_parity_registry_roundtrip` — push, list, watch, fetch,
  assert one `RegistryEntry` per push with stable `run_id`.
- `test_kkr_parity_submit_message_cap` — supply a 600-char `_msg`,
  assert the replacement rejects with the same 500-char limit
  (`kkr.py:558`).
- `test_kkr_parity_dry_run_no_api_call` — patch the Kaggle API to
  raise on any call, assert dry-run completes without invoking it.

```

```markdown
# requirements-skeptic report for migrating tools/legacy/kkr.py into KCA

Source: tools/legacy/kkr.py @ 6231fd1f54b6, tools/legacy/kkr.yaml @ 0543e71a5aa1
Upstream: docs/evidence/m9_4-kkr-replay/legacy-archaeologist.md

_Produced under the M9.4 Discovery / Debate Gate (M9.4-T005). The agent
body lives in `.claude/agents/requirements-skeptic.md`; this artefact
is a manual execution of that agent's protocol against the proposed
KCA replacement of the legacy `kkr.py` flow._

## hidden_constraints

1. What is the maximum number of distinct Kaggle owners the replacement
   must support concurrently in one orchestration run? — consequence
   if unanswered: the replacement may pick a single-owner credential
   pattern (env vars set once at startup) and silently degrade the
   `harrysun2006` ↔ `firefly2006` dual-account workflow encoded in
   `kkr.yaml:57–121`.
2. Is `.env.{owner}` part of the public KCA contract, or an
   implementation detail the platform reserves the right to change? —
   consequence: if it's public, the KCA installer and onboarding docs
   need a documented `.env.<owner>` convention; if private, the
   platform owes users a migration path and a deprecation window.
3. Are `kaggle==1.8.3` monkey-patches (`kkr.yaml:31, 38`) still
   required against the version the platform pins, or are they
   superseded? — consequence: shipping the replacement without
   testing against the actually-pinned `kaggle` could silently break
   `model_sources` parsing or H100 `docker_image` overrides on first
   real push.
4. What is the maximum submission message length the replacement
   enforces? — consequence: legacy caps at 500 chars
   (`kkr.py:558`); a different cap downstream is a silent contract
   change.
5. Is the local registry (`.kkr/registry/`) the canonical state, or
   is the Supabase DB the canonical state with the local registry
   as a cache? — consequence: ambiguity here causes split-brain
   between offline-developed runs and platform-tracked runs.

## personas_and_accounts

1. The legacy tool encodes `harrysun2006` (`h` suffix) and
   `firefly2006` (`m` suffix) as distinct Kaggle owners and
   `andreasbis` as a kernel-source supplier (`kkr.yaml:7, 58, 66, 77,
   83, 90, 98, 108, 116, 61, 69`). Which of these survive in the
   replacement, with what role? — consequence: a single-owner
   replacement drops 50% of the live submission paths.
2. Does the replacement allow per-experiment owner override at the
   CLI, the way `--env <path>` overrides at `kkr.py:534–537`? —
   consequence: removing per-experiment override forces users to
   relaunch the platform between owner switches.
3. Are there additional Kaggle owners the user runs under not
   present in this committed `kkr.yaml`? — consequence: the
   archaeology may have under-counted because the YAML is committed
   but the actual `.env.*` files are gitignored.
4. Does the platform track which owner a given submission ran under
   in the `submissions` / `runs` table? — consequence: without an
   owner column the leaderboard-attribution audit trail breaks.
5. How does the platform reconcile a user being a GitHub identity, a
   Supabase user, AND a Kaggle owner — possibly with N:N mapping
   per project? — consequence: if the data model assumes 1:1, the
   multi-account case cannot be modelled at all.

## side_effects

1. Does the replacement preserve `--dry-run` on every subcommand, or
   only on push/submit? — consequence: dry-run gaps mean the smoke
   test path can't cover watch/fetch/status without hitting Kaggle.
2. The legacy `_load_env_for_owner` calls `load_dotenv(...,
   override=True)` at `kkr.py:543`, mutating `os.environ` in-process.
   Does the replacement isolate per-job credentials, or share the
   ambient environment? — consequence: shared env means one job can
   read the next job's secrets.
3. What reverses an accidental kernel push? — consequence: if the
   replacement does not surface a "delete-version" path,
   misconfigured pushes accumulate as draft versions Kaggle never
   garbage-collects.
4. What reverses an accidental competition submit? — consequence:
   Kaggle does not allow submission deletion; the platform must
   prevent rather than recover. Is the approval gate sufficient?
5. Where do `extracted_dirs` (`kkr.py:178`) land in the replacement?
   Inside the workspace, or in a platform-managed artifact store? —
   consequence: workspace bloat vs. unclear retention policy.

## edge_cases

1. What happens when a push starts under owner A and a credential
   switch happens mid-watch? — consequence: stale `KAGGLE_USERNAME`
   in the in-process env hits the wrong Kaggle account during
   status polling.
2. What happens if `_msg` formatting produces an empty string after
   trimming? — consequence: legacy raises at `_format_submit_message`
   only on >500 chars (`kkr.py:558`); empty `_msg` silently submits
   with `kkr@{ts}` default.
3. What happens if `kkr.yaml` has overlapping `kernel_sources`
   entries across `_base` and per-config? — consequence:
   `union_list` (`kkr.py:421`) deduplicates by simple equality;
   structured (dict) entries may not deduplicate as expected.
4. What happens during a partial registry write — process killed
   between `_save_manifest` and `_save_registry`? — consequence:
   orphaned manifest with no registry entry will not appear in
   `list`.
5. What happens if two concurrent `push` invocations allocate the
   same run id? — consequence: `_create_new_run` at `kkr.py:1511`
   uses `allocate=not args.dry_run` (`kkr.py:1523`); concurrent
   non-dry-run pushes may collide.

## rollback

1. If the replacement ships and a user wants to fall back to
   `tools/legacy/kkr.py`, is the legacy CLI still expected to work
   against the same `.kkr/registry/` directory? — consequence: if
   the registry schema is changed in flight, both tools see a
   broken registry.
2. Is the migration step idempotent? — consequence: re-running it
   after a partial failure should be safe.
3. Does the replacement write any state that the legacy CLI cannot
   ignore? — consequence: forward-incompatible additions silently
   poison rollback.
4. Is there an "export to legacy YAML" path for emergency rollback?
   — consequence: without it, the only fallback is the last commit
   of `kkr.yaml`, which loses any per-experiment edits made through
   the platform.
5. What is the rollback gate: a CLI command, a feature flag, a
   redeploy, or an out-of-band manual procedure? — consequence:
   ambiguity here means rollback during an incident is slow.

## explicit_unknowns

- Whether the `harrysun2006` / `firefly2006` owners are still active
  Kaggle accounts (cannot be inferred from the committed YAML
  alone — see memory `reference_supabase_db` for unrelated
  authoritative-config patterns).
- Whether `andreasbis/aimo-3-utils` is a permanently public Kaggle
  utility kernel or a moving target.
- Whether the H100 `docker_image` `gcr.io/kaggle-private-byod/...`
  (`kkr.yaml:39`) requires special Kaggle account whitelisting; the
  comment "可以 patch kaggle 1.8.3, 来使用 H100 GPU" hints at it but
  doesn't confirm.
- Whether the replacement is expected to support `submit_type:
  local` (CSV submit) AND `submit_type: notebook` (kernel push)
  through the same code path, or split per ADR-0009 / M10.
- Whether the platform's `kca kaggle push` (M10) is intended to
  *replace* `kkr.py push` or to *co-exist* with it during
  transition.
```

```markdown
# design-red-team report for the KCA replacement of `tools/legacy/kkr.py`

Source: tools/legacy/kkr.py @ 6231fd1f54b6, tools/legacy/kkr.yaml @ 0543e71a5aa1
Upstream archaeology: docs/evidence/m9_4-kkr-replay/legacy-archaeologist.md
Upstream skeptic:     docs/evidence/m9_4-kkr-replay/requirements-skeptic.md

_Produced under the M9.4 Discovery / Debate Gate (M9.4-T005). The
agent body lives in `.claude/agents/design-red-team.md`; this
artefact is a manual execution of that agent's protocol. The
"proposed design" being refuted is the current M9 / M10 trajectory
that absorbed `kkr.py`'s push/submit semantics into `tools/kca/kg.py`
(via `cmd_push`, `cmd_submit`) without an explicit multi-owner
contract._

## alternatives

1. **Owner-as-first-class field in `RunSpec`.** Introduce an explicit
   `owner: str` field on the platform's run/experiment record and on
   every CLI subcommand (`kca kaggle push --owner harrysun2006 ...`).
   Resolve credentials by looking up a Supabase-managed
   `kaggle_credentials` table keyed by `(project_id, owner)`. Sketch:
   the CLI passes `owner` through to a worker; the worker loads the
   matching credential set into a short-lived per-job environment
   (no `os.environ` mutation). Key tradeoff vs proposal: adds one
   schema column and one Supabase RLS path, but eliminates ambient
   credential state and makes "which owner pushed this kernel" a
   queryable fact rather than a log artefact. Closest legacy
   evidence: `kkr.py:528–548` (per-owner env), `kkr.py:520` (owner
   derived from `id`).

2. **Per-job dotenv subprocess isolation.** Keep the
   `.env.{owner}` convention from `kkr.py:541`, but run each
   Kaggle-touching subcommand in a fresh subprocess with only the
   selected dotenv loaded, instead of mutating the parent process's
   `os.environ` (`kkr.py:543`). Sketch: `kca` shells out to a small
   `kaggle-runner` subprocess; the parent never sees credential
   state. Key tradeoff vs proposal: zero schema change, lower risk
   of credential bleed between concurrent jobs, but adds
   per-subcommand fork overhead and makes long-running watch loops
   slightly harder to instrument with the platform's OTEL spans
   (`agent_telemetry_spans` from M6).

3. **Credential-scoped tool wrappers via the M7 permission policy.**
   Treat `kaggle_submit(owner)` and `kernel_push(owner)` as separate
   operations in `.kca/permissions/*.yaml` (M7 policy layer), each
   with its own `allow/ask/deny` resolution and its own audit row.
   Sketch: tools never directly read credentials; the permission
   layer materialises a short-lived credential token per call.
   Key tradeoff vs proposal: tightest audit story (every owner-scoped
   external write is a distinct permission decision), at the cost
   of expanding the M7 policy surface from one Kaggle-write operation
   to N (one per active owner) and requiring policy authors to
   enumerate owners in advance. Closest legacy evidence:
   `kkr.py:587–595` (single ambient `KaggleApi`).

## dropped_capabilities

- **Multi-account submission via suffix convention.** The legacy
  `kkr.yaml` runs four config families (a/b/c/d) each in `h` /
  `m` variants, routing to `harrysun2006` and `firefly2006`
  respectively. The current platform trajectory has no explicit
  owner field on its run record; absorbing `kkr.py push/submit`
  into `tools/kca/kg.py::cmd_push` without §3's owner-as-first-class
  field silently collapses this to a single owner. Evidence:
  `tools/legacy/kkr.yaml:57–121` (every per-config block declares
  its own `id: owner/slug`); `tools/legacy/kkr.py:520` (owner
  parsed from `id`); `tools/legacy/kkr.py:528–548` (owner-keyed
  env-file resolution). Survives in: alternative 1, alternative 2,
  alternative 3, legacy.
- **Per-experiment `--env <path>` override.** Legacy CLI allowed
  overriding the dotenv path on a single invocation
  (`tools/legacy/kkr.py:535–537`). The proposed `kca kaggle push`
  signature (per `docs/m10-loop-prompts.md` "What's in scope") does
  not expose a `--env` flag. Evidence: `tools/legacy/kkr.py:2165`.
  Survives in: alternative 2, legacy.
- **`kernel_sources` cross-owner reuse.** Legacy YAML can reference
  another owner's kernel (`andreasbis/aimo-3-utils`) as a build
  source. Evidence: `tools/legacy/kkr.yaml:61, 69`. Survives in:
  legacy, alternative 1 (with an explicit
  `cross_owner_kernel_sources` allow-list); not yet wired into
  alternative 3.
- **Stable JSON shape for `--json` output.** Legacy `_emit_ok` at
  `tools/legacy/kkr.py:332` and `_emit_fail` define a contract many
  ad-hoc scripts depend on. The platform's `kca kaggle push --json`
  emits a different shape (an `experiment_runs` row). Evidence:
  unavailable in the current branch — route to `open_disagreements`.

## long_term_costs

cognitive_load:    Without an explicit owner field, every new
                   contributor must read `_load_env_for_owner` to
                   understand that `kca kaggle push` silently picks a
                   credential from `os.environ` and that the
                   `.env.<owner>` filesystem schema is load-bearing.
                   Alternative 1 trades that for one schema column
                   and one CLI flag.
ops_burden:        Ambient-credential failures look like "the wrong
                   account submitted" — a 3am page that requires
                   reading audit logs to reconstruct. Alternative 2
                   reduces this to "subprocess exited 1"; alternative
                   3 surfaces it as a denied permission policy
                   resolution before any external write.
extensibility:     Next likely scope expansions: (a) a third Kaggle
                   account for a teammate, (b) per-owner Kaggle API
                   throttling (Kaggle's rate limits are per-owner,
                   not per-IP). The current trajectory needs a code
                   change to absorb (a); alternative 1 needs a row
                   insert. Neither (a) nor (b) is easy on the
                   current trajectory because owner is not modelled
                   at all.
blast_radius:     Worst case on the current trajectory: a job
                   intended for `firefly2006` pushes to
                   `harrysun2006` because the ambient env was set
                   by the previous job. That kernel push goes on
                   the wrong leaderboard, may consume the other
                   account's daily-submission quota, and the
                   `submissions` row has no field to record which
                   owner ran it. Alternatives 1 and 3 prevent this
                   structurally; alternative 2 prevents it via
                   subprocess isolation.

## open_disagreements

- The current M10 plan accepts the proposed
  `tools/kca/kg.py::cmd_push` without an explicit owner contract.
  Disagree — next step: open a follow-up issue
  (labels: `area:kaggle`, `type:feature`, `policy:approval-required`)
  to add an `owner` field on `runs` / `experiment_runs` and a
  `--owner` flag on `kca kaggle push` / `kca kaggle submit` before
  the next live kernel-push milestone after M10.
- The `--env <path>` override is not in the M10 scope. Disagree —
  next step: ask human whether `.env.<owner>` is the public
  contract (in which case `--env <path>` is the documented escape
  hatch) or an implementation detail (in which case the platform
  owes a migration to a credentials table).
- The `_msg` 500-char cap and the `{ts}` template are not
  re-documented in the M10 spec. Disagree — next step: spike a
  parity test (`tests/test_kkr_submit_message_cap`) that exercises
  the cap against `tools/kca/kg.py::cmd_submit` before M11.
- The legacy `_emit_ok` / `_emit_fail` JSON shape may have
  consumers outside this repo. Disagree — next step: research the
  JSON-shape contract (grep for `kkr_push.json`, `kkr_watch.json`
  filename literals in any sister repo); defer to a follow-up
  issue if a real consumer is found.
- The `kaggle==1.8.3` monkey-patch dependency is hidden tribal
  knowledge. Disagree — next step: write a smoke test against the
  pinned `kaggle` version (in `tests/test_kaggle_version_smoke.py`)
  that asserts `owner/model-slug` parsing and `docker_image`
  field acceptance work without patches; if it fails, the
  knowledge becomes a test failure rather than a silent push
  failure.

```

            self.timeout_s = int(os.environ.get("KCA_REVIEWER_TIMEOUT_S", timeout_s))
        except ValueError:
            self.timeout_s = timeout_s
        self.dry_run = dry_run
        self.dry_verdict = dry_verdict
        self.dry_rationale = dry_rationale

    def review_dry_run(self) -> ReviewVerdict:
        return ReviewVerdict(
            verdict=self.dry_verdict,
            rationale=self.dry_rationale,
            evidence={"mode": "dry_run"},
            cost_usd=0.0,
            reviewer_model=self.model,
        )

    def review(self, req: ReviewRequest) -> ReviewVerdict:
        if self.dry_run:
            return self.review_dry_run()
        return self._review_live(req)

    def _review_live(self, req: ReviewRequest) -> ReviewVerdict:
        user_prompt = _render_prompt(req)
        messages = [
            {"role": "system", "content": _REVIEWER_SYSTEM_PROMPT},
            {"role": "user", "content": user_prompt},
        ]
        started = time.monotonic()
        try:
            import litellm  # noqa: F401  (lazy import; only required when live)

            response = litellm.completion(
                model=self.model,
                messages=messages,
                max_tokens=self.max_tokens,
                temperature=0.0,
                timeout=self.timeout_s,
            )
        except Exception as exc:
            return ReviewVerdict(
                verdict="abstain",
                rationale=f"reviewer model error: {exc}",
                evidence={"error": str(exc), "duration_s": time.monotonic() - started},
                cost_usd=0.0,
                reviewer_model=self.model,
            )
        msg = response.choices[0].message
        text = (msg.content or "").strip()
        # Strip code fences if any.
        if text.startswith("```"):
            text = text.strip("`")
            text = text.split("\n", 1)[1] if "\n" in text else text
            text = text.rstrip("`")
        verdict = "abstain"
        rationale = text
        evidence: dict[str, Any] = {}
        try:
            parsed = json.loads(text)
            v = str(parsed.get("verdict", "")).lower().strip()
            if v in {"approve", "reject", "abstain"}:
                verdict = v
            rationale = str(parsed.get("rationale", "") or rationale)
            ev = parsed.get("evidence")
            if isinstance(ev, dict):
                evidence = ev
        except Exception as exc:
            evidence = {"parse_error": str(exc), "raw": text[:500]}
        usage = getattr(response, "usage", None)
        cost_usd = 0.0
        if usage is not None:
            cost_usd = float(getattr(usage, "total_cost", 0.0) or 0.0)
        return ReviewVerdict(
            verdict=verdict,
            rationale=rationale,
            evidence=evidence,
            cost_usd=cost_usd,
            reviewer_model=self.model,
        )

```markdown
## M11: authorized CTF/lab workflow

_Renumbered from old M10 on 2026-05-24 to make room for the
notebook-submission regression milestone (new M10)._

Goal: support CTF-style challenges only inside explicit authorization boundaries.

Planned capabilities:

- Challenge scope and authorization metadata.
- Local container/lab-only execution.
- Solver script generation and testing.
- Writeup generation.
- Hard policy blocks for external scanning, real targets, credential theft, persistence, or unsafe actions.

Exit criteria:

- CTF workflow is useful for local/sandbox labs and safely refuses out-of-scope activity.

## M12: Devpost / hackathon workflow

_Renumbered from old M11 on 2026-05-24. Planning landed 2026-05-26 —
`docs/m12-loop-prompts.md` + ten `docs/tasks/M12-T00x-*.md` specs._

Goal: validate the full platform loop with a real Devpost-style
**hackathon submission** end-to-end, and in doing so generalize the
competition-policy layer beyond Kaggle so M11 (CTF) and future
platforms can reuse it. M9 validated the **CSV-submission** path on
Spaceship Titanic; M10 validates the **notebook / kernel-push** path on
Petals to the Metal; M12 validates the **hackathon-submission** path on
a hackathon picked in M12-T000 under human approval.

The `arch:` task in this milestone is **M12-T001**: a Discovery /
Debate Gate run (`docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` §7) that produces
ADR-0016 defining the generalized `competition_type` enum and
team-scoped policy resolver. CTF-friendly enum values (`ctf`) ship in
M12 so M11 can plug in without a second schema migration.

### M12 task sequence

| Task | Description | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| M12-T000 | Survey 2–3 candidate Devpost / hackathon events; human picks target slug. READ_ONLY; no DB writes. | — |
| M12-T001 | `arch:` Discovery / Debate Gate on competition-policy generalization; ADR-0016 (`competition_type` enum, team-scoped resolver). | T000 |
| M12-T002 | Migration `0008_m12_competition_type_teams.sql` — `competitions.competition_type` enum (default `kaggle`), `teams`, `team_memberships`, `competitions.deadline`, `competitions.submission_format`. Policy resolver refactor. Backwards-compatible. | T001 |
| M12-T003 | `tools/kca/devpost.py` + `kca devpost register/fetch/info` (READ_ONLY). Lightweight HTTP first; Playwright fallback per `tools/kca/research_fetch.py` pattern. | T002 |
| M12-T004 | `.kca/skills/hackathon-experiment-loop/SKILL.md` + `.kca/permissions/hackathon-runner.yaml` + `submission_checklist` tool. | T002, T003 |
| M12-T005 | UI: `ui/src/pages/HackathonDeadline.tsx` + `ui/src/pages/SubmissionChecklist.tsx`; routes; vitest + Playwright smoke. Reuse `ApprovalInbox` / `DecisionGate`. | T002 |
| M12-T006 | Worker runs `hackathon-experiment-loop` end-to-end locally; produces `runs/<slug>/<run_id>/submission_pack/` (README, demo plan, source link). No external write. | T003, T004 |
| M12-T007 | Reviewer gate fires for `devpost_submit`; human approves via `kca decisions approve`; **ONE** real Devpost submission; record row in `submissions` (platform=`devpost`). | T006 |
| M12-T008 | `tests/test_m12_e2e.py` (dry-run, no creds) + `tests/test_m12_smoke.py` (DB-gated). Mirror M9 / M10 patterns. | T002–T007 |
| M12-T009 | Exit criteria validation + `docs/m12-final-review.md` + PROJECT_STATE / README / milestones updates + handoff + `worktree-milestone-pr`. | all |

Planned capabilities:

- **Generalized competition-policy layer** (ADR-0016): `competition_type`
  enum (`kaggle`, `devpost`, `hackathon_devpost`, `ctf`, `generic`);
  policy resolver routes on type; M11 reuses the schema.
- **Minimal team model**: `teams` + `team_memberships` tables; idea
  board / submission scope by team. No invite / role flow in M12.
- **Hackathon rules and deadline tracking**: `competitions.deadline`
  + `competitions.submission_format` (jsonb); UI deadline countdown.
- **Idea / discussion board** reusing `research_items`; no new table.
- **App prototype workflows** as a hackathon-flavoured skill;
  produces a structured submission pack.
- **Submission checklist + approval gates**: templated checklist
  page in UI; new `devpost_submit` reviewer gate.
- **Real Devpost submission** under explicit human approval — one
  per milestone, mirroring M9 `kaggle_submit` discipline.

Regression target: hackathon slug picked in M12-T000 from a candidate
list of 2–3 Devpost events. Human selects via comment on the closing
GitHub issue before T001 begins. The picked slug is recorded in
`docs/evidence/m12/t000-candidates.md` and referenced from every
later task closeout.

Exit criteria — proposed (final list in `docs/m12-loop-prompts.md`):

- Candidate hackathon picked; entry registered in `competitions` with
  `competition_type='devpost'` (or `hackathon_devpost`).
- ADR-0016 merged; the three Discovery / Debate Gate reports under
  `docs/evidence/m12/t001/discovery/` carry their canonical
  acceptance lines verbatim.
- Migration `0008_m12_competition_type_teams.sql` applied; all
  existing Kaggle competitions still resolve their policy correctly
  (`competition_type` defaults to `kaggle`).
- `kca devpost fetch --slug <picked>` returns metadata; no submit /
  upload / write action runs in T003.
- `hackathon-experiment-loop` skill runs locally and produces a
  submission pack at `runs/<slug>/<run_id>/submission_pack/`.
- Reviewer gate fires for `devpost_submit`; human approves; exactly
  ONE real Devpost submission lands; `submissions` row written with
  `platform='devpost'` + external submission URL.
- `tests/test_m12_e2e.py` passes in CI without credentials; the
  Devpost adapter refuses to submit without env vars present.
- `docs/m12-final-review.md` PASS, mirroring the M9 / M10 layout.

Out-of-scope follow-ups (file as issues if surfaced):

- Hook-level enforcement of the Discovery / Debate Gate (deferred from M9.4).
- Full team-invite / role-based permission flow.
- Other hackathon platforms (HackerEarth, MLH, Devfolio).
- Auto-generated demo video / readme from agent run logs.
```
