```python
def ensure_default_project(conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None) -> str:
    """Return the bootstrap project id; create the row if absent.

    The row is normally inserted by migration 0002. This is a defensive
    no-op upsert so kca works against a DB that was partially migrated.
    """
    return _with_conn(conn, _ensure_default_project)


def _ensure_default_project(conn: "psycopg.Connection") -> str:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            """
            insert into projects (id, name, kind, description)
            values (%s::uuid, 'local-default', 'general',
                    'Default project for local kca calls.')
            on conflict (id) do nothing
            """,
            (DEFAULT_PROJECT_ID,),
        )
    conn.commit()
    return DEFAULT_PROJECT_ID


def ensure_competition(
    slug: str,
    platform: str = "kaggle",
    title: str | None = None,
    project_id: str | None = None,
    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
) -> str:
    """Upsert a competitions row keyed by (platform, slug). Return its id (uuid str)."""
    project_id = project_id or DEFAULT_PROJECT_ID
    return _with_conn(conn, _ensure_competition, slug, platform, title, project_id)


def _ensure_competition(
    conn: "psycopg.Connection",
    slug: str,
    platform: str,
    title: str | None,
    project_id: str,
) -> str:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            """
            insert into competitions (project_id, platform, slug, title)
            values (%s::uuid, %s, %s, %s)
            on conflict (platform, slug) do update
              set title = coalesce(excluded.title, competitions.title)
            returning id::text
            """,
            (project_id, platform, slug, title),
        )
        row = cur.fetchone()
    conn.commit()
    assert row is not None
    return row["id"]

def create_experiment_run(
    experiment_id: str,
    external_run_id: str,
    run_dir: str,
    command: str | None = None,
    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
) -> str:
    """Create an experiment_runs row. Return its id (uuid str)."""
    return _with_conn(
        conn, _create_experiment_run, experiment_id, external_run_id, run_dir, command
    )


def _create_experiment_run(
    conn: "psycopg.Connection",
    experiment_id: str,
    external_run_id: str,
    run_dir: str,
    command: str | None,
) -> str:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            """
            insert into experiment_runs
              (experiment_id, external_run_id, run_dir, command, run_number)
            values (
              %s::uuid, %s, %s, %s,
              coalesce((select max(run_number) + 1 from experiment_runs where experiment_id = %s::uuid), 1)
            )
            returning id::text
            """,
            (experiment_id, external_run_id, run_dir, command, experiment_id),
        )
        row = cur.fetchone()
    conn.commit()
    assert row is not None
    return row["id"]


def record_metric_m2(
    experiment_run_id: str,
    key: str,
    value: float,
    metadata: dict | None = None,
    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
) -> dict:
    """M2: insert into experiment_run_metrics event table + jsonb snapshot."""
    metadata = metadata or {}
    return _with_conn(
        conn, _record_metric_m2, experiment_run_id, key, float(value), metadata
    )


def _record_metric_m2(
    conn: "psycopg.Connection",
    experiment_run_id: str,
    key: str,
    value: float,
    metadata: dict,
) -> dict:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            """
            insert into experiment_run_metrics
              (experiment_run_id, key, value, metadata)
            values (%s::uuid, %s, %s, %s::jsonb)
            returning id, key, value, recorded_at
            """,
            (experiment_run_id, key, value, json.dumps(metadata)),
        )
        event = cur.fetchone()
        # Update the denormalized snapshot. Cast text/numeric explicitly so
        # Postgres can resolve jsonb_build_object's variadic "any" overload.
        cur.execute(
            """
            update experiment_runs
              set metrics = coalesce(metrics, '{}'::jsonb) ||
                            jsonb_build_object(
                              %s::text,
                              jsonb_build_object('value', %s::numeric, 'recorded_at', now())
                            )
              where id = %s::uuid
            """,
            (key, value, experiment_run_id),
        )
    conn.commit()
    assert event is not None
    return dict(event)


def list_runs_m2(
    competition_slug: str | None = None,
    limit: int = 100,
    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
) -> list[dict]:
    """M2: join experiments + experiment_runs filtered by run_dir prefix."""
    return _with_conn(conn, _list_runs_m2, competition_slug, limit)


def _list_runs_m2(
    conn: "psycopg.Connection",
    competition_slug: str | None,
    limit: int,
) -> list[dict]:
    # Note: competitions is not directly linked to experiments yet; for M2 we
    # filter via run_dir prefix (runs/<slug>/...) until a join column is added.
    query = """
        select
          er.id::text          as experiment_run_id,
          er.external_run_id   as run_id,
          er.run_dir,
          er.metrics,
          er.created_at,
          e.id::text           as experiment_id,
          e.name               as experiment_name,
          e.hypothesis,
          e.tags
        from experiment_runs er
        join experiments e on e.id = er.experiment_id
        {where}
        order by er.created_at desc
        limit %s
    """
    params: list[Any] = []
    if competition_slug:
        query = query.format(where="where er.run_dir like %s")
        params.append(f"runs/{competition_slug}/%")
    else:
        query = query.format(where="")
    params.append(limit)
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(query, params)
        rows = cur.fetchall()
    return [dict(r) for r in rows]


def find_run_by_dir(
    run_dir: str,
    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
) -> dict | None:
    """Look up an experiment_run by its run_dir path. Return the row or None."""
    return _with_conn(conn, _find_run_by_dir, run_dir)


def _find_run_by_dir(conn: "psycopg.Connection", run_dir: str) -> dict | None:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            """
            select
              er.id::text         as experiment_run_id,
              er.external_run_id  as run_id,
              er.run_dir,
              e.id::text          as experiment_id
            from experiment_runs er
            join experiments e on e.id = er.experiment_id
            where er.run_dir = %s
            order by er.created_at desc
            limit 1
            """,
            (run_dir,),
        )
        row = cur.fetchone()
    return dict(row) if row else None

def create_job(
    project_id: str,
    prompt: str,
    policy: dict,
    model: str = "claude-sonnet-4-6",
    competition_slug: str | None = None,
    session_id: str | None = None,
    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
) -> str:
    """Insert a new queued agent_jobs row. Returns job_id (uuid str)."""
    return _with_conn(
        conn,
        _create_job,
        project_id,
        prompt,
        policy,
        model,
        competition_slug,
        session_id,
    )


def _create_job(
    conn: "psycopg.Connection",
    project_id: str,
    prompt: str,
    policy: dict,
    model: str,
    competition_slug: str | None,
    session_id: str | None,
) -> str:
    competition_id = None
    if competition_slug:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                "SELECT id::text FROM competitions WHERE slug = %s LIMIT 1",
                (competition_slug,),
            )
            row = cur.fetchone()
            if row:
                competition_id = row["id"]
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            """
            INSERT INTO agent_jobs
              (project_id, session_id, competition_id, status, payload,
               prompt, model, policy)
            VALUES
              (%s::uuid, %s::uuid, %s::uuid, 'queued', %s::jsonb,
               %s, %s, %s::jsonb)
            RETURNING id::text
            """,
            (
                project_id,
                session_id,
                competition_id,
                json.dumps(policy),
                prompt,
                model,
                json.dumps(policy),
            ),
        )
        row = cur.fetchone()
    conn.commit()
    assert row is not None
    return row["id"]


def get_job(job_id: str, conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None) -> dict:
    """Fetch one agent_jobs row as a dict. Raises KeyError if not found."""
    return _with_conn(conn, _get_job, job_id)


def _get_job(conn: "psycopg.Connection", job_id: str) -> dict:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM agent_jobs WHERE id = %s::uuid",
            (job_id,),
        )
        row = cur.fetchone()
    if row is None:
        raise KeyError(f"agent_jobs row not found: {job_id}")
    return dict(row)


def lease_job(
    job_id: str,
    worker_id: str,
    lease_seconds: int = 300,
    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
) -> bool:
    """Atomically set status='running', leased_by, leased_until.

    Returns True if successfully leased, False if already running/leased.
    """
    return _with_conn(conn, _lease_job, job_id, worker_id, lease_seconds)


def _lease_job(
    conn: "psycopg.Connection",
    job_id: str,
    worker_id: str,
    lease_seconds: int,
) -> bool:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            """
            UPDATE agent_jobs
               SET status = 'running',
                   leased_by = %s,
                   leased_until = now() + (%s || ' seconds')::interval,
                   started_at = COALESCE(started_at, now())
             WHERE id = %s::uuid
               AND status IN ('queued', 'paused')
            """,
            (worker_id, str(lease_seconds), job_id),
        )
        updated = cur.rowcount
    conn.commit()
    return updated > 0


def update_job(
    job_id: str,
    *,
    status: str | None = None,
    workspace_path: str | None = None,
    turns_used: int | None = None,
    cost_usd: float | None = None,
    error: str | None = None,
    started_at=None,
    finished_at=None,
    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
) -> None:
    """Partial update of agent_jobs columns. Only non-None kwargs are updated."""
    fields: list[str] = []
    params: list[Any] = []
    if status is not None:
        fields.append("status = %s::job_status")
        params.append(status)
    if workspace_path is not None:
        fields.append("workspace_path = %s")
        params.append(workspace_path)
    if turns_used is not None:
        fields.append("turns_used = %s")
        params.append(turns_used)
    if cost_usd is not None:
        fields.append("cost_usd = %s")
        params.append(cost_usd)
    if error is not None:
        fields.append("error = %s")
        params.append(error)
    if started_at is not None:
        fields.append("started_at = %s")
        params.append(started_at)
    if finished_at is not None:
        fields.append("finished_at = %s")
        params.append(finished_at)
    if not fields:
        return
    _with_conn(conn, _update_job, job_id, fields, params)


def _update_job(
    conn: "psycopg.Connection",
    job_id: str,
    fields: list[str],
    params: list[Any],
) -> None:
    set_clause = ", ".join(fields)
    params.append(job_id)
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            f"UPDATE agent_jobs SET {set_clause} WHERE id = %s::uuid",
            params,
        )
    conn.commit()

def _list_jobs(
    conn: "psycopg.Connection",

def _get_competition_by_slug(conn: "psycopg.Connection", slug: str) -> dict:

def update_competition(

    local_clone_path: str | None = None,
    competition_policy: dict | None = None,
    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
) -> None:
    """Partial update of competitions columns. Only non-None kwargs are set."""
    fields: list[str] = []
    params: list[Any] = []
    if repo_url is not None:
        fields.append("repo_url = %s")
        params.append(repo_url)
    if default_branch is not None:
        fields.append("default_branch = %s")
        params.append(default_branch)
    if local_clone_path is not None:
        fields.append("local_clone_path = %s")
        params.append(local_clone_path)
    if competition_policy is not None:
        fields.append("competition_policy = %s::jsonb")
        params.append(json.dumps(competition_policy))
    if not fields:
        return
    _with_conn(conn, _update_competition, competition_id, fields, params)


def _update_competition(
    conn: "psycopg.Connection",
    competition_id: str,
    fields: list[str],
    params: list[Any],
) -> None:

    params.append(competition_id)

        )

def create_experiment(
    competition_id: str,
    hypothesis: str,
    *,
    job_id: str | None = None,
    branch: str | None = None,
    config: dict | None = None,
    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
) -> str:
    """Insert an experiments row (M4 schema). Returns experiment_id."""
    return _with_conn(
        conn,
        _create_experiment_m4,
        competition_id,
        hypothesis,
        job_id,
        branch,
        config or {},
    )


def _create_experiment_m4(
    conn: "psycopg.Connection",
    competition_id: str,
    hypothesis: str,
    job_id: str | None,
    branch: str | None,
    config: dict,
) -> str:
    # The M1 experiments table requires project_id + name; the M4 INSERT must
    # populate them as well so both schema shapes coexist on the same row.
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            "SELECT project_id::text FROM competitions WHERE id = %s::uuid",
            (competition_id,),
        )
        comp_row = cur.fetchone()
        project_id = (comp_row or {}).get("project_id") or DEFAULT_PROJECT_ID
        synth_name = (branch or hypothesis or "m4-experiment")[:120]
        cur.execute(
            """
            INSERT INTO experiments
              (project_id, name, competition_id, job_id, hypothesis, branch, config)
            VALUES
              (%s::uuid, %s, %s::uuid, %s::uuid, %s, %s, %s::jsonb)
            RETURNING id::text
            """,
            (
                project_id,
                synth_name,
                competition_id,
                job_id,
                hypothesis,
                branch,
                json.dumps(config),
            ),
        )
        row = cur.fetchone()
    conn.commit()
    assert row is not None
    return row["id"]


def get_experiment(
    experiment_id: str,

) -> dict:

        raise KeyError(f"experiment not found: {experiment_id}")

def _create_run_m4(

) -> str:

            INSERT INTO experiment_runs
              (experiment_id, job_id, run_dir, command, status, started_at)
            VALUES
              (%s::uuid, %s::uuid, %s, %s, 'running', now())

def update_run(
    run_id: str,
    *,
    status: str | None = None,
    metrics: dict | None = None,
    artifact_paths: list | None = None,
    analysis: str | None = None,
    finished_at=None,
    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
) -> None:
    """Partial update of experiment_runs (M4 schema)."""
    fields: list[str] = []
    params: list[Any] = []
    if status is not None:
        fields.append("status = %s")
        params.append(status)
    if metrics is not None:
        fields.append("metrics = %s::jsonb")
        params.append(json.dumps(metrics))
    if artifact_paths is not None:
        fields.append("artifact_paths = %s::jsonb")
        params.append(json.dumps(artifact_paths))
    if analysis is not None:
        fields.append("analysis = %s")
        params.append(analysis)
    if finished_at is not None:
        fields.append("finished_at = %s")
        params.append(finished_at)
    if not fields:
        return
    _with_conn(conn, _update_run_m4, run_id, fields, params)


def _update_run_m4(
    conn: "psycopg.Connection",
    run_id: str,
    fields: list[str],
    params: list[Any],
) -> None:
    set_clause = ", ".join(fields)
    params.append(run_id)
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            f"UPDATE experiment_runs SET {set_clause} WHERE id = %s::uuid",
            params,
        )
    conn.commit()


def record_metric(
    run_id: str,
    key: str,
    value: float,
    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
) -> None:
    """Merge {key: value} into experiment_runs.metrics (M4: single jsonb UPDATE)."""
    _with_conn(conn, _record_metric_m4, run_id, key, float(value))


def _record_metric_m4(
    conn: "psycopg.Connection",
    run_id: str,
    key: str,
    value: float,
) -> None:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            """
            UPDATE experiment_runs
               SET metrics = coalesce(metrics, '{}'::jsonb)
                             || jsonb_build_object(%s::text, %s::float)
             WHERE id = %s::uuid
            """,
            (key, value, run_id),
        )
    conn.commit()


def list_runs(
    experiment_id: str | None = None,
    competition_id: str | None = None,
    limit: int = 20,
    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
) -> list[dict]:
    """List experiment_runs (M4). Filter by experiment_id or competition_id."""
    return _with_conn(conn, _list_runs_m4, experiment_id, competition_id, limit)


def _list_runs_m4(
    conn: "psycopg.Connection",
    experiment_id: str | None,
    competition_id: str | None,
    limit: int,
) -> list[dict]:
    if experiment_id is not None:
        query = (
            "SELECT * FROM experiment_runs WHERE experiment_id = %s::uuid "
            "ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT %s"
        )
        params: list[Any] = [experiment_id, limit]
    elif competition_id is not None:
        query = (
            "SELECT er.* FROM experiment_runs er "
            "JOIN experiments e ON e.id = er.experiment_id "
            "WHERE e.competition_id = %s::uuid "
            "ORDER BY er.created_at DESC LIMIT %s"
        )
        params = [competition_id, limit]
    else:
        query = "SELECT * FROM experiment_runs ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT %s"
        params = [limit]
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(query, params)
        rows = cur.fetchall()
    return [dict(r) for r in rows]

    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
) -> str:
    """Insert a row into agent_reviews. Returns the new review id."""
    if verdict not in _VALID_VERDICTS:
        raise ValueError(
            f"verdict must be one of {sorted(_VALID_VERDICTS)}, got {verdict!r}"
        )
    return _with_conn(
        conn,
        _create_review,
        job_id,
        reviewer_model,
        verdict,
        reviewer_kind,
        target_op,
        rationale,
        evidence or {},
        run_id,
        float(cost_usd),
        decision_id,
        otel_span_id,
    )


def _create_review(
    conn: "psycopg.Connection",
    job_id: str,
    reviewer_model: str,
    verdict: str,
    reviewer_kind: str,
    target_op: str | None,
    rationale: str | None,
    evidence: dict,
    run_id: str | None,
    cost_usd: float,
    decision_id: str | None,
    otel_span_id: str | None,
) -> str:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            """
            INSERT INTO agent_reviews
              (job_id, run_id, reviewer_model, reviewer_kind, target_op,
               verdict, rationale, evidence, cost_usd, decision_id, otel_span_id)
            VALUES
              (%s::uuid, %s::uuid, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s::jsonb, %s, %s::uuid, %s)
            RETURNING id::text
            """,
            (
                job_id,
                run_id,
                reviewer_model,
                reviewer_kind,
                target_op,
                verdict,
                rationale,
                json.dumps(evidence),
                cost_usd,
                decision_id,
                otel_span_id,
            ),
        )
        row = cur.fetchone()
    conn.commit()
    assert row is not None
    return row["id"]


def get_review(
    review_id: str,
    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
) -> dict:
    """Fetch one agent_reviews row. Raises KeyError if not found."""
    return _with_conn(conn, _get_review, review_id)


def _get_review(conn: "psycopg.Connection", review_id: str) -> dict:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT * FROM agent_reviews WHERE id = %s::uuid", (review_id,))
        row = cur.fetchone()
    if row is None:
        raise KeyError(f"agent_reviews row not found: {review_id}")
    return dict(row)


def list_reviews(
    job_id: str | None = None,
    verdict: str | None = None,
    limit: int = 50,
    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
) -> list[dict]:

    return _with_conn(conn, _list_reviews, job_id, verdict, limit)


def _list_reviews(
    conn: "psycopg.Connection",
    job_id: str | None,
    verdict: str | None,
    limit: int,
) -> list[dict]:
    clauses: list[str] = []
    params: list[Any] = []
    if job_id is not None:
        clauses.append("job_id = %s::uuid")
        params.append(job_id)
    if verdict is not None:
        clauses.append("verdict = %s")
        params.append(verdict)
    where = ("WHERE " + " AND ".join(clauses)) if clauses else ""
    params.append(limit)
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            f"SELECT * FROM agent_reviews {where} ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT %s",
            params,
        )
        rows = cur.fetchall()
    return [dict(r) for r in rows]


def find_review_for_op(
    job_id: str,

) -> dict | None:

def _find_review_for_op(

) -> dict | None:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:

             ORDER BY created_at DESC
             LIMIT 1
            """,

        )
        row = cur.fetchone()
    return dict(row) if row else None


def record_span(
    *,

) -> int:

def insert_tool_audit(
    rec: dict,
    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
) -> int:
    """Insert one agent_tool_audit row from an audit record dict.

    Best-effort: if the DB is unreachable, returns -1 and prints a warning
    to stderr instead of raising. Caller is responsible for keeping the
    JSONL file backend in sync.

    Expected ``rec`` shape (matches ``AuditRecord.to_dict()``):
      timestamp, session_id, skill_name, tool_name, operation, decision,
      mode, policy_profile, audit_required, args_hash[, job_id, extra].

    Note: ``append_job_event(event_type="tool_audit", ...)`` is the M7-era
    audit path and is preserved for the offline-only mode. Prefer this
    function for new callers — it gives a typed table and indexes for
    operator queries.
    """
    try:
        return _with_conn(conn, _insert_tool_audit, rec)
    except Exception as exc:
        import sys

        sys.stderr.write(f"[insert_tool_audit warn] {exc}\n")
        return -1


def _insert_tool_audit(conn: "psycopg.Connection", rec: dict) -> int:
    extra = rec.get("extra") or {}
    job_id = rec.get("job_id")
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            """
            INSERT INTO agent_tool_audit
              (ts, session_id, job_id, skill_name, tool_name, operation,
               decision, mode, policy_profile, audit_required, args_hash, extra)
            VALUES
              (%s, %s::uuid, %s::uuid, %s, %s, %s,
               %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s::jsonb)
            RETURNING id
            """,
            (
                rec.get("timestamp"),
                rec.get("session_id"),
                job_id,
                rec.get("skill_name"),
                rec.get("tool_name"),
                rec.get("operation"),
                rec.get("decision"),
                rec.get("mode", "default"),
                rec.get("policy_profile", "default"),
                bool(rec.get("audit_required", False)),
                rec.get("args_hash", ""),
                json.dumps(extra),
            ),
        )
        row = cur.fetchone()
    conn.commit()
    assert row is not None
    return row["id"]


def _with_conn(conn, fn, *args, **kwargs):
    """Call fn(conn, *args) using the provided conn or a freshly opened one.

    When this function opens the connection, it also closes it.
    """
    if conn is not None:
        return fn(conn, *args, **kwargs)
    c = get_conn()
    try:
        return fn(c, *args, **kwargs)
    finally:
        c.close()
```

```python
"""kca research: record cited, trust-labeled web research items.

Subcommands:
  fetch  — pull a URL via http or playwright, store artifacts, insert row.
  add    — register a research_items row by URL (no fetch).
  list   — list research items, optionally by competition.
  show   — show one research item by id.
  cite   — link a research_item to a run/experiment/job with optional quote.

Untrusted-data principle: fetched bytes are saved verbatim and never
executed; we extract structural text only.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any
from urllib.parse import urlparse

from _types import EXIT_OK, EXIT_RUNTIME, SideEffect
from _util import REPO_ROOT


VALID_TRUSTS = {"official", "trusted_public", "community", "untrusted", "unknown"}


def _emit(payload: dict) -> int:
    print(json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, default=str))
    return EXIT_OK if payload.get("ok") else EXIT_RUNTIME


def _db_or_warn():
    """Return (db_module, warning_or_none). warning_or_none is set when DB
    connection info / driver isn't available; callers may still degrade."""
    try:
        import db as _db

        _db.get_conn().close()
        return _db, None
    except Exception as e:
        try:
            import db as _db

            return _db, f"db_unavailable: {type(e).__name__}: {e}"
        except Exception as e2:
            return None, f"db_import_failed: {e2}"


def _allowed_domains() -> list[str] | None:
    raw = os.environ.get("KCA_RESEARCH_ALLOW_DOMAINS")
    if not raw:
        return None
    return [d.strip().lower() for d in raw.split(",") if d.strip()]


def _domain_allowed(url: str) -> bool:
    allow = _allowed_domains()
    if allow is None:
        return False  # gate required by default
    host = (urlparse(url).hostname or "").lower()
    return any(host == d or host.endswith("." + d) for d in allow)


def _resolve_competition_id(slug: str | None):
    """Look up competition id by slug. Returns (id_or_none, warning_or_none)."""
    if not slug:
        return None, None
    try:
        import db as _db

        row = _db.get_competition_by_slug(slug)
        return row.get("id"), None
    except Exception as e:
        return None, f"competition_lookup_failed: {type(e).__name__}: {e}"
```

```python
"""M9 smoke tests — regression assertions for Spaceship Titanic.

This module is **assertion-only**. It does not retrain models, does not
re-submit to Kaggle, and does not write to the DB. It reads the metrics
recorded by:

  - M9-T002 (baseline LR, ``experiment_runs.external_run_id='baseline-lr'``)
  - M9-T005 (HGB + feature engineering, ``external_run_id='hgb-fe-v1'``)
  - M9-T004 (the single approved real Kaggle submission, recorded in
    ``submissions.public_score``; the submissions row's
    ``experiment_run_id`` FK points back to the baseline-lr run)

and asserts:

  - ``cv_lr >= 0.78``         (M9 sanity guard, see docs/milestones.md §M9)
  - ``cv_hgb >= 0.80``        (M9 sanity guard)
  - ``cv_hgb > cv_lr``        (HGB beat LR on the same CV split)
  - ``public_score IS NOT NULL`` for the M9-T004 submission row

Tests are DB-aware and SKIP cleanly when ``SUPABASE_DB_URL`` is unset OR
when the M9 seed rows (LR run, HGB run, M9-T004 submission) are absent —
so the no-DB CI job stays green, and the live-DB CI job (fresh postgres,
migrations only, no seed data) also stays green. They FAIL on a real
regression only when run against a DB that *does* hold M9 data.

Run with:
    python -m pytest tests/test_m9_smoke.py -v
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT))
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT / "tools" / "kca"))

requires_db = pytest.mark.skipif(
    not os.environ.get("SUPABASE_DB_URL"),
    reason="SUPABASE_DB_URL not set",
)

# M9 thresholds — these are sanity guards copied from docs/milestones.md §M9.
# They are deliberately well below the recorded values so a real regression
# (data leakage, broken CV split, mis-recorded metric) trips them, but
# routine variance from seed/version drift does not.
LR_CV_FLOOR = 0.78
HGB_CV_FLOOR = 0.80

# External run names (experiment_runs.external_run_id).
LR_RUN_NAME = "baseline-lr"
HGB_RUN_NAME = "hgb-fe-v1"

# The one real Kaggle submission from M9-T004, identified by its
# Kaggle-side submission id. Looking up by external_submission_id keeps
# the test stable across DB recreations.
M9_T004_EXTERNAL_SUBMISSION_ID = "52955657"


def _fetch_cv_accuracy(cur, external_run_id: str) -> float | None:
    """Return the recorded cv_accuracy for an experiment_runs row, or None.

    Reads ``metrics->'cv_accuracy'->>'value'`` which is the shape
    written by the M2 metrics path (see ``tools/kca/db.py::record_metric``).

    Returns None when no row exists for ``external_run_id`` so the caller
    can distinguish "no seed data" (fresh CI DB) from "regression".
    """
    cur.execute(
        """
        SELECT (metrics->'cv_accuracy'->>'value')::float AS cv_accuracy
        FROM experiment_runs
        WHERE external_run_id = %s
        ORDER BY created_at DESC
        LIMIT 1
        """,
        (external_run_id,),
    )
    row = cur.fetchone()
    if row is None:
        return None
    cv = row[0]
    assert cv is not None, (
        f"experiment_runs[{external_run_id!r}].metrics->'cv_accuracy'->>'value' is NULL"
    )
    return float(cv)


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def m9_metrics():
    """Read all four M9 regression metrics from the DB in one connection.

    Skips cleanly when any seed row (LR run, HGB run, M9-T004 submission)
    is missing — e.g. against the live-db CI job's fresh postgres, which
    has migrations applied but no recorded M9 data. The regression
    assertions only mean something when the seed data is present, so we
    don't want an empty DB to masquerade as a regression.
    """
    import psycopg

    with psycopg.connect(os.environ["SUPABASE_DB_URL"]) as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cv_lr = _fetch_cv_accuracy(cur, LR_RUN_NAME)
            cv_hgb = _fetch_cv_accuracy(cur, HGB_RUN_NAME)

            cur.execute(
                """
                SELECT id, public_score, experiment_run_id
                FROM submissions
                WHERE external_submission_id = %s
                """,
                (M9_T004_EXTERNAL_SUBMISSION_ID,),
            )
            sub = cur.fetchone()

    missing = []
    if cv_lr is None:
        missing.append(f"experiment_runs[{LR_RUN_NAME!r}]")
    if cv_hgb is None:
        missing.append(f"experiment_runs[{HGB_RUN_NAME!r}]")
    if sub is None:
        missing.append(f"submissions[{M9_T004_EXTERNAL_SUBMISSION_ID!r}]")
    if missing:
        pytest.skip(
            "M9 seed data not present in DB ("
            + ", ".join(missing)
            + "); regression assertions require a DB seeded by M9-T002/T004/T005"
        )

    return {
        "cv_lr": cv_lr,
        "cv_hgb": cv_hgb,
        "submission_id": sub[0],
        "public_score": sub[1],
        "submission_experiment_run_id": sub[2],
    }


@requires_db
def test_lr_cv_meets_floor(m9_metrics):
    cv = m9_metrics["cv_lr"]
    assert cv >= LR_CV_FLOOR, (
        f"LR baseline cv_accuracy={cv:.6f} fell below M9 floor {LR_CV_FLOOR}; "
        "do NOT lower the threshold — investigate the run first"
    )


@requires_db
def test_hgb_cv_meets_floor(m9_metrics):
    cv = m9_metrics["cv_hgb"]
    assert cv >= HGB_CV_FLOOR, (
        f"HGB+FE cv_accuracy={cv:.6f} fell below M9 floor {HGB_CV_FLOOR}; "
        "do NOT lower the threshold — investigate the run first"
    )


@requires_db
def test_hgb_beats_lr_on_cv(m9_metrics):
    cv_lr = m9_metrics["cv_lr"]
    cv_hgb = m9_metrics["cv_hgb"]
    assert cv_hgb > cv_lr, (
        f"HGB CV {cv_hgb:.6f} did NOT beat LR CV {cv_lr:.6f}; "
        "the second experiment is expected to improve over the baseline"
    )


@requires_db
def test_m9_t004_public_score_recorded(m9_metrics):
    score = m9_metrics["public_score"]
    assert score is not None, (
        f"submissions row for external_submission_id="
        f"{M9_T004_EXTERNAL_SUBMISSION_ID!r} has NULL public_score"
    )
    # Sanity: a Kaggle accuracy LB score sits in (0, 1].
    assert 0.0 < float(score) <= 1.0, (
        f"public_score={score!r} outside plausible range (0, 1]"
    )
```

```sql
-- 0004_m4_competition_repo.sql
-- M4: per-competition repo, experiment branches, runs, and submissions.
--
-- Forward-only. Idempotent. Additive — extends the M1/M2 tables in 0001 so
-- both the M2 (project_id+name) and M4 (competition_id+hypothesis) shapes
-- coexist. NOT NULL constraints are deferred for nullable additive columns
-- because existing rows would otherwise block ALTER.
--
-- No destructive drops.

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Part A: extend competitions with repo metadata + policy.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ALTER TABLE competitions
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS repo_url           text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS default_branch     text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'main',
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS local_clone_path   text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS competition_policy jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Part B: experiments (M4 columns layered on the M1/M2 table).
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS experiments (
  id              uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  competition_id  uuid REFERENCES competitions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  job_id          uuid REFERENCES agent_jobs(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  hypothesis      text,
  branch          text,
  config          jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  status          text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active',
  created_at      timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at      timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

ALTER TABLE experiments
```

````markdown
# ADR-0006: Configurable approval gates — default allow

Status: accepted  
Date: 2026-05-19  
Decided in: `docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-19-r1.md`  
Supersedes: prior implicit policy of "always require approval for remote writes"

---

## Context

Earlier platform design required human approval for all Kaggle submissions, kernel
pushes, and git pushes. This was chosen conservatively during M0–M2 setup.

The user's actual Kaggle workflow (see `docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-17-r1.md`) is
iterative and fast. Requiring manual approval on every submission adds friction
without meaningfully increasing safety for an experienced user who:
- Has already reviewed the code in the job's experiment run
- Understands the submission mechanics
- Wants the agent to handle routine mechanics autonomously

The main human decision points are **strategic** (switch model, switch approach,
ensemble), not operational (submit file X, push kernel Y).

## Decision

All approval gates are **configurable per project** and **default to allow (no approval required)**.

### Default policy

```json
{
  "approval_gates": {
    "kaggle_submit":    false,
    "kernel_push":      false,
    "dataset_upload":   true,
    "git_push":         false,
    "git_force_push":   true,
    "supabase_migrate": true,
    "delete_artifact":  true
````
</details>

```markdown
# ADR-0015: Memory-promotion model — canonical files and propose-only path

## Status

Accepted (M9.3, 2026-05-26).

## Context

Project decisions land in three places during day-to-day work: GitHub
issue / PR / review comments, meeting-notes markdown files under
`docs/meeting-notes/`, and Claude Code session activity. The
[`session-memory-and-audit.md`](../architecture/session-memory-and-audit.md)
design note describes the three-tier raw → curated → core memory model;
the [`github-as-agent-interface.md`](../architecture/github-as-agent-interface.md)
note explains why a comment is *evidence, not a decision*.

Until M9.3, the step that crosses from evidence to canonical memory was
ad-hoc — sometimes done by hand, sometimes silently skipped. We need:

- An explicit, narrow list of which files are **canonical memory** (the
  Tier 3 surface this ADR governs), so the promotion step has a clear
  target.
- A **propose-only** path so that promotion is a reviewable diff and
  not a quiet rewrite.
- A clear boundary between this canonical memory and the user's
  Claude Code auto-memory directory at `memory/`, so the two systems
  do not stomp on each other.

## Decision

### Canonical memory (four files / patterns)

The `memory-promotion` skill targets exactly these four:

1. `PROJECT_STATE.md` — current milestone, open decisions, completed
   milestones.
2. `docs/milestones.md` — milestone roster, scope, dependency order.
3. `docs/handoffs/m{N}-handoff.md` — per-milestone exit state.
4. `docs/adr/NNNN-*.md` — long-lived architectural decisions.

```

```sql
-- 0008_m11_ctf.sql
-- M11: authorized CTF / lab workflow — event / challenge / attempt schema.
--
-- Forward-only. Idempotent. Additive. All indexes use IF NOT EXISTS so the
-- migration is safe to re-apply.
--
-- Tables:
--   ctf_events        — top-level event identity (per-project, per-slug).
--   ctf_challenges    — jeopardy-style challenges within an event, optionally
--                       linked to a ctf_scopes (0001) authorization row.
--   ctf_attempts      — every flag-submit attempt, accepted or not.
--
-- The pre-existing ctf_scopes table from 0001_init.sql is left untouched.
-- Cross-link: see docs/adr/0016-ctf-data-model.md for the full design and
-- the M12 competition_type open question.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ctf_events (
  id                 uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  project_id         uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  slug               text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  name               text NOT NULL,
  ctftime_event_id   integer,
  event_url          text,
  start_at           timestamptz,
  end_at             timestamptz,
  scoring            text DEFAULT 'jeopardy',
  credentials_ref    text,  -- path hint, e.g. '~/.ctf/<slug>.json'; never the value
  notes              text,
  created_at         timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ctf_events_project
  ON ctf_events(project_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ctf_challenges (
  id                    uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  event_id              uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES ctf_events(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  scope_id              uuid REFERENCES ctf_scopes(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  slug                  text NOT NULL,
  name                  text NOT NULL,
  category              text NOT NULL CHECK (
    category IN ('web','crypto','rev','pwn','forensics','osint','misc')
  ),
  points                integer,
  description           text,
  expected_flag_format  text,
  attachments_path      text,
  remote_endpoint       text,
  created_at            timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE (event_id, slug)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ctf_challenges_event
  ON ctf_challenges(event_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ctf_challenges_scope
  ON ctf_challenges(scope_id) WHERE scope_id IS NOT NULL;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ctf_attempts (
  id                uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  challenge_id      uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES ctf_challenges(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  run_id            uuid REFERENCES experiment_runs(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  accepted          boolean,
  http_status       integer,
  flag_length       integer,  -- NEVER the flag value
  -- Multi-account / team identity columns (T000 design-red-team carry-over).
  -- The kkr.py M9.4 replay surfaced the "owner on the submission row" gap;
  -- recording which event credential actually hit the event prevents the
  -- same failure mode (wrong-team-id submission, mis-attributed accept).
  event_account     text,
  team_id           text,
  submitted_at      timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  response_excerpt  text  -- 256-char cap, redact any string that looks like a flag
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ctf_attempts_challenge
  ON ctf_attempts(challenge_id, submitted_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ctf_attempts_run
  ON ctf_attempts(run_id) WHERE run_id IS NOT NULL;

-- Enable RLS now; add real policies once auth/user model is finalized
-- (same posture as ctf_scopes in migration 0001).
ALTER TABLE ctf_events     ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE ctf_challenges ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE ctf_attempts   ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

```

```python
The canonical DB layer for kca is `tools/kca/db.py` (M2–M8). New milestone
schema modules may register their helpers here when the milestone task spec
calls for a package-style import path (e.g. M11-T001 → `src.db.ctf`).

Each submodule MUST import `tools/kca/db.py` (added to sys.path by callers)
to reuse the shared `get_conn()` + connection-management primitives so the
remote-write gate, autocommit posture, and dict_row factory stay aligned.
"""
```

```python
"""CTF DB helpers (M11-T001).

Thin wrappers around `tools/kca/db.get_conn()` for the M11 schema:
`ctf_events`, `ctf_challenges`, `ctf_attempts`. The pre-existing
`ctf_scopes` table from migration 0001 is treated as read-only here;
authoring scope rows belongs to `tools/kca/ctf.py` (M11-T003).

Side-effect classification:
  - All helpers are LOCAL_WRITE / LOCAL_READ. Remote-write gating
    happens at the underlying `tools/kca/db.get_conn()` layer.

Invariants enforced here (cross-link: docs/adr/0016-ctf-data-model.md):

  - The flag *value* is never accepted as a parameter and never persisted.
    `record_attempt` takes `flag_length` (int) only.
  - `response_excerpt` is truncated to 256 chars; callers are expected to
    pre-scrub anything matching `expected_flag_format`.
  - `credentials_ref` on events is a path hint (string), not a credential
    value; the helper rejects values that look like credentials.

Module is importable without a live DB — connection happens lazily inside
each helper (delegated to `tools.kca.db._with_conn`).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

# Make tools/kca/ importable for the shared `db` module + helpers. The
# downstream `tools/kca/db.py` adds repo-root to sys.path via dotenv, so
# we mirror its discovery path.
_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
_TOOLS_KCA = _REPO_ROOT / "tools" / "kca"
if str(_TOOLS_KCA) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(_TOOLS_KCA))

import db as _db  # noqa: E402  (path manipulation must precede import)

__all__ = [
    "register_event",
    "add_challenge",
    "set_scope_for_challenge",
    "record_attempt",
    "list_events",
    "get_challenge",
    "list_attempts",
    "VALID_CATEGORIES",
    "RESPONSE_EXCERPT_MAX_LEN",
]

VALID_CATEGORIES: tuple[str, ...] = (
    "web",
    "crypto",
    "rev",
    "pwn",
    "forensics",
    "osint",
    "misc",
)

RESPONSE_EXCERPT_MAX_LEN = 256

# Heuristic prefixes used to reject obvious credential-value leakage into
# `credentials_ref`. The intent is a path hint; we refuse anything that
# looks like a token, JSON blob, or env-var value pair.
_CREDENTIAL_VALUE_MARKERS = ("=", "{", '"token"', "Bearer ", "sk-", "eyJ")


def _validate_credentials_ref(ref: str | None) -> None:
    if ref is None:
        return
    if any(marker in ref for marker in _CREDENTIAL_VALUE_MARKERS):
        raise ValueError(
            "credentials_ref must be a path hint (e.g. '~/.ctf/<slug>.json'), "
            "never the credential value itself"
        )


def _truncate_excerpt(text: str | None) -> str | None:
    if text is None:
        return None
    if len(text) <= RESPONSE_EXCERPT_MAX_LEN:
        return text
    return text[: RESPONSE_EXCERPT_MAX_LEN - 1] + "…"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Events
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def register_event(
    project_id: str,
    slug: str,
    name: str,
    *,
    ctftime_event_id: int | None = None,
    event_url: str | None = None,
    start_at: Any = None,
    end_at: Any = None,
    scoring: str = "jeopardy",
    credentials_ref: str | None = None,
    notes: str | None = None,
    conn=None,
) -> str:
    """Insert a ctf_events row. Returns the new event id (uuid str).

    Idempotent on (project_id, slug): re-inserting the same slug returns
    the existing row's id. Other columns are NOT updated on conflict.
    """
    if not slug:
        raise ValueError("slug is required")
    if not name:
        raise ValueError("name is required")
    _validate_credentials_ref(credentials_ref)
    return _db._with_conn(
        conn,
        _register_event,
        project_id,
        slug,
        name,
        ctftime_event_id,
        event_url,
        start_at,
        end_at,
        scoring,
        credentials_ref,
        notes,
    )


def _register_event(
    conn,
    project_id: str,
    slug: str,
    name: str,
    ctftime_event_id: int | None,
    event_url: str | None,
    start_at: Any,
    end_at: Any,
    scoring: str,
    credentials_ref: str | None,
    notes: str | None,
) -> str:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            """
            INSERT INTO ctf_events
              (project_id, slug, name, ctftime_event_id, event_url,
               start_at, end_at, scoring, credentials_ref, notes)
            VALUES
              (%s::uuid, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s)
            ON CONFLICT (slug) DO UPDATE
              SET slug = EXCLUDED.slug
            RETURNING id::text
            """,
            (
                project_id,
                slug,
                name,
                ctftime_event_id,
                event_url,
                start_at,
                end_at,
                scoring,
                credentials_ref,
                notes,
            ),
        )
        row = cur.fetchone()
    conn.commit()
    assert row is not None
    return row["id"]


def list_events(
    project_id: str | None = None,
    limit: int = 100,
    conn=None,
) -> list[dict]:
    """List ctf_events rows newest first. Optional project_id filter."""
    return _db._with_conn(conn, _list_events, project_id, limit)


def _list_events(conn, project_id: str | None, limit: int) -> list[dict]:
    if project_id is not None:
        query = (
            "SELECT * FROM ctf_events WHERE project_id = %s::uuid "
            "ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT %s"
        )
        params: list[Any] = [project_id, limit]
    else:
        query = "SELECT * FROM ctf_events ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT %s"
        params = [limit]
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(query, params)
        rows = cur.fetchall()
    return [dict(r) for r in rows]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Challenges
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def add_challenge(
    event_id: str,
    slug: str,
    name: str,
    category: str,
    *,
    points: int | None = None,
    description: str | None = None,
    expected_flag_format: str | None = None,
    attachments_path: str | None = None,
    remote_endpoint: str | None = None,
    scope_id: str | None = None,
    conn=None,
) -> str:
    """Insert a ctf_challenges row. Returns the new challenge id (uuid str).

    Idempotent on (event_id, slug): re-inserting the same (event, slug)
    pair returns the existing row's id without modifying any column.
    """
    if not slug:
        raise ValueError("slug is required")
    if not name:
        raise ValueError("name is required")
    if category not in VALID_CATEGORIES:
        raise ValueError(
            f"category must be one of {VALID_CATEGORIES!r}, got {category!r}"
        )
    return _db._with_conn(
        conn,
        _add_challenge,
        event_id,
        slug,
        name,
        category,
        points,
        description,
        expected_flag_format,
        attachments_path,
        remote_endpoint,
        scope_id,
    )


def _add_challenge(
    conn,
    event_id: str,
    slug: str,
    name: str,
    category: str,
    points: int | None,
    description: str | None,
    expected_flag_format: str | None,
    attachments_path: str | None,
    remote_endpoint: str | None,
    scope_id: str | None,
) -> str:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            """
            INSERT INTO ctf_challenges
              (event_id, scope_id, slug, name, category, points,
               description, expected_flag_format, attachments_path,
               remote_endpoint)
            VALUES
              (%s::uuid, %s::uuid, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s)
            ON CONFLICT (event_id, slug) DO UPDATE
              SET slug = EXCLUDED.slug
            RETURNING id::text
            """,
            (
                event_id,
                scope_id,
                slug,
                name,
                category,
                points,
                description,
                expected_flag_format,
                attachments_path,
                remote_endpoint,
            ),
        )
        row = cur.fetchone()
    conn.commit()
    assert row is not None
    return row["id"]


def set_scope_for_challenge(
    challenge_id: str,
    scope_id: str | None,
    conn=None,
) -> None:
    """Set / clear the ctf_challenges.scope_id FK to ctf_scopes(id)."""
    _db._with_conn(conn, _set_scope_for_challenge, challenge_id, scope_id)


def _set_scope_for_challenge(
    conn,
    challenge_id: str,
    scope_id: str | None,
) -> None:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            """
            UPDATE ctf_challenges
               SET scope_id = %s::uuid
             WHERE id = %s::uuid
            """,
            (scope_id, challenge_id),
        )
    conn.commit()


def get_challenge(
    event_slug: str,
    challenge_slug: str,
    conn=None,
) -> dict | None:
    """Look up a single ctf_challenges row by (event_slug, challenge_slug).

    Returns the row dict (including the joined event_id), or None if no
    matching row exists.
    """
    return _db._with_conn(conn, _get_challenge, event_slug, challenge_slug)


def _get_challenge(conn, event_slug: str, challenge_slug: str) -> dict | None:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            """
            SELECT c.*
              FROM ctf_challenges c
              JOIN ctf_events e ON e.id = c.event_id
             WHERE e.slug = %s AND c.slug = %s
             LIMIT 1
            """,
            (event_slug, challenge_slug),
        )
        row = cur.fetchone()
    return dict(row) if row else None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Attempts
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def record_attempt(
    challenge_id: str,
    accepted: bool | None,
    http_status: int | None,
    flag_length: int | None,
    response_excerpt: str | None,
    *,
    run_id: str | None = None,
    event_account: str | None = None,
    team_id: str | None = None,
    conn=None,
) -> str:
    """Insert a ctf_attempts row. Returns the new attempt id (uuid str).

    `flag_length` records only the integer length — the flag value MUST
    never be persisted. `response_excerpt` is truncated to 256 chars.
    `event_account` and `team_id` record the credential identity that
    actually made the submission (multi-account safety; see ADR-0016 and
    the M9.4 kkr.py replay).

    Note on length-vs-identifier disclosure (per task spec invariant):
    the helper rejects passing `flag_length` together with a
    `response_excerpt` that already contains the literal phrase
    "flag length" — a pattern that would let an observer reconstruct
    the flag from row contents alone. Callers should pre-scrub the
    excerpt before invoking this helper.
    """
    if flag_length is not None and flag_length < 0:
        raise ValueError("flag_length must be non-negative")
    if (
        flag_length is not None
        and response_excerpt is not None
        and "flag length" in response_excerpt.lower()
    ):
        raise ValueError(
            "response_excerpt must not echo 'flag length' alongside the "
            "numeric flag_length column; scrub the excerpt first"
        )
    excerpt = _truncate_excerpt(response_excerpt)
    return _db._with_conn(
        conn,
        _record_attempt,
        challenge_id,
        accepted,
        http_status,
        flag_length,
        excerpt,
        run_id,
        event_account,
        team_id,
    )


def _record_attempt(
    conn,
    challenge_id: str,
    accepted: bool | None,
    http_status: int | None,
    flag_length: int | None,
    response_excerpt: str | None,
    run_id: str | None,
    event_account: str | None,
    team_id: str | None,
) -> str:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            """
            INSERT INTO ctf_attempts
              (challenge_id, run_id, accepted, http_status, flag_length,
               event_account, team_id, response_excerpt)
            VALUES
              (%s::uuid, %s::uuid, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s)
            RETURNING id::text
            """,
            (
                challenge_id,
                run_id,
                accepted,
                http_status,
                flag_length,
                event_account,
                team_id,
                response_excerpt,
            ),
        )
        row = cur.fetchone()
    conn.commit()
    assert row is not None
    return row["id"]


def list_attempts(
    challenge_id: str,
    limit: int = 50,
    conn=None,
) -> list[dict]:
    """List ctf_attempts for a challenge, newest first."""
    return _db._with_conn(conn, _list_attempts, challenge_id, limit)


def _list_attempts(conn, challenge_id: str, limit: int) -> list[dict]:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            """
            SELECT * FROM ctf_attempts
             WHERE challenge_id = %s::uuid
             ORDER BY submitted_at DESC
             LIMIT %s
            """,
            (challenge_id, limit),
        )
        rows = cur.fetchall()
    return [dict(r) for r in rows]
```

```python
"""M11-T001 smoke tests — CTF schema + DB helpers.

DB-gated. SKIP cleanly when ``SUPABASE_DB_URL`` is unset, mirroring the
``tests/test_m9_smoke.py`` posture so the no-DB CI job stays green.

Tests exercise:

  - register_event idempotency on (project_id, slug)
  - add_challenge insertion + category enum guard
  - record_attempt with multi-account (event_account / team_id) carry-over
  - get_challenge by (event_slug, challenge_slug)
  - list_events / list_attempts
  - response_excerpt truncation to 256 chars
  - flag-value invariant: helper rejects "flag length" leakage
  - credentials_ref rejects credential-value markers
  - FK cascade: deleting an event removes its challenges + attempts
  - unique-constraint violation on duplicate (event_id, slug)

Each test owns its rows and cleans up by deleting the parent event
(which cascades to challenges + attempts) so re-runs are safe and the
DB is left as-found.

Run with:
    SUPABASE_DB_URL=postgresql://postgres:postgres@172.22.0.2:5432/postgres \\
        python -m pytest tests/test_m11_db.py -v
"""

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent

@pytest.fixture
def cleanup_events():
    """Track event ids created in a test; delete them on teardown so
    re-runs are idempotent and other tests don't see leftover rows."""
    created: list[str] = []
    yield created
    if not created:
        return
    if not os.environ.get("SUPABASE_DB_URL"):

    import db as _kca_db

    with _kca_db.get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            for event_id in created:

def test_event_delete_cascades_to_challenges_and_attempts(project_id):
    """ON DELETE CASCADE: removing an event removes its challenges and
    (via the challenge cascade) its attempts."""
    import db as _kca_db
    from src.db import ctf

    slug = f"m11-casc-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}"
    event_id = ctf.register_event(project_id=project_id, slug=slug, name="evt")
    challenge_id = ctf.add_challenge(
        event_id=event_id,
        slug="web-1",
        name="casc-test",
        category="web",
    )
    ctf.record_attempt(
        challenge_id=challenge_id,
        accepted=False,
        http_status=400,
        flag_length=None,
        response_excerpt=None,
    )

    with _kca_db.get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute("DELETE FROM ctf_events WHERE id = %s::uuid", (event_id,))
        conn.commit()
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                "SELECT count(*)::int AS n FROM ctf_challenges WHERE id = %s::uuid",
                (challenge_id,),
            )
            assert cur.fetchone()["n"] == 0
            cur.execute(
                "SELECT count(*)::int AS n FROM ctf_attempts WHERE challenge_id = %s::uuid",
                (challenge_id,),
            )
            assert cur.fetchone()["n"] == 0
```

````markdown
# ADR-0016: CTF data model — events, challenges, attempts

## Status

Accepted (M11-T001, 2026-06-09). Lands with
`supabase/migrations/0008_m11_ctf.sql` and `src/db/ctf.py`.

Cross-link: [`docs/evidence/m11/discovery/design-red-team.md`](../evidence/m11/discovery/design-red-team.md),
[`docs/evidence/m11/discovery/legacy-archaeologist.md`](../evidence/m11/discovery/legacy-archaeologist.md),
[`docs/evidence/m11/discovery/requirements-skeptic.md`](../evidence/m11/discovery/requirements-skeptic.md).

## Context

M11 is the first non-Kaggle competition platform on the agent stack.
The CTFtime workflow (planning Q&A, `docs/m11-loop-prompts.md` §at-a-glance)
needs persistent, queryable records for three things:

1. **Events** — which CTFtime-listed event we are participating in, when
   it runs, and where the credentials for it live.
2. **Challenges** — per-event jeopardy items the agent might attempt,
   each optionally bound to a `ctf_scopes` (migration 0001) authorization
   row.
3. **Attempts** — every flag submission, accepted or not, with enough
   identity context that "which credential ran this" is answerable from
   the row alone.

The pre-existing `ctf_scopes` table from migration 0001 covers
authorization (target URLs, local-only flag, expiry). M11 adds the three
tables above; `ctf_scopes` is referenced via an FK from
`ctf_challenges.scope_id` but is otherwise untouched.

## Decision

### 1. Multi-event identity model

```
projects (0001)
  └─ ctf_events  (slug UNIQUE globally; per-project FK)
       └─ ctf_challenges  (UNIQUE (event_id, slug))
            └─ ctf_attempts  (FK to challenge; FK to experiment_runs.id)
```

- `ctf_events.slug` is **globally unique** so that
  `~/.ctf/<slug>.json` credential paths are unambiguous and so the
  `kca ctf event` subcommands can address events by slug alone (no
  `--project` flag for the common case).
- `(event_id, slug)` is unique on `ctf_challenges` so challenge slugs
  scope per-event — two events can both have `web-1`.
- `ctf_challenges.scope_id` is nullable and `ON DELETE SET NULL`: a
  challenge can pre-exist its authorization row (T004 creates
  challenges before T002 wires the full scope policy), and deleting a
  stale scope must not cascade-delete challenge history.
- `ctf_attempts.run_id` FK to `experiment_runs(id)` is nullable and
  `ON DELETE SET NULL` so attempts survive run cleanup.

### 2. `credentials_ref` is a path hint, not a value

`ctf_events.credentials_ref` is a `text` column intended to store a
path hint such as `~/.ctf/picoctf-2024.json` or an env-var prefix such
as `CTF_PICOCTF_2024_`. It **never** holds the credential value
itself.

The Python helper `register_event` validates the input and refuses any
string containing the heuristic markers
`= { "token" Bearer  sk- eyJ`, which catch the
common shapes of accidentally-pasted tokens, JSON blobs, env-var
key=value pairs, and JWTs. This is a defense-in-depth measure on top of:

- the hook-layer carve-out for `~/.ctf/*` reads
  (M11-T002 owns `.claude/hooks/guard_tool.py`),
- the M11-T008 audit-grep test (no `~/.ctf/*` content in any test run's
  stdout/stderr),
- and the dev-phase secret denylist enforced at the harness layer.

### 3. `flag_length` recorded, `flag_value` NOT recorded

`ctf_attempts.flag_length` stores the integer length of the submitted
flag. The flag *value* is never accepted as a function parameter and
never persisted to any column. This invariant exists because:

- A future "flag dictionary leak" failure mode (the row-level analogue
  of the kkr.py output-leakage gap, see
  [legacy-archaeologist §3](../evidence/m11/discovery/legacy-archaeologist.md))
  is structurally prevented when the DB cannot return the value.
- Operators who need to debug a wrong-flag submission can still
  reconstruct the flag from the agent's local audit log
  (`agent_tool_audit` / `experiment_runs` artifacts) under explicit
  approval — that path is gated, the DB path is not.

The Python helper `record_attempt` additionally refuses to store a
`response_excerpt` that contains the literal phrase "flag length"
alongside a non-null `flag_length` column — this catches the failure
mode where the event API's error body itself echoes "incorrect flag
length: 42", which combined with `flag_length=42` would let any reader
infer length without the row's column. Callers must pre-scrub the
excerpt; the excerpt is also truncated to **256 chars**.

### 4. Multi-account / team identity on the attempt row

Per the T000 design-red-team report
([§dropped_capabilities/2 + §open_disagreements/2](../evidence/m11/discovery/design-red-team.md)),
the kkr.py M9.4 replay surfaced a critical gap: a submissions table
without an explicit credential-identity column cannot answer "which
credential made this submission" after the fact. The same gap in
`ctf_attempts` would re-incarnate the failure mode.

M11-T001 therefore adds **two columns to `ctf_attempts`** beyond the
task-spec skeleton:

| Column          | Type | Nullable | Why                                    |
|-----------------|------|----------|----------------------------------------|
| `event_account` | text | yes      | The username / e-mail / handle that authenticated to the event API at submit time. |
| `team_id`       | text | yes      | The team identifier reported back by the event API (if the event has team scoring). |

Both columns are populated by `record_attempt(... event_account=...,
team_id=...)` and surfaced on `list_attempts`. They are nullable so
single-account events and pre-T007 dry-runs do not need to lie.

### 5. Retention policy for failed attempts

Default: **keep indefinitely**. The attempt-level redaction lives in
`response_excerpt` (256-char cap, callers pre-scrub). There is no
TTL job. Rationale:

- Failed-attempt history is load-bearing for post-event audit ("did
  the agent try the same wrong flag 50 times?") and rate-limit
  evidence ("the event API returned 429 on the 3rd attempt").
- The columns we keep are all low-cardinality / low-volume; the
  whole table is small relative to `agent_tool_audit`.
- A future retention policy may add `ctf_attempts.expires_at` plus a
  cron, but that decision is M12+ scope (see open question 1).

### 6. RLS enabled, no policies yet

All three tables `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` but ship without
policies, mirroring `ctf_scopes` in migration 0001. The kca CLI
connects as `postgres` (RLS bypassed); UI / supabase-js callers will
need policies before they can read these tables. Policies are
deferred until the auth model lands (see ADR follow-ups in M12 / M13).

## Consequences

### Pros

- Schema is the smallest delta that addresses the kkr.py failure mode
  structurally (`event_account` + `team_id` on every attempt).
- `flag_value` is not in the schema, so the leak-by-DB-query path is
  closed by construction.
- All three tables are FK-cascaded from a single parent
  (`projects → ctf_events → ctf_challenges → ctf_attempts`), so
  cleanup is a single `DELETE FROM ctf_events WHERE …`.

### Cons / known limits

- The schema carries the most cognitive load of the four
  alternatives surfaced in the design-red-team report (three new
  tables + the existing `ctf_scopes` + a FK back to `projects`,
  not `competitions`). Alternative 1 (`competition_type` discriminator
  on the existing `competitions` table) would have been zero new
  tables. We accept the cost in exchange for a clean CTF-only query
  surface during M11; see open question 1 below.
- The `category` column is a CHECK-constrained string, not a Postgres
  ENUM. This is consistent with the precedent in 0007 (`decision`
  CHECK on `agent_tool_audit`) and avoids the
  `ALTER TYPE … ADD VALUE` migration headache when a new category
  (e.g. `hardware`) shows up. The cost is per-row CHECK enforcement
  rather than catalog-level type safety; downstream analytics use
  string comparisons.
- `credentials_ref` validation is a Python-layer heuristic, not a DB
  CHECK. A motivated caller writing raw SQL can still insert a
  credential value into the column. The hook layer and the M11-T008
  audit-grep test are the two other layers that catch this; the DB
  is not the only line of defense.

## Open questions (deferred)

1. **Overlap with M12 `competition_type`.** M12 is already planning a
   `competition_type` discriminator on the existing `competitions`
   table (see `docs/milestones.md` §M12 and
   [design-red-team §alternatives/1](../evidence/m11/discovery/design-red-team.md)).
   When M12 lands, the three M11 tables may be folded into
   `competitions` / `competition_subtasks` / `submissions` rather than
   continuing to live as a parallel trinity. **This ADR is M11-scoped
   and does not block on the M12 decision.** A follow-up ADR / issue
   should capture the migration path at M12 close.
2. **Stable JSON shape for `kca ctf flag submit --json`.** M11-T003
   owns the CLI; the JSON shape is not pinned here. If a downstream
   tool (UI Approval Inbox, T008 audit-grep) needs to parse the
   output, that contract belongs in a T003 / T009 amendment.
3. **Per-event rate-limit metadata.** The design-red-team report
   surfaced "per-challenge attempts-per-hour" as a dropped capability.
   M11 records attempts after the fact only; a pre-submit gate that
   consults a per-challenge counter is deferred to M11 follow-ups or
   M12+.
4. **Subprocess-isolated credential reads.** The credential file is
   currently read in-process by the worker (see
   [design-red-team §open_disagreements/6](../evidence/m11/discovery/design-red-team.md)).
   A future spike may move the read into a dedicated subprocess so
   the parent worker never holds the token in-process. Not blocking
   M11.

## Alternatives considered

See [`docs/evidence/m11/discovery/design-red-team.md` §alternatives](../evidence/m11/discovery/design-red-team.md)
for the full red-team analysis. In brief:

1. **Reuse `competitions` with a `competition_type` discriminator** —
   zero new tables, but reshapes the Kaggle-shaped `submissions`
   table. Deferred to M12 (see open question 1).
2. **Scope-as-policy: rich `ctf_scopes` + `competitions`** — one new
   table instead of three; reuses the kaggle_submit reviewer-gate
   chain. Rejected for M11 because it tangles authorization and
   identity into a single table.
3. **Stateless / file-backed CTF identity, DB only for attempts** —
   events / challenges as YAML in `data/ctf/`; only attempts hit the
   DB. Rejected because cross-event analytics becomes a filesystem
   walk and FK integrity for `ctf_attempts.event_slug` cannot be
   enforced.
4. **Per-event sandbox with no shared identity** — each event in its
   own short-lived docker network with mounted credential. Strongest
   isolation, but doubles per-job latency and complicates OTEL.
   Deferred to M13+ if the threat model demands it.

## References

- [Migration `0008_m11_ctf.sql`](../../supabase/migrations/0008_m11_ctf.sql)
- [`src/db/ctf.py`](../../src/db/ctf.py) — DB helpers
- [`tests/test_m11_db.py`](../../tests/test_m11_db.py) — smoke tests
- [`docs/evidence/m11/discovery/design-red-team.md`](../evidence/m11/discovery/design-red-team.md)

- [`docs/evidence/m11/discovery/requirements-skeptic.md`](../evidence/m11/discovery/requirements-skeptic.md)
- [`docs/evidence/m9_4-kkr-replay/legacy-archaeologist.md`](../evidence/m9_4-kkr-replay/legacy-archaeologist.md) §3 — the "owner on the submission row" gap precedent
- [`supabase/migrations/0001_init.sql`](../../supabase/migrations/0001_init.sql) — `ctf_scopes` and base tables
- [ADR-0005](0005-job-taxonomy.md) — `project_kind` enum + platform slugs
- [ADR-0006](0006-configurable-approval-gates.md) — approval-op data shape
````

```sql
-- 0008_m11_ctf.sql
-- M11: authorized CTF / lab workflow — event / challenge / attempt schema.
--
-- Forward-only. Idempotent. Additive. All indexes use IF NOT EXISTS so the
-- migration is safe to re-apply.
--
-- Tables:
--   ctf_events        — top-level event identity (per-project, per-slug).
--   ctf_challenges    — jeopardy-style challenges within an event, optionally
--                       linked to a ctf_scopes (0001) authorization row.
--   ctf_attempts      — every flag-submit attempt, accepted or not.
--
-- The pre-existing ctf_scopes table from 0001_init.sql is left untouched.
-- Cross-link: see docs/adr/0016-ctf-data-model.md for the full design and
-- the M12 competition_type open question.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ctf_events (
  id                 uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  project_id         uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  slug               text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  name               text NOT NULL,
  ctftime_event_id   integer,
  event_url          text,
  start_at           timestamptz,
  end_at             timestamptz,
  scoring            text DEFAULT 'jeopardy',
  credentials_ref    text,  -- path hint, e.g. '~/.ctf/<slug>.json'; never the value
  notes              text,
  created_at         timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ctf_events_project
  ON ctf_events(project_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ctf_challenges (
  id                    uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  event_id              uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES ctf_events(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  scope_id              uuid REFERENCES ctf_scopes(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  slug                  text NOT NULL,
  name                  text NOT NULL,
  category              text NOT NULL CHECK (
    category IN ('web','crypto','rev','pwn','forensics','osint','misc')
  ),
  points                integer,
  description           text,
  expected_flag_format  text,
  attachments_path      text,
  remote_endpoint       text,
  created_at            timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE (event_id, slug)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ctf_challenges_event
  ON ctf_challenges(event_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ctf_challenges_scope
  ON ctf_challenges(scope_id) WHERE scope_id IS NOT NULL;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ctf_attempts (
  id                uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  challenge_id      uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES ctf_challenges(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  run_id            uuid REFERENCES experiment_runs(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  accepted          boolean,
  http_status       integer,
  flag_length       integer,  -- NEVER the flag value
  -- Multi-account / team identity columns (T000 design-red-team carry-over).
  -- The kkr.py M9.4 replay surfaced the "owner on the submission row" gap;
  -- recording which event credential actually hit the event prevents the
  -- same failure mode (wrong-team-id submission, mis-attributed accept).
  event_account     text,
  team_id           text,
  submitted_at      timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  response_excerpt  text  -- 256-char cap, redact any string that looks like a flag
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ctf_attempts_challenge
  ON ctf_attempts(challenge_id, submitted_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ctf_attempts_run
  ON ctf_attempts(run_id) WHERE run_id IS NOT NULL;

-- Enable RLS now; add real policies once auth/user model is finalized
-- (same posture as ctf_scopes in migration 0001).
ALTER TABLE ctf_events     ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE ctf_challenges ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE ctf_attempts   ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

```
</details>

````markdown
# M11 — Loop Prompts

_Authorized CTF / lab workflow milestone — first non-Kaggle competition platform on
the kaggle-code-agent stack._
_For sequential, partly autonomous execution on Arch Linux._
_Prerequisite: M9 exit confirmed (live LB recorded on Spaceship Titanic; see
`docs/m9-final-review.md`). M10 may run in parallel; the only hard dependency
M11 inherits from M10 is the dotenv-leak fix (issue #11), which must be
merged on `main` before **M11-T008** writes its e2e refusal tests._
_Shared rules: every Loop Prompt below MUST follow `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md`
(sequencing, no real Kaggle/Anthropic outside designated approval paths, DB DSN +
sandbox bypass, **per-milestone worktree by default**, secret denylist, **§7
Discovery / Debate Gate for `arch:` tagged tasks**)._

---

## M11 at a glance

M11 is the **first CTF / authorized-lab regression** for this platform, and
the first milestone to validate that the worker / reviewer / approval-inbox
stack works for a **non-Kaggle competition policy**. M9 + M10 covered Kaggle
CSV submission and Kaggle kernel push respectively. M11 covers CTF jeopardy:
challenge inventory, scoped solver execution, and flag submission to the
event endpoint.

The CTF user pattern (from the planning Q&A) is:

1. Check [CTFtime calendar](https://ctftime.org/calendar/) for upcoming events.
2. Register on the event site **as a human** (no browser-automated sign-up in
   M11); record event credentials under `~/.ctf/<event-slug>.json` or
   `CTF_<EVENT>_*` env vars.
3. For each challenge: read description, download attachments, decide whether
   the challenge is local-only (zip / docker bundle) or remote (must hit the
   event's challenge endpoint).
4. Solve locally where possible; submit the flag to the event's API.

M11 brings (1) into a `kca ctf event register` LOCAL_WRITE flow, defers (2)
to the human, exercises (3) end-to-end against a **frozen past-event bundle**
under `data/ctf/<event>/<challenge>/` for deterministic CI, and exercises (4)
once for real against a **single live CTFtime-listed event** under explicit
human approval.

M11 is **not** a leaderboard-chasing milestone. The acceptance criterion is
that the CTF workflow runs end-to-end correctly under the approval gates and
hard-refuses out-of-scope targets. Solver quality / category coverage is
captured as future work — see `docs/architecture/m11-ctf-workflow.md` §
"Out of scope".

Direct entry into M11 is blocked until **all** are true:

- M9 is merged on `main` (`docs/m9-final-review.md` exists and reports PASS).
- The Discovery / Debate Gate (M11-T000) has produced all three subagent
  reports with byte-for-byte acceptance lines under
  `docs/evidence/m11/discovery/`.
- Issue #11 (dotenv-leak / secret-file hygiene in pytest subprocess) is
  merged on `main`. This is a soft pre-req for **M11-T008** (the e2e
  refusal-path test): M11-T000 through M11-T007 may proceed in parallel
  with #11 work.
- The local Supabase container is running; migration `0001_init.sql`'s
  `ctf_scopes` table is reachable.

### What's in scope

| Capability | Owned by | M11 touches |
|---|---|---|
| Discovery / Debate Gate for CTF data model + new approval ops | `.claude/agents/{legacy-archaeologist,requirements-skeptic,design-red-team}.md`, `docs/architecture/discovery-debate-gate.md` | T000 — all three reports + byte-checkable acceptance |
| Event / challenge / attempt schema | `supabase/migrations/0008_m11_ctf.sql` + `src/db/ctf.py` | T001 |
| New approval operations (`challenge_run`, `flag_submit`, `network_egress`) | `.kca/permissions/{default,permissive-dev,competition-runner}.yaml`, `src/worker/reviewer.py`, `src/worker/worker.py`, `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/hooks/guard_tool.py` | T002 |
| `kca ctf` CLI surface | `tools/kca/ctf.py` + `tools/kca/kca.py::add_parsers` | T003 |
| Frozen past-event challenge bundle (1 web + 1 crypto) | `data/ctf/<event-slug>/{web-1,crypto-1}/` | T004 |
| Agent worker drives ctf-sandbox skill to solve locally | `src/worker/`, `.claude/skills/ctf-sandbox/SKILL.md`, `tools/kca/run.py` | T005 |
| Reviewer-gate before solver run + flag submit | `src/worker/reviewer.py`, `services/decision_api/app.py`, UI Approval Inbox | T006 |
| ONE real flag submission to a live CTFtime event | `tools/kca/ctf.py::cmd_flag_submit`, `ctf_attempts` table | T007 — single real call |
| E2E refusal-path tests | `tests/test_m11_e2e.py`, `tests/test_m11_smoke.py` | T008 |
| ADRs + architecture doc | `docs/adr/0016-ctf-data-model.md`, `docs/adr/0017-ctf-approval-gates.md`, `docs/architecture/m11-ctf-workflow.md` | T001 / T002 / T009 |
| Final review + handoff | `milestone-final-review` skill, `worktree-milestone-pr` skill | T009 |
| GitHub issue / label workflow | `.github/labels.yml`, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature-work.yml`, PR template | every task |

### What's NOT in scope

- Running flag submissions outside T007's single approved call.
- Browser-automated event sign-up. M11 reads human-supplied credentials only.
- Pwn / reverse-engineering / forensics agent-loop solves. The taxonomy
  supports them (`ctf_challenges.category`) but the M11 solve loop exercises
  only `web` + `crypto`. Filed as follow-up issues at milestone close.
- CTFtime calendar polling / auto-event-watch / scheduled-job auto-submit.
- Changing production Supabase.
- Implementing M10 follow-ups (parallel milestone; cross-cutting items file
  as their own issues).
- Implementing M9 follow-ups A, C, D, E (still tracked as issues #14, #15, #16,
  #17). Issue #11 is the only soft pre-req (see entry gates).

DB / sandbox details: see `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` §3 — the local
`supabase-db` container (`postgresql://postgres:s3cr3t@172.21.0.4:5432/postgres`)
needs `dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true`. The real CTF event API call inside
M11-T007 also needs sandbox bypass and an approved `ctf_scopes.target_urls`
entry covering the submit endpoint.
````
