## GitHub issue / label workflow for M11

Each M11 task is filed as a GitHub issue using the `feature-work.yml` form,
labelled per task type. The canonical **M11 proposal issue** (TBD —
filed before T000 starts) collects the planning Q&A decisions; individual
task issues link back to it.

| Task | Issue labels at file time | Labels added by triage | Labels at merge |
|---|---|---|---|
| M11-T000 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `arch:`, `area:agent`, `area:docs` | `ai:ready` (after AC + owner) | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M11-T001 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `arch:`, `area:supabase`, `area:db` | `ai:ready` (after T000 closed) | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M11-T002 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `arch:`, `area:worker`, `area:security`, `area:policy` | `ai:ready` (after T001 closed) | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M11-T003 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:cli`, `area:ctf` | `ai:ready` (after T001 + T002 closed) | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M11-T004 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:ctf`, `area:fixtures` | `ai:ready` (after T003 closed) | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M11-T005 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:worker`, `area:ctf` | `ai:ready` (after T004 closed) | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M11-T006 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:worker`, `area:supabase`, `area:ui` | `ai:ready` (after T005 closed) | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M11-T007 | `type:feature`, `ai:blocked`, `policy:approval-required`, `decision:needed`, `area:ctf`, `priority:P0` | `decision:confirmed` + `ai:ready` only after human comment "approved to submit" | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M11-T008 | `type:test-gap`, `ai:triage`, `area:testing`, `area:ci` | `ai:ready` only after issue #11 is closed | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M11-T009 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:release`, `area:docs` | `ai:ready` after T000–T008 closed | `ai:implementing` → close |

T007 is the only task that starts `ai:blocked` and requires a
`decision:confirmed` comment with an explicit "approved to submit" record
before triage may promote it to `ai:ready`. This is enforced by the
`github-issue-triage` agent rules in `.claude/skills/github-issue-triage/`.

T008 is the only task gated on closing a separate issue (#11). The
triage agent should refuse to promote T008 to `ai:ready` while
`gh issue view 11 --json state` returns `"OPEN"`.

The PR for each task uses `.github/pull_request_template.md`. The
"Remote side effects" section is load-bearing: T007's PR is the ONLY
M11 PR that may check the "Live external API call" box, and must link the
approval comment from the closing issue.

---

## Approval gates (summary)

| Gate | When it fires | Where the approval is recorded | Who can approve |
|---|---|---|---|
| `challenge_run` | Worker is about to invoke a solver against a target whose URL is in `ctf_scopes.target_urls` OR is a local in-scope service | `agent_reviews` row + `human_decisions` row + (T007 only) comment on the closing GitHub issue | Project owner / reviewer named on the issue |
| `flag_submit` | `tools/kca/ctf.py::cmd_flag_submit` is invoked with `--dry-run=False` | `agent_reviews` row + `human_decisions` row + (T007 only) approval comment | Project owner |
| `network_egress` | Worker attempts to call any host NOT in `ctf_scopes.target_urls` AND the host is not on the global allowlist | DENY at the reviewer-gate; recorded as `agent_reviews.verdict=reject` + audit row in `agent_tool_audit` | Not applicable — deny is final; the human must edit the scope row to widen it |
| `kaggle_submit` | Not used in M11 | n/a | n/a |
| `kernel_push` | Not used in M11 | n/a | n/a |

The CTF approval flow inside M11 is:

```
worker stages solver / flag artifact + target URL
  → reviewer-gate writes agent_reviews row + agent_job_events
    (target_op="challenge_run" or "flag_submit")
  → decision_api surfaces pending decision (POST /decisions queued;
    UI reads via supabase-js until issue #15 lands GET /decisions)
  → UI Approval Inbox renders pending decision
  → human approves via UI (POST /decisions/<id>/approve) OR
    `kca decisions approve --id <id>`
  → (T007 only) human comments "approved to submit" on the closing
    issue
  → triage agent promotes issue to `decision:confirmed` + `ai:ready`
  → M11-T007 Loop Prompt runs ONE `kca ctf flag submit`
  → ctf_attempts row written with accepted=true|false + http_status
  → PR opens with the approval comment linked
```

A second real flag submission inside M11 is **out of scope**. If a
follow-up challenge in M11-T005 or M11-T007 surfaces another flag
that the human wants submitted, file it as a new M11-followup issue
and gate it the same way.

## Rollback / stop criteria

Stop the milestone — do **not** advance to the next Loop Prompt — if any of
these is true:

- A real CTF event call returns an error from the event API outside T007's
  single approved call (rate limit, scope violation, bad credentials). The
  fix path is local: regenerate solver / re-verify scope and re-request
  approval; do NOT silently retry.
- The reviewer gate (M11-T006) fails to fire for `challenge_run` or
  `flag_submit` when it should, or fires when it shouldn't.
- Any `policy:approval-required` issue advances without the corresponding
  `decision:confirmed` label and comment.
- Any test in the validation suite regresses from green to red.
- The DSN, Kaggle credentials, `~/.ctf/*`, or `.env*` are accidentally
  printed in any log, audit row, or PR. Stop and rotate the credential
  immediately.
- The Discovery / Debate Gate at T000 surfaces an undecided question that
  invalidates the data model (e.g. multi-event identity collision; team-
  account vs. individual-account ambiguity). Pause, draft a new ADR, and
  restart T000.
- A `network_egress` deny fails to trigger for an attempted call to a host
  outside the scope row (silent egress = critical security regression).
- Issue #11 is reopened mid-milestone with evidence that the leak
  re-emerged. Halt T008 work until #11 is green again.

If M11 needs a new architectural decision (e.g. multi-event credential
rotation; pwn/rev solver harness; CTFtime calendar auto-watch), **pause
and ask** — those are M11-followup / M13 decisions, not M11 expansion.
Open an ADR draft in `docs/adr/` and stop the milestone there.

# M11-T002: New approval operations + reviewer-gate wiring

## Milestone
M11: authorized CTF / lab workflow. **`arch:` tagged** — introduces three
new approval-policy operations (`challenge_run`, `flag_submit`,
`network_egress`) and wires them through the reviewer-gate path. Discovery
/ Debate Gate evidence (T000, specifically `design-red-team.md`) is the
source of truth for the operation shape and defaults.

## Goal
Add the three new operations to `.kca/permissions/*.yaml`, extend
`src/worker/reviewer.py::should_consult_reviewer`, extend
`src/worker/worker.py::_tool_call` to emit the new `target_op` strings,
add the relevant entries to `.claude/settings.json` and
`.claude/hooks/guard_tool.py`, and document the contract in
`docs/adr/0017-ctf-approval-gates.md`.

## Read first

1. `PROJECT_STATE.md`
2. M11-T000 closeout + `docs/evidence/m11/discovery/design-red-team.md`
3. M11-T001 closeout
4. `docs/adr/0006-configurable-approval-gates.md` — operation data shape
5. `.kca/permissions/default.yaml`, `permissive-dev.yaml`,
   `competition-runner.yaml`
6. `src/worker/reviewer.py` — `should_consult_reviewer`, `run_review`,
   `target_op` shape
7. `src/worker/worker.py` — `_tool_call`, `target_op` extraction
8. `.claude/settings.json` — ask-list pattern for `Bash(kaggle …)` and
   `Bash(gh …)` entries
9. `.claude/hooks/guard_tool.py` — secret denylist pattern
10. `docs/tasks/M9-T003-reviewer-approval-gate.md` (`kaggle_submit`
    precedent)
11. `docs/tasks/M10-T003-kernel-push-reviewer-gate.md` (`kernel_push`
    precedent)

## Scope

1. **Permission policy entries.** Add to each profile:

   ```yaml
   - operation: challenge_run
     default_decision: ask
     reason: Executing a solver against an authorized CTF target — gate by default.
     audit_required: true
   - operation: flag_submit
     default_decision: ask
     reason: Submitting a flag to a CTF event API — external side effect.
     audit_required: true
   - operation: network_egress
     default_decision: deny
     reason: Egress outside ctf_scopes.target_urls is denied; widen scope row to allow.
     audit_required: true
     conditional_allow:
       when_in_scope: ask   # if request URL ∈ ctf_scopes.target_urls
   ```
   In `permissive-dev.yaml`, `challenge_run` and `flag_submit` stay on
   `ask` (no auto-allow for the live submission path). In
   `competition-runner.yaml`, `challenge_run` may move to
   `conditional_allow: allow when_in_scope` but `flag_submit` stays on
   `ask` regardless — flag submission is the highest-blast-radius op.

2. **`src/worker/reviewer.py`.** Extend `should_consult_reviewer` to
   return `True` for the three new ops; extend `run_review` to render
   the right context for each (target URL for `challenge_run` /
   `network_egress`; event slug + challenge slug for `flag_submit`;
   NEVER the flag value).

3. **`src/worker/worker.py`.** Extend `_tool_call` to emit `target_op`
   for the new operations. `challenge_run` fires when a solver tool is
   about to invoke against a target whose URL is in a `ctf_scopes`
   row or is a local in-scope service; `flag_submit` fires when
   `tools/kca/ctf.py::cmd_flag_submit` is invoked with `--dry-run=False`;
   `network_egress` fires when any worker-issued HTTP call's host is
   NOT in the union of `ctf_scopes.target_urls` rows for the current
   project AND NOT on the global allowlist.

4. **`.claude/settings.json`.** Add to the ask-list:
   - `Bash(kca ctf flag submit*)` — ask
   - `Bash(kca ctf solver run*)` — ask (only when `--dry-run=False`)
   - Do NOT add `kca ctf event/challenge/scope` — those are LOCAL_WRITE
     and run under `allow`.

5. **`.claude/hooks/guard_tool.py`.** Extend the secret denylist to
   cover `~/.ctf/*.json`, `**/ctf-credentials.json`, and any path
   matching `CTF_*_TOKEN` env-var dumps. The hook denies direct file
   reads of these paths except when invoked from within
   `tools/kca/ctf.py::_load_event_credentials` (single allow-listed
   call-site).

6. **`docs/adr/0017-ctf-approval-gates.md`.** Document:
   - The three new operations + defaults + `audit_required` flag.
   - The `conditional_allow.when_in_scope` semantics (how the worker
     checks `ctf_scopes.target_urls` membership).
   - Why `network_egress` is deny-default while `challenge_run` and
     `flag_submit` are ask-default.
   - Audit row shape (`agent_reviews` + `human_decisions` + the new
     `agent_tool_audit` columns if any).
   - Cross-link to T000's `design-red-team.md` for alternatives /
     dropped capabilities.

7. **Tests.** Add `tests/test_reviewer_m11.py` covering:
   - `should_consult_reviewer('challenge_run')` → True
   - `should_consult_reviewer('flag_submit')` → True
   - `should_consult_reviewer('network_egress')` → True
   - Reviewer `run_review` for `flag_submit` does NOT include the flag
     value in the rendered context.
   - Permission policy resolution: `challenge_run` in `default.yaml`
     resolves to `ask`; in `competition-runner.yaml` with the worker
     in `when_in_scope` resolves to `allow`.

## Non-goals

- Do not add the `kca ctf` CLI commands. T003 owns those.
- Do not author or insert challenge / event fixtures. T004 owns them.
- Do not exercise the reviewer-gate end-to-end with a real worker

## Acceptance criteria

## Permissions

# design-red-team report for the M11 CTF architecture (T000)

Sources:
- Proposed design: `docs/tasks/M11-T000-discovery-debate-gate.md` +
  `docs/m11-loop-prompts.md` (`ctf_events` / `ctf_challenges` /
  `ctf_attempts` schema; new ops `challenge_run` / `flag_submit` /
  `network_egress`; CTFtime → register-as-human → per-event-creds →
  solve → submit workflow).
- Upstream archaeology: `docs/evidence/m11/discovery/legacy-archaeologist.md`
- Upstream skeptic: `docs/evidence/m11/discovery/requirements-skeptic.md`

_Produced under the M11-T000 Discovery / Debate Gate. The agent body
lives in `.claude/agents/design-red-team.md`; this artefact is a
manual execution of that agent's protocol. The "proposed design"
being refuted is the M11 trajectory described in
`docs/m11-loop-prompts.md:62–98` — a per-project `ctf_events` table
with three new approval ops, registered manually by the human and
written from `tools/kca/ctf.py`._

## alternatives

1. **Reuse `competitions` with a `competition_type` discriminator.**
   Instead of a parallel `ctf_events` / `ctf_challenges` / `ctf_attempts`
   trinity, fold CTF into the existing `competitions` /
   `submissions` tables and introduce a `competition_type` enum
   (`kaggle | ctf | hackathon | generic`). Sketch: a CTF event is a
   `competitions` row with `competition_type='ctf'`, challenges are
   `competition_subtasks` (a small new table or a JSONB column on
   `competitions`), and flag submits land in the existing
   `submissions` table with `platform='ctf'`. Key tradeoff vs the
   proposal: zero parallel-table cognitive load (one table per
   concept, not two), but the `submissions` table — already shaped
   around CSV file uploads — gains shape it wasn't designed for
   (flag string, accepted boolean, http_status). Closest precedent:
   M12 is already planning this exact discriminator at the platform
   level (`docs/milestones.md:891–892`). Evidence:
   `docs/adr/0005-job-taxonomy.md:30` (`competition.platform ∈
   {kaggle, ctf, hackathon}` is already the intent).

2. **Scope-as-policy: collapse `ctf_events` into rich `ctf_scopes`
   rows + `competitions` for event identity.** Promote `ctf_scopes`
   to carry the event identity (slug, year, credentials-ref,
   target_urls, expires_at, team_id) and use the existing
   `competitions` table for top-level event metadata
   (name, deadline, platform=`ctf`). Challenges become first-class
   `challenges` rows under `competitions` (one new table, not three),
   and attempts become `submissions` rows. Sketch: one new table
   (`competition_challenges`) instead of three; `ctf_scopes` gains
   `event_account`, `team_id`, and an FK to `competitions`. Key
   tradeoff vs proposal: smaller schema delta and re-uses the
   reviewer-gate/audit chain that already exists for
   `kaggle_submit` on `submissions`, but loses the clean CTF-only
   query surface (every CTF analytics query joins through
   `competitions`).

3. **Stateless / file-backed CTF identity, DB only for attempts.**
   Keep events + challenges as on-disk YAML/JSON files under
   `data/ctf/<event>/manifest.yaml` (the same place the T004 bundle
   lives) and write only `ctf_attempts` rows to the DB (FK to
   `ctf_scopes` for authorization context, FK to `projects`, no FK
   to a DB-resident `ctf_events`). Sketch: `kca ctf event register`
   becomes `kca ctf event init <slug>` which scaffolds the on-disk
   manifest; the human edits it and commits; the worker reads
   `data/ctf/<slug>/manifest.yaml` at run time. Key tradeoff vs
   proposal: events / challenges become first-class git artefacts
   (reviewable in PR, diffable, auditable), but cross-project
   analytics ("how many flags across all events") becomes a
   filesystem walk instead of a SQL query, and the schema cannot
   enforce referential integrity for `ctf_attempts.event_slug`.

4. **(Bonus) Per-event sandbox with no shared identity.** Spin
   each event up in its own short-lived docker network with its
   own `~/.ctf/<event-slug>.json` mounted; the worker has no
   ambient credential and no cross-event view. Sketch: the M11
   `challenge_run` op is implemented as `docker run --network
   ctf-<slug> --env-file ~/.ctf/<slug>.env …`; `flag_submit` is
   `httpx.post` from inside the same container. Key tradeoff:
   strongest isolation (a compromise of one event's worker
   cannot read another event's credential), but doubles the
   per-job latency and complicates the OTEL telemetry pipeline.

## dropped_capabilities

- **Per-challenge attempts-per-hour rate-limit** as a first-class
  schema field. The proposed `ctf_attempts` shape captures only
  `accepted` + `http_status` after the fact; the platform has no
  pre-submit gate that consults a per-challenge attempt-counter.
  Evidence: `docs/m11-loop-prompts.md:111` ("M11-T005 records
  `ctf_attempts` row + `experiment_runs`") and
  `supabase/migrations/0001_init.sql:211–223` (no `attempts_count`
  or `last_attempt_at` column on `ctf_scopes`). Survives in:
  alternative 1 (CTFd-style rate-limit could live as a column on
  `competitions.submission_format` JSONB), alternative 2
  (`ctf_scopes.max_attempts_per_hour`), legacy (kkr.py had
  `--interval`/`--timeout` flags at `tools/legacy/kkr.py:2207–2215`
  for Kaggle; CTF needs an analogue).
- **Multi-event credential identity on the attempt row.** The
  proposed `ctf_attempts` is FK'd to `ctf_challenges`+`ctf_events`
  but does not carry the credential identity that actually made the
  submission (event_account / team_id). Evidence: the M11 task
  summary at `docs/m11-loop-prompts.md:62–77` mentions team_id only
  in the credential JSON file, not in the attempts row; the kkr.py
  replay precedent at
  `docs/evidence/m9_4-kkr-replay/legacy-archaeologist.md` §3 calls
  out exactly this "owner on the submission row" gap. Survives in:
  alternative 2 (`ctf_scopes.event_account` carries through to the
  attempt), alternative 4 (the sandbox network is the identity).
- **`--env <path>` override on a per-invocation basis.** The legacy
  kkr.py exposed `--env <path>` at `tools/legacy/kkr.py:535–537`;
  the M11 plan does not surface an analogous flag on `kca ctf flag
  submit` (the credential is implicitly `~/.ctf/<slug>.json` or the
  `CTF_<EVENT>_*` env vars; no override path). Evidence:
  `docs/m11-loop-prompts.md:621–667` (planning Q&A item 5
  describes the two paths and treats them as exhaustive).
  Survives in: legacy, alternative 2 (the scope row could carry a
  `credentials_path_override` column), alternative 4 (the
  `--env-file` is a docker flag).
- **CTF-category enumeration enforced by the schema.** The proposal
  leaves `ctf_challenges.category` as free text per
  `docs/m11-loop-prompts.md:62–77`; this drops the ability to do
  `WHERE category IN ('web', 'crypto')` queries with type safety.
  Evidence: archaeology §8 (`ctf-sandbox/SKILL.md:31` lists the
  five categories as ambient assumption, not enforced enum). The
  proposal explicitly accepts this; the cost is downstream
  analytics drift.
- **Stable JSON shape for `kca ctf flag submit --json`.** The
  proposal at `docs/m11-loop-prompts.md:255–256` says "echo only
  `accepted=true|false` + http status, never the flag string
  itself", but does not pin the JSON keys. Evidence: unavailable
  in the current branch — route to `open_disagreements`.

## long_term_costs

cognitive_load:    A new contributor must hold three new tables
                   (`ctf_events`, `ctf_challenges`, `ctf_attempts`)
                   plus the existing `ctf_scopes` plus the
                   relationship-to-`projects`-but-not-`competitions`
                   asymmetry in their head before they can write
                   one CTF query. Alternative 1 trades all three for
                   one `competition_type` column; alternative 2 adds
                   one new table; alternative 3 keeps only the
                   `ctf_attempts` table. The proposal carries the
                   most cognitive weight of all four options.
ops_burden:        Four-tables-with-FKs means a schema migration
                   failure leaves a half-applied state; `0008_m11_ctf.sql`
                   must wrap in a transaction with savepoints, and
                   the rollback `0009_*` must drop tables in
                   FK-reverse order. At 3am, a failed submit during
                   T007 must be reconcilable from the
                   `agent_reviews` row alone — does the proposal
                   guarantee the `(agent_reviews.id, ctf_attempts.id)`
                   pairing? Skeptic §side_effects/3 calls this out
                   (`docs/evidence/m11/discovery/requirements-skeptic.md`).
extensibility:     Next likely scope expansions: (a) M12's
                   `competition_type` enum (in progress per
                   `docs/milestones.md:891–892`), and (b) a second
                   CTF event running concurrently under the same
                   project (the picoCTF-during-weekend-CTF case).
                   The proposal needs a schema migration for (a) and
                   needs `ctf_events.is_active` plus an index for
                   (b); alternative 1 absorbs both for free
                   (because `competition_type` already lives on
                   `competitions`).
blast_radius:      Worst case: a wrong flag is submitted under
                   the wrong event-account because the
                   `ctf_attempts` row has no event_account
                   discriminator and the worker picked the wrong
                   credential file from `~/.ctf/*.json`. The
                   `submissions`-style audit row points at the
                   project but not the event-account, so the
                   incident response cannot answer "which credential
                   ran this" without re-reading the worker's
                   in-process env. This is the kkr.py failure mode
                   re-incarnated; the proposal does not structurally
                   prevent it (see `dropped_capabilities` §2).
                   Alternative 2 and alternative 4 prevent it
                   structurally.

## open_disagreements

- The proposal adds three new tables when M12 is already planning
  a `competition_type` enum that would let CTF reuse `competitions`
  + `submissions`. Disagree — next step: open a follow-up issue
  (labels: `area:supabase`, `area:ctf`, `area:schema`,
  `policy:approval-required`) asking whether M11-T001 should land a
  parallel schema or wait for M12-T002's `competition_type` and
  fold CTF in at M12 close. Evidence:
  `docs/milestones.md:891–892`, `docs/m12-loop-prompts.md`
  (alternative 1 is already partly committed at the M12 layer).
- `ctf_attempts` has no `event_account` / `team_id` / `submitted_by`
  column to record *which* credential actually hit the event.
  Disagree — next step: spike a schema patch adding
  `ctf_attempts.event_account` (text) and `ctf_attempts.team_id`
  (text, nullable) before M11-T001 is committed; the kkr.py replay
  precedent shows the kind of gap this prevents. Evidence:
  `docs/evidence/m11/discovery/legacy-archaeologist.md` §3,
  `docs/evidence/m9_4-kkr-replay/legacy-archaeologist.md` §3.
- The proposed `network_egress` op is described as "deny outside
  an authorized `ctf_scopes.target_urls` row; ask when scope+URL
  match" (`docs/m11-loop-prompts.md:212–214`). It is unclear at
  which layer the deny actually fires — hook (`.claude/hooks/guard_tool.py`),
  reviewer (`src/worker/reviewer.py`), or HTTP client (httpx
  request interceptor). Disagree — next step: ask human which
  layer owns enforcement; the wrong choice means the deny can be
  bypassed by a tool that does not go through that layer (e.g.
  subprocess curl bypasses an httpx interceptor).
- The proposal leaves `ctf_challenges.category` as free text
  (M11-T001 spec) but the M11 plan exercises only `web` + `crypto`.
  Disagree — next step: file a follow-up issue (labels:
  `area:ctf`, `area:schema`, `type:tech-debt`) to revisit
  enum-ifying `category` after M11-T009 once the actual taxonomy is
  empirically known. Evidence:
  `docs/m11-loop-prompts.md:317` (web+crypto exercised), legacy
  archaeology §8 (`ctf-sandbox/SKILL.md:31` ambient five-category
  list).
- The proposal does not pin a JSON-output shape for `kca ctf flag
  submit --json` beyond "accepted + http status"
  (`docs/m11-loop-prompts.md:255–256`). Disagree — next step:
  research-brief whether any downstream tool (the M11 UI Approval
  Inbox, the T008 audit-grep test, the milestone-final-review
  pipeline) parses this output; if yes, pin the keys in ADR-0016.
  Evidence: unavailable in the current branch (parallel to the
  kkr.py `_emit_ok` JSON-shape question at
  `docs/evidence/m9_4-kkr-replay/design-red-team.md` §dropped_capabilities/4).
- The proposal treats `~/.ctf/<event-slug>.json` as ambient state
  read by the worker process; the hook-layer carve-out
  (`docs/m11-loop-prompts.md:213`, "extend `.claude/hooks/guard_tool.py`
  to cover `~/.ctf/*.json` reads outside the allow-listed `kca ctf`

  never holds the token in-process. Evidence:
  `docs/evidence/m9_4-kkr-replay/design-red-team.md` §alternatives/2
  (subprocess isolation as a recurring solution to ambient-credential
  drift).

Output MUST include ≥3 alternatives, ≥1 dropped capability with file:line evidence, all four long-term-cost axes, and ≥1 actionable `open_disagreements` entry.

````python
"""Sync reviewer agent (M6-T004 / ADR-0012).

When the primary worker is about to call a high-stakes operation
(`kaggle_submit`, `supabase_migrate`, `git_force_push`, `dataset_upload`,
`delete_artifact`), the reviewer reads the job's event trail and final
plan, calls a reviewer model via LiteLLM, and returns a verdict
(`approve` | `reject` | `abstain`). Sync-only for M6.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any


DEFAULT_REVIEWER_MODEL = "claude-opus-4-7"
DEFAULT_TRIGGER_OPS = (
    "kaggle_submit",
    "supabase_migrate",
    "git_force_push",
    "dataset_upload",
    "delete_artifact",
)


@dataclass
class ReviewRequest:
    job_id: str
    target_op: str
    tool_name: str
    tool_input: dict
    final_message: str | None = None
    event_trail: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)


@dataclass
class ReviewVerdict:
    verdict: str
    rationale: str
    evidence: dict
    cost_usd: float
    reviewer_model: str


_REVIEWER_SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
    "You are a sync reviewer for a Kaggle/CTF code agent. The primary "
    "worker is about to invoke a high-stakes operation. Read the job "
    "context below and decide whether the call should proceed.\n\n"
    "Return STRICT JSON only (no prose, no markdown), exactly: "
    '{"verdict": "approve|reject|abstain", '
    '"rationale": "<one paragraph>", '
    '"evidence": {"key_signals": [...]}}\n\n'
    "Use approve when the plan and tool input clearly match the stated "
    "task and contain no destructive surprise. Use reject when the call "
    "would touch the wrong data, push the wrong file, leak secrets, or "
    "violate competition/CTF rules. Use abstain when context is too thin "
    "to decide; a human will be paged."
)


def _trim_event_trail(events: list[dict], max_events: int = 20) -> list[dict]:
    """Keep at most the most-recent max_events events, drop bulky fields."""
    if len(events) > max_events:
        events = events[-max_events:]
    pruned: list[dict] = []
    for ev in events:
        pruned.append(
            {
                "event_type": ev.get("event_type"),
                "turn_number": ev.get("turn_number"),
                "event_data": ev.get("event_data"),
            }
        )
    return pruned


_EVENT_TRAIL_TRIAGE_THRESHOLD = 8 * 1024  # 8 KB


def _render_prompt(req: ReviewRequest) -> str:
    trail = _trim_event_trail(req.event_trail)
    trail_json = json.dumps(trail, default=str, ensure_ascii=False)
    summary_block: str | None = None
    if len(trail_json) > _EVENT_TRAIL_TRIAGE_THRESHOLD:
        try:
            from src.worker import triage as _triage

            sresult = _triage.summarise_text(trail_json)
            if sresult.get("ok") and sresult.get("summary"):
                summary_block = (
                    f"(event_trail triaged to {sresult.get('endpoint')}:"
                    f"{sresult.get('model')})\n{sresult['summary']}"
                )
        except Exception:
            summary_block = None
    body = {
        "job_id": req.job_id,
        "target_op": req.target_op,
        "tool_name": req.tool_name,
        "tool_input": req.tool_input,
        "final_message": req.final_message,
    }
    if summary_block is not None:
        body["event_trail_summary"] = summary_block
    else:
        body["event_trail"] = trail
    rendered = json.dumps(body, default=str, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
    return f"REVIEW REQUEST:\n{rendered}\n\nReturn STRICT JSON only."


def _trigger_ops_from_env() -> set[str]:
    raw = os.environ.get("KCA_REVIEWER_TRIGGER_OPS", "")
    if not raw.strip():
        return set(DEFAULT_TRIGGER_OPS)
    return {p.strip() for p in raw.split(",") if p.strip()}


def should_consult_reviewer(operation: str) -> bool:
    """Return True if the given operation is in the configured trigger set."""
    return operation in _trigger_ops_from_env()


def escalate_reject() -> bool:
    return os.environ.get("KCA_REVIEWER_ESCALATE_REJECT", "1").strip() == "1"


class Reviewer:
    """Sync reviewer. Calls LiteLLM unless dry_run=True."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        model: str | None = None,
        max_tokens: int = 2048,
        timeout_s: int = 120,
        dry_run: bool = False,
        dry_verdict: str = "approve",
        dry_rationale: str = "dry-run reviewer auto-approve",
    ) -> None:
        self.model = (
            model or os.environ.get("KCA_REVIEWER_MODEL") or DEFAULT_REVIEWER_MODEL
        )
        try:
            self.max_tokens = int(os.environ.get("KCA_REVIEWER_MAX_TOKENS", max_tokens))
        except ValueError:
            self.max_tokens = max_tokens
        try:
            self.timeout_s = int(os.environ.get("KCA_REVIEWER_TIMEOUT_S", timeout_s))
        except ValueError:
            self.timeout_s = timeout_s
        self.dry_run = dry_run
        self.dry_verdict = dry_verdict
        self.dry_rationale = dry_rationale

    def review_dry_run(self) -> ReviewVerdict:
        return ReviewVerdict(
            verdict=self.dry_verdict,
            rationale=self.dry_rationale,
            evidence={"mode": "dry_run"},
            cost_usd=0.0,
            reviewer_model=self.model,
        )

    def review(self, req: ReviewRequest) -> ReviewVerdict:
        if self.dry_run:
            return self.review_dry_run()
        return self._review_live(req)

    def _review_live(self, req: ReviewRequest) -> ReviewVerdict:
        user_prompt = _render_prompt(req)
        messages = [
            {"role": "system", "content": _REVIEWER_SYSTEM_PROMPT},
            {"role": "user", "content": user_prompt},
        ]
        started = time.monotonic()
        try:
            import litellm  # noqa: F401  (lazy import; only required when live)

            response = litellm.completion(
                model=self.model,
                messages=messages,
                max_tokens=self.max_tokens,
                temperature=0.0,
                timeout=self.timeout_s,
            )
        except Exception as exc:
            return ReviewVerdict(
                verdict="abstain",
                rationale=f"reviewer model error: {exc}",
                evidence={"error": str(exc), "duration_s": time.monotonic() - started},
                cost_usd=0.0,
                reviewer_model=self.model,
            )
        msg = response.choices[0].message
        text = (msg.content or "").strip()
        # Strip code fences if any.
        if text.startswith("```"):
            text = text.strip("`")
            text = text.split("\n", 1)[1] if "\n" in text else text
            text = text.rstrip("`")
        verdict = "abstain"
        rationale = text
        evidence: dict[str, Any] = {}
        try:
            parsed = json.loads(text)
            v = str(parsed.get("verdict", "")).lower().strip()
            if v in {"approve", "reject", "abstain"}:
                verdict = v
            rationale = str(parsed.get("rationale", "") or rationale)
            ev = parsed.get("evidence")
            if isinstance(ev, dict):
                evidence = ev
        except Exception as exc:
            evidence = {"parse_error": str(exc), "raw": text[:500]}
        usage = getattr(response, "usage", None)
        cost_usd = 0.0
        if usage is not None:
            cost_usd = float(getattr(usage, "total_cost", 0.0) or 0.0)
        return ReviewVerdict(
            verdict=verdict,
            rationale=rationale,
            evidence=evidence,
            cost_usd=cost_usd,
            reviewer_model=self.model,
        )

````

    def _tool_call(
        self, executor: "ToolExecutor", tool_name: str, tool_input: dict
    ) -> str:
        """M8 tool dispatch with ToolSpec + JobPolicy enforcement.

        Resolution order:
          1. JobPolicy.tool_decisions[tool_name]: "deny" → PolicyViolation;
             "ask" → ApprovalRequired (pauses job, records human_decisions);
             "allow" or unset → fall through.
          2. ToolSpec.sandbox: "unsandboxed" requires the policy decision to
             be "allow"; "isolated_workspace" requires cwd to be the job
             workspace.
          3. ToolSpec.timeout_s wraps the call so a hung tool cannot exceed
             the declared budget (applies to ``run_bash`` and other
             subprocess-shaped tools; in-process tools observe it via a best
             effort signal-based deadline).
          4. Every decision is audited via
             ``tools.kca.agent.audit.log_policy_decision`` so the
             ``agent_tool_audit`` table records the outcome.
        """
        decision = (self.policy.tool_decisions or {}).get(tool_name)
        spec = self._tool_spec(tool_name)
        self._audit_tool_decision(
            tool_name=tool_name,
            decision=decision or "allow",
            spec=spec,
            tool_input=tool_input,
        )

        if decision == "deny":
            raise PolicyViolation(tool_name, decision="deny")
        if decision == "ask":
            # Surface as ApprovalRequired so the existing pause/decision flow
            # handles it (writes human_decisions + agent_job_events).
            side_effect = "LOCAL_WRITE"
            if spec is not None:
                side_effect = getattr(spec, "side_effect", side_effect) or side_effect
            raise ApprovalRequired(tool_name, tool_input, side_effect)

        if spec is not None:
            self._enforce_tool_spec(spec, tool_input)
            timeout = getattr(spec, "timeout_s", None)
        else:
            timeout = None

        if timeout and timeout > 0:
            return self._call_with_deadline(executor, tool_name, tool_input, timeout)
        return executor.execute(tool_name, tool_input)

    def _tool_spec(self, tool_name: str):
        """Resolve a ToolSpec from the kca agent tool_registry, if available."""
        try:
            import sys as _sys

            _sys.path.insert(
                0,
                str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / "tools" / "kca"),
            )
            from agent.tool_registry import get_tool  # type: ignore

            return get_tool(tool_name)
        except Exception:
            return None

    def _enforce_tool_spec(self, spec, tool_input: dict) -> None:
        """Cross-check sandbox + isolated_workspace constraints from ToolSpec."""
        sandbox = getattr(spec, "sandbox", None)
        if sandbox == "isolated_workspace":
            # The worker's cwd is the job workspace; tools that resolve paths
            # via ToolExecutor._guard_path already reject traversal. We just
            # confirm the workspace looks set (a None workspace is a bug).
            if not self.workspace:
                raise PolicyViolation(spec.name, decision="missing_workspace")
        # ``unsandboxed`` requires explicit "allow" — already gated above; this
        # is a belt-and-braces check.
        if sandbox == "unsandboxed":
            decision = (self.policy.tool_decisions or {}).get(spec.name)
            if decision != "allow":
                raise PolicyViolation(spec.name, decision="unsandboxed_needs_allow")

    def _call_with_deadline(
        self,
        executor: "ToolExecutor",
        tool_name: str,
        tool_input: dict,
        timeout_s: int,
    ) -> str:
        """Best-effort timeout wrapper. ``run_bash`` already times out via
        subprocess; for other tools we just honour the ToolSpec on a wall
        clock and surface a string error if exceeded.
        """
        if tool_name == "run_bash":
            ti = dict(tool_input)
            ti.setdefault("timeout_s", timeout_s)
            return executor.execute(tool_name, ti)
        # In-process tools: run inline; if a future tool turns out to be
        # blocking we can wrap it with signal.alarm/threading.Timer here.
        return executor.execute(tool_name, tool_input)

    def _audit_tool_decision(
        self,
        *,
        tool_name: str,
        decision: str,
        spec,
        tool_input: dict,
    ) -> None:
        try:
            import sys as _sys

            _sys.path.insert(
                0,
                str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent),
            )
            from tools.kca.agent.audit import log_policy_decision  # type: ignore

            log_policy_decision(
                tool=tool_name,
                operation=tool_name,
                decision=decision,
                skill_name=self.policy.skill_name,
                mode=self.policy.mode,
                policy_profile=self.policy.policy_profile,
                args=tool_input,
                audit_required=bool(getattr(spec, "audit_required", False))
                if spec is not None
                else False,
                job_id=self.job_id if self.db_url else None,
            )
        except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover
            import sys as _sys

            _sys.stderr.write(f"[audit warn] {exc}\n")

    def _handle_approval_required(
        self, exc: ApprovalRequired, budget: BudgetTracker, start: float
    ) -> WorkerResult:
        """Pause the job and record a decision request.

        M6: when the gating operation is one of KCA_REVIEWER_TRIGGER_OPS,
        first consult the sync reviewer. Reviewer.approve auto-resumes,
        reviewer.reject either escalates to humans (default) or fails the
        job (when KCA_REVIEWER_ESCALATE_REJECT=0), and reviewer.abstain
        falls through to the existing human-decisions path.
        """
        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        # M6 reviewer pre-check
        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        reviewer_outcome = self._maybe_consult_reviewer(exc, budget)
        if reviewer_outcome == "approve":
            # Re-execute the gated tool with one-shot bypass.
            return WorkerResult(
                status="reviewer_approved",
                turns_used=budget.turns,
                cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
                duration_s=time.monotonic() - start,
                final_message="reviewer approved",
                stop_reason="reviewer_approve",
            )
        if reviewer_outcome == "reject_fail":
            self._update_status(
                "failed",
                error="reviewer rejected high-stakes operation",
                budget=budget,
            )
            return WorkerResult(
                status="failed",

          None             — reviewer not consulted (op not in trigger set or

          "approve"        — reviewer approved; caller resumes the tool
          "reject_fail"    — reviewer rejected and ESCALATE_REJECT=0
          "reject_escalate"— reviewer rejected, caller should page humans
          "abstain"        — reviewer abstained, caller should page humans
        """
        from src.worker.reviewer import (
            Reviewer,
            ReviewRequest,
            should_consult_reviewer,
            escalate_reject,

        target_op = exc.tool_name
        if not should_consult_reviewer(target_op):
            return None
        if not self.db_url:
            # No DB → no event trail and no place to record the verdict.
            # The dry-run worker still records the reviewer span via OTEL when
            # T005 wires it up; for now just skip silently.
            return None
        try:
            import sys as _sys

            _sys.path.insert(
                0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / "tools" / "kca")
            )
            import db as _db

            # Skip if reviewer already ran for (job_id, target_op).
            try:
                existing = _db.find_review_for_op(self.job_id, target_op)
            except Exception:
                existing = None
            if existing is not None:
                return None
            events = []
            try:
                events = _db.list_job_events(self.job_id)
            except Exception:
                events = []
            req = ReviewRequest(
                job_id=self.job_id,
                target_op=target_op,
                tool_name=exc.tool_name,
                tool_input=exc.tool_input,
                final_message=None,
                event_trail=events,
            )
            reviewer = Reviewer(dry_run=self.dry_run)
            verdict = reviewer.review(req)
            try:
                _db.create_review(
                    job_id=self.job_id,
                    reviewer_model=verdict.reviewer_model,
                    verdict=verdict.verdict,
                    target_op=target_op,
                    rationale=verdict.rationale,
                    evidence=verdict.evidence,
                    cost_usd=verdict.cost_usd,
                )
            except Exception:
                pass
            if verdict.verdict == "approve":
                self._append_event(
                    "approval_resume",
                    budget.turns,
                    event_data={
                        "source": "reviewer",
                        "verdict": "approve",
                        "target_op": target_op,
                        "rationale": verdict.rationale[:200],
                    },
                )
                return "approve"
            if verdict.verdict == "reject":
                if escalate_reject():
                    self._append_event(
                        "reviewer_reject",
                        budget.turns,
                        event_data={
                            "target_op": target_op,
                            "rationale": verdict.rationale[:200],
                            "escalated": True,
                        },
                    )
                    return "reject_escalate"
                self._append_event(
                    "reviewer_reject",
                    budget.turns,
                    event_data={
                        "target_op": target_op,
                        "rationale": verdict.rationale[:200],
                        "escalated": False,
                    },
                )
                return "reject_fail"
            # abstain → fall through
            self._append_event(
                "reviewer_abstain",
                budget.turns,
                event_data={
                    "target_op": target_op,
                    "rationale": verdict.rationale[:200],
                },
            )
            return "abstain"
        except Exception:
            return None

    def _append_event(
        self,
        event_type: str,
        turn_number: int,
        *,
        input_tokens: int | None = None,
        output_tokens: int | None = None,
        cost_usd: float | None = None,
        event_data: dict | None = None,

"""Tool registry: metadata for every agent-facing tool."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

SIDE_EFFECT_LEVELS = {"READ_ONLY", "LOCAL_WRITE", "REMOTE_WRITE", "SUBMISSION"}
APPROVAL_LABELS = {"allow", "ask", "deny"}
SANDBOX_LABELS = {"sandboxed", "unsandboxed", "isolated_workspace"}


@dataclass
class ToolSpec:
    name: str
    description: str
    side_effect: str
    approval_label: str
    timeout_s: int
    sandbox: str
    tags: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    input_schema: dict = field(default_factory=dict)


def _spec(
    name: str,
    description: str,
    side_effect: str,
    approval_label: str,
    timeout_s: int,
    sandbox: str,
    tags: list[str],
    input_schema: dict | None = None,
) -> ToolSpec:
    assert side_effect in SIDE_EFFECT_LEVELS, side_effect
    assert approval_label in APPROVAL_LABELS, approval_label
    assert sandbox in SANDBOX_LABELS, sandbox
    return ToolSpec(
        name=name,
        description=description,
        side_effect=side_effect,
        approval_label=approval_label,
        timeout_s=timeout_s,
        sandbox=sandbox,
        tags=tags,
        input_schema=input_schema or {"type": "object"},
    )


_TOOLS: list[ToolSpec] = [
    _spec(
        "bash",
        "Run a shell command.",
        "LOCAL_WRITE",
        "ask",
        30,
        "unsandboxed",
        ["shell"],
        {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {"command": {"type": "string"}},
            "required": ["command"],
        },
    ),
    _spec(
        "read_file",
        "Read a file from the workspace.",
        "READ_ONLY",
        "allow",
        5,
        "sandboxed",
        ["filesystem"],
        {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {"path": {"type": "string"}},
            "required": ["path"],
        },
    ),
    _spec(
        "edit_file",
        "Edit an existing file.",
        "LOCAL_WRITE",
        "allow",
        10,
        "sandboxed",
        ["filesystem"],
    ),
    _spec(
        "write_file",
        "Write a new file.",
        "LOCAL_WRITE",
        "allow",
        10,
        "sandboxed",
        ["filesystem"],
    ),
    _spec(
        "web_fetch",
        "Fetch a single URL.",
        "READ_ONLY",
        "allow",
        30,
        "sandboxed",
        ["network"],
    ),
    _spec(
        "web_search",
        "Run a web search query.",
        "READ_ONLY",
        "allow",
        30,
        "sandboxed",
        ["network"],
    ),
    _spec(
        "git_commit",
        "Create a git commit in the workspace.",
        "LOCAL_WRITE",
        "allow",
        30,
        "sandboxed",
        ["git"],
    ),
    _spec(
        "git_push",
        "Push commits to a remote.",
        "REMOTE_WRITE",
        "ask",
        30,
        "unsandboxed",
        ["git", "network"],
    ),
    _spec(
        "gh_pr_create",
        "Create a GitHub PR.",
        "REMOTE_WRITE",
        "allow",
        30,
        "unsandboxed",
        ["git", "github"],
    ),
    _spec(
        "gh_pr_merge",
        "Merge a GitHub PR.",
        "REMOTE_WRITE",
        "ask",
        30,
        "unsandboxed",
        ["git", "github"],
    ),
    _spec(
        "kaggle_submit",
        "Submit predictions to Kaggle.",
        "SUBMISSION",
        "ask",
        60,
        "unsandboxed",
        ["kaggle"],
    ),
    _spec(
        "kaggle_push",
        "Push a Kaggle kernel/notebook.",
        "SUBMISSION",
        "ask",
        60,
        "unsandboxed",
        ["kaggle"],
    ),
    _spec(
        "supabase_migrate",
        "Apply a Supabase migration to the remote DB.",
        "REMOTE_WRITE",
        "ask",
        60,
        "unsandboxed",
        ["db"],
    ),
    _spec(
        "run_tests",
        "Run the project test suite.",
        "LOCAL_WRITE",
        "allow",
        120,
        "sandboxed",
        ["tests"],
    ),
    _spec(
        "litellm_call",
        "Invoke a routed LLM endpoint.",
        "LOCAL_WRITE",
        "allow",
        120,
        "sandboxed",
        ["llm"],
    ),
    _spec(
        "create_artifact",
        "Create an artifact under the workspace artifacts directory.",
        "LOCAL_WRITE",
        "allow",
        10,
        "sandboxed",
        ["filesystem", "artifact"],
    ),
]

TOOL_REGISTRY: dict[str, ToolSpec] = {t.name: t for t in _TOOLS}


def get_tool(name: str) -> ToolSpec | None:
    return TOOL_REGISTRY.get(name)


def list_tools(
    *, side_effect: str | None = None, tag: str | None = None
) -> list[ToolSpec]:
    items = list(TOOL_REGISTRY.values())
    if side_effect is not None:
        items = [t for t in items if t.side_effect == side_effect]
    if tag is not None:
        items = [t for t in items if tag in t.tags]
    return sorted(items, key=lambda t: t.name)


def default_decision(tool_name: str) -> str:
    tool = get_tool(tool_name)
    if tool is None:
        return "ask"
    return tool.approval_label

````markdown
# M9-T003: Reviewer gate + approval inbox

## Milestone
M9: live end-to-end regression test — Spaceship Titanic.

## Goal
Drive the worker to the point where `kaggle_submit` is the next action.
The M6 reviewer gate must fire, writing an `agent_reviews` row and a
pending `human_decisions` row. The decision_api surfaces the pending
decision and the UI Approval Inbox renders it. A human approves via
`kca decisions approve` (M9-T003 only — M9-T004 runs the real submit).

This task assumes **M9-T002 closeout is PASS** with a staged
`submission.csv`.

## Read first

1. M9-T002 closeout
2. `src/worker/reviewer.py`
3. `services/decision_api/app.py`
4. `tools/kca/decisions.py`
5. `supabase/migrations/0006_m6_reviews_spans.sql`
6. `ui/src/pages/ApprovalInbox.tsx`, `ui/src/pages/DecisionGate.tsx`
7. `docs/architecture/m8-ui-shell.md`

## Scope

1. Re-invoke the worker with the staged submission and a
   `kaggle_submit`-bound next action.
2. Confirm the reviewer-gate fires:
   - row written to `agent_reviews`;
   - row written to `human_decisions` with `status='pending'`;
   - event written to `agent_job_events`.
3. Confirm the decision_api `GET /decisions?status=pending` returns the
   row.
4. Confirm the UI Approval Inbox shows the pending decision when run
   locally (`pnpm -C ui dev`, open `/inbox`).
5. Approve via `kca decisions approve --id <decision_id> --note
   "M9-T003 dry approval; real submit happens in T004"`.
6. The approval should **not** trigger a real `kaggle competitions submit`
   here — verify by inspecting the worker stop reason.

## Non-goals

- Do not run a real `kaggle competitions submit`. T004 is the only
  Loop Prompt that does.
- Do not change `services/decision_api/` auth model.
- Do not change `tools/kca/decisions.py` semantics — observe only.
- Do not introduce a new approval policy class.

## Acceptance criteria

- `agent_reviews` row exists for the M9 run.
- `human_decisions` row exists with `status='pending'` then `approved`.
- `agent_job_events` shows the `reviewer_decision` event.
- `kca decisions list --json` shows the approved row.
- `services/decision_api/tests/test_decision_api.py` still passes
  (regression).
- Approval gate did NOT auto-trigger a real Kaggle submit (the closeout
  must state how this was verified — e.g. worker stopped on
  `policy_violation` or `pending_submission`).

## Permissions

- DB read/write via `dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true` only.
- Local UI dev server is allowed.
- No `kaggle competitions submit`.
- `git commit` / `git push` deferred to milestone closeout.

## Closeout format

```
M9-T003 closeout
  agent_reviews.id: <uuid>
  human_decisions.id: <uuid>  status: approved
  agent_job_events: <count> events written (reviewer_decision present)
  decision_api GET /decisions: pending=0 after approve
  UI render verified: YES | NO
  Real submit triggered? NO  (verified via worker stop reason: <reason>)
  Acceptance: PASS | FAIL — link to issue
  Next: M9-T004 BLOCKED on a `decision:confirmed` comment for real submit
```

## Stop condition

Stop after 60 turns. If the reviewer-gate does NOT fire, do NOT continue
to T004 — investigate first.

````

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Claude Code PreToolUse guardrail hook for permissive KCA development.

Policy:
- Allow normal development work without prompts.
- Deny secret access and host-destructive operations.
- Ask only for irreversible or decision-level operations.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def emit(decision: str, reason: str) -> None:
    print(
        json.dumps(
            {
                "hookSpecificOutput": {
                    "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
                    "permissionDecision": decision,
                    "permissionDecisionReason": reason,
                }
            }
        )
    )


def normalize_path(value: str) -> str:
    if not value:
        return ""
    return os.path.expanduser(value).replace("\\", "/")


def path_is_protected(path: str) -> bool:
    """Dev-phase carve-out: project .env, .env.local, .env.development and
    ~/.kaggle/kaggle.json are readable so kca / Claude Code can pick up the
    local DSN and Kaggle test credentials without manual handoffs.
    .env.production and .env.test remain protected — these may contain
    production/staging credentials. SSH / AWS / gcloud / gh OAuth token /
    generic secrets/ dir stay protected.
    """
    p = normalize_path(path)
    protected_fragments = [
        "/secrets/",
        "/.ssh/",
        "/.aws/",
        "/.config/gcloud/",
        "/.config/gh/hosts.yml",
        "/.netrc",
        "/id_rsa",
        "/id_ed25519",
    ]
    protected_names = {
        ".env.production",
        ".env.test",
        ".netrc",
        "id_rsa",
        "id_ed25519",
        "hosts.yml",
    }
    name = Path(p).name
    return name in protected_names or any(
        fragment in p for fragment in protected_fragments
    )


def compact(command: str) -> str:
    return " ".join(command.strip().split())


def bash_decision(command: str) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
    c = compact(command)
    lc = c.lower()

    # Hard deny: host-destructive, privilege escalation, secret
    # exfiltration, and permanent-deletion remote writes. Project .env
    # and ~/.kaggle/kaggle.json are intentionally not in the secret list
    # (dev-phase carve-out — see path_is_protected docstring).
    deny_patterns = [
        (r"\bsudo\b", "Refusing sudo from the agent."),
        (r"\bsu\s+", "Refusing su from the agent."),
        (r"\bdoas\b", "Refusing doas from the agent."),
        (
            r"\brm\s+-rf\s+(/|~|\$HOME)(\s|$)",
            "Refusing recursive deletion of root/home.",
        ),
        (
            r"\brm\s+-rf\s+/\S+",
            "Refusing recursive deletion of absolute filesystem paths.",
        ),
        (r"\bchmod\s+777\b", "Refusing chmod 777."),
        (r"\bchown\s+.*\s+(/|~|\$HOME)\b", "Refusing ownership change on broad paths."),
        (r"\bdd\s+.*\bof=/dev/", "Refusing raw disk write."),
        (r"\bmkfs(\.|\s|$)", "Refusing filesystem formatting command."),
        (r"\bshutdown\b|\breboot\b|\bhalt\b", "Refusing host power command."),
        (r"\bgit\s+push\s+(-f|--force|--force-with-lease)", "Refusing force push."),
        (
            r"\bgit\s+push\b[^|]*?(--delete\b|\s:\S)",
            "Refusing remote branch deletion (preserve GitHub branch history).",
        ),
        (
            r"\bgh\s+(issue|label|release|repo|secret|webhook|ssh-key|gpg-key|cache|run)\s+delete\b",
            "Refusing permanent GitHub deletion (issues / labels / releases / repo / secrets / webhooks / keys / caches / runs).",
        ),
        (
            r"\bgh\s+extension\s+remove\b",
            "Refusing gh extension removal.",
        ),
        (
            r"\bdocker\s+run\b.*\s--privileged\b",
            "Refusing privileged Docker container.",
        ),
        (
            r"\b(cat|less|more|head|tail|grep|rg|awk|sed|xxd|od|strings)\b.*(id_rsa|id_ed25519|\.aws|\.ssh|\.config/gcloud|secrets/|hosts\.yml|\.netrc)",
            "Refusing shell read of protected secrets.",
        ),
        (
            r"\b(curl|wget|scp|rsync)\b.*(id_rsa|id_ed25519|\.aws|\.ssh|secrets/|metadata\.google|169\.254\.169\.254)",
            "Refusing shell exfiltration/metadata access pattern.",
        ),
        (
            r"\b(psql|sqlite3)\b.*\b(drop\s+database|drop\s+schema)\b",
            "Refusing database/schema drop from the agent.",
        ),
    ]
    for pattern, reason in deny_patterns:
        if re.search(pattern, lc, flags=re.IGNORECASE):
            return "deny", reason

    # Ask: irreversible or product/competition decision gates.
    ask_patterns = [
        (
            r"\brm\b",
            "File deletion requires approval unless implemented through an approved cleanup command.",
        ),
        (r"\brmdir\b", "Directory deletion requires approval."),
        (r"\bfind\b.*\s-delete\b", "find -delete requires approval."),
        (r"\bgit\s+clean\b", "git clean requires approval."),
        (r"\bkaggle\s+kernels\s+push\b", "Kaggle kernel push requires human approval."),
        (
            r"\bkaggle\s+datasets\s+(create|version)\b",
            "Kaggle dataset publication requires human approval.",
        ),
        (
            r"\bpython\s+tools/kca/kca\.py\s+kaggle\s+(push|upload)\b",
            "KCA Kaggle publication requires human approval.",
        ),
        (
            r"\bsupabase\s+db\s+(push|reset)\b",
            "Remote/destructive Supabase database operation requires approval.",
        ),
        (
            r"\b(psql|sqlite3)\b.*\b(truncate|delete\s+from)\b",
            "Destructive SQL requires approval.",
        ),
        (
            r"\bdocker\s+compose\s+down\b.*\s-v\b",
            "Docker volume deletion requires approval.",
        ),
    ]
    for pattern, reason in ask_patterns:
        if re.search(pattern, lc, flags=re.IGNORECASE):
            return "ask", reason

    return None, None


def main() -> int:
    try:
        payload = json.load(sys.stdin)
    except Exception as exc:
        emit("deny", f"Guard hook could not parse input: {exc}")
        return 0

    tool = payload.get("tool_name", "")
    tool_input = payload.get("tool_input") or {}

    if tool in {"Read", "Edit", "Write"}:
        file_path = tool_input.get("file_path") or tool_input.get("path") or ""
        if path_is_protected(file_path):
            emit("deny", f"Protected path blocked: {file_path}")
            return 0

    if tool == "Bash":
        command = tool_input.get("command") or ""
        decision, reason = bash_decision(command)
        if decision and reason:
            emit(decision, reason)
            return 0

    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

```

````markdown
# ADR-0006: Configurable approval gates — default allow

Status: accepted  
Date: 2026-05-19  
Decided in: `docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-19-r1.md`  
Supersedes: prior implicit policy of "always require approval for remote writes"

---

## Context

Earlier platform design required human approval for all Kaggle submissions, kernel
pushes, and git pushes. This was chosen conservatively during M0–M2 setup.

The user's actual Kaggle workflow (see `docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-17-r1.md`) is
iterative and fast. Requiring manual approval on every submission adds friction
without meaningfully increasing safety for an experienced user who:
- Has already reviewed the code in the job's experiment run
- Understands the submission mechanics
- Wants the agent to handle routine mechanics autonomously

The main human decision points are **strategic** (switch model, switch approach,
ensemble), not operational (submit file X, push kernel Y).

## Decision

All approval gates are **configurable per project** and **default to allow (no approval required)**.

### Default policy

```json
{
  "approval_gates": {
    "kaggle_submit":    false,
    "kernel_push":      false,
    "dataset_upload":   true,
    "git_push":         false,
    "git_force_push":   true,
    "supabase_migrate": true,
    "delete_artifact":  true
  }
}
```

`true` = requires human approval before executing.  
`false` = agent executes autonomously (logged, auditable, but no pause).

`dataset_upload`, `git_force_push`, `supabase_migrate`, and `delete_artifact` default
to `true` because they are infrequent, higher-blast-radius operations.

### Per-competition override

A competition record can override the project defaults:
```json
{
  "competition_policy": {
    "kaggle_submit":  true,
    "max_daily_submissions": 5
  }
}
```

Useful if a competition has strict submission limits or the user wants to be more
careful during the final days before deadline.

### Per-job override

A job can further restrict (but not loosen) the project/competition policy:
```json
{
  "job_approval_override": {
    "kaggle_submit": true
  }
}
```

Jobs cannot lower gates below what the competition policy sets.

## Implementation

### In `tools/kca/kg.py` (previously `kaggle.py`)

Replace the hard-wired `KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1` env-var gate with a policy lookup:

```python
def _check_approval_gate(operation: str, policy: dict) -> None:
    """Raise ApprovalRequired if the operation needs human approval per policy."""
    approval_gates = policy.get('approval_gates', {})
    requires = approval_gates.get(operation, OPERATION_DEFAULTS[operation])
    if requires:
        raise ApprovalRequired(operation, policy)
```

`OPERATION_DEFAULTS` mirrors the table above. The `KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE` env var is kept
as an emergency override for CI/scripted contexts but is no longer the primary gate.

### In `src/worker/tools.py` (`ToolExecutor`)

`ToolExecutor` receives the job's resolved approval policy and calls `_check_approval_gate`
before executing any REMOTE_WRITE or SUBMISSION tool.

### In `scripts/run_job.py`

Policy resolution order (highest priority first):
1. Per-job `job_approval_override`
2. Competition `competition_policy`
3. Project `approval_gates`
4. Platform defaults (table above)

### In `kca decisions`

When an approval gate fires, the worker:
1. Inserts a `human_decisions` row with `status='pending'`.
2. Logs the decision_id to stderr.
3. Returns `WorkerResult(status='paused')`.

The human resolves with `kca decisions approve --id <id>` or via the future UI.
The job can then be restarted (M4+ resume logic).

## Consequences

- **Positive:** Faster iteration. Agent can run a full research → implement → submit
  cycle without human touch on routine operations.
- **Positive:** Experienced users are not blocked by unnecessary gates.
- **Positive:** All operations are still logged in `agent_job_events` — autonomy does
  not mean invisibility.
- **Negative:** Higher risk of an unintended submission on a fresh competition if the
  user forgets to set `kaggle_submit: true` for that competition.
- **Mitigation:** New competition records should remind the user to review the approval
  policy before the first `submit` job runs. Platform UI (M7) will surface this clearly.
- **Mitigation:** `kca decisions list` still works as an audit trail for all completed
  actions, even auto-approved ones.

## Human intervention points (unchanged)

The following always require human judgment regardless of approval gate settings:
- **Major direction changes:** switch model, switch approach, ensemble strategy.
- **Budget exhaustion:** when `max_cost_usd` is hit, human decides whether to increase.
- **Data policy decisions:** using external data, expanding training set beyond competition data.
- **Final submission selection:** choosing which 1–2 runs to use as final submissions.

These are not gate-able by the platform — they are judgment calls that belong to
the human and are surfaced via the analysis and eval job outputs.

````

# ADR-0016: CTF data model — events, challenges, attempts

## Status

Accepted (M11-T001, 2026-06-09). Lands with
`supabase/migrations/0008_m11_ctf.sql` and `src/db/ctf.py`.

Cross-link: [`docs/evidence/m11/discovery/design-red-team.md`](../evidence/m11/discovery/design-red-team.md),
[`docs/evidence/m11/discovery/legacy-archaeologist.md`](../evidence/m11/discovery/legacy-archaeologist.md),
[`docs/evidence/m11/discovery/requirements-skeptic.md`](../evidence/m11/discovery/requirements-skeptic.md).

## Context

M11 is the first non-Kaggle competition platform on the agent stack.
The CTFtime workflow (planning Q&A, `docs/m11-loop-prompts.md` §at-a-glance)
needs persistent, queryable records for three things:

1. **Events** — which CTFtime-listed event we are participating in, when
   it runs, and where the credentials for it live.
2. **Challenges** — per-event jeopardy items the agent might attempt,
   each optionally bound to a `ctf_scopes` (migration 0001) authorization
   row.
3. **Attempts** — every flag submission, accepted or not, with enough
   identity context that "which credential ran this" is answerable from
   the row alone.

The pre-existing `ctf_scopes` table from migration 0001 covers
authorization (target URLs, local-only flag, expiry). M11 adds the three
tables above; `ctf_scopes` is referenced via an FK from
`ctf_challenges.scope_id` but is otherwise untouched.

## Decision

### 1. Multi-event identity model

```
projects (0001)
  └─ ctf_events  (slug UNIQUE globally; per-project FK)
       └─ ctf_challenges  (UNIQUE (event_id, slug))
            └─ ctf_attempts  (FK to challenge; FK to experiment_runs.id)
```

- `ctf_events.slug` is **globally unique** so that
  `~/.ctf/<slug>.json` credential paths are unambiguous and so the
  `kca ctf event` subcommands can address events by slug alone (no
  `--project` flag for the common case).
- `(event_id, slug)` is unique on `ctf_challenges` so challenge slugs
  scope per-event — two events can both have `web-1`.
- `ctf_challenges.scope_id` is nullable and `ON DELETE SET NULL`: a
  challenge can pre-exist its authorization row (T004 creates
````

+def _redact_tool_input(target_op: str, tool_input: dict) -> dict:
+    """Strip secret-shaped fields from the reviewer-rendered tool_input.
+
+    M11 (ADR-0017): for `flag_submit` the flag value MUST NEVER appear in
+    the reviewer prompt, agent_reviews.rationale, agent_job_events.event_data,
+    or any audit row. The reviewer only needs the event slug, challenge slug,
+    and the flag length to decide.
+    """
+    if not isinstance(tool_input, dict):
+        return tool_input
+    if target_op != "flag_submit":
+        return tool_input
+    redacted: dict[str, Any] = {}
+    for k, v in tool_input.items():
+        if k in _FLAG_INPUT_KEYS:
+            try:
+                length = len(v) if isinstance(v, (str, bytes, list, tuple)) else None
+            except Exception:
+                length = None
+            redacted[k] = {"_redacted": True, "length": length}
+        else:
+            redacted[k] = v
+    return redacted
+
+

```markdown
# ADR-0017: CTF approval gates — `challenge_run`, `flag_submit`, `network_egress`

## Status

Accepted (M11-T002, 2026-06-09). Lands with `.kca/permissions/*.yaml`,
`src/worker/reviewer.py`, `src/worker/worker.py`, `.claude/settings.json`,
and `.claude/hooks/guard_tool.py`.

Cross-links:
- [`docs/evidence/m11/discovery/design-red-team.md`](../evidence/m11/discovery/design-red-team.md)
  — the open question about WHICH LAYER enforces `network_egress` is
  resolved here (`§ Enforcement layer pinning` below).
- [`docs/adr/0006-configurable-approval-gates.md`](0006-configurable-approval-gates.md)
  — operation data shape this ADR extends.
- [`docs/adr/0016-ctf-data-model.md`](0016-ctf-data-model.md) — the
  `ctf_scopes` / `ctf_attempts` rows the gate writes against.

## Context

M11 introduces the first non-Kaggle competition platform on the agent
stack: authorized CTF / lab workflows. Two new high-blast-radius
operations need a reviewer gate:

1. **`challenge_run`** — executing a solver against an authorized CTF
   target (local in-scope service OR a URL in
   `ctf_scopes.target_urls`).
2. **`flag_submit`** — submitting a flag string to the event's API.

A third operation, **`network_egress`**, exists to catch worker-issued
HTTP calls whose host falls outside the union of
`ctf_scopes.target_urls` rows for the current project. Unlike
`challenge_run` and `flag_submit`, `network_egress` is a *deny-by-default
silent backstop*, not a gate that fires for an intentional action.

Without these three operations, the platform has only `kaggle_submit` /
`kernel_push` style gates, which are leaderboard-shaped and assume the
target URL is implicit (`kaggle.com`). CTF events have per-event
target URLs (the picoCTF case, the bbbctf case), and the wrong target +
the wrong flag would be a critical incident with no leaderboard
infrastructure to limit blast radius.

## Decision

Add three operations to `.kca/permissions/*.yaml`, extend the reviewer
trigger set, and wire a tool-name → target-op mapping in the worker so
synthetic CTF tools surface as the correct operation string on the
`agent_reviews` row.

### 1. Operations + defaults

| Operation | `default.yaml` | `permissive-dev.yaml` | `competition-runner.yaml` | `audit_required` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `challenge_run` | `ask` | `ask` (no dev auto-allow) | `ask`, `conditional_allow.when_in_scope: allow` | `true` |
| `flag_submit` | `ask` | `ask` | `ask` (no conditional allow) | `true` |
| `network_egress` | `deny`, `conditional_allow.when_in_scope: ask` | same | same | `true` |

Rationale for the asymmetry:
- `challenge_run` may move to `allow` under `competition-runner` when the
  target URL is in `ctf_scopes.target_urls` — the human has already
  authorized the scope row, and gating every solver attempt would
  destroy the workflow.
- `flag_submit` stays on `ask` regardless of profile. Flag submission is
  the highest-blast-radius op (wrong flag from wrong account = team
  ban; correct flag with wrong credential file = audit gap matching the
  kkr.py replay failure mode). No auto-allow path.
- `network_egress` defaults to `deny`. The only relaxation path is
  `conditional_allow.when_in_scope: ask` — if the request host matches a
  `ctf_scopes.target_urls` row, the gate fires for human approval
  instead of silently denying. To widen access, the human edits the
  scope row, not the policy.

### 2. `conditional_allow.when_in_scope` semantics

`when_in_scope` is consulted by the worker before raising
`ApprovalRequired`. The check shape (M11-T003 / T005 implement the
worker side; T002 records only the policy YAML):

1. The worker resolves the project's `ctf_scopes` rows that are not
   expired (`expires_at` IS NULL OR `expires_at` > now()).
2. The union of `target_urls` (textarray on each row) is computed.
3. For `challenge_run` / `network_egress`, the call's destination URL
   host is compared to that union (exact-host match for M11; subdomain
   match is filed as a follow-up).
4. If matched, `conditional_allow.when_in_scope` is honored:
   `allow` → run without a gate; `ask` → raise `ApprovalRequired` and
   fire the reviewer.
5. If unmatched: fall back to `default_decision`.

### 3. Enforcement layer pinning

The design-red-team report
(`docs/evidence/m11/discovery/design-red-team.md` § `open_disagreements`
4th bullet) raised the open question: which layer enforces
`network_egress`? Three candidates exist:

- **Reviewer-gate** (`src/worker/reviewer.py`): fires when the worker
  raises `ApprovalRequired(operation="network_egress")`.
- **Hook layer** (`.claude/hooks/guard_tool.py`): denies known-bad
  hosts at Claude Code's PreToolUse step.
- **HTTP-client interceptor** (httpx middleware): wraps every outbound
  request from the worker.

**Decision (binding for M11):**

1. **Primary authority: the reviewer-gate.** When the worker is about
   to issue a request whose host is outside the in-scope union, it
   raises `ApprovalRequired("network_egress", ...)`. The reviewer-gate
   is the deny-default authority. This is what `.kca/permissions/*.yaml`
   pins.
2. **Secondary defense: the hook layer.** `.claude/hooks/guard_tool.py`
   denies known-bad hosts (metadata services, CTF credential paths)
   even before the reviewer fires. This catches shell-level egress
   attempts (`curl`, `wget`, `scp`, `rsync`) and direct Read/Edit of
   `~/.ctf/*.json`.
3. **Out of scope for M11: the httpx interceptor.** A per-request
   httpx middleware that consults `ctf_scopes.target_urls` on every
   outbound HTTP call is *the right long-term answer* (it survives
   subprocess and direct-Python paths the worker doesn't know about),
   but it requires touching `tools/kca/research_fetch.py` and every
   other httpx-using surface. Filed as a follow-up: `M12 / M13
   network-egress-interceptor`.

The known consequence of the layer choice: a subprocess `curl` issued
from inside a `bash` tool call bypasses both the reviewer-gate and the
hook layer's regex (for hosts not in `deny_patterns`). M11 mitigates by
hard-asking on every `bash` call under `default.yaml` and by the M11-T005
solver flow running `docker-compose up` against a *local* network only —
the live event egress is gated to T007's single approved call.

### 4. Audit row shape

For each gated operation, the worker writes:

- `agent_reviews` row with `target_op` ∈
  {`challenge_run`, `flag_submit`, `network_egress`} and the reviewer's
  `verdict` / `rationale`. For `flag_submit`, **the flag value never
  appears** in `rationale`, `evidence`, or the rendered prompt — the
  reviewer module's `_redact_tool_input` replaces the flag with
  `{"_redacted": true, "length": N}` before prompt rendering.
- `human_decisions` row with `status='pending'` then `approved` /
  `denied`. The decision_api surfaces it; the UI Approval Inbox
  renders it; T006 exercises the round-trip.
- `agent_job_events` rows for `reviewer_decision`, `approval_resume`,
  and `reviewer_reject` / `reviewer_abstain` as appropriate (same
  shape as M9 / M10).
- `agent_tool_audit` row via
  `tools/kca/agent/audit.log_policy_decision` recording the resolved
  policy decision. For `network_egress` denies, this is the audit row
  that captures the attempt — no agent_reviews row is written if the
  resolution short-circuits at `default_decision: deny` (the human
  must widen `ctf_scopes.target_urls` to even attempt the call).

No new `agent_tool_audit` columns are added in M11-T002; the existing
shape captures `tool`, `operation`, `decision`, `policy_profile`,
`mode`, `audit_required`, `args` (with the same flag-redaction posture
applied via `args.flag = {"_redacted": True, ...}` when `tool ==
"flag_submit"`).

### 5. Alternatives + dropped capabilities

Cross-link
[`docs/evidence/m11/discovery/design-red-team.md`](../evidence/m11/discovery/design-red-team.md)
for the full design-red-team analysis. Summary of what M11 explicitly
*did not* adopt:

- **Single `ctf_op` operation with sub-action discriminator** —
  considered; rejected because the policy YAMLs already key on
  per-operation rows and a discriminator would push the
  ask/deny/conditional-allow logic into worker code.
- **Per-request httpx interceptor instead of reviewer-gate** —
  deferred to M12/M13 as noted above.
- **Auto-widen `ctf_scopes.target_urls` on a reviewer-approved
  `network_egress`** — rejected. The reviewer can approve a one-shot
  egress without widening the persistent scope row; the human edits
  the scope row to widen access for future calls.
- **A `flag_submit_dry_run` operation distinct from `flag_submit`** —
  rejected. The `--dry-run=False` flag on the kca CLI is the gate;
  dry-runs do not raise the operation.
- **Per-challenge rate-limit as a policy field** — out of scope. The
  red-team report flagged this as a dropped capability; it is filed
  as a follow-up against `ctf_scopes` schema extensions.

## Consequences

- **Positive:** The CTF workflow has a clean three-op surface that
  maps 1:1 to the reviewer-gate / audit chain that already exists
  for `kaggle_submit` / `kernel_push`.
- **Positive:** The flag value never reaches the reviewer prompt or
  any audit row — eliminates a leakage path that would otherwise
  appear in `agent_reviews.rationale` (LLM-generated text) and in
  the OTEL span for the reviewer call.
- **Positive:** `network_egress` deny-by-default makes the wrong host
  a hard error rather than a silent leak. The kkr.py replay failure
  mode (ambient credential + wrong endpoint) is structurally
  prevented for new CTF events.
- **Negative:** A subprocess `curl` from inside `bash` can bypass the
  reviewer-gate. Mitigation: `bash` is `ask` under `default.yaml` and
  every bash invocation is audited. M12/M13 will harden via httpx
  interceptor.
- **Negative:** The `conditional_allow.when_in_scope` field is a new
  YAML shape; tools that read the policy file (the worker, the UI's
  policy preview) need to handle it. M11-T002 lands the YAML; the
  worker-side check is wired in M11-T005.

## Implementation notes (for M11-T003+ wiring)

- The worker resolves `tool_name → target_op` via the
  `_TOOL_TO_TARGET_OP` map in `src/worker/worker.py`. Adding a new CTF
  tool means adding a row there; the reviewer trigger set in
  `src/worker/reviewer.py::DEFAULT_TRIGGER_OPS` already covers the
  three operation strings.
- The reviewer-rendered prompt is built by
  `src/worker/reviewer.py::_render_prompt`, which calls
  `_redact_tool_input` before serializing `tool_input` to JSON. For
  `flag_submit`, fields named `flag` / `flag_value` / `submission` are
  replaced with `{"_redacted": True, "length": N}`. The reviewer
  receives event_slug + challenge_slug + flag_length; this is
  sufficient context for the abstain/approve/reject decision.
- `~/.ctf/<slug>.json` files are denied at the hook layer for
  `Read` / `Edit` / `Write` tools and for shell `cat|less|...|curl|wget`
  reads. The Python `tools/kca/ctf.py::_load_event_credentials`
  call-site (T003) reads via Python `open()` from inside the kca
  process, which the hook layer does not intercept (this is the
  designed seam).

```
