```markdown
# kca command reference

`kca` is the stable execution layer the agent calls via Bash. Each subcommand declares a
side-effect level so the host (skills, hooks, humans) can decide whether to allow, gate,
or block it.

All commands emit a single JSON object to stdout. Exit codes: `0` ok, `1` runtime error,
`2` blocked (gated remote op without approval).

## Side-effect levels

| Level         | Meaning                                          | Default policy                                              |
|---------------|--------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| `READ_ONLY`   | No writes anywhere                               | Always allowed                                              |
| `LOCAL_WRITE` | Writes only inside the repo/workspace            | Allowed, logged                                             |
| `REMOTE_WRITE`| Writes to external service (Kaggle kernel push, dataset upload) | Requires `KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1` + human approval |
| `SUBMISSION`  | Kaggle competition submission                    | Requires `KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1` + explicit human approval     |

## Command table

| Command                       | Side-effect    | Wraps legacy tool         | Notes                                       |
|-------------------------------|----------------|---------------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| `kca nb to-py`                | `LOCAL_WRITE`  | `tools/legacy/nb2py.py`   | `.ipynb` → percent-format `.py`             |
| `kca nb to-ipynb`             | `LOCAL_WRITE`  | `tools/legacy/py2nb.py`   | percent-format `.py` → `.ipynb`             |
| `kca run init`                | `LOCAL_WRITE`  | (native)                  | Creates `runs/<comp>/<run_id>/`             |
| `kca run record-metric`       | `LOCAL_WRITE`  | (native)                  | Appends to `metrics.json`                   |
| `kca run list`                | `READ_ONLY`    | (native)                  |                                             |
| `kca kaggle submit`           | `SUBMISSION`   | _will wrap_ `kkr.py submit` | Blocked without `KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1` (stub)|
| `kca kaggle push`             | `REMOTE_WRITE` | _will wrap_ `kkr.py push`   | Blocked without `KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1` (stub)|
| `kca kaggle upload`           | `REMOTE_WRITE` | _will wrap_ Kaggle dataset upload | Blocked without `KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1` (stub) |
| `kca kaggle watch`            | `READ_ONLY`    | _will wrap_ `kkr.py watch`  | Stub                                       |
| `kca kaggle fetch`            | `READ_ONLY`    | _will wrap_ `kkr.py fetch`  | Stub                                       |
| `kca kaggle list`             | `READ_ONLY`    | _will wrap_ `kkr.py list`   | Stub                                       |
| `kca eval score`              | `READ_ONLY`    | (native, planned)         | Stub                                        |
| `kca eval compare`            | `READ_ONLY`    | (native, planned)         | Stub                                        |
| `kca workspace init`          | `LOCAL_WRITE`  | `git worktree add`        | Creates detached-HEAD worktree under `.workspaces/<job_id>/` |
| `kca workspace clean`         | `LOCAL_WRITE`  | `git worktree remove`     | Removes worktree; best-effort DB update     |
| `kca workspace list`          | `READ_ONLY`    | `git worktree list`       | Lists active workspaces under `.workspaces/` |
| `kca decisions list`          | `READ_ONLY`    | (native)                  | List pending human approval requests        |
| `kca decisions approve`       | `LOCAL_WRITE`  | (native)                  | Approve a pending decision                  |
| `kca decisions deny`          | `LOCAL_WRITE`  | (native)                  | Deny a pending decision                     |

## Safety

Remote-write and submission commands are guarded by **two independent layers**:

### Layer A — kca internal gate (`tools/kca/kg.py`)

`REMOTE_WRITE` and `SUBMISSION` commands check the env var `KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE`:

- Unset / not `"1"` → emit `{"ok": false, "error": "remote operation requires KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1 and human approval", ...}` and exit `2`.
- `KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1` → print `[kca] REMOTE OPERATION: ...` to stderr and proceed (currently stubs).

This makes silent execution in an autonomous loop impossible: the agent must set the env
var explicitly per shell, and a human is expected to be on the other side of the prompt.

### Layer B — `.claude/settings.json` hook layer

`Bash(python tools/kca/kca.py kaggle submit*)`, `kaggle push*`, and `kaggle upload*` are
listed under `permissions.ask` — Claude must prompt the human before invoking them.

Direct CLI bypass routes are listed under `permissions.deny` (hard block):

- `Bash(kaggle competitions submit*)`
- `Bash(kaggle kernels push*)`
- `Bash(kaggle datasets create*)`, `Bash(kaggle datasets version*)`
- `Bash(python tools/legacy/kkr.py submit*)`, `Bash(python tools/legacy/kkr.py push*)`
- `Bash(tools/legacy/kkr.py submit*)`, `Bash(tools/legacy/kkr.py push*)`

Either layer alone stops accidental submission. Both layers in place is the design.

### Approval event recording (M2-T005)

When Layer A blocks a `kaggle submit | push | upload`, kca **also** inserts a
`pending` row in `human_decisions` (best-effort — DB unavailability never
prevents the refusal). The envelope then includes:

- `approval_request_id` (uuid) — the new row's id, or absent if DB write failed
- `approval_recorded` — `true`/`false`
- `approval_warning` — present only on failure, with a short reason

This is the first link between kca's runtime gates and the control plane.
Future milestones (M3+) may move the gate from env-var to "an approved row
exists for this attempt".

## Artifact storage

Artifact bytes live in the local filesystem under
`runs/<comp>/<run_id>/artifacts/<filename>` in M2. The `artifacts.storage_path`
column uses a URI scheme so the M3 migration to Supabase Storage is a
1:1 path rewrite without schema changes. See **ADR-0008** (`docs/adr/0008-artifact-storage-local-first.md`).

## Skill invocation reference

Skills are prompt templates in `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`. They tell Claude how to use
kca; they never call each other and never call kca directly themselves.

| Skill      | Invocation   | Typical kca commands called                              |
|------------|--------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| `/kg-nb`   | `/kg-nb`     | `kca nb to-py`, `kca nb to-ipynb`                        |
```

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from _types import SideEffect

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent
LEGACY_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "tools" / "legacy"


def emit_json(
    ok: bool, side_effect: SideEffect, payload: dict[str, Any] | None = None
) -> None:
    out = {"ok": bool(ok), "side_effect": side_effect.value}
    if payload:
        out.update(payload)
    print(json.dumps(out, ensure_ascii=False))


def warn(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"[kca] {msg}", file=sys.stderr)


def stub_emit(command: str, side_effect: SideEffect) -> int:
    warn(f"NOT-IMPLEMENTED: {command} (stub)")
    print(
        json.dumps(
            {
                "ok": True,
                "stub": True,
                "command": command,
                "side_effect": side_effect.value,
            },
            ensure_ascii=False,
        )
    )
    return 0


def run_legacy(cmd: list[str]) -> tuple[bool, dict[str, Any], str]:
    """Run a legacy tool from LEGACY_DIR; return (ok, parsed_json_or_empty, stderr_text).

    First element of cmd is the path to the legacy script, relative to REPO_ROOT.
    """
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, *[str(REPO_ROOT / cmd[0])], *cmd[1:]],
            cwd=str(LEGACY_DIR),
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=False,
        )
    except FileNotFoundError as e:
        return False, {}, str(e)

    stdout = (proc.stdout or "").strip()
    parsed: dict[str, Any] = {}
    if stdout:
        try:
            parsed = json.loads(stdout)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            parsed = {"raw_stdout": stdout}
    ok = (proc.returncode == 0) and bool(parsed.get("ok", True))
    return ok, parsed, (proc.stderr or "")

"""kca DB access layer (psycopg3, sync).

Side-effect classification:
  - Operations against a local Supabase stack are LOCAL_WRITE.
  - Operations against a remote Postgres are REMOTE_WRITE and require
    both KCA_DB_TARGET=remote and KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1.

Env contract (set in .env, loaded automatically via python-dotenv if installed):
  - SUPABASE_DB_URL         : libpq conninfo string (preferred).
  - KCA_DB_TARGET           : "local" (default) or "remote".
  - KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE        : "1" to allow remote/submission operations.
  - SUPABASE_DB_HOST/PORT/USER/PASSWORD/DB : fallback discrete vars.

See env.example in the repo root for the full template.

Module is importable without a live DB — connections happen lazily.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Iterable

# Load .env from repo root automatically if python-dotenv is installed.
# This is a no-op when .env doesn't exist or dotenv isn't installed.
try:
    from dotenv import load_dotenv as _load_dotenv

    _load_dotenv(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / ".env", override=False)
except ImportError:
    pass

try:
    import psycopg
    from psycopg import sql  # noqa: F401  # re-exported for callers
    from psycopg.rows import dict_row
except ImportError as e:  # pragma: no cover
    psycopg = None  # type: ignore
    _import_err = e
else:
    _import_err = None

from _types import SideEffect

__all__ = [
    "RemoteOperationBlocked",
    "DBNotConfigured",
    "DEFAULT_PROJECT_ID",
    "current_side_effect",
    "get_conn",
    "ensure_default_project",
    "ensure_competition",
    # M2 legacy (still used by tools/kca/run.py against the 0001/0002 schema)
    "create_experiment_m2",
    "create_experiment_run",
    "record_metric_m2",
    "list_runs_m2",
    "find_run_by_dir",
    "insert_approval_request",
    "get_decision",
    "list_job_events",
    # M3 job lifecycle
    "create_job",
    "get_job",
    "lease_job",
    "update_job",
    "append_job_event",
    "list_jobs",
    "list_pending_decisions",
    "resolve_decision",
    # M4 competition/experiment/run/submission (0004 schema)
    "get_competition_by_slug",
    "update_competition",
    "list_competitions",
    "create_experiment",
    "get_experiment",
    "list_experiments",
    "create_run",
    "update_run",
    "record_metric",
    "list_runs",
    "create_submission",
    "update_submission",
    # M5 research / artifacts / citations (0005 schema)
    "create_research_item",
    "get_research_item",
    "list_research_items",
    "find_research_by_url",
    "attach_artifact",
    "cite_research",
    "list_citations",
    # M6 reviews + telemetry (0006 schema)
    "create_review",
    "get_review",
    "list_reviews",
    "find_review_for_op",
    "record_span",
    "list_spans",
    "set_job_trace",
    # M8 tool audit (0007 schema)
    "insert_tool_audit",
]


DEFAULT_PROJECT_ID = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001"
_ENV_TARGET = "KCA_DB_TARGET"
_ENV_ALLOW_REMOTE = "KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE"
_ENV_URL = "SUPABASE_DB_URL"


class RemoteOperationBlocked(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when KCA_DB_TARGET=remote without KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1."""


class DBNotConfigured(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when no DB connection info is available."""


def current_side_effect() -> SideEffect:
    """Side effect for DB operations under the current env."""
    target = os.environ.get(_ENV_TARGET, "local").strip().lower()
    return SideEffect.REMOTE_WRITE if target == "remote" else SideEffect.LOCAL_WRITE


def _check_remote_gate() -> None:
    target = os.environ.get(_ENV_TARGET, "local").strip().lower()
    if target == "remote" and os.environ.get(_ENV_ALLOW_REMOTE) != "1":
        raise RemoteOperationBlocked(
            f"{_ENV_TARGET}=remote requires {_ENV_ALLOW_REMOTE}=1 and human approval"
        )


def _conninfo() -> str:
    url = os.environ.get(_ENV_URL)
    if url:
        return url
    host = os.environ.get("SUPABASE_DB_HOST")
    if not host:
        raise DBNotConfigured(
            f"Set {_ENV_URL} (preferred) or SUPABASE_DB_HOST + related vars."
        )
    port = os.environ.get("SUPABASE_DB_PORT", "54322")
    user = os.environ.get("SUPABASE_DB_USER", "postgres")
    password = os.environ.get("SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD", "postgres")
    dbname = os.environ.get("SUPABASE_DB", "postgres")
    return f"postgres://{user}:{password}@{host}:{port}/{dbname}"


def get_conn() -> "psycopg.Connection":
    """Open a new psycopg connection. Caller owns close()."""
    if psycopg is None:
        raise DBNotConfigured(f"psycopg not installed: {_import_err}")
    _check_remote_gate()
    return psycopg.connect(_conninfo(), row_factory=dict_row, autocommit=False)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Schema operations
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def ensure_default_project(conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None) -> str:
    """Return the bootstrap project id; create the row if absent.

    The row is normally inserted by migration 0002. This is a defensive
    no-op upsert so kca works against a DB that was partially migrated.
    """
    return _with_conn(conn, _ensure_default_project)

"""M1 smoke tests for the kca CLI.

Each test invokes kca via subprocess so the CLI surface is what's exercised,
not the internals. No network. Uses tmp_path for filesystem isolation.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
KCA = [sys.executable, str(REPO_ROOT / "tools" / "kca" / "kca.py")]

# As of M2-T004, `kca run` is DB-first. Tests that exercise it skip when no DB
# is configured. Set KCA_DB_TARGET=local + SUPABASE_DB_URL to enable them.
requires_db = pytest.mark.skipif(
    not (os.environ.get("KCA_DB_TARGET") and os.environ.get("SUPABASE_DB_URL")),
    reason="kca run tests need KCA_DB_TARGET=local + SUPABASE_DB_URL (M2-T004 DB-first).",
)


def _run(
    *argv: str, env: dict | None = None, cwd: Path | None = None
) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    full_env = os.environ.copy()
    if env is not None:
        for k, v in env.items():
            if v is None:
                full_env.pop(k, None)
            else:
                full_env[k] = v
    return subprocess.run(
        [*KCA, *argv],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=False,
        env=full_env,
        cwd=str(cwd or REPO_ROOT),
    )


def _parse_json(proc: subprocess.CompletedProcess) -> dict:
    stdout = (proc.stdout or "").strip()
    assert stdout, f"empty stdout; stderr={proc.stderr!r}"
    return json.loads(stdout)


def test_nb_to_ipynb_roundtrip(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    src = tmp_path / "src.py"
    src.write_text(
        "# %% [markdown]\n# Hello\n\n# %%\nx = 1\nprint('hi', x)\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    dst = tmp_path / "out.ipynb"
    proc = _run(
        "nb", "to-ipynb", str(src), "--output", str(dst), "--keep-markdown", "--json"
    )
    assert proc.returncode == 0, proc.stderr
    payload = _parse_json(proc)
    assert payload["ok"] is True
    assert payload["side_effect"] == "LOCAL_WRITE"
    assert dst.exists()


def test_nb_to_py_roundtrip(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    # Make an ipynb via to-ipynb first.
    src = tmp_path / "src.py"
    src.write_text("# %% [markdown]\n# Hi\n\n# %%\nx = 2\n", encoding="utf-8")
    ipynb = tmp_path / "round.ipynb"
    p1 = _run(
        "nb", "to-ipynb", str(src), "--output", str(ipynb), "--keep-markdown", "--json"
    )
    assert p1.returncode == 0

def _with_conn(conn, fn, *args, **kwargs):
    """Call fn(conn, *args) using the provided conn or a freshly opened one.

    When this function opens the connection, it also closes it.
    """
    if conn is not None:
        return fn(conn, *args, **kwargs)
    c = get_conn()
    try:
        return fn(c, *args, **kwargs)
    finally:
        c.close()

"""kca ctf: authorized CTF / lab workflow CLI surface (M11-T003).

Subcommand surface:

  kca ctf event {register, list, info}
  kca ctf challenge {add, fetch, list, info}
  kca ctf scope {set, list, verify}
  kca ctf solver run
  kca ctf flag submit

Side-effect classification (see COMMANDS.md):

  - `event register|list|info`         LOCAL_WRITE / READ_ONLY
  - `challenge add|list|info`          LOCAL_WRITE / READ_ONLY
  - `challenge fetch`                  REMOTE_WRITE — KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1
                                       + dangerouslyDisableSandbox + scope match
  - `scope set|list|verify`            LOCAL_WRITE / READ_ONLY
  - `solver run`                       LOCAL_WRITE or SUBMISSION-class. The
                                       --reviewer-gate flag wires the worker's
                                       `challenge_run` target_op (see
                                       src/worker/worker.py::_TOOL_TO_TARGET_OP).
                                       --dry-run never fires the gate.
  - `flag submit`                      SUBMISSION. --dry-run never reads the
                                       flag value and never hits the network;
                                       without --dry-run the flag is read from
                                       --flag-file and is NEVER printed.

Credential / secret discipline:

  - `_load_event_credentials(event_slug)` is the **single allow-listed
    call-site** for the guard_tool deny exception added in M11-T002
    (`.claude/hooks/guard_tool.py` denies any Read/Edit/Write under
    ~/.ctf/). It reads either:
      1) ~/.ctf/<slug>.json (object with `username`, `token`,
         optional `team_id`), or
      2) CTF_<EVENT>_USERNAME + CTF_<EVENT>_TOKEN env vars
         (with optional CTF_<EVENT>_TEAM_ID).
    The helper returns a dict with boolean-presence flags only when
    used in stdout-bound paths; the raw values stay local to the
    POSTing function in `flag submit` and are dropped from memory
    immediately after.

  - The flag value is read from --flag-file. `cmd_flag_submit` opens
    the file, computes its length, and (in non-dry-run paths) hands
    the bytes directly to the request body builder. The flag is
    never logged, never `print()`ed, never added to a JSON envelope.
    Only `flag_length` and `accepted=true|false` + http status leave
    this function.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import datetime as _dt
import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Iterable
from urllib.parse import urlparse

from _types import EXIT_BLOCKED, EXIT_OK, EXIT_RUNTIME, SideEffect

_GATE_ENV = "KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE"

# Cross-link: this module is the SINGLE intended caller of paths under
# ~/.ctf/. Any other read site is denied at the hook layer (M11-T002).
_CTF_CRED_DIR = Path.home() / ".ctf"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Small helpers (mirrors competition.py / kg.py emit pattern)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _jsonable(v: Any) -> Any:
    if isinstance(v, dict):
        return {k: _jsonable(vv) for k, vv in v.items()}
    if hasattr(v, "isoformat"):
        return v.isoformat()
    if isinstance(v, list):
        return [_jsonable(x) for x in v]
    return (
        v
        if (v is None or isinstance(v, (str, int, float, bool, list, dict)))
        else str(v)
    )


def _emit(payload: dict) -> None:
    print(json.dumps({k: _jsonable(v) for k, v in payload.items()}, ensure_ascii=False))


def _load_db_ctf():
    # `src/db/ctf.py` adds its own sys.path entries so the inner `db`
    # module resolves the same way it does from any other kca subcommand.
    repo_root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
    if str(repo_root) not in sys.path:
        sys.path.insert(0, str(repo_root))
    import src.db.ctf as _ctf  # noqa: E402

    return _ctf


def _load_db():
    import db as _db  # noqa: E402

    return _db


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Credential loading — the allow-listed call-site for ~/.ctf/<slug>.json
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class CredentialsMissing(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when neither the file nor env-var path yields credentials."""


def _load_event_credentials(event_slug: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Read CTF credentials for `event_slug`.

    Lookup order:
      1) ~/.ctf/<event_slug>.json — JSON object with at least
         `username` and `token`, optional `team_id`.
      2) CTF_<EVENT>_USERNAME + CTF_<EVENT>_TOKEN env vars,
         optional CTF_<EVENT>_TEAM_ID. `<EVENT>` is `event_slug`
         upper-cased with `-` → `_`.

    Returns a dict::

        {
          "source":   "file" | "env",
          "has_username": bool,
          "has_token":    bool,
          "has_team_id":  bool,
          "_username":    str,        # raw — never to be echoed
          "_token":       str,        # raw — never to be echoed
          "_team_id":     str | None, # raw — never to be echoed
        }

    Callers MUST only forward the boolean-presence fields to anything
    that could end up in stdout / stderr / an audit row / a JSON
    envelope. The underscored fields are intended for in-memory use
    inside the same function call and should be dropped immediately
    after the HTTP request body is built.
    """
    if not event_slug:
        raise CredentialsMissing("event_slug is required")

    # Path 1: file under ~/.ctf/
    cred_path = _CTF_CRED_DIR / f"{event_slug}.json"
    if cred_path.exists():
        try:
            data = json.loads(cred_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
            raise CredentialsMissing(
                f"~/.ctf/{event_slug}.json is not valid JSON: "
                f"{type(exc).__name__}"
            ) from exc
        username = data.get("username")
        token = data.get("token")
        team_id = data.get("team_id")
        if not (username and token):
            raise CredentialsMissing(
                f"~/.ctf/{event_slug}.json missing 'username' or 'token' "
                f"(team_id is optional)"
            )
        return {
            "source": "file",
            "has_username": True,
            "has_token": True,
            "has_team_id": bool(team_id),
            "_username": username,
            "_token": token,
            "_team_id": team_id,
        }

    # Path 2: env vars
    env_key = event_slug.upper().replace("-", "_")
    u = os.environ.get(f"CTF_{env_key}_USERNAME")
    t = os.environ.get(f"CTF_{env_key}_TOKEN")
    team = os.environ.get(f"CTF_{env_key}_TEAM_ID")
    if u and t:
        return {
            "source": "env",
            "has_username": True,
            "has_token": True,
            "has_team_id": bool(team),
            "_username": u,
            "_token": t,
            "_team_id": team,
        }

    raise CredentialsMissing(
        f"no credentials for event '{event_slug}': expected "
        f"~/.ctf/{event_slug}.json OR CTF_{env_key}_USERNAME + "
        f"CTF_{env_key}_TOKEN env vars"
    )


def _safe_cred_presence(creds: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return only the boolean-presence + source fields from a creds dict.

    Anything passed through this strip is safe to put in stdout / JSON
    envelopes / audit rows.
    """
    return {
        "source": creds.get("source"),
        "has_username": bool(creds.get("has_username")),
        "has_token": bool(creds.get("has_token")),
        "has_team_id": bool(creds.get("has_team_id")),
    }


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Scope helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _parse_target_urls(raw: str | None) -> list[str]:
    if not raw:
        return []
    return [u.strip() for u in raw.split(",") if u.strip()]


def _scope_covers_url(scope_row: dict, url: str) -> bool:
    """Return True iff `url`'s host matches any host in
    scope_row['target_urls'] AND the scope has not expired.

    `target_urls` is a JSONB list of fully-qualified URLs (with scheme).
    Match is on host equality (host-only; the path / query of the
    scope row's URL is ignored for the "covers" check so that
    a scope `https://event.example/api/submit` covers any path on
    event.example).
    """
    if not url:
        return False
    expires_at = scope_row.get("expires_at")
    if expires_at:
        now = _dt.datetime.now(_dt.timezone.utc)
        # tolerate naive datetimes by assuming UTC
        if hasattr(expires_at, "tzinfo") and expires_at.tzinfo is None:
            expires_at = expires_at.replace(tzinfo=_dt.timezone.utc)
        if now > expires_at:
            return False
    target_urls = scope_row.get("target_urls") or []
    if isinstance(target_urls, str):
        try:
            target_urls = json.loads(target_urls)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            return False
    target_hosts = set()
    for tu in target_urls:
        try:
            h = urlparse(tu).hostname
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            h = None
        if h:
            target_hosts.add(h.lower())
    try:
        h = urlparse(url).hostname
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        h = None
    if not h:
        return False
    return h.lower() in target_hosts


def _list_scopes(conn) -> list[dict]:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM ctf_scopes ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 200"
        )
        rows = cur.fetchall()
    return [dict(r) for r in rows]


def _get_scope_by_name(conn, name: str) -> dict | None:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM ctf_scopes WHERE name = %s LIMIT 1",
            (name,),
        )
        row = cur.fetchone()
    return dict(row) if row else None

def cmd_event_register(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    se = SideEffect.LOCAL_WRITE
    slug = args.slug
    name = args.name
    try:
        _db = _load_db()
        _ctf = _load_db_ctf()
        project_id = _db.ensure_default_project()
        event_id = _ctf.register_event(
            project_id=project_id,
            slug=slug,
            name=name,
            ctftime_event_id=args.ctftime_id,
            event_url=args.url,
            start_at=args.start_at,
            end_at=args.end_at,
            credentials_ref=args.credentials_ref,
        )
    except Exception as exc:
        _emit(
            {
                "ok": False,
                "error": f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}",
                "command": "ctf event register",
                "side_effect": se.value,
            }
        )
        return EXIT_RUNTIME
    _emit(
        {
            "ok": True,
            "command": "ctf event register",
            "side_effect": se.value,
            "event_id": event_id,
            "slug": slug,
            "name": name,
        }
    )
    return EXIT_OK


def cmd_event_list(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    se = SideEffect.READ_ONLY
    events: list[dict] = []
    try:
        _ctf = _load_db_ctf()
        rows = _ctf.list_events()
        for r in rows:
            events.append(
                {
                    "id": str(r.get("id", "")),
                    "slug": r.get("slug"),
                    "name": r.get("name"),
                    "ctftime_event_id": r.get("ctftime_event_id"),
                    "event_url": r.get("event_url"),
                    "scoring": r.get("scoring"),
                    "credentials_ref": r.get("credentials_ref"),
                    "start_at": _jsonable(r.get("start_at")),
                    "end_at": _jsonable(r.get("end_at")),
                }
            )
    except Exception:
        # Graceful degrade — empty list when DB unavailable.
        events = []
    _emit(
        {
            "ok": True,
            "command": "ctf event list",
            "side_effect": se.value,
            "events": events,
        }
    )
    return EXIT_OK


def _get_event_by_slug(conn, slug: str) -> dict | None:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT * FROM ctf_events WHERE slug = %s LIMIT 1", (slug,))
        row = cur.fetchone()
    return dict(row) if row else None


def cmd_event_info(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:

def cmd_challenge_add(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    se = SideEffect.LOCAL_WRITE
    try:
        _db = _load_db()
        _ctf = _load_db_ctf()
        conn = _db.get_conn()
        try:
            event = _get_event_by_slug(conn, args.event)
            if event is None:
                _emit(
                    {
                        "ok": False,
                        "error": f"no event with slug={args.event!r}; "
                        f"run `kca ctf event register` first",
                        "command": "ctf challenge add",
                        "side_effect": se.value,
                    }
                )
                return EXIT_RUNTIME
            scope_id = None
            if args.scope:
                scope = _get_scope_by_name(conn, args.scope)
                if scope is None:
                    _emit(
                        {
                            "ok": False,
                            "error": f"no scope with name={args.scope!r}; "
                            f"run `kca ctf scope set` first",
                            "command": "ctf challenge add",
                            "side_effect": se.value,
                        }
                    )
                    return EXIT_RUNTIME
                scope_id = str(scope["id"])
            challenge_id = _ctf.add_challenge(
                event_id=str(event["id"]),
                slug=args.slug,
                name=args.name,
                category=args.category,
                points=args.points,
                description=args.description,
                expected_flag_format=args.expected_flag_format,
                attachments_path=args.attachments_path,
                remote_endpoint=args.remote_endpoint,
                scope_id=scope_id,
                conn=conn,
            )
        finally:
            conn.close()
    except Exception as exc:
        _emit(
            {
                "ok": False,
                "error": f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}",
                "command": "ctf challenge add",
                "side_effect": se.value,
            }
        )
        return EXIT_RUNTIME
    _emit(
        {
            "ok": True,
            "command": "ctf challenge add",
            "side_effect": se.value,
            "challenge_id": challenge_id,
            "event_slug": args.event,
            "challenge_slug": args.slug,
            "category": args.category,
            "scope_attached": bool(args.scope),
        }
    )
    return EXIT_OK


def cmd_challenge_fetch(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """REMOTE_WRITE: fetch challenge attachments from the event endpoint.

    Stub in M11-T003 — the real network call belongs to T005 (in-scope
    local solve) and T007 (single approved live submission). This
    command exists to validate the gate: it refuses without
    KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1 and without a matching ctf_scopes row.
    """
    se = SideEffect.REMOTE_WRITE
    if os.environ.get(_GATE_ENV) != "1":
        _emit(
            {
                "ok": False,
                "error": f"remote operation requires {_GATE_ENV}=1 and human "
                f"approval",
                "command": "ctf challenge fetch",
                "side_effect": se.value,
            }
        )
        return EXIT_BLOCKED

    # Scope check — look up the challenge's scope row, verify it covers
    # the challenge's remote_endpoint host.
    try:
        _db = _load_db()
        conn = _db.get_conn()
        try:
            with conn.cursor() as cur:
                cur.execute(
                    """
                    SELECT c.remote_endpoint, c.scope_id, s.target_urls,
                           s.expires_at, s.name AS scope_name
                      FROM ctf_challenges c
                      JOIN ctf_events e ON e.id = c.event_id
                      LEFT JOIN ctf_scopes s ON s.id = c.scope_id
                     WHERE e.slug = %s AND c.slug = %s
                     LIMIT 1
                    """,
                    (args.event, args.slug),
                )
                row = cur.fetchone()
        finally:
            conn.close()
    except Exception as exc:
        _emit(
            {
                "ok": False,
                "error": f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}",
                "command": "ctf challenge fetch",
                "side_effect": se.value,
            }
        )
        return EXIT_RUNTIME
    if row is None:
        _emit(
            {
                "ok": False,
                "error": f"no challenge ({args.event!r}, {args.slug!r})",
                "command": "ctf challenge fetch",
                "side_effect": se.value,
            }
        )
        return EXIT_RUNTIME
    endpoint = row.get("remote_endpoint")
    if not endpoint:
        _emit(
            {
                "ok": False,
                "error": "challenge has no remote_endpoint; nothing to fetch",
                "command": "ctf challenge fetch",
                "side_effect": se.value,
            }
        )
        return EXIT_RUNTIME
    scope_row = dict(row) if row else {}
    if not _scope_covers_url(scope_row, endpoint):
        _emit(
            {
                "ok": False,
                "error": "scope does not cover remote_endpoint or has expired",
                "command": "ctf challenge fetch",
                "side_effect": se.value,
                "scope_name": scope_row.get("scope_name"),
                "endpoint_host": urlparse(endpoint).hostname,
            }
        )
        return EXIT_BLOCKED

    # M11-T003 stops here: the actual fetch lives in T005 (uses
    # research_fetch / playwright reuse path). Stub returns ok=True with
    # `dispatched=False` so the caller knows the gate passed but no
    # network call was made in this Loop Prompt.
    _emit(
        {
            "ok": True,
            "command": "ctf challenge fetch",
            "side_effect": se.value,
            "dispatched": False,
            "note": "T003 stub — actual fetch wired in T005",
            "via": args.via,
            "endpoint_host": urlparse(endpoint).hostname,
        }
    )
    return EXIT_OK

def cmd_scope_set(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    se = SideEffect.LOCAL_WRITE
    urls = _parse_target_urls(args.target_urls)
    try:
        _db = _load_db()
        project_id = _db.ensure_default_project()
        conn = _db.get_conn()
        try:
            with conn.cursor() as cur:
                cur.execute(
                    """
                    INSERT INTO ctf_scopes
                      (project_id, name, authorized_scope, target_urls,
                       local_only, expires_at)
                    VALUES
                      (%s::uuid, %s, %s, %s::jsonb, %s, %s)
                    ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
                    RETURNING id::text
                    """,
                    (
                        project_id,
                        args.slug,
                        args.authorized,
                        json.dumps(urls),
                        bool(args.local_only),
                        args.expires_at,
                    ),
                )
                row = cur.fetchone()
                if row is None:
                    # ctf_scopes has no UNIQUE constraint on `name`; the
                    # ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING path won't fire for repeat
                    # names. Update the existing row by name instead.
                    cur.execute(
                        """
                        UPDATE ctf_scopes
                           SET authorized_scope = %s,
                               target_urls = %s::jsonb,
                               local_only = %s,
                               expires_at = %s
                         WHERE name = %s
                         RETURNING id::text
                        """,
                        (
                            args.authorized,
                            json.dumps(urls),
                            bool(args.local_only),
                            args.expires_at,
                            args.slug,
                        ),
                    )
                    row = cur.fetchone()
                if row is None:
                    cur.execute(
                        """
                        INSERT INTO ctf_scopes
                          (project_id, name, authorized_scope, target_urls,
                           local_only, expires_at)
                        VALUES
                          (%s::uuid, %s, %s, %s::jsonb, %s, %s)
                        RETURNING id::text
                        """,
                        (
                            project_id,
                            args.slug,
                            args.authorized,
                            json.dumps(urls),
                            bool(args.local_only),
                            args.expires_at,
                        ),
                    )
                    row = cur.fetchone()
            conn.commit()
        finally:
            conn.close()
    except Exception as exc:
        _emit(
            {
                "ok": False,
                "error": f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}",
                "command": "ctf scope set",
                "side_effect": se.value,
            }
        )
        return EXIT_RUNTIME
    _emit(
        {
            "ok": True,
            "command": "ctf scope set",
            "side_effect": se.value,
            "scope_id": row["id"] if row else None,
            "name": args.slug,
            "target_urls": urls,
            "local_only": bool(args.local_only),
        }
    )
    return EXIT_OK


def cmd_scope_list(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    se = SideEffect.READ_ONLY
    scopes: list[dict] = []
    try:
        _db = _load_db()
        conn = _db.get_conn()
        try:
            rows = _list_scopes(conn)
        finally:
            conn.close()
        for r in rows:
            scopes.append(
                {
                    "id": str(r.get("id", "")),
                    "name": r.get("name"),
                    "authorized_scope": r.get("authorized_scope"),
                    "target_urls": r.get("target_urls"),
                    "local_only": r.get("local_only"),
                    "expires_at": _jsonable(r.get("expires_at")),
                }
            )
    except Exception:
        scopes = []
    _emit(
        {
            "ok": True,
            "command": "ctf scope list",
            "side_effect": se.value,
            "scopes": scopes,
        }
    )
    return EXIT_OK


def cmd_scope_verify(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Exit 0 iff `args.url` ∈ target_urls of `args.slug` AND not expired.

    Used by skills + the worker as a pre-flight check before any
    network_egress / challenge_run / flag_submit op.
    """
    se = SideEffect.READ_ONLY
    try:
        _db = _load_db()
        conn = _db.get_conn()
        try:
            scope = _get_scope_by_name(conn, args.slug)
        finally:
            conn.close()
    except Exception as exc:
        _emit(
            {
                "ok": False,
                "error": f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}",
                "command": "ctf scope verify",
                "side_effect": se.value,
            }
        )
        return EXIT_RUNTIME
    if scope is None:
        _emit(
            {
                "ok": False,
                "covered": False,
                "error": f"no scope with name={args.slug!r}",
                "command": "ctf scope verify",
                "side_effect": se.value,
            }
        )
        return EXIT_RUNTIME
    covered = _scope_covers_url(scope, args.url)
    _emit(
        {
            "ok": bool(covered),
            "covered": bool(covered),
            "scope_name": scope.get("name"),
            "url_host": urlparse(args.url).hostname,
            "command": "ctf scope verify",
            "side_effect": se.value,
        }
    )
    return EXIT_OK if covered else EXIT_BLOCKED

def cmd_solver_run(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Drive a solver against (event, challenge). M11-T003 stub.

    Side-effect:
      - --dry-run                 LOCAL_WRITE (no gate fires)
      - not --dry-run             SUBMISSION-class (gates via the
                                  worker's `challenge_run` target_op)

    The actual solver-loop body lives in T005 (web + crypto bundled
    challenges) and the reviewer gate exercises in T006. T003 only
    surfaces the CLI signature and the gate refusal path.
    """
    if args.dry_run:
        se = SideEffect.LOCAL_WRITE
        _emit(
            {
                "ok": True,
                "command": "ctf solver run",
                "side_effect": se.value,
                "dry_run": True,
                "event_slug": args.event,
                "challenge_slug": args.challenge,
                "reviewer_gate": False,
                "note": "T003 stub — solver body wired in T005",
            }
        )
        return EXIT_OK

    se = SideEffect.SUBMISSION
    if args.reviewer_gate and os.environ.get(_GATE_ENV) != "1":
        # Reviewer-gate ON without remote allowance: refuse cleanly.
        _emit(
            {
                "ok": False,
                "command": "ctf solver run",
                "side_effect": se.value,
                "error": f"ApprovalRequired: challenge_run (set {_GATE_ENV}=1 "
                f"after human approval)",
                "target_op": "challenge_run",
            }
        )
        return EXIT_BLOCKED

    # T003 stub — actual solver dispatch lands in T005.
    _emit(
        {
            "ok": True,
            "command": "ctf solver run",
            "side_effect": se.value,
            "dispatched": False,
            "event_slug": args.event,
            "challenge_slug": args.challenge,
            "reviewer_gate": bool(args.reviewer_gate),
            "target_op": "challenge_run",
            "note": "T003 stub — solver body wired in T005",
        }
    )
    return EXIT_OK


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# flag submit
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _read_flag_length(flag_file: Path) -> int:
    """Return only the integer length of the flag file's content.

    The bytes never escape this helper. The full flag bytes are read
    lazily by `cmd_flag_submit` ONLY in the non-dry-run path immediately
    before the (future) HTTP POST; T003 never performs the POST.
    """
    with flag_file.open("rb") as f:
        # 16KB cap is generous; flags are typically < 200 bytes.
        raw = f.read(16 * 1024)
    return len(raw.strip())


def cmd_flag_submit(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Submit a flag for a challenge.

    --dry-run path (no remote allowance needed):
      - Open --flag-file with stat() only and read the header to compute
        flag_length. The flag VALUE is not retained beyond this stack
        frame and is never printed.
      - Echo the prospective request shape: event_slug, challenge_slug,
        flag_length, credential presence booleans, and side_effect.

    Non-dry-run path:
      - Refuse without KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1.
      - Refuse without a matching ctf_scopes row covering the event's
        submit URL (looked up from ctf_challenges.remote_endpoint).
      - T003 STOPS here. The real POST lives in T007 under the single
        approved live-event call.

    The flag value is NEVER printed, NEVER returned, NEVER added to any
    envelope. Only `flag_length`, `accepted=true|false`, and `http_status`
    leave this function.
    """
    se = SideEffect.SUBMISSION
    flag_path = Path(args.flag_file).expanduser()

    if not flag_path.exists():
        _emit(
            {
                "ok": False,
                "command": "ctf flag submit",
                "side_effect": se.value,
                "error": f"flag file not found: {flag_path}",
            }
        )
        return EXIT_RUNTIME

    # --dry-run: read only the length, never the value. No network. No
    # credential file is opened either — we just check presence.
    if args.dry_run:
        try:
            flag_length = _read_flag_length(flag_path)
        except OSError as exc:
            _emit(
                {
                    "ok": False,
                    "command": "ctf flag submit",
                    "side_effect": SideEffect.LOCAL_WRITE.value,
                    "error": f"read flag file: {type(exc).__name__}",
                    "dry_run": True,
                }
            )
            return EXIT_RUNTIME
        # Best-effort presence check — does NOT touch the file under
        # ~/.ctf/<slug>.json beyond loading + immediately discarding
        # the values from the returned dict.
        cred_presence: dict[str, Any] = {
            "source": None,
            "has_username": False,
            "has_token": False,
            "has_team_id": False,
        }
        try:
            raw = _load_event_credentials(args.event)
            cred_presence = _safe_cred_presence(raw)
            # Explicit drop. `raw` is GC'd at function return anyway,
            # but being explicit signals the contract to readers.
            raw.clear()
        except CredentialsMissing:
            pass
        _emit(
            {
                "ok": True,
                "command": "ctf flag submit",
                "side_effect": SideEffect.LOCAL_WRITE.value,
                "dry_run": True,
                "event_slug": args.event,
                "challenge_slug": args.challenge,
                "flag_length": flag_length,
                "credentials": cred_presence,
                "note": "T003 dry-run; T007 owns the single live submit",
            }
        )
        return EXIT_OK

    # Non-dry-run: enforce all four pre-conditions before T007 runs.
    if os.environ.get(_GATE_ENV) != "1":
        _emit(
            {
                "ok": False,
                "command": "ctf flag submit",
                "side_effect": se.value,
                "error": f"remote operation requires {_GATE_ENV}=1 and human "
                f"approval",
                "target_op": "flag_submit",
            }
        )
        return EXIT_BLOCKED

    # Scope check: look up the challenge's remote_endpoint + scope row.
    try:
        _db = _load_db()
        conn = _db.get_conn()
        try:
            with conn.cursor() as cur:
                cur.execute(
                    """
                    SELECT c.remote_endpoint, c.scope_id, s.target_urls,
                           s.expires_at, s.name AS scope_name
                      FROM ctf_challenges c
                      JOIN ctf_events e ON e.id = c.event_id
                      LEFT JOIN ctf_scopes s ON s.id = c.scope_id
                     WHERE e.slug = %s AND c.slug = %s
                     LIMIT 1
                    """,
                    (args.event, args.challenge),
                )
                row = cur.fetchone()
        finally:
            conn.close()
    except Exception as exc:
        _emit(
            {
                "ok": False,
                "command": "ctf flag submit",
                "side_effect": se.value,
                "error": f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}",
            }
        )
        return EXIT_RUNTIME

    if row is None:
        _emit(
            {
                "ok": False,
                "command": "ctf flag submit",
                "side_effect": se.value,
                "error": f"no challenge ({args.event!r}, {args.challenge!r})",
            }
        )
        return EXIT_RUNTIME

    endpoint = row.get("remote_endpoint")
    scope_row = dict(row)
    if not endpoint or not _scope_covers_url(scope_row, endpoint):
        _emit(
            {
                "ok": False,
                "command": "ctf flag submit",
                "side_effect": se.value,
                "error": "scope does not cover remote_endpoint or has expired",
                "scope_name": scope_row.get("scope_name"),
                "target_op": "flag_submit",
            }
        )
        return EXIT_BLOCKED

    # T003 STOPS HERE. The actual POST + ctf_attempts row write belongs
    # to T007's one-shot live submission. Surface the gate-passed
    # envelope so callers can confirm wiring without exfiltration.
    _emit(
        {
            "ok": True,
            "command": "ctf flag submit",
            "side_effect": se.value,
            "dispatched": False,
            "event_slug": args.event,
            "challenge_slug": args.challenge,
            "target_op": "flag_submit",
            "note": "T003 stub — live POST owned by T007",
        }
    )
    return EXIT_OK


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Subparser registration
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def add_parsers(sub: argparse._SubParsersAction) -> None:
    ctf = sub.add_parser(
        "ctf",
        help="Authorized CTF / lab workflow (event / challenge / scope / "
        "solver / flag). See COMMANDS.md.",
    )
    ctf_sub = ctf.add_subparsers(dest="ctf_cmd", required=True)

    # event ---------------------------------------------------------------
    p_event = ctf_sub.add_parser(
        "event", help="Event (CTF round) lifecycle (LOCAL_WRITE / READ_ONLY)"
    )
    event_sub = p_event.add_subparsers(dest="event_cmd", required=True)

    p_ev_reg = event_sub.add_parser(
        "register",
        help="Register a CTF event row (LOCAL_WRITE, idempotent on --slug).",
    )
    p_ev_reg.add_argument("--slug", required=True)
    p_ev_reg.add_argument("--name", required=True)
    p_ev_reg.add_argument("--ctftime-id", dest="ctftime_id", type=int, default=None)
    p_ev_reg.add_argument("--url", default=None, help="Event homepage URL")
    p_ev_reg.add_argument("--start-at", dest="start_at", default=None)
    p_ev_reg.add_argument("--end-at", dest="end_at", default=None)
    p_ev_reg.add_argument(
        "--credentials-ref",
        dest="credentials_ref",
        default=None,
        help="Path hint (e.g. ~/.ctf/<slug>.json) — never the credential value.",
    )
    p_ev_reg.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    p_ev_reg.set_defaults(func=cmd_event_register)

    p_ev_list = event_sub.add_parser(
        "list", help="List registered CTF events (READ_ONLY)."
    )
    p_ev_list.add_argument("--project", default=None)
    p_ev_list.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    p_ev_list.set_defaults(func=cmd_event_list)

    p_ev_info = event_sub.add_parser(
        "info", help="Show one CTF event row (READ_ONLY)."
    )
    p_ev_info.add_argument("--slug", required=True)
    p_ev_info.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    p_ev_info.set_defaults(func=cmd_event_info)

    # challenge -----------------------------------------------------------
    p_chal = ctf_sub.add_parser(
        "challenge",
        help="Challenge lifecycle (LOCAL_WRITE for add; REMOTE_WRITE for fetch).",
    )
    chal_sub = p_chal.add_subparsers(dest="challenge_cmd", required=True)

    p_chal_add = chal_sub.add_parser(
        "add", help="Add a challenge to a registered event (LOCAL_WRITE)."
    )
    p_chal_add.add_argument("--event", required=True)
    p_chal_add.add_argument("--slug", required=True)
    p_chal_add.add_argument("--name", required=True)
    p_chal_add.add_argument(
        "--category",
        required=True,
        choices=["web", "crypto", "rev", "pwn", "forensics", "osint", "misc"],
    )
    p_chal_add.add_argument("--points", type=int, default=None)
    p_chal_add.add_argument("--description", default=None)
    p_chal_add.add_argument(
        "--expected-flag-format", dest="expected_flag_format", default=None
    )
    p_chal_add.add_argument(
        "--attachments-path", dest="attachments_path", default=None
    )
    p_chal_add.add_argument(
        "--remote-endpoint", dest="remote_endpoint", default=None
    )
    p_chal_add.add_argument(
        "--scope",
        default=None,
        help="Name of an existing ctf_scopes row to attach.",
    )
    p_chal_add.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    p_chal_add.set_defaults(func=cmd_challenge_add)

    p_chal_fetch = chal_sub.add_parser(
        "fetch",
        help="Fetch challenge attachments / endpoint snapshot "
        "(REMOTE_WRITE; requires KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1 + scope match).",
    )
    p_chal_fetch.add_argument("--event", required=True)
    p_chal_fetch.add_argument("--slug", required=True)
    p_chal_fetch.add_argument(
        "--via", choices=["http", "playwright"], default="http"
    )
    p_chal_fetch.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    p_chal_fetch.set_defaults(func=cmd_challenge_fetch)

    p_chal_list = chal_sub.add_parser(
        "list", help="List challenges for an event (READ_ONLY)."
    )
    p_chal_list.add_argument("--event", required=True)
    p_chal_list.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    p_chal_list.set_defaults(func=cmd_challenge_list)

    p_chal_info = chal_sub.add_parser(
        "info", help="Show one challenge row (READ_ONLY)."
    )
    p_chal_info.add_argument("--event", required=True)
    p_chal_info.add_argument("--slug", required=True)
    p_chal_info.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    p_chal_info.set_defaults(func=cmd_challenge_info)

    # scope ---------------------------------------------------------------
    p_scope = ctf_sub.add_parser(
        "scope",
        help="ctf_scopes authorization rows (LOCAL_WRITE / READ_ONLY).",
    )
    scope_sub = p_scope.add_subparsers(dest="scope_cmd", required=True)

    p_scope_set = scope_sub.add_parser(
        "set", help="Insert or update a ctf_scopes row (LOCAL_WRITE)."
    )
    p_scope_set.add_argument("--slug", required=True, help="Scope name (unique-ish).")
    p_scope_set.add_argument("--authorized", required=True)
    p_scope_set.add_argument(
        "--target-urls",
        dest="target_urls",
        required=True,
        help="Comma-separated list of fully-qualified URLs.",
    )
    p_scope_set.add_argument("--local-only", action="store_true", dest="local_only")
    p_scope_set.add_argument("--expires-at", dest="expires_at", default=None)
    p_scope_set.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    p_scope_set.set_defaults(func=cmd_scope_set)

    p_scope_list = scope_sub.add_parser(
        "list", help="List ctf_scopes rows (READ_ONLY)."
    )
    p_scope_list.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    p_scope_list.set_defaults(func=cmd_scope_list)

    p_scope_verify = scope_sub.add_parser(
        "verify",
        help="Exit 0 iff URL ∈ target_urls AND scope not expired (READ_ONLY).",
    )
    p_scope_verify.add_argument("--slug", required=True)
    p_scope_verify.add_argument("--url", required=True)
    p_scope_verify.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    p_scope_verify.set_defaults(func=cmd_scope_verify)

    # solver --------------------------------------------------------------
    p_solver = ctf_sub.add_parser(
        "solver",
        help="Solver lifecycle. --dry-run is LOCAL_WRITE; otherwise "
        "SUBMISSION-class via the worker's challenge_run target_op.",
    )
    solver_sub = p_solver.add_subparsers(dest="solver_cmd", required=True)

    p_solver_run = solver_sub.add_parser(
        "run",
        help="Run a solver against (event, challenge). --dry-run skips the "
        "reviewer gate; --reviewer-gate makes the challenge_run gate fire.",
    )
    p_solver_run.add_argument("--event", required=True)
    p_solver_run.add_argument("--challenge", required=True)
    p_solver_run.add_argument("--dry-run", dest="dry_run", action="store_true")
    p_solver_run.add_argument(
        "--reviewer-gate",
        dest="reviewer_gate",
        action="store_true",
        help="Force the challenge_run reviewer gate (T006 wiring).",
    )
    p_solver_run.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    p_solver_run.set_defaults(func=cmd_solver_run)

    # flag ----------------------------------------------------------------
    p_flag = ctf_sub.add_parser(
        "flag",
        help="Flag submission. --dry-run is LOCAL_WRITE; otherwise SUBMISSION.",
    )
    flag_sub = p_flag.add_subparsers(dest="flag_cmd", required=True)

    p_flag_submit = flag_sub.add_parser(
        "submit",
        help="Submit a flag for a challenge. Flag is read from --flag-file "
        "and NEVER echoed. --dry-run skips the network call.",
    )
    p_flag_submit.add_argument("--event", required=True)
    p_flag_submit.add_argument("--challenge", required=True)
    p_flag_submit.add_argument(
        "--flag-file",
        dest="flag_file",
        required=True,
        help="Path to a file containing the flag string. Never echoed.",
    )
    p_flag_submit.add_argument("--dry-run", dest="dry_run", action="store_true")
    p_flag_submit.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    p_flag_submit.set_defaults(func=cmd_flag_submit)


__all__ = [
    "add_parsers",
    "cmd_event_register",
    "cmd_event_list",
    "cmd_event_info",
    "cmd_challenge_add",
    "cmd_challenge_fetch",
    "cmd_challenge_list",
    "cmd_challenge_info",
    "cmd_scope_set",
    "cmd_scope_list",
    "cmd_scope_verify",
    "cmd_solver_run",
    "cmd_flag_submit",
    "_load_event_credentials",
    "_safe_cred_presence",
    "_scope_covers_url",
    "CredentialsMissing",
]

"""M11-T003 smoke tests for the `kca ctf` CLI surface.

What this file covers:

  1. `kca ctf --help` lists the five sub-namespaces.
  2. `_load_event_credentials` resolves file + env-var paths and never
     surfaces raw values via `_safe_cred_presence`.
  3. `_scope_covers_url` matches on host and rejects expired scopes.
  4. `kca ctf flag submit --dry-run` works without `KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1`
     and never echoes the flag value or credential values.
  5. `kca ctf flag submit` (no `--dry-run`) refuses without
     `KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1` (gate-blocked exit 2).
  6. `kca ctf scope verify` exit-code contract via direct helper call
     (the DB-bound CLI path is exercised in T008 with a live DB).
  7. `cmd_event_register` is idempotent when called twice with the same
     slug (asserted via the underlying helper signature; the live
     idempotency round-trip lands in tests/test_kca_ctf_db.py when a
     DB is reachable).
  8. `_read_flag_length` reads only the integer length; the bytes are
     not exposed.
  9. Audit-grep: no flag value or credential value appears in any
     subprocess stdout/stderr captured in this file.

All tests are sandbox-safe: no real DB, no real network, no flag
strings printed.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import datetime as _dt
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
KCA = [sys.executable, str(REPO_ROOT / "tools" / "kca" / "kca.py")]

# Make tools/kca importable directly so unit-test calls can hit
# `tools.kca.ctf` internals without going via subprocess.
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT / "tools" / "kca"))

import ctf as ctf_mod  # noqa: E402


# A flag-like sentinel that must NEVER appear in any captured stdout
# or stderr from a subprocess. The audit-grep at the end of this file
# checks this across collected output.
_SENTINEL_FLAG = "flag{m11_t003_sentinel_DO_NOT_LEAK}"
_SENTINEL_TOKEN = "tok_m11_t003_DO_NOT_LEAK_eyJsZWFr"
_SENTINEL_USER = "user_m11_t003_DO_NOT_LEAK"

_CAPTURED_STDOUT: list[str] = []
_CAPTURED_STDERR: list[str] = []


def _run(*argv: str, env: dict | None = None) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    full_env = os.environ.copy()
    # Strip parent-process DB / remote env so the no-network tests can't
    # accidentally hit a live DB.
    for k in (
        "KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE",
        "KCA_DB_TARGET",
        "SUPABASE_DB_URL",
        "SUPABASE_DB_HOST",
    ):
        full_env.pop(k, None)
    if env is not None:
        for k, v in env.items():
            if v is None:
                full_env.pop(k, None)
            else:
                full_env[k] = v
    proc = subprocess.run(
        [*KCA, *argv],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=False,
        env=full_env,
        cwd=str(REPO_ROOT),
    )
    _CAPTURED_STDOUT.append(proc.stdout or "")
    _CAPTURED_STDERR.append(proc.stderr or "")
    return proc


def _parse_last_json(stdout: str) -> dict:
    """kca emits a single JSON object on the last non-empty stdout line."""
    lines = [ln for ln in (stdout or "").splitlines() if ln.strip()]
    assert lines, f"empty stdout"
    return json.loads(lines[-1])


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Top-level surface
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_ctf_help_lists_five_sub_namespaces() -> None:
    proc = _run("ctf", "--help")
    assert proc.returncode == 0, proc.stderr
    out = proc.stdout
    for ns in ("event", "challenge", "scope", "solver", "flag"):
        assert ns in out, f"missing namespace {ns!r} in `kca ctf --help`"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "argv",
    [
        ("ctf", "event", "register", "--help"),
        ("ctf", "event", "list", "--help"),
        ("ctf", "event", "info", "--help"),
        ("ctf", "challenge", "add", "--help"),
        ("ctf", "challenge", "fetch", "--help"),
        ("ctf", "challenge", "list", "--help"),
        ("ctf", "challenge", "info", "--help"),
        ("ctf", "scope", "set", "--help"),
        ("ctf", "scope", "list", "--help"),
        ("ctf", "scope", "verify", "--help"),
        ("ctf", "solver", "run", "--help"),
        ("ctf", "flag", "submit", "--help"),
    ],
)
def test_each_subcommand_has_help(argv) -> None:
    proc = _run(*argv)
    assert proc.returncode == 0, (argv, proc.stderr)
    assert "usage: kca ctf" in proc.stdout


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Credential loading allow-list — file path + env path
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_load_event_credentials_from_file(tmp_path, monkeypatch) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(ctf_mod, "_CTF_CRED_DIR", tmp_path)
    (tmp_path / "demo.json").write_text(
        json.dumps({"username": _SENTINEL_USER, "token": _SENTINEL_TOKEN}),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    creds = ctf_mod._load_event_credentials("demo")
    assert creds["source"] == "file"
    assert creds["has_username"] is True
    assert creds["has_token"] is True
    assert creds["has_team_id"] is False
    # The safe-presence stripper drops underscored values.
    safe = ctf_mod._safe_cred_presence(creds)
    safe_dump = json.dumps(safe)
    assert _SENTINEL_USER not in safe_dump
    assert _SENTINEL_TOKEN not in safe_dump


def test_load_event_credentials_from_env(tmp_path, monkeypatch) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(ctf_mod, "_CTF_CRED_DIR", tmp_path)  # empty dir
    monkeypatch.setenv("CTF_DEMO_EVENT_USERNAME", _SENTINEL_USER)
    monkeypatch.setenv("CTF_DEMO_EVENT_TOKEN", _SENTINEL_TOKEN)
    creds = ctf_mod._load_event_credentials("demo-event")
    assert creds["source"] == "env"
    assert creds["has_username"] is True
    assert creds["has_token"] is True


def test_load_event_credentials_missing(tmp_path, monkeypatch) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(ctf_mod, "_CTF_CRED_DIR", tmp_path)
    # ensure env not set
    for k in list(os.environ):
        if k.startswith("CTF_") and k.endswith(("_USERNAME", "_TOKEN", "_TEAM_ID")):
            monkeypatch.delenv(k, raising=False)
    with pytest.raises(ctf_mod.CredentialsMissing):
        ctf_mod._load_event_credentials("absent-event")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Scope coverage helper
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_scope_covers_url_host_match() -> None:
    scope = {
        "target_urls": [
            "https://event.example/api/submit",
            "https://www.event.example",
        ],
        "expires_at": None,
    }
    assert ctf_mod._scope_covers_url(scope, "https://event.example/anything")
    assert ctf_mod._scope_covers_url(
        scope, "https://www.event.example/api/submit"
    )
    assert not ctf_mod._scope_covers_url(scope, "https://kaggle.com/submit")
    assert not ctf_mod._scope_covers_url(scope, "")


def test_scope_covers_url_rejects_expired() -> None:
    past = _dt.datetime.now(_dt.timezone.utc) - _dt.timedelta(days=1)
    scope = {
        "target_urls": ["https://event.example/submit"],
        "expires_at": past,
    }
    assert not ctf_mod._scope_covers_url(scope, "https://event.example/submit")


def test_scope_covers_url_accepts_jsonb_string() -> None:
    # Postgres jsonb is occasionally returned as a JSON string by some
    # adapters — make sure the helper handles that shape too.
    scope = {
        "target_urls": json.dumps(["https://event.example/submit"]),
        "expires_at": None,
    }
    assert ctf_mod._scope_covers_url(scope, "https://event.example/anything")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. flag submit --dry-run
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_flag_submit_dry_run_no_remote_allow(tmp_path) -> None:
    flag_file = tmp_path / "flag.txt"
    flag_file.write_text(_SENTINEL_FLAG, encoding="utf-8")
    proc = _run(
        "ctf",
        "flag",
        "submit",
        "--event",
        "demo-event",
        "--challenge",
        "demo-challenge",
        "--flag-file",
        str(flag_file),
        "--dry-run",
    )
    assert proc.returncode == 0, proc.stderr
    payload = _parse_last_json(proc.stdout)
    assert payload["ok"] is True
    assert payload["dry_run"] is True
    assert payload["command"] == "ctf flag submit"
    assert payload["flag_length"] == len(_SENTINEL_FLAG)
    # The flag value, sentinel chars, etc. MUST NOT appear in either
    # stdout or stderr of this subprocess.
    assert _SENTINEL_FLAG not in proc.stdout
    assert _SENTINEL_FLAG not in proc.stderr


def test_flag_submit_no_dry_run_refuses_without_remote_allow(tmp_path) -> None:
    flag_file = tmp_path / "flag.txt"
    flag_file.write_text(_SENTINEL_FLAG, encoding="utf-8")
    proc = _run(
        "ctf",
        "flag",
        "submit",
        "--event",
        "demo-event",
        "--challenge",
        "demo-challenge",
        "--flag-file",
        str(flag_file),
    )
    assert proc.returncode == 2, (proc.stdout, proc.stderr)
    payload = _parse_last_json(proc.stdout)
    assert payload["ok"] is False
    assert payload["target_op"] == "flag_submit"
    assert "KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE" in payload["error"]
    assert _SENTINEL_FLAG not in proc.stdout
    assert _SENTINEL_FLAG not in proc.stderr


def test_flag_submit_dry_run_does_not_echo_credentials(
    tmp_path, monkeypatch
) -> None:
    # Stage a fake credential file under a tmp dir; monkeypatch the
    # module-level dir so we don't even touch the real ~/.ctf/.
    cred_dir = tmp_path / "ctf-creds"
    cred_dir.mkdir()
    monkeypatch.setattr(ctf_mod, "_CTF_CRED_DIR", cred_dir)
    (cred_dir / "demo-event.json").write_text(
        json.dumps({"username": _SENTINEL_USER, "token": _SENTINEL_TOKEN}),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    flag_file = tmp_path / "flag.txt"
    flag_file.write_text(_SENTINEL_FLAG, encoding="utf-8")

    # Invoke cmd_flag_submit directly to exercise the credential read
    # code path under the monkeypatched dir (subprocess wouldn't see
    # the monkeypatch).
    import argparse

    args = argparse.Namespace(
        event="demo-event",
        challenge="demo-challenge",
        flag_file=str(flag_file),
        dry_run=True,
        json=False,
    )

    import io

    buf = io.StringIO()
    real_stdout = sys.stdout
    try:
        sys.stdout = buf
        rc = ctf_mod.cmd_flag_submit(args)
    finally:
        sys.stdout = real_stdout
    assert rc == 0
    out = buf.getvalue()
    payload = json.loads(out.strip().splitlines()[-1])
    assert payload["dry_run"] is True
    assert payload["flag_length"] == len(_SENTINEL_FLAG)
    assert payload["credentials"]["has_username"] is True
    assert payload["credentials"]["has_token"] is True
    # No raw values anywhere in the emitted output.
    assert _SENTINEL_FLAG not in out
    assert _SENTINEL_TOKEN not in out
    assert _SENTINEL_USER not in out
    _CAPTURED_STDOUT.append(out)

def test_solver_run_dry_run_no_gate() -> None:
    proc = _run(
        "ctf", "solver", "run",
        "--event", "demo-event",
        "--challenge", "demo-challenge",
        "--dry-run",
    )
    assert proc.returncode == 0, proc.stderr

def test_solver_run_with_reviewer_gate_refuses_without_remote_allow() -> None:
    proc = _run(
        "ctf", "solver", "run",
        "--event", "demo-event",
        "--challenge", "demo-challenge",
        "--reviewer-gate",
    )
    assert proc.returncode == 2, (proc.stdout, proc.stderr)
    payload = _parse_last_json(proc.stdout)
    assert payload["ok"] is False
    assert payload["target_op"] == "challenge_run"

def test_scope_verify_helper_exit_zero_for_in_scope() -> None:
    scope = {
        "target_urls": ["https://event.example/api/submit"],
        "expires_at": None,
    }
    assert ctf_mod._scope_covers_url(scope, "https://event.example/anything")


def test_scope_verify_helper_exit_nonzero_for_out_of_scope() -> None:

    }
    assert not ctf_mod._scope_covers_url(scope, "https://other.example/x")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. event register idempotency — helper signature check
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_event_register_helper_idempotent_signature() -> None:
    # The underlying `register_event` helper uses ON CONFLICT (slug) DO
    # UPDATE SET slug = EXCLUDED.slug RETURNING id — i.e. idempotent on
    # slug. We assert that the helper signature exposes the
    # `credentials_ref` path-hint parameter (not the value itself), as
    # the CLI command relies on.
    from inspect import signature

    sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT))
    from src.db.ctf import register_event

    sig = signature(register_event)
    params = sig.parameters
    assert "slug" in params
    assert "credentials_ref" in params
    # The helper should NOT accept any param that smells like a
    # credential value rather than a hint.
    for forbidden in ("password", "token", "username", "secret"):
        assert forbidden not in params, (
            f"register_event accepts {forbidden!r} — should be a path hint only"
        )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. flag-file length-only read
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_read_flag_length_returns_int_only(tmp_path) -> None:
    f = tmp_path / "flag.txt"
    f.write_text(_SENTINEL_FLAG + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    n = ctf_mod._read_flag_length(f)
    assert isinstance(n, int)
    assert n == len(_SENTINEL_FLAG)  # strip() removes the trailing \n


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Audit-grep — no sentinel ever appears in captured subprocess output
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_audit_grep_no_flag_or_credential_in_captured_output() -> None:
    blob = "\n".join(_CAPTURED_STDOUT + _CAPTURED_STDERR)
    assert _SENTINEL_FLAG not in blob, (
        "sentinel flag leaked into subprocess stdout/stderr"
    )
    assert _SENTINEL_TOKEN not in blob, (
        "sentinel token leaked into subprocess stdout/stderr"
    )
    assert _SENTINEL_USER not in blob, (
        "sentinel username leaked into subprocess stdout/stderr"
    )

+| `kca ctf scope verify`        | `READ_ONLY`    | (native)                  | Exit 0 iff URL ∈ `target_urls` AND scope not expired; else exit 2 |
+| `kca ctf solver run`          | `SUBMISSION`*  | (planned via worker)      | `--dry-run` is `LOCAL_WRITE`; otherwise fires `challenge_run` reviewer gate |
+| `kca ctf flag submit`         | `SUBMISSION`   | (planned via worker)      | `--dry-run` is `LOCAL_WRITE`; otherwise fires `flag_submit` reviewer gate. Flag value is read from `--flag-file` and is **never echoed**. |
+
+\*`kca ctf solver run` is `LOCAL_WRITE` under `--dry-run` and elevates to
+`SUBMISSION`-class via the worker's `challenge_run` target_op when
+`--reviewer-gate` is set. Cross-link: `src/worker/worker.py::_TOOL_TO_TARGET_OP`.
+
+### `kca ctf` reviewer-gate map
+
+| CLI invocation                          | Reviewer-gate op  | Default policy (per ADR-0017) |
+|-----------------------------------------|-------------------|-------------------------------|
+| `kca ctf solver run` (no `--dry-run`, with `--reviewer-gate`) | `challenge_run` | ask |
+| `kca ctf flag submit` (no `--dry-run`)  | `flag_submit`     | ask |
+| `kca ctf challenge fetch` (no `--dry-run`) | `network_egress` | deny outside `ctf_scopes.target_urls`; ask when scope+URL match |
+
+The `--dry-run` form on every gated subcommand bypasses the network and
+the reviewer gate while still emitting a JSON envelope describing the
+prospective side effect — useful for skill prompts and CI smoke tests.
+
+### `kca ctf flag submit` — flag-value discipline
+
+- The flag value is **read from `--flag-file`** (the file is opened
+  inside the Python process; nothing under `~/.ctf/` is read by the
+  Claude Code Read/Edit/Write tools).
+- The command emits only the integer `flag_length`, `accepted=true|false`
+  and the event's HTTP status. The flag string is **never** added to
+  any JSON envelope, audit row, log line, or PR body.
+- The credential-loading helper `_load_event_credentials(event_slug)`
+  is the single allow-listed call-site for the guard_tool deny
+  exception over `~/.ctf/<slug>.json` added in M11-T002. It returns
+  boolean-presence fields (`has_username` / `has_token` /
+  `has_team_id`) for any output-bound code path; the underscored
+  raw fields stay local to the POST-building stack frame.
