````markdown
# kaggle-code-agent Milestones

Status: M0–M9 done; M9.2 ✓ done (/save-log operator-tooling skill); M10 in planning (notebook-submission regression — Petals to the Metal)  
Created: 2026-05-16  
Scope: hybrid human + AI code competition platform

## Product thesis

`kaggle-code-agent` is a platform for human users to collaborate with AI code agents on code competitions and authorized challenge environments.

Initial focus: Kaggle competitions.  
Later extensions: authorized CTF/lab challenges, Devpost, hackathons, benchmark competitions, and other policy-scoped coding contests.

The platform should help a human user:

- discuss ideas and strategies;
- research competition rules, data, notebooks, papers, discussions, and baseline approaches;
- create, modify, test, and iterate code;
- track experiments, artifacts, results, submissions, and analysis;
- require human approval for external side effects such as Kaggle submissions or remote kernel pushes;
- summarize learnings and produce final writeups.

## Source of truth

**GitHub repo + Claude Code + CI + Supabase migrations.**

All product source code, migrations, tests, architecture decisions, and task specs live in this repository. AI tools do not share hidden memory reliably across sessions or products. Claude Code is the primary development environment for all layers: CLI, backend, UI shell, and worker.

Lovable may be used for visual prototyping or landing-page mockups only. It is not the source of truth for schema, migrations, agent runners, or any backend logic.

## Terminology: two meanings of "code agent"

This project uses two related but distinct agent concepts.

### 1. Platform-development coding agents

These are external AI tools used to build this repository.

Examples:

- Claude Code CLI / VS Code / Desktop / Web (primary);
- ChatGPT Pro / Cursor (supplementary);
- GitHub Actions / Claude Code Web / Routines for cloud automation.

Role:

- write and review this product's source code;
- update docs, tasks, tests, and architecture decisions;
- run local tests and CI repair loops;
- open branches/PRs under human supervision.

Important rule: these tools do not share hidden memory reliably. GitHub repository files are the durable source of truth.

### 2. Runtime competition code agents

These are agents launched by the finished platform to help a human user compete.

Initial runtime direction:

- Claude Agent SDK as the first core worker/harness;
- isolated workspace/container per job;
- Python/notebook-first for Kaggle;
- TypeScript/Python service boundary depending on platform vs worker needs;
- future model router for Claude, GPT-style models, local vLLM/Ollama models, and specialized tools.

Runtime agents must operate under competition-specific policy, sandboxing, budget limits, approval gates, and audit logging.

## Architecture north star

```text
Human user / future UI
        ↓
TypeScript-first platform/control plane
  - project/session/job/task queue
  - policy and approval gates
  - discussion/research/analysis records
  - experiment/run/submission/artifact records
  - model router configuration
        ↓
Worker layer
  - Python-first Kaggle workers
  - Claude Agent SDK runtime sessions
  - notebooks/scripts/tools/kca wrappers
  - Playwright/browser/research tools
  - sandboxed execution and evaluation
        ↓
External systems
  - GitHub repo / branches / PRs
  - Supabase DB/storage/edge functions later
  - Kaggle API/CLI, only with approval for remote side effects
  - authorized CTF/lab/hackathon platforms under explicit policy
```

## Cross-cutting rules

- GitHub repo files are the project memory and source of truth.
- Each agent task gets a branch/worktree/PR when it modifies code.
- Main branch remains stable and protected.
- Do not allow multiple AI sessions to edit the same branch/files at the same time.
- No secrets in repo, prompts, logs, artifacts, or screenshots.
- Kaggle submissions, kernel pushes, dataset uploads, and other remote side effects require explicit human approval.
- CTF/lab work must be local/sandboxed or explicitly authorized.
- Every task prompt should include acceptance criteria and a stop condition.
- Every worker loop should have budget, turn, time, and side-effect limits.
- Tests and local validation should run before external submission.

## Milestone final-review protocol

After every milestone final review, before marking done:

1. Update `PROJECT_STATE.md` — set current milestone, summarize open decisions, and record any new known blockers.
2. Update `README.md` current milestone section to name the new active milestone and goal.
3. Update `docs/milestones.md` — mark the finished milestone `✓ done`, add a one-line summary of what landed, and note any follow-ups carried forward.
4. Write `docs/handoffs/m{x}-handoff.md` — a per-milestone, ready-to-paste context prompt for the next AI tool / session that will start M{x+1}. Use `docs/handoff-prompt.md` as the canonical template; populate the "State at handoff", "Read these files first", and "Current task" sections from the M{x} final review and the M{x+1} entry in this file. The generic `docs/handoff-prompt.md` stays as the template; the per-milestone instances live under `docs/handoffs/`.

  `delete_artifact`). Verdict `approve | reject | abstain` lands in a new
  `agent_reviews` table; `approve` satisfies the matching approval gate
  without human intervention, `reject` escalates (default) or fails the
  job, `abstain` falls through to the existing human-decisions flow.
- Local-model layer (`src/worker/local_model.py`) talks to vLLM / Ollama
  endpoints on the user's GPU hosts (`snorlax` RTX 4090, `may` RTX 3090)
  via OpenAI-compatible HTTP. Numbered-slot env config
  (`KCA_LOCAL_ENDPOINT_<n>_*`), priority ordering, a TTL-cached probe, and
  a `KCA_LOCAL_FALLBACK_MODEL` cloud fallback.
- New job types `log_triage` and `summarise` route to the local layer by
  default; `kca local probe / pick / triage` surfaces endpoint state.
- OTEL instrumentation per ADR-0007 with three exporters: stderr (dev),
  SQLite (`.agent/telemetry.sqlite`), and Supabase
  (`agent_telemetry_spans`). Spans cover job / turn / tool / reviewer /
  local-probe.
- TC-3 Spaceship Titanic exercises the reviewer-gate path end-to-end on a
  binary-classification submission flow.

Exit criteria: all met. See `docs/m6-final-review.md`.

## M7: KCA CLI architecture — command / skill / tool / job / permission policy ✓ done

_Shipped 2026-05-21: four-layer CLI scaffold (command/skill/tool/job), skill loader, tool registry (16 tools), three permission profiles, `kca skill list/show/run` + `kca tool list/audit/doctor`, four seed skills, audit JSONL, 15 smoke tests, and `docs/architecture/kca-cli-architecture.md`. 28/28 exit checks PASS — see `docs/m7-final-review.md`._

Goal: implement the full KCA command/skill/tool/job architecture so the platform
has a stable, inspectable CLI that can drive agent workflows, replace ad-hoc
`python tools/kca/kca.py` calls, and enforce structured permission decisions.

This is distinct from the product UI shell (M8): M7 is operator/developer-facing
and headless. The UI in M8 will call into the same CLI/API surface.

See `docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-21-r1.md` §1–3 for full design rationale.

### Four-layer model

| Layer | Description |
|---|---|
| **Command** | Deterministic CLI/API entry points for operators (`kca job run`, `kca decision approve`). |
| **Skill** | Agent-facing workflow recipes stored under `.kca/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter. Callable via `kca skill run <name>` or slash-style invocation. |
| **Tool** | Executable actions with input/output schema, timeout, permission label, sandbox metadata, and audit logging. |
| **Job** | Durable records that run a skill through the agent loop with budget, turn, cost, runtime limits, and decision gates. |

### M7 task sequence

| Task | Description | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| M7-T000 | Audit + repair `.github/workflows/` — fix failing CI checks, add no-db + lint jobs | — |
| M7-T001 | Skill loader: read `.kca/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter; argument substitution | — |
| M7-T002 | Command registry: register KCA CLI subcommands declaratively | T001 |
| M7-T003 | Tool registry: tool metadata, approval policy labels, sandbox metadata | T001 |
| M7-T004 | Permission policy layer: allow/ask/deny resolution with structured JSON policy records | T003 |
| M7-T005 | Slash-style invocation: `kca skill run <name> [args] [--dry-run]` shows permissions + rendered prompt | T001, T004 |
| M7-T006 | Audit logging: record every tool execution in `agent_job_events` with policy decision | T004 |
| M7-T007 | Seed `.kca/skills/` with `run-milestone`, `triage-log`, `prepare-submission`, `review-pr` | T001 |
| M7-T008 | `tests/test_m7_smoke.py`: skill parsing, arg substitution, permission resolution, command registry, decision gates | T001–T006 |
| M7-T009 | Documentation: `docs/architecture/kca-cli-architecture.md` explaining Commands vs Skills vs Tools vs Jobs | all |
| M7-T010 | M7 exit criteria validation + `docs/m7-final-review.md` | all |

### Permission policy design

Runtime agent permissions are data, not ad-hoc prompts:

```json
{
  "operation": "kaggle.submit",
  "default_decision": "ask",
  "reason": "External competition submission",
  "allowed_in_modes": ["human-approved", "competition-finalization"],
  "audit_required": true
}
```

Allow by default: edit workspace files, run tests/benchmark, create artifacts,
summarize logs, call LiteLLM/local models, create branch, commit, create PR.

Decision gate: submit to Kaggle, merge PR, publish dataset/kernel, apply
remote Supabase migration, spend above budget threshold, change model tier,
change competition direction/objective.

Deny: read secrets, write outside workspace, sudo/root, rm outside workspace,
drop database/schema, force push, network exfiltration.

### Recommended directory layout

```text
.kca/
  skills/
    run-milestone/SKILL.md
    triage-log/SKILL.md
    prepare-submission/SKILL.md
    review-pr/SKILL.md
  tools/tools.yaml
  permissions/
    default.yaml
    permissive-dev.yaml
    competition-runner.yaml

tools/kca/
  kca.py
  commands/
    job.py  skill.py  tool.py  decision.py
    workspace.py  kaggle.py  supabase.py
  agent/
    runner.py  skill_loader.py  tool_executor.py
    permission_policy.py  audit.py
```

Exit criteria:

- `kca skill list` shows available skills from `.kca/skills/`.
- `kca skill show <name>` prints parsed metadata and body.
- `kca skill run <name> ... --dry-run` prints planned tool permissions and rendered prompt without executing.
- Permission policy resolves allow/ask/deny for any (operation, mode) pair.
- Audit log records every tool execution with policy decision.
- `.github/workflows/` CI passes on main branch (no-db + lint at minimum).
- `tests/test_m7_smoke.py` passes without API keys or DB.
- Documentation explains Commands vs Skills vs Tools vs Jobs.

# Kaggle Code Agent — Project State

_Last updated: 2026-05-26 (M9.4 close)_

## Product intent
Build a hybrid human + AI competition engineering workbench. The first target is Kaggle-style competitions, with future support for authorized CTF/lab challenges. The system should research, discuss ideas with humans, edit code, run tests/evaluations, analyze results, iterate, and prepare submissions under human-approved guardrails.

## Chosen architecture direction
- Hybrid architecture.
- Claude Code Desktop/CLI for interactive project development and dogfooding (primary development tool for all layers).
- Claude Agent SDK for the production coding worker.
- Python-first worker for Kaggle/ML/CTF execution.
- TypeScript/Supabase control plane and UI shell (developed in Claude Code, not Lovable).
- GitHub + Claude Code + CI + Supabase migrations are the source of truth. All decisions, architecture, task specs, and safety rules live in repo files.
- Supabase is the control plane and audit database, not the primary code execution environment.

## Current MVP boundary
1. Local-first repository workflow with `CLAUDE.md`, skills, hooks, subagents, and GitHub.
2. Supabase schema for projects, sessions, jobs, messages, research notes, experiments, runs, submissions, artifacts, approvals, and `agent_tool_audit` (M8).
3. Kaggle baseline loop: understand competition, create validation, run baseline, record metrics, iterate, prepare submission.
4. Browser/research loop: fetch pages, summarize sources, track trust and citations.
5. Multi-agent reviewer gate + OTEL telemetry + local GPU model layer.
6. Authorized CTF sandbox loop only for explicit challenge environments.
7. Operator-facing UI: Dashboard, Run Timeline (OTEL swim-lane), Experiments, Research, Approval Inbox + Decision Gate, Artifact Browser.

## Human approval gates
Require approval for:
- Kaggle competition submissions.
- Kaggle kernel/notebook pushes.
- Any remote write operation.
- Any operation touching credentials, secrets, or account settings.
- Any CTF action outside a declared sandbox/challenge scope.
- PR merges (create is allowed, merge requires approval).

Mutations from the UI flow through `services/decision_api/` (FastAPI) →
`tools/kca/decisions.py` → DB. The browser bundle never holds a
Supabase service-role key. The M7 permission policy resolution stays
authoritative.

- **M0**: project baseline and memory discipline ✓
- **M1**: local Kaggle tooling wrapper baseline ✓

- **M3**: Python-first competition worker v0 ✓

- **M5**: research and browser workflow ✓

- **M8**: product UI shell + M7 follow-ups (audit table, schema gate, ToolSpec enforcement, decision_api) ✓
- **M8.5**: pre-M9 hardening — CI repair + GitHub Issues/PR/labels interface + M9 planning ✓
- **M9**: live end-to-end Kaggle regression test — Spaceship Titanic ✓

# ADR-0016: CTF data model — events, challenges, attempts

## Status

Accepted (M11-T001, 2026-06-09). Lands with
`supabase/migrations/0008_m11_ctf.sql` and `src/db/ctf.py`.

Cross-link: [`docs/evidence/m11/discovery/design-red-team.md`](../evidence/m11/discovery/design-red-team.md),
[`docs/evidence/m11/discovery/legacy-archaeologist.md`](../evidence/m11/discovery/legacy-archaeologist.md),
[`docs/evidence/m11/discovery/requirements-skeptic.md`](../evidence/m11/discovery/requirements-skeptic.md).

## Context

M11 is the first non-Kaggle competition platform on the agent stack.
The CTFtime workflow (planning Q&A, `docs/m11-loop-prompts.md` §at-a-glance)
needs persistent, queryable records for three things:

1. **Events** — which CTFtime-listed event we are participating in, when
   it runs, and where the credentials for it live.
2. **Challenges** — per-event jeopardy items the agent might attempt,
   each optionally bound to a `ctf_scopes` (migration 0001) authorization
   row.
3. **Attempts** — every flag submission, accepted or not, with enough
   identity context that "which credential ran this" is answerable from
   the row alone.

The pre-existing `ctf_scopes` table from migration 0001 covers
authorization (target URLs, local-only flag, expiry). M11 adds the three
tables above; `ctf_scopes` is referenced via an FK from
`ctf_challenges.scope_id` but is otherwise untouched.
```

"""M11-T005: drive the local solver loop against both bundled challenges.

Operates against the frozen `kca-fixtures-2026` event (T004 bundles):

  - web-1-cookie-monster (docker-compose, Flask, unsigned-cookie tamper)
  - crypto-1-tiny-rsa    (in-process, 143-bit RSA factor + decrypt)

Sequence per challenge:

  1. Read `challenge.yaml` + `description.md` + attachments. Log the
     category strategy.
  2. For web: generate a fresh flag, sha256 it, write it into the
     bundle's `expected.sha256` (the README documents this contract —
     the harness owns the flag value, the bundle only holds the hash).
     Export `KCA_FIXTURE_FLAG`, `docker compose up -d`, wait for the
     service to come up, run the cookie-tamper exploit via
     `solver_template.py::solve`, verify the recovered flag against
     `expected.sha256`. Then `docker compose down -v`.
     For crypto: in-process `solve()` (already deterministic from the
     committed params; no flag generation, no docker).
  3. Compute `flag_length` and a sha256 of the flag (used ONLY to grep
     audit logs for accidental disclosure — never persisted).
  4. `kca run init` + `kca run record-metric --key flag_length` for the
     experiment_runs row.
  5. `record_attempt(accepted=True, flag_length=<len>, response_excerpt
     '<scrubbed>')` into `ctf_attempts`.
  6. `kca ctf solver run --dry-run` for the gate-path side-effect
     record (T006 owns the gate-ON path).
  7. Drop the flag from memory.

Hygiene invariants:

  - The flag string never enters a log, a DB column, or a JSON payload
    that we control.
  - `expected.sha256` is rewritten for the web challenge; this is the
    documented "deterministic per harness invocation" contract.
  - The crypto challenge's `expected.sha256` is NOT touched (the flag
    is mathematically determined by the committed `params.json`).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import importlib.util
import json
import os
import secrets
import string
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import httpx

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT))
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT / "tools" / "kca"))

import db as _db  # type: ignore  # noqa: E402

from src.db import ctf as ctf_db  # noqa: E402

EVENT_SLUG = "kca-fixtures-2026"
EVENT_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "data" / "ctf" / EVENT_SLUG

"""M11 smoke tests — regression assertions against the M11 cloud DB seed.

DB-gated, assertion-only. Mirrors the ``tests/test_m9_smoke.py`` and
``tests/test_m10_smoke.py`` posture: SKIPs cleanly without
``SUPABASE_DB_URL``, and SKIPs cleanly when the M11 seed rows are
absent (so a fresh CI Postgres with migrations only stays green).

The M11 seed lives in the `kca-fixtures-2026` event row populated by
T004 / T005 / T006. This file asserts:

  - Migration ``0008_m11_ctf.sql`` is applied (4 ctf_* tables present).
  - ``ctf_events`` contains the ``kca-fixtures-2026`` row.
  - ``ctf_challenges`` contains both bundled challenges (web + crypto)
    for that event.
  - ``ctf_scopes`` contains the matching scope rows referenced by the
    bundle yaml files.
  - ``agent_reviews`` has at least 2 rows with target_op ∈
    {challenge_run, flag_submit} from T006.
  - ``ctf_attempts`` has at least 2 rows with ``accepted=true`` from
    T005 (local solves) and T006 (gate round-trip).

Run with:
    SUPABASE_DB_URL=... python -m pytest tests/test_m11_smoke.py -v
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT))
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT / "tools" / "kca"))

requires_db = pytest.mark.skipif(
    not os.environ.get("SUPABASE_DB_URL"),
    reason="SUPABASE_DB_URL not set",
)

# Canonical seed slug. Set in T004; both T005 and T006 attach their
# rows to this event.

WEB_CHALLENGE_SLUG = "web-1-cookie-monster"
CRYPTO_CHALLENGE_SLUG = "crypto-1-tiny-rsa"
# Scope names per the bundle yamls (data/ctf/.../challenge.yaml::scope_ref).
WEB_SCOPE_NAME = "ctf-local-kca-fixtures-2026-web-1"
CRYPTO_SCOPE_NAME = "ctf-local-kca-fixtures-2026-crypto-1"

CRYPTO_SCOPE_NAME = "ctf-local-kca-fixtures-2026-crypto-1"

EXPECTED_CHALLENGES = 2

EXPECTED_T006_REVIEWS = 2  # one challenge_run + one flag_submit
EXPECTED_ACCEPTED_ATTEMPTS = 2  # T005 web + T005 crypto baseline


def _table_exists(cur, table_name: str) -> bool:
    cur.execute(
        """
        SELECT EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.tables
           WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name = %s
        )
        """,
        (table_name,),
    )
    row = cur.fetchone()
    return bool(row[0])


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def db_conn():
    """Open one Postgres connection for the module. Skips cleanly when
    ``SUPABASE_DB_URL`` is unset.
    """
    if not os.environ.get("SUPABASE_DB_URL"):
        pytest.skip("SUPABASE_DB_URL not set")
    import psycopg

    conn = psycopg.connect(os.environ["SUPABASE_DB_URL"])
    try:
        yield conn
    finally:
        conn.close()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Schema presence — migration 0008 applied
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@requires_db
def test_migration_0008_tables_present(db_conn):
    """All four M11 tables exist. SKIP (not FAIL) on a pre-migration DB
    so the live-db CI job doesn't trip when 0008 hasn't been applied
    yet."""
    expected = ("ctf_events", "ctf_challenges", "ctf_scopes", "ctf_attempts")
    with db_conn.cursor() as cur:
        missing = [t for t in expected if not _table_exists(cur, t)]
    if missing:
        pytest.skip(
            f"M11 migration 0008 not applied (missing tables: {missing}); "
            "live-db job is green pre-migration"
        )
    # All four present — explicit PASS.
    assert missing == []

# M11 CTF workflow architecture

_Milestone: M11 — authorized CTF / lab workflow._
_Date: 2026-06-09._

## 1. CTFtime calendar discovery and event registration (human action)

The CTF entry point is the [CTFtime calendar](https://ctftime.org/calendar/).
The human browses upcoming events, decides which to enter, and registers
on the event site directly (no browser-automated sign-up in M11).

After registration the human:

1. Creates a credential file at `~/.ctf/<event-slug>.json` with shape:
   ```json
   { "username": "...", "token": "...", "team_id": "..." }
   ```
   (`team_id` is optional; omit for individual participation.)
   Alternatively: set `CTF_<EVENT>_USERNAME` + `CTF_<EVENT>_TOKEN` env vars.
2. Runs `kca ctf event register --slug <event-slug> --name "..." --url "..." --start <ISO> --end <ISO>` to create a `ctf_events` row in the local DB. This is a LOCAL_WRITE; it does not touch the event site.
3. Runs `kca ctf event info --slug <event-slug>` (READ_ONLY) to verify the row.

The `.claude/hooks/guard_tool.py` hook denies direct `~/.ctf/*.json` reads from any path except the allow-listed `kca ctf` flow. The credential is never echoed in logs, audit rows, or PRs.

## 2. Credential file shape and load path

Credential resolution order (first match wins):

1. `~/.ctf/<event-slug>.json` — JSON object with `username`, `token`, optional `team_id`.
2. Environment variables `CTF_<EVENT_SLUG_UPPER>_USERNAME` and `CTF_<EVENT_SLUG_UPPER>_TOKEN`.

The `kca ctf flag submit` command calls `_load_event_credentials(slug)` which:

- reads the JSON file via a guarded path (`.claude/hooks/guard_tool.py` carve-out);
- or reads the env vars;
- raises `CredentialsError` if neither is found, returning exit code 1 with the message "CTF credentials not found — set `~/.ctf/<slug>.json` or env vars" (no credential value emitted).

The credential is held in memory only for the duration of the HTTP call.
It is never written to `ctf_attempts` or any other DB row.

## 3. Challenge inventory and category triage

After event registration:

1. `kca ctf challenge add --event <slug> --challenge-slug <slug> --category web --points 100 --description "..."` inserts a `ctf_challenges` row (LOCAL_WRITE).
2. `kca ctf challenge list --event <slug>` lists challenges with their category and scope reference.
3. `kca ctf scope set --event <slug> --challenge <slug> --target-urls "http://localhost:18080" --local-only true` creates or updates a `ctf_scopes` row.

Category triage in the solver loop:

- `web` — docker-compose service; solver uses httpx against localhost; no external network needed for frozen bundles.
- `crypto` — in-process Python; no network; deterministic from committed parameters.
- `pwn`, `rev`, `forensics` — recognized as valid categories in `ctf_challenges.category` but the M11 solve loop does not implement agent loops for these; filed as M11 follow-up.

The challenge inventory is read-only from the perspective of the solver worker.
Adding challenges requires a separate `kca ctf challenge add` invocation (LOCAL_WRITE, not subject to the `challenge_run` gate).

## 4. Solver execution under the `challenge_run` gate

The `challenge_run` operation (ADR-0017) gates any solver invocation against a target whose URL appears in `ctf_scopes.target_urls` OR is a local in-scope service.

Gate flow for a local-solve run:

1. Worker stages the solver invocation: target URL + challenge slug.
2. `should_consult_reviewer("challenge_run")` returns True for all three permission profiles.
3. `run_review(target_op="challenge_run", ...)` writes an `agent_reviews` row.
4. `decision_api` surfaces the pending decision; the UI Approval Inbox renders it.
5. Human approves via UI or `kca decisions approve --id <id>`.
6. Worker proceeds: `kca ctf solver run --event <slug> --challenge <slug>`.
7. For `web`: `docker compose up -d` → wait for HTTP 200 → run `solver_template.py::solve()` → capture flag → `docker compose down -v`.
8. For `crypto`: in-process `solver_template.py::solve()` → capture flag.

The `kca ctf solver run --dry-run` path skips the gate entirely (records a
dry-run audit row but does not open an `agent_reviews` row).

Solver execution is local only. No remote challenge endpoint is contacted
in the M11 frozen-bundle path; the gate fires to establish the approval-flow
discipline for when a live event's challenge endpoint IS the target.

## 5. Flag recovery and sha256 verification

After the solver returns:

1. The flag string is held only in the local Python process variable.
2. `hashlib.sha256(flag.encode()).hexdigest()` computes the digest.
3. The digest is compared against `expected.sha256` in the challenge bundle:
   - Match → `accepted=true` in the resulting `ctf_attempts` row.
   - No match → `accepted=false`; the solve loop halts and reports the discrepancy without printing the flag or the expected value.
4. `flag_length` (integer) is recorded in `experiment_runs` via `kca run record-metric --key flag_length --value <N>`.
5. `ctf_db.record_attempt(challenge_id=..., accepted=True, http_status=None, flag_length=N, response_excerpt="<scrubbed>")` writes the `ctf_attempts` row. The flag string is never passed to this function.
6. The flag is dropped from the local variable immediately after step 5.

For the web challenge (`web-1-cookie-monster`) the harness generates a fresh flag per run and writes its sha256 into `expected.sha256` before starting docker-compose. The `expected.sha256` file is the single stable artifact; the flag value is ephemeral.

For the crypto challenge (`crypto-1-tiny-rsa`) the flag is mathematically determined by the committed `params.json` (RSA parameters); `expected.sha256` is static and committed.

## 6. Flag submission under the `flag_submit` gate

The `flag_submit` operation (ADR-0017) gates any call to a live event's submit API.

Gate flow:

1. Worker stages the flag submission: event slug + challenge slug + flag string (in memory only).
2. `should_consult_reviewer("flag_submit")` returns True for all three profiles.
3. `run_review(target_op="flag_submit", ...)` writes an `agent_reviews` row (rationale includes challenge slug + event slug only; NOT the flag value).
4. Human approves via UI or `kca decisions approve --id <id>`.
5. For a live event (T007): `kca ctf flag submit --event <slug> --challenge <slug> --flag <flag>` runs the actual HTTP POST to the event's submit endpoint. The `ctf_scopes.target_urls` row must cover the submit endpoint. `KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1` must be set.
6. The `ctf_attempts` row is written with `accepted=true|false`, `http_status=<int>`, `flag_length=<N>`. The flag string is NOT stored in the DB.
7. The CLI output is exactly `accepted=true` or `accepted=false` plus the HTTP status. The flag is never echoed to stdout.

For LOCAL_WRITE dry-run paths (no live event), `http_status` is stored as `null`; `accepted` reflects the local sha256 comparison result.

## 7. Out-of-scope follow-ups

The following capabilities are recognized by the M11 data model and taxonomy
but are deferred to future milestones:

### Pwn / rev / forensics solve loops

`ctf_challenges.category` supports `pwn`, `rev`, `forensics` but M11 only
implements agent-loop solvers for `web` and `crypto`. Follow-up: author
`ctf-sandbox/SKILL.md` extensions for pwntools-based binary exploitation,
Ghidra / radare2 assisted reverse engineering, and forensic-artifact analysis.

### CTFtime calendar auto-watch

M11 requires the human to manually check CTFtime. A future milestone should
add `kca ctf event watch --ctftime` that polls the CTFtime API (with human
approval for each new event it proposes to register) and surfaces upcoming
events on the UI Dashboard. Blocked on: CTFtime API rate-limit policy,
team-credential rotation, and the per-event scope-set automation.

### Multi-event identity rotation

`ctf_attempts.event_account` and `ctf_attempts.team_id` columns (M11 T001
carry-over from T000 multi-account debate) exist to track which account
ran which attempt. M11 does not implement the rotation logic: picking a
different `~/.ctf/<slug>.json` per attempt or per event day. Follow-up:
author a `ctf-identity-rotation` policy in `.kca/permissions/` and wire
it to the credential-load path in `cmd_flag_submit`.

### Per-challenge rate-limit column

ADR-0017 notes a `ctf_scopes` extension: a `rate_limit_per_hour` column
so the worker can self-throttle before the gate fires. Not implemented in
M11. Follow-up: migration 0009 extension + guard in `cmd_flag_submit`.

### Hook-level enforcement of the Discovery / Debate Gate

Deferred from M9.4: a PreToolUse hook that refuses `Edit` on `src/**`
for `arch:` tasks without `discovery/` evidence under
`docs/evidence/<milestone>/discovery/`. Not implemented in M11.

### httpx-level `network_egress` interceptor for subprocess egress

ADR-0017 §enforcement-layer-pinning records that the `httpx`-level
interceptor for subprocess calls that bypass the reviewer-gate (e.g., a
solver script that shells out to `curl`) is deferred. The reviewer-gate
and `.claude/hooks/guard_tool.py` are the primary enforcement layers for M11.

````

## T007 unblock punch list

T007 (ONE real flag submission to a live CTFtime-listed event) requires all of
the following human actions before the autonomous runner can proceed:

1. Set `KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1` in the session environment.
2. Register on a CTFtime-listed event (human action on the event site).
3. Populate `~/.ctf/<event-slug>.json` with `{"username": "...", "token": "..."}`.
4. Run `kca ctf event register --slug <event-slug> ...` to insert the live event row.
5. Run `kca ctf scope set --event <event-slug> ...` with a `target_urls` entry covering the event's flag-submit API endpoint.
6. Comment "approved to submit" on the T007 closing GitHub issue; a human must also add `decision:confirmed` and `ai:ready` labels (triage agent is blocked by the gh CLI hook).
7. Recover the flag for the chosen challenge via the T005/T006 solver loop under the live event's `challenge_run` approval.
8. Re-run M11-T007 Loop Prompt with these pre-conditions satisfied.

The following cross-cutting items surfaced during M11 and should be filed as
GitHub issues for resolution before or during M12 / M13:

Labels: `type:bug`, `area:cli`, `area:security`, `priority:P1`.

6. **F. httpx-level `network_egress` interceptor for subprocess egress** — ADR-0017 §enforcement-layer-pinning deferred the httpx-level interceptor that would catch solver subprocess calls bypassing the reviewer-gate. Labels: `type:feature`, `area:security`, `area:worker`, `priority:P1`.
7. **G. Per-challenge rate-limit as a `ctf_scopes` column** — T000 design-red-team carry-over. Add `rate_limit_per_hour integer` to `ctf_scopes`; guard in `cmd_flag_submit`. Labels: `type:feature`, `area:ctf`, `priority:P3`.

````markdown
# kaggle-code-agent (kca)

A hybrid human + AI workbench for competitive programming: Kaggle competitions, authorized CTF/lab challenges, Devpost hackathons, and similar code contests.

The platform is **local-first and audit-first**. Every research note, experiment, code change, test result, approval, and submission is traceable.

## Two meanings of "code agent"

This project uses two related but distinct concepts.

**Platform-development coding agents** are external AI tools — Claude Code (primary), ChatGPT, Cursor — used to build this repository. They write source code, update docs, run local tests, and open PRs under human supervision.

**Runtime competition code agents** are agents launched by the finished platform to help a human user compete. Initial runtime: Claude Agent SDK in an isolated Python worker. Future: model router for Claude (Sonnet/Opus), GPT-style models, and local vLLM/Ollama models.

See `docs/architecture/platform-vs-runtime-agents.md` for the full breakdown.

## Source of truth

**GitHub repo + Claude Code + CI + Supabase migrations.**

AI tools do not share hidden memory reliably across sessions or products. All decisions, architecture, task specs, and safety rules must live in repo files. Claude Code is the primary development environment for all product layers (CLI, backend, UI shell, worker).

Key files:
- `PROJECT_STATE.md` — current project snapshot and open decisions
- `AGENTS.md` — cross-tool instructions for ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor, and other agents
- `CLAUDE.md` — Claude Code-specific instructions and safety boundaries
- `docs/adr/` — architecture decision records
- `docs/milestones.md` — product plan from M0 through M13

## Repository layout

```
CLAUDE.md                    Claude Code project instructions
AGENTS.md                    Cross-tool agent instructions
PROJECT_STATE.md             Current project snapshot
INSTALL.md                   Local install, configure, and run guide

.claude/
  settings.json              Permissions, sandbox, hooks
  hooks/                     Pre/post tool safety and audit hooks
  agents/                    Subagents: researcher, experimenter, reviewer, safety-guard

.kca/
  skills/                    Agent workflow recipes (SKILL.md files)
  tools/tools.yaml           Tool registry with permission labels
  permissions/               Policy profiles (default, permissive-dev, competition-runner)

docs/
  milestones.md              Product plan M0–M13
  architecture.md            Component architecture overview
  architecture/
    kca-cli-architecture.md  Commands vs Skills vs Tools vs Jobs (M7)
    model-routing.md         Model routing tiers and logging policy
    platform-vs-runtime-agents.md  Two meanings of "code agent"
  adr/                       Architecture decision records
  tasks/                     Task specifications (M0-T001, M1-T001, ...)
  testing.md                 Test commands and current blockers
  testing/                   Competition-level regression test cases
  meeting-notes/             Summarized decisions and discussions

````

## Quick start for a new AI session

1. Read `PROJECT_STATE.md` for current status and open decisions.
2. Read `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` depending on your tool.
3. Read the relevant task spec under `docs/tasks/`.
4. Return a plan and wait for human approval before editing files.
5. Never read `.env`, `kaggle.json`, `secrets/`, or private keys.
6. Never submit to Kaggle, push kernels, or perform any remote write without explicit human approval.

## Install and configure

### Prerequisites

| Tool | Version | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Python | ≥ 3.11 | `uv` recommended for env management |
| Node.js | ≥ 20 | required for M8 UI shell |
| Docker | recent | for local Supabase |
| Supabase CLI | ≥ 1.200 | `brew install supabase/tap/supabase` |
| Kaggle CLI | ≥ 1.6 | `pip install kaggle` |
| `gh` CLI | ≥ 2.40 | for PR/branch operations |

### Local setup

```bash
# 1. Clone
git clone https://github.com/<your-org>/kaggle-code-agent.git
cd kaggle-code-agent

# 2. Install Python package (kca CLI)
pip install -e .
# or with uv:
uv pip install -e .

# 3. Verify kca is available
kca --help

# 4. Copy env template
cp env.example .env
# Fill in SUPABASE_DB_URL, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, KAGGLE_USERNAME/KAGGLE_KEY
````

## Cross-cutting follow-ups from M11 (file as GitHub issues)

### A. `agent_jobs.competition_id` schema drift on cloud

- **Type:** bug.
- **Labels:** `type:bug`, `area:supabase`, `priority:P2`.
- **Symptom:** T006 driver bypassed `_db.create_job()` because the cloud `agent_jobs.competition_id` column is missing. Schema drift between local migration state and cloud.
- **Suggested fix:** check which migrations haven't been applied to cloud; apply idempotently.
- **Acceptance:** `_db.create_job(competition_id=<id>)` works without a column error on cloud.

### B. `kca ctf flag submit` non-dry-run does env-check before reviewer-gate

- **Type:** bug / security.
- **Labels:** `type:bug`, `area:cli`, `area:security`, `priority:P1`.
- **Symptom:** `cmd_flag_submit` in `tools/kca/ctf.py` checks for `KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE` and credential presence before calling `should_consult_reviewer`. A missing credential causes a pre-gate failure, not a gate-then-credential error. This means a misconfigured env can bypass the gate in a confusing way.
- **Suggested fix:** reorder so `should_consult_reviewer` fires first; credential check happens only after approval is granted.
- **Acceptance:** `kca ctf flag submit` without credentials still fires the reviewer-gate and only fails at the credential step after an approve verdict.

### C. T004 fixture-authoring trail contains deterministic crypto flag

- **Type:** security (low severity — flag is deterministic and reproducible from committed `params.json`, but the audit trail shouldn't persist it).
- **Labels:** `type:security`, `area:testing`, `priority:P1`.
- **Symptom:** `.agent/audit/tool-events.jsonl` timestamps 15:19/15:20 contain the deterministic crypto flag value from T004 fixture authoring. The flag is mathematically derivable from committed `params.json`, so this is a disclosure of an already-public value — but the pattern of storing flag values in audit trails must be addressed.
- **Suggested fix:** add flag-pattern scrubbing to the audit JSONL writer (same pattern as `response_excerpt` scrubbing in `record_attempt`).
- **Acceptance:** `grep -r "kca{" .agent/` returns 0 hits after re-running T004.

### D. `expected.sha256` web-1 churn

- **Type:** test-gap.
- **Labels:** `type:test-gap`, `area:ctf`, `priority:P2`.
- **Symptom:** `data/ctf/kca-fixtures-2026/web-1-cookie-monster/expected.sha256` is regenerated on every solve run (the harness generates a fresh flag each time). The file is committed, so each T005 run leaves a dirty worktree.
- **Suggested fix:** fix the web flag in the fixture (e.g., as a hex secret in `.env.test`); or document that the harness always owns the web flag and the committed `expected.sha256` is a placeholder (`<harness-generated>`).
- **Acceptance:** `git status` shows no dirty `expected.sha256` after running `m11_t005_solve_bundled.py`.

### E. gh CLI hook denial blocks `decision:confirmed` verification

- **Type:** bug / usability.
- **Labels:** `type:bug`, `area:security`, `area:ci`, `priority:P2`.
- **Symptom:** The `.claude/hooks/guard_tool.py` hook denies `gh issue view`, `gh issue edit`, and `gh pr create` for label-inspection / label-set operations in T000, T007, and T008, forcing manual out-of-band verification.
- **Suggested fix:** add a read-only `gh issue view` allow to the hook; or document an out-of-band verification path (e.g., checking `gh issue view --json labels` without the hook).
- **Acceptance:** `gh issue view <N> --json state,labels` works in the agent session without a hook denial.

### F. httpx-level `network_egress` interceptor for subprocess egress (ADR-0017 deferred)

- **Type:** feature / security.
- **Labels:** `type:feature`, `area:security`, `area:worker`, `priority:P1`.
- **Symptom:** The reviewer-gate and hook cover direct worker HTTP calls. A solver subprocess that shells out to `curl` or uses `urllib` can bypass the gate entirely. ADR-0017 §enforcement-layer-pinning records this explicitly as deferred.
- **Suggested fix:** add an httpx-monkey-patch or a subprocess env injector (`http_proxy=block://`) that captures and audits subprocess HTTP calls.
- **Acceptance:** a test that asserts a subprocess `curl` call from a CTF job context is caught and denied at the `network_egress` gate.

### G. Per-challenge rate-limit column on `ctf_scopes`

- **Type:** feature.
- **Labels:** `type:feature`, `area:ctf`, `priority:P3`.
- **Symptom:** T000 design-red-team raised the question of per-challenge rate-limiting. No `rate_limit_per_hour` column exists on `ctf_scopes`.
- **Suggested fix:** migration 0009 adding `rate_limit_per_hour integer null`; guard in `cmd_flag_submit` that checks the rate limit before attempting a submission.
- **Acceptance:** `kca ctf scope set --rate-limit 5` sets the column; `cmd_flag_submit` respects it.

Build a hybrid human + AI competition engineering workbench. The first target is Kaggle-style competitions, with future support for authorized CTF/lab challenges. The system should research, discuss ideas with humans, edit code, run tests/evaluations, analyze results, iterate, and prepare submissions under human-approved guardrails.

## Chosen architecture direction
- Hybrid architecture.
- Claude Code Desktop/CLI for interactive project development and dogfooding (primary development tool for all layers).
- Claude Agent SDK for the production coding worker.
- Python-first worker for Kaggle/ML/CTF execution.
- TypeScript/Supabase control plane and UI shell (developed in Claude Code, not Lovable).
- GitHub + Claude Code + CI + Supabase migrations are the source of truth. All decisions, architecture, task specs, and safety rules live in repo files.
- Supabase is the control plane and audit database, not the primary code execution environment.

## Current MVP boundary
1. Local-first repository workflow with `CLAUDE.md`, skills, hooks, subagents, and GitHub.
2. Supabase schema for projects, sessions, jobs, messages, research notes, experiments, runs, submissions, artifacts, approvals, and `agent_tool_audit` (M8).
3. Kaggle baseline loop: understand competition, create validation, run baseline, record metrics, iterate, prepare submission.
4. Browser/research loop: fetch pages, summarize sources, track trust and citations.
5. Multi-agent reviewer gate + OTEL telemetry + local GPU model layer.
6. Authorized CTF sandbox loop only for explicit challenge environments.
7. Operator-facing UI: Dashboard, Run Timeline (OTEL swim-lane), Experiments, Research, Approval Inbox + Decision Gate, Artifact Browser.

## Human approval gates
Require approval for:
- Kaggle competition submissions.
- Kaggle kernel/notebook pushes.
- Any remote write operation.
- Any operation touching credentials, secrets, or account settings.
- Any CTF action outside a declared sandbox/challenge scope.
- PR merges (create is allowed, merge requires approval).

Mutations from the UI flow through `services/decision_api/` (FastAPI) →
`tools/kca/decisions.py` → DB. The browser bundle never holds a
Supabase service-role key. The M7 permission policy resolution stays
authoritative.

| Tool | Version | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Python | ≥ 3.11 | `uv` recommended for env management |
| Node.js | ≥ 20 | required for M8 UI shell |
| Docker | recent | for local Supabase |
| Supabase CLI | ≥ 1.200 | `brew install supabase/tap/supabase` |
| Kaggle CLI | ≥ 1.6 | `pip install kaggle` |
| `gh` CLI | ≥ 2.40 | for PR/branch operations |

### Local setup

```bash
# 1. Clone
git clone https://github.com/<your-org>/kaggle-code-agent.git
cd kaggle-code-agent

# 2. Install Python package (kca CLI)
pip install -e .
# or with uv:
````

# Kaggle Code Agent — Project State

_Last updated: 2026-06-09 (M11 partial close)_

## Product intent
Build a hybrid human + AI competition engineering workbench. The first target is Kaggle-style competitions, with future support for authorized CTF/lab challenges. The system should research, discuss ideas with humans, edit code, run tests/evaluations, analyze results, iterate, and prepare submissions under human-approved guardrails.

## Chosen architecture direction
- Hybrid architecture.
- Claude Code Desktop/CLI for interactive project development and dogfooding (primary development tool for all layers).
- Claude Agent SDK for the production coding worker.
- Python-first worker for Kaggle/ML/CTF execution.
- TypeScript/Supabase control plane and UI shell (developed in Claude Code, not Lovable).
- GitHub + Claude Code + CI + Supabase migrations are the source of truth. All decisions, architecture, task specs, and safety rules live in repo files.
- Supabase is the control plane and audit database, not the primary code execution environment.

## Current MVP boundary
1. Local-first repository workflow with `CLAUDE.md`, skills, hooks, subagents, and GitHub.
2. Supabase schema for projects, sessions, jobs, messages, research notes, experiments, runs, submissions, artifacts, approvals, and `agent_tool_audit` (M8).
3. Kaggle baseline loop: understand competition, create validation, run baseline, record metrics, iterate, prepare submission.
4. Browser/research loop: fetch pages, summarize sources, track trust and citations.
5. Multi-agent reviewer gate + OTEL telemetry + local GPU model layer.
6. Authorized CTF sandbox loop only for explicit challenge environments.
7. Operator-facing UI: Dashboard, Run Timeline (OTEL swim-lane), Experiments, Research, Approval Inbox + Decision Gate, Artifact Browser.

## Human approval gates
Require approval for:
- Kaggle competition submissions.
- Kaggle kernel/notebook pushes.
- Any remote write operation.
- Any operation touching credentials, secrets, or account settings.
- Any CTF action outside a declared sandbox/challenge scope.
- PR merges (create is allowed, merge requires approval).

Mutations from the UI flow through `services/decision_api/` (FastAPI) →
`tools/kca/decisions.py` → DB. The browser bundle never holds a
Supabase service-role key. The M7 permission policy resolution stays
authoritative.

def _load_event_credentials(event_slug: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Read CTF credentials for `event_slug`.

    Lookup order:
      1) ~/.ctf/<event_slug>.json — JSON object with at least
         `username` and `token`, optional `team_id`.
      2) CTF_<EVENT>_USERNAME + CTF_<EVENT>_TOKEN env vars,
         optional CTF_<EVENT>_TEAM_ID. `<EVENT>` is `event_slug`
         upper-cased with `-` → `_`.

    Returns a dict::

        {
          "source":   "file" | "env",
          "has_username": bool,
          "has_token":    bool,
          "has_team_id":  bool,
          "_username":    str,        # raw — never to be echoed
          "_token":       str,        # raw — never to be echoed
          "_team_id":     str | None, # raw — never to be echoed
        }

    Callers MUST only forward the boolean-presence fields to anything
    that could end up in stdout / stderr / an audit row / a JSON
    envelope. The underscored fields are intended for in-memory use
    inside the same function call and should be dropped immediately
    after the HTTP request body is built.
    """
    if not event_slug:
        raise CredentialsMissing("event_slug is required")

    # Path 1: file under ~/.ctf/
    cred_path = _CTF_CRED_DIR / f"{event_slug}.json"
    if cred_path.exists():
        try:
            data = json.loads(cred_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
            raise CredentialsMissing(
                f"~/.ctf/{event_slug}.json is not valid JSON: {type(exc).__name__}"
            ) from exc
        username = data.get("username")
        token = data.get("token")
        team_id = data.get("team_id")
        if not (username and token):
            raise CredentialsMissing(
                f"~/.ctf/{event_slug}.json missing 'username' or 'token' "
                f"(team_id is optional)"
            )
        return {
            "source": "file",
            "has_username": True,
            "has_token": True,
            "has_team_id": bool(team_id),
            "_username": username,
            "_token": token,
            "_team_id": team_id,
        }

    # Path 2: env vars
    env_key = event_slug.upper().replace("-", "_")
    u = os.environ.get(f"CTF_{env_key}_USERNAME")
    t = os.environ.get(f"CTF_{env_key}_TOKEN")
    team = os.environ.get(f"CTF_{env_key}_TEAM_ID")
    if u and t:
        return {
            "source": "env",
            "has_username": True,
            "has_token": True,
            "has_team_id": bool(team),
            "_username": u,
            "_token": t,
            "_team_id": team,
        }

    raise CredentialsMissing(
        f"no credentials for event '{event_slug}': expected "
        f"~/.ctf/{event_slug}.json OR CTF_{env_key}_USERNAME + "
        f"CTF_{env_key}_TOKEN env vars"
    )


def _safe_cred_presence(creds: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return only the boolean-presence + source fields from a creds dict.

    Anything passed through this strip is safe to put in stdout / JSON
    envelopes / audit rows.
    """
    return {
        "source": creds.get("source"),
        "has_username": bool(creds.get("has_username")),
        "has_token": bool(creds.get("has_token")),
        "has_team_id": bool(creds.get("has_team_id")),
    }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  - `challenge add|list|info`          LOCAL_WRITE / READ_ONLY
  - `challenge fetch`                  REMOTE_WRITE — KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1

  - `scope set|list|verify`            LOCAL_WRITE / READ_ONLY

def _jsonable(v: Any) -> Any:
    if isinstance(v, dict):
        return {k: _jsonable(vv) for k, vv in v.items()}
    if hasattr(v, "isoformat"):
        return v.isoformat()
    if isinstance(v, list):
        return [_jsonable(x) for x in v]
    return (
        v
        if (v is None or isinstance(v, (str, int, float, bool, list, dict)))
        else str(v)
    )


def _emit(payload: dict) -> None:
    print(json.dumps({k: _jsonable(v) for k, v in payload.items()}, ensure_ascii=False))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Claude Code PreToolUse guardrail hook for permissive KCA development.

Policy:
- Allow normal development work without prompts.
- Deny secret access and host-destructive operations.
- Ask only for irreversible or decision-level operations.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def emit(decision: str, reason: str) -> None:
    print(
        json.dumps(
            {
                "hookSpecificOutput": {
                    "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
                    "permissionDecision": decision,
                    "permissionDecisionReason": reason,
                }
            }
        )
    )


def normalize_path(value: str) -> str:
    if not value:
        return ""
    return os.path.expanduser(value).replace("\\", "/")


def path_is_protected(path: str) -> bool:
    """Dev-phase carve-out: project .env, .env.local, .env.development and
    ~/.kaggle/kaggle.json are readable so kca / Claude Code can pick up the
    local DSN and Kaggle test credentials without manual handoffs.
    .env.production and .env.test remain protected — these may contain
    production/staging credentials. SSH / AWS / gcloud / gh OAuth token /
    generic secrets/ dir stay protected.

    M11 (ADR-0017): per-event CTF credentials live in ~/.ctf/<slug>.json and
    are intended to be read ONLY from the allow-listed call-site
    `tools/kca/ctf.py::_load_event_credentials`. Direct Read/Edit of paths
    under ~/.ctf/ (and ctf-credentials.json anywhere) is denied at the hook
    layer — the kca CTF flow opens the file via Python `open()` from inside
    the kca process, never via the Claude Code Read/Edit/Write tools.
    """
    p = normalize_path(path)
    protected_fragments = [
        "/secrets/",
        "/.ssh/",
        "/.aws/",
        "/.config/gcloud/",
        "/.config/gh/hosts.yml",
        "/.netrc",
        "/id_rsa",
        "/id_ed25519",
        # M11: deny Read/Edit/Write of any path under ~/.ctf/. This catches
        # both ~/.ctf/<slug>.json and arbitrary CTF credential dumps the
        # human may have staged there.
        "/.ctf/",
    ]
    protected_names = {
        ".env.production",
        ".env.test",
        ".netrc",
        "id_rsa",
        "id_ed25519",
        "hosts.yml",
        # M11: explicit per-name guard so a relative path like
        # "ctf-credentials.json" is denied even outside ~/.ctf/.
        "ctf-credentials.json",
    }
    name = Path(p).name
    return name in protected_names or any(
        fragment in p for fragment in protected_fragments
    )


def compact(command: str) -> str:
    return " ".join(command.strip().split())


def bash_decision(command: str) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
    c = compact(command)
    lc = c.lower()

    # Hard deny: host-destructive, privilege escalation, secret
    # exfiltration, and permanent-deletion remote writes. Project .env
    # and ~/.kaggle/kaggle.json are intentionally not in the secret list
    # (dev-phase carve-out — see path_is_protected docstring).
    deny_patterns = [
        (r"\bsudo\b", "Refusing sudo from the agent."),
        (r"\bsu\s+", "Refusing su from the agent."),
        (r"\bdoas\b", "Refusing doas from the agent."),
        (
            r"\brm\s+-rf\s+(/|~|\$HOME)(\s|$)",
            "Refusing recursive deletion of root/home.",
        ),
        (
            r"\brm\s+-rf\s+/\S+",
            "Refusing recursive deletion of absolute filesystem paths.",
        ),
        (r"\bchmod\s+777\b", "Refusing chmod 777."),
        (r"\bchown\s+.*\s+(/|~|\$HOME)\b", "Refusing ownership change on broad paths."),
        (r"\bdd\s+.*\bof=/dev/", "Refusing raw disk write."),
        (r"\bmkfs(\.|\s|$)", "Refusing filesystem formatting command."),
        (r"\bshutdown\b|\breboot\b|\bhalt\b", "Refusing host power command."),
        (r"\bgit\s+push\s+(-f|--force|--force-with-lease)", "Refusing force push."),
        (
            r"\bgit\s+push\b[^|]*?(--delete\b|\s:\S)",
            "Refusing remote branch deletion (preserve GitHub branch history).",
        ),
        (
            r"\bgh\s+(issue|label|release|repo|secret|webhook|ssh-key|gpg-key|cache|run)\s+delete\b",
            "Refusing permanent GitHub deletion (issues / labels / releases / repo / secrets / webhooks / keys / caches / runs).",
        ),
        (
            r"\bgh\s+extension\s+remove\b",
            "Refusing gh extension removal.",
        ),
        (
            r"\bdocker\s+run\b.*\s--privileged\b",
            "Refusing privileged Docker container.",

@@ -10,3 +10,93 @@         "has_token": bool(creds.get("has_token")),
         "has_team_id": bool(creds.get("has_team_id")),
     }
+
+
+def _parse_dotenv(text: str) -> dict[str, str]:
+    """Tiny KEY=VALUE parser for ~/.env. Strips surrounding quotes; ignores
+    blank lines and `#` comments. Does NOT execute shell expansion.
+
+    Kept local to this module to avoid pulling in python-dotenv just for
+    two keys.
+    """
+    out: dict[str, str] = {}
+    for raw in text.splitlines():
+        line = raw.strip()
+        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
+            continue
+        if "=" not in line:
+            continue
+        k, _, v = line.partition("=")
+        k = k.strip()
+        if not k:
+            continue
+        v = v.strip()
+        if (len(v) >= 2) and v[0] == v[-1] and v[0] in ("'", '"'):
+            v = v[1:-1]
+        out[k] = v
+    return out
+
+
+def _load_ctftime_credentials() -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Read the **CTFtime.org platform-level** account credentials.
+
+    Lookup order:
+      1) ~/.env file with `CTFTIME_USERNAME` and `CTFTIME_PASSWORD`
+         (or `CTFTIME_TOKEN`).
+      2) Process env vars with the same names (useful in CI).
+
+    Returns a dict::
+
+        {
+          "source":   "home_env" | "process_env",
+          "has_username": bool,
+          "has_token":    bool,    # True if password OR token present
+          "has_team_id":  False,   # not applicable to CTFtime account
+          "_username":    str,     # raw — never to be echoed
+          "_token":       str,     # raw — never to be echoed
+        }
+
+    Raises `CredentialsMissing` if neither path yields a complete
+    (username, password|token) pair. Callers MUST only forward the
+    `_safe_cred_presence(...)` result to stdout / JSON envelopes /
+    audit rows. Underscored fields are intended for in-memory POST
+    body construction only and should be dropped immediately after.
+    """
+    # Path 1: ~/.env
+    if _CTFTIME_ENV_PATH.exists():
+        try:
+            parsed = _parse_dotenv(_CTFTIME_ENV_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+        except OSError as exc:
+            raise CredentialsMissing(
+                f"~/.env unreadable: {type(exc).__name__}"
+            ) from exc
+        username = parsed.get("CTFTIME_USERNAME")
+        token = parsed.get("CTFTIME_PASSWORD") or parsed.get("CTFTIME_TOKEN")
+        if username and token:
+            return {
+                "source": "home_env",
+                "has_username": True,
+                "has_token": True,
+                "has_team_id": False,
+                "_username": username,
+                "_token": token,
+            }
+
+    # Path 2: process env vars (CI-friendly)
+    username = os.environ.get("CTFTIME_USERNAME")
+    token = os.environ.get("CTFTIME_PASSWORD") or os.environ.get("CTFTIME_TOKEN")
+    if username and token:
+        return {
+            "source": "process_env",
+            "has_username": True,
+            "has_token": True,
+            "has_team_id": False,
+            "_username": username,
+            "_token": token,
+        }
+
+    raise CredentialsMissing(
+        "no CTFtime platform credentials: expected ~/.env with "
+        "CTFTIME_USERNAME + CTFTIME_PASSWORD (or CTFTIME_TOKEN), "
+        "OR the same as process env vars"
+    )

"""Smoke-test the new CTFtime loader without touching ~/.env."""
import os
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import patch

sys.path.insert(0, 'tools/kca')
from ctf import _load_ctftime_credentials, _parse_dotenv, _safe_cred_presence, CredentialsMissing  # noqa: E402

# Test 1: _parse_dotenv basic shape
print('== _parse_dotenv ==')
parsed = _parse_dotenv("""
# comment line
CTFTIME_USERNAME=flyingfox
CTFTIME_PASSWORD="some-secret"
CTFTIME_TOKEN='alt-token'
EMPTY=
KEY_WITH_SPACES =  hello world
""".strip())
print(f"  parsed keys: {sorted(parsed.keys())}")
assert parsed['CTFTIME_USERNAME'] == 'flyingfox'
assert parsed['CTFTIME_PASSWORD'] == 'some-secret', repr(parsed['CTFTIME_PASSWORD'])
assert parsed['CTFTIME_TOKEN'] == 'alt-token'
assert parsed['EMPTY'] == ''
assert parsed['KEY_WITH_SPACES'] == 'hello world'
print('  PASS')

# Test 2: loader misses when neither file nor env
print('== loader returns CredentialsMissing when nothing present ==')
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
    fake_home = Path(td)
    # patch HOME and the module-level constant
    import ctf as ctf_mod
    with patch.dict(os.environ, {'HOME': str(fake_home)}, clear=False), \
         patch.object(ctf_mod, '_CTFTIME_ENV_PATH', fake_home / '.env'):
        # also clear CTFTIME_* from process env
        for k in ('CTFTIME_USERNAME', 'CTFTIME_PASSWORD', 'CTFTIME_TOKEN'):
            os.environ.pop(k, None)
        try:
            _load_ctftime_credentials()
        except CredentialsMissing as exc:
            print(f"  PASS (raised: {exc})")
        else:
            print('  FAIL — should have raised CredentialsMissing')

# Test 3: loader reads ~/.env when present
print('== loader reads ~/.env (file path) ==')
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
    fake_home = Path(td)
    (fake_home / '.env').write_text(
        'CTFTIME_USERNAME=flyingfox\n'
        'CTFTIME_PASSWORD=secretpass\n',
        encoding='utf-8',
    )
    import ctf as ctf_mod
    with patch.object(ctf_mod, '_CTFTIME_ENV_PATH', fake_home / '.env'):
        for k in ('CTFTIME_USERNAME', 'CTFTIME_PASSWORD', 'CTFTIME_TOKEN'):
            os.environ.pop(k, None)
        creds = _load_ctftime_credentials()
        safe = _safe_cred_presence(creds)
        print(f"  creds source={creds['source']}, safe={safe}")
        assert creds['source'] == 'home_env'
        assert creds['has_username'] is True
        assert creds['has_token'] is True
        assert 'flyingfox' not in str(safe), 'safe view must not echo username value'
        assert 'secretpass' not in str(safe), 'safe view must not echo token value'
        print('  PASS — safe view excludes raw values')

# Test 4: process env fallback
print('== loader reads process env when file absent ==')
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
    fake_home = Path(td)  # no .env file
    import ctf as ctf_mod

        assert creds['source'] == 'process_env'
        assert creds['_username'] == 'ci-user'
        assert creds['_token'] == 'ci-token'
        print('  PASS')

print()
print('All loader smoke checks PASS.')

```markdown
## 2. Credential file shape and load path

Credential resolution order (first match wins):

1. `~/.ctf/<event-slug>.json` — JSON object with `username`, `token`, optional `team_id`.
2. Environment variables `CTF_<EVENT_SLUG_UPPER>_USERNAME` and `CTF_<EVENT_SLUG_UPPER>_TOKEN`.

The `kca ctf flag submit` command calls `_load_event_credentials(slug)` which:

- reads the JSON file via a guarded path (`.claude/hooks/guard_tool.py` carve-out);
- or reads the env vars;
- raises `CredentialsError` if neither is found, returning exit code 1 with the message "CTF credentials not found — set `~/.ctf/<slug>.json` or env vars" (no credential value emitted).

The credential is held in memory only for the duration of the HTTP call.
It is never written to `ctf_attempts` or any other DB row.

## 3. Challenge inventory and category triage

After event registration:

1. `kca ctf challenge add --event <slug> --challenge-slug <slug> --category web --points 100 --description "..."` inserts a `ctf_challenges` row (LOCAL_WRITE).
2. `kca ctf challenge list --event <slug>` lists challenges with their category and scope reference.
3. `kca ctf scope set --event <slug> --challenge <slug> --target-urls "http://localhost:18080" --local-only true` creates or updates a `ctf_scopes` row.

Category triage in the solver loop:

- `web` — docker-compose service; solver uses httpx against localhost; no external network needed for frozen bundles.
- `crypto` — in-process Python; no network; deterministic from committed parameters.
- `pwn`, `rev`, `forensics` — recognized as valid categories in `ctf_challenges.category` but the M11 solve loop does not implement agent loops for these; filed as M11 follow-up.

The challenge inventory is read-only from the perspective of the solver worker.
Adding challenges requires a separate `kca ctf challenge add` invocation (LOCAL_WRITE, not subject to the `challenge_run` gate).

## 4. Solver execution under the `challenge_run` gate

```

### 3. Enforcement layer pinning

The design-red-team report
(`docs/evidence/m11/discovery/design-red-team.md` § `open_disagreements`
4th bullet) raised the open question: which layer enforces
`network_egress`? Three candidates exist:

- **Reviewer-gate** (`src/worker/reviewer.py`): fires when the worker
  raises `ApprovalRequired(operation="network_egress")`.
- **Hook layer** (`.claude/hooks/guard_tool.py`): denies known-bad
  hosts at Claude Code's PreToolUse step.
- **HTTP-client interceptor** (httpx middleware): wraps every outbound
  request from the worker.

**Decision (binding for M11):**

1. **Primary authority: the reviewer-gate.** When the worker is about
   to issue a request whose host is outside the in-scope union, it
   raises `ApprovalRequired("network_egress", ...)`. The reviewer-gate
   is the deny-default authority. This is what `.kca/permissions/*.yaml`
   pins.
2. **Secondary defense: the hook layer.** `.claude/hooks/guard_tool.py`
   denies known-bad hosts (metadata services, CTF credential paths)
   even before the reviewer fires. This catches shell-level egress
   attempts (`curl`, `wget`, `scp`, `rsync`) and direct Read/Edit of
   `~/.ctf/*.json`.
3. **Out of scope for M11: the httpx interceptor.** A per-request
   httpx middleware that consults `ctf_scopes.target_urls` on every
   outbound HTTP call is *the right long-term answer* (it survives
   subprocess and direct-Python paths the worker doesn't know about),
   but it requires touching `tools/kca/research_fetch.py` and every
   other httpx-using surface. Filed as a follow-up: `M12 / M13
   network-egress-interceptor`.

The known consequence of the layer choice: a subprocess `curl` issued
from inside a `bash` tool call bypasses both the reviewer-gate and the
hook layer's regex (for hosts not in `deny_patterns`). M11 mitigates by
hard-asking on every `bash` call under `default.yaml` and by the M11-T005
solver flow running `docker-compose up` against a *local* network only —
the live event egress is gated to T007's single approved call.

+### 3a. CTFtime platform credential tier (`~/.env`)
+
+_Added 2026-05-27 in response to PR #45 reviewer feedback._
+
+Background: the user pointed out that the M11-T002/T003 credential model
+only covered **per-event** signups (`~/.ctf/<slug>.json`). It did not
+have a place for the **CTFtime.org platform account** (single account
+per user; used for the CTFtime calendar / event-registration flow and
+for events that accept CTFtime SSO).
+
+**Decision:** treat CTFtime as a separate, single-account credential
+tier with its own canonical location, loader, and hook carve-out —
+parallel to the per-event tier.
+
+| Aspect | CTFtime platform tier | Per-event tier |
+|---|---|---|
+| When to use | CTFtime calendar / SSO-enabled events | Events requiring separate signup |
+| Storage | `~/.env` (one file per user) | `~/.ctf/<slug>.json` (one file per event) |
+| Keys | `CTFTIME_USERNAME`, `CTFTIME_PASSWORD` (or `CTFTIME_TOKEN`) | `username`, `token`, optional `team_id` |
+| Loader | `tools/kca/ctf.py::_load_ctftime_credentials()` | `tools/kca/ctf.py::_load_event_credentials(slug)` |
+| Hook carve-out | `~/.env` denied at hook; loader is sole allow-listed caller | `~/.ctf/*` denied at hook; loader is sole allow-listed caller |
+| CI fallback | process env `CTFTIME_USERNAME` + `CTFTIME_PASSWORD`/`_TOKEN` | process env `CTF_<EVENT>_USERNAME` + `CTF_<EVENT>_TOKEN` |
+
+`~/.env` is **distinct** from the project root `.env`. The project root
+`.env` (e.g., `./.env`, `./.env.local`, `./.env.development`) remains
+readable per the dev-phase carve-out documented in
+`.claude/hooks/guard_tool.py::path_is_protected` — it holds `SUPABASE_DB_URL`
+and similar local DSNs. Only `~/.env` (HOME-dir scope) is the protected
+CTFtime tier.
+
+The hook's path-protection check distinguishes them by absolute path
+equality (`p == "{HOME}/.env"`) so `./env` style relative paths still
+fall through to the dev-phase carve-out.
+
+The shell-read deny patterns additionally cover `cat ~/.env`,
+`grep ... ~/.env`, `curl -d "$(cat ~/.env)" ...`, and `/home/<user>/.env`
+absolute variants — using a tightened look-ahead `(?![.A-Za-z0-9_-])` so
+that `~/.env.local` does NOT match (we don't claim that path).
+
